title: SARS-CoV-2 Vaccination and Attenuation of Breakthrough Infection Severity: A Systematic Global Review and Meta-analysis.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) vaccines provide strong protection against severe outcomes but do not fully prevent infection, and the extent to which they attenuate disease severity among breakthrough infections remains unclear. Existing evidence is limited by small sample sizes, potential selection bias, and inconsistent findings. METHODS: We conducted a systematic selection and meta-analysis of studies identified from a living systematic review of global observational studies reporting vaccine effectiveness (VE) against symptomatic infection and hospitalization. We computed the relative VE (rVE) against hospitalization versus symptomatic infection for matched VE pairs, representing vaccine-induced attenuation of severity. Multilevel meta-analysis and metaregression were used to pool estimates and assess effect modifiers. RESULTS: A total of 184 VE pairs from 37 studies were included. The pooled rVE was 51% (95% confidence interval [CI]: 39%, 60%) for broadly defined symptomatic infection and 19% (95% CI: 12%, 25%) for medically attended symptomatic infection, indicating significant attenuation of disease severity among vaccinated cases. Given substantial heterogeneity, interpretation focused on stratified and adjusted analyses. Attenuation was lower in older adults aged ≥60 years and showed no significant waning over time. Variant patterns differed by endpoint definition: attenuation was weaker for Omicron subvariants when broadly defined symptomatic infection was the comparator. No significant differences were observed between vaccine platforms. CONCLUSIONS: COVID-19 vaccination markedly reduces the risk of progression from symptomatic infection to hospitalization. Attenuation of severity was sustained over time and did not differ significantly by vaccine platform but was lower in older adults and varied by symptomatic-infection definition and variant period.
journal: Clinical infectious diseases : an official publication of the Infectious Diseases Society of America

analysis.scope_and_question: This review investigates the effectiveness of SARS-CoV-2 vaccines in reducing the severity of breakthrough infections, focusing on hospitalization and symptomatic infection outcomes. The central question is whether vaccination attenuates disease severity among those who become infected despite immunization.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review is a systematic global analysis and meta-analysis of observational studies. It includes 37 studies with 184 VE pairs, using multilevel meta-analysis and metaregression to pool estimates and assess effect modifiers. The methodology involves computing relative VE (rVE) against hospitalization versus symptomatic infection for matched VE pairs.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The pooled relative VE against hospitalization was 51% (95% CI: 39%, 60%) for broadly defined symptomatic infection and 19% (95% CI: 12%, 25%) for medically attended symptomatic infection, indicating that vaccination significantly reduces the risk of progression to hospitalization. analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The evidence is limited by small sample sizes, potential selection bias, and inconsistent findings. Substantial heterogeneity was noted, necessitating a focus on stratified and adjusted analyses. There is also variability in attenuation based on the definition of symptomatic infection and the variant period, with weaker attenuation observed for Omicron subvariants when broadly defined symptomatic infection was the comparator.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: Further research is needed to address the variability in attenuation across different symptomatic-infection definitions and variant periods. analysis.summary_en: This systematic global review and meta-analysis evaluates the effectiveness of SARS-CoV-2 vaccines in reducing the severity of breakthrough infections. The study includes 184 vaccine effectiveness (VE) pairs from 37 observational studies, analyzing the relative VE against hospitalization and medically attended symptomatic infection. The pooled rVE was 51% and 19%, respectively, indicating significant attenuation of disease severity among vaccinated individuals. However, the evidence is limited by small sample sizes, selection bias, and heterogeneity, with lower attenuation observed in older adults and for Omicron subvariants. The findings suggest that vaccination markedly reduces the risk of progression to hospitalization, with no significant differences by vaccine platform. Research should focus on understanding variability in attenuation across different definitions and variant periods, and surveillance should account for these factors to optimize public health strategies.

elements_zh.scope_and_question: 本综述探讨了严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 疫苗 在降低突破性感染严重程度方面的有效性,重点关注住院和有症状感染结果。核心问题是:疫苗接种 是否能减轻那些尽管接种疫苗仍感染的人的疾病严重程度。
elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 该综述是一项系统性的全球分析和观察性研究的元分析。它包括37项研究,共184对疫苗效力(VE)数据,采用多层次元分析和元回归方法来汇总估计值并评估效应修饰因素。该方法涉及计算针对住院与有症状感染的相对疫苗效力(rVE)以匹配的疫苗效力对进行分析。
elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 对于广泛定义的有症状感染,汇总的相对VE(rVE)为51%(95% CI:39%,60%),对于需要医疗干预的有症状感染,汇总的rVE为19%(95% CI:12%,25%),表明疫苗接种显著降低了从有症状感染进展到住院的风险。严重程度的减轻效果随时间保持稳定,且不因疫苗平台而显著不同,但在≥60岁的老年人中减轻程度较低。
elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 证据受到样本量小、潜在选择偏倚和不一致结果的限制。注意到存在显著异质性,因此分析重点放在分层和调整后的分析上。此外,根据有症状感染的定义和变异时期的不同,减轻效果存在差异,当以广泛定义的有症状感染作为比较时,对奥密克戎亚变种的减轻效果较弱。
elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 需要进一步研究以解决不同有症状感染定义和变异时期之间减轻效果的差异。监测和诊断策略应考虑这些因素,同时应监测疫苗在老年人中的有效性,以确保其对严重结果的持续保护。

title: Immunogenicity and Safety of Coadministration of AS01E-Adjuvanted Respiratory Syncytial Virus Prefusion F Protein Vaccine and a COVID-19 mRNA Vaccine in Adult s Aged ≥50 Years: A Phase 3, Randomized, Noninferiority Trial.
abstract: BACKGROUND: This trial evaluated coadministration of the AS01E-adjuvanted respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) prefusion F protein-based vaccine (adjuvanted RSVPreF3) and an Omicron XBB.1.5-based coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) mRNA vaccine in ≥50-year-olds. METHODS: This phase 3, open-label, multicenter trial randomized ≥50-year-olds 1:1 to coadministration (Co-Ad group) or sequential administration approximately 1 month apart (Control group) of adjuvanted RSVPreF3 and the COVID-19 mRNA vaccine. Primary objectives were to demonstrate noninferiority of humoral immune responses at 1 month postvaccination in terms of RSV-A, RSV-B, and severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) neutralizing titers, with the upper limit of the 95% CI of adjusted geometric mean titer (GMT) group ratios (Control/Co-Ad) ≤1.50. Secondary objectives included assessment of reactogenicity up to 4 days and safety up to 6 months after vaccination. Noninferiority was achieved for RSV-A (GMT ratio: 1.12 [95% CI: .97-1.28]) and RSV-B (GMT ratio: 1.08 [95% CI: .94-1.23]) and marginally missed for SARS-CoV-2 Omicron XBB.1.5 (GMT ratio: 1.31 [95% CI: 1.13-1.51]). Within 4 days postvaccination, the most frequently reported solicited events were administration-site pain, myalgia, and fatigue. Most solicited events were of mild-to-moderate intensity, and the overall median duration was ≤3 days and comparable between groups. Unsolicited and serious adverse events were generally balanced between groups. CONCLUSIONS: Adjuvanted RSVPreF3 coadministered with a COVID-19 mRNA vaccine maintained an acceptable safety profile in ≥50-year-olds. The marginal miss of the noninferiority criterion for SARS-CoV-2 does not suggest clinically relevant interference. Therefore, the results support the coadministration of these vaccines. CLINICAL TRIALS REGISTRATION: Clinical Trials.gov.
journal: Clinical infectious diseases : an official publication of the Infectious Diseases Society of America

analysis.summary_en: This phase 3, randomized, noninferiority trial assessed the immunogenicity and safety of coadministering an AS01E-adjuvanted RSV prefusion F protein vaccine and an Omicron XBB.1.5-based mRNA vaccine in adults aged ≥50 years. The study compared coadministration with sequential administration, with primary endpoints focusing on immune responses against RSV-A, RSV-B, and SARS-CoV-2. Noninferiority was achieved for RSV-A and RSV-B, but the SARS-CoV-2 endpoint was marginally missed. Reactogenicity and safety were generally acceptable, with most events being mild-to-moderate and resolving within 3 days. The findings suggest that coadministration of these vaccines is safe and maintains acceptable immune responses, supporting their use in older adults. The study's results do not indicate clinically relevant interference between the vaccines, and the evidence is strong given the design and outcomes.

title: Immunogenicity and Safety of PHH-1V COVID-19 Vaccine as a Heterologous Booster in Adolescents.
abstract: BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: PHH-1V, a protein-based, non-mRNA, bivalent, adjuvanted COVID-19 vaccine, has demonstrated strong immunogenicity and favorable safety as a booster in adults. This study evaluated PHH-1V as a heterologous booster in adolescents. METHODS: HIPRA-HH-3 was a phase IIb, open-label, multicenter, noninferiority trial assessing the immunogenicity and safety of PHH-1V in 240 healthy adolescents (≥ 12 to < 18 years) primed with BNT162b2. Immunogenicity (N = 90) was assessed by measuring neutralizing antibodies against SARS-CoV-2 variants and total binding antibodies in adolescent participants vs young adults (≥ 18 to ≤ 25 years) (N = 81) from a previous trial, who had also been boosted with PHH-1V. T-cell responses at day 14 post booster were also evaluated. Antibody durability and adverse events (AEs) were assessed through day 336. RESULTS: Neutralizing titers-against Omicron BA.1 (primary endpoint), WH1, Beta, and Delta variants-and total binding antibodies were significantly higher in adolescents than in young adults (P < .001), demonstrating noninferiority (margin < 1.5). T-cell responses against BA.1 and Beta also increased significantly (P < .001). Cross-variant antibody titers remained above baseline (day 0) through day 336. AEs were mostly mild/moderate, primarily injection-site pain and headache within 28 days. No related serious AEs were reported. CONCLUSIONS: As a heterologous booster in adolescents, PHH-1V is safe and elicits cellular and sustained humoral responses with cross-variant immune recognition, which support the use of PHH-1V in adolescent vaccination strategies. Data in younger and specific risk groups are still needed.

analysis.research_question_and_background: This study aimed to evaluate the immunogenicity and safety of PHH-1V as a heterologous booster in adolescents, building on its demonstrated effectiveness in adults.
analysis.study_design_and_population: HIPRA-HH-3 was a phase IIb, open-label, multicenter, noninferiority trial involving 240 healthy adolescents (≥ 12 to < 18 years) who had previously received BNT162b2 as a prime vaccine.
analysis.methods: Immunogenicity was assessed by measuring neutralizing antibodies against SARS-CoV-2 variants and total binding antibodies in adolescents compared to young adults (≥ 18 to ≤ 25 years) from a previous trial. T-cell responses were evaluated at day 14 post-booster, and antibody durability and adverse events were monitored through day 336.
analysis.main_results: Neutralizing titers against Omicron BA.1, WH1, Beta, and Delta variants, as well as total binding antibodies, were significantly higher in adolescents than in young adults (P < .001). Cross-variant antibody titers remained above baseline through day 336. Adverse events were mostly mild/moderate, with injection-site pain and headache being the most common within 28 days. No serious adverse events were reported.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings demonstrate that PHH-1V as a heterologous booster in adolescents elicits strong immune responses and is safe, supporting its inclusion in adolescent vaccination strategies.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These results provide evidence for the effectiveness and safety of PHH-1V in adolescents, which can inform vaccination strategies and contribute to broader public health efforts against SARS-CoV-2.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its focus on a specific age group and the absence of data on younger populations or specific risk groups, which may affect generalizability. The evidence is strong, with statistically significant results and a well-defined noninferiority margin.

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluated the immunogenicity and safety of PHH-1V as a heterologous booster in adolescents. The phase IIb, open-label, multicenter trial involved 240 healthy adolescents who had previously received BNT162b2. Immunogenicity was assessed by measuring neutralizing antibodies against SARS-CoV-2 variants and total binding antibodies, comparing adolescents to young adults from a prior trial. T-cell responses were evaluated at day 14 post-booster, and antibody durability and adverse events were monitored through day 336. Results showed significantly higher neutralizing titers against Omicron BA.1, WH1, Beta, and Delta variants in adolescents compared to young adults (P < .001), with cross-variant antibody titers remaining above baseline. Adverse events were mostly mild/moderate, with no serious events reported. The authors concluded that PHH-1V is safe and elicits strong immune responses in adolescents, supporting its use in vaccination strategies. However, they noted the need for further data in younger populations and specific risk groups.

analysis_en.research_question_and_background: This study aimed to evaluate the immunogenicity and safety of PHH-1V as a heterologous booster in adolescents, building on its demonstrated effectiveness in adults.
analysis_en.study_design_and_population: HIPRA-HH-3 was a phase IIb, open-label, multicenter, noninferiority trial involving 240 healthy adolescents (≥ 12 to < 18 years) who had previously received BNT162b2 as a prime vaccine.
analysis_en.methods: Immunogenicity was assessed by measuring neutralizing antibodies against SARS-CoV-2 variants and total binding antibodies in adolescents compared to young adults (≥ 18 to ≤ 25 years) from a previous trial. T-cell responses were evaluated at day 14 post-booster, and antibody durability and adverse events were monitored through day 336.
analysis_en.main_results: Neutralizing titers against Omicron BA.1, WH1, Beta, and Delta variants, as well as total binding antibodies, were significantly higher in adolescents than in young adults (P < .001). Cross-variant antibody titers remained above baseline through day 336. Adverse events were mostly mild/moderate, with injection-site pain and headache being the most common within 28 days. No serious adverse events were reported.
analysis_en.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings demonstrate that PHH-1V as a heterologous booster in adolescents elicits strong immune responses and is safe, supporting its inclusion in adolescent vaccination strategies.
analysis_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These results provide evidence for the effectiveness and safety of PHH-1V in adolescents, which can inform vaccination strategies and contribute to broader public health efforts against SARS-CoV-2.
analysis_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its focus on a specific age group and the absence of data on younger populations or specific risk groups, which may affect generalizability. The evidence is strong, with statistically significant results and a well-defined noninferiority margin.

title_zh: Immunogenicity and Safety of PHH-1V COVID-19 Vaccine as a Heterologous Booster in Adolescents.
source_body_en: BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: PHH-1V, a protein-based, non-mRNA, bivalent, adjuvanted COVID-19 vaccine, has demonstrated strong immunogenicity and favorable safety as a booster in adults. This study evaluated PHH-1V as a heterologous booster in adolescents. METHODS: HIPRA-HH-3 was a phase IIb, open-label, multicenter, noninferiority trial assessing the immunogenicity and safety of PHH-1V in 240 healthy adolescents (≥ 12 to < 18 years) primed with BNT162b2. Immunogenicity (N = 90) was assessed by measuring neutralizing antibodies against SARS-CoV-2 variants and total binding antibodies in adolescent participants vs young adults (≥ 18 to ≤ 25 years) (N = 81) from a previous trial, who had also been boosted with PHH-1V. T-cell responses at day 14 post booster were also evaluated. Antibody durability and adverse events (AEs) were assessed through day 336. RESULTS: Neutralizing titers-against Omicron BA.1 (primary endpoint), WH1, Beta, and Delta variants-and total binding antibodies were significantly higher in adolescents than in young adults (P < .001), demonstrating noninferiority (margin < 1.5). T-cell responses against BA.1 and Beta also increased significantly (P < .001). Cross-variant antibody titers remained above baseline (day 0) through day 336. AEs were mostly mild/moderate, primarily injection-site pain and headache within 28 days. No related serious AEs were reported. CONCLUSIONS: As a heterologous booster in adolescents, PHH-1V is safe and elicits cellular and sustained humoral responses with cross-variant immune recognition, which support the use of PHH-1V in adolescent vaccination strategies. Data in younger and specific risk groups are still needed.

title: Real-World Effectiveness of International Border Health Interventions in Mitigating the Spread of SARS-CoV-2 During the First Years of the COVID-19 Pandemic, 2020-2023: A Systematic Review.
abstract: Many vaccine-related and nonpharmaceutical interventions, including travel-related measures, were established to mitigate the spread of SARS-CoV-2. Some countries began to impose measures on travelers from Wuhan, China, the location of the first identified COVID-19 cases, as early as December 31, 2019. The objective of this systematic review was to assess real-world effectiveness of travel-related measures in mitigating the international spread of SARS-CoV-2 during the declared public health emergency from 2020 to 2023. Inclusion criteria encompassed interventional and observational studies describing international travel-related mitigation measures and their effect on cases, hospitalizations, or deaths. Modeling studies were excluded. Electronic searches were performed using Embase (OVID), Global Health (OVID), CINAHL (EBSCOHost), Cochrane Library, Scopus, Medline (OVID), and World Health Organization COVID-19 Global Literature to identify studies published from January 1, 2020, through February 24, 2023. The ROBINS-I tool was used to assess risk of bias. A total of 37 observational studies met inclusion criteria for the review. Of these, 9 (24%) described quarantine-related interventions, 4 (11%) testing-only interventions, 6 (16%) border closures, 5 (14%) vaccination/immunity-based interventions, and 13 (35%) multiple interventions. Risk of bias was judged to be serious or critical for 14 (38%) of the studies. Comparison groups and outcomes were heterogeneous, but most described a positive effect on improving measured decreasing outcomes of interest. Although significant biases may be associated with these observational studies, international travel-related measures may have been effective in temporarily mitigating the spread of SARS-CoV-2 early in the pandemic. However, many measures became less effective as SARS-CoV-2 spread globally. In future pandemics, countries should consider designing evaluation strategies when measures are planned, before implementation.

title: [Dynamics of behavioral factors and attitudes toward vaccination in moscow during the COVID-19 pandemic: from the acute phase to adaptation].
abstract: BACKGROUND: The transition of the COVID-19 pandemic from the acute phase to adaptation was accompanied by changes in preventive behavior, institutional trust, emotional state and attitudes toward vaccination. OBJECTIVE: To analyze the dynamics of awareness, preventive behavior, trust, emotional state and attitudes toward vaccination among Moscow residents in 2021 compared with 2020. MATERIALS AND METHODS: The survey tool was developed by the WHO Regional Office for Europe with support from the University of Erfurt and adapted to the Moscow context. CATI was conducted using a stratified dual-frame sample. The article analyzes the 4th and 5th survey waves: February 2021 (n = 1038) and July-August 2021 (n = 998). RESULTS: By the 5th wave, adherence to most preventive measures decreased, especially social distancing, limiting contacts and using hand sanitizers. The proportion not wearing gloves increased sharply after the requirement was lifted. The mean self-assessment of emotional state decreased to 3.47 points; institutional assessments declined and vaccination attitudes became more polarized. CONCLUSIONS: Public health strategies should combine consistent scientific communication, targeted work with vaccine-hesitant groups and horizontal trust.

title: Comparative analysis of production and kinetic assay conditions and parameters for SARS-CoV-2 main protease (Mpro): a systematic review
abstract: Abstract The main protease (Mpro) of SARS-CoV-2 plays a crucial role in the viral replication cycle and is a key target for COVID-19 antiviral drugs. In this review, we conducted an extensive bibliographic search on the main challenges and experimental limitations reported in the production and biochemical characterization of the Mpro. A large variability in the kinetic parameters was revealed, which compromises comparisons across various studies and the evaluation of inhibitor efficacy. The studies indicate that these discrepancies are mainly associated with experimental limitations, such as low substrate solubility, optical irregularity due to the inner-filter effect, and variations in the oligomeric state of Mpro. This review summarizes and discusses the different strategies for Mpro expression in Escherichia coli and purification, with emphasis on obtaining an N-terminal tag-free enzyme, essential for homodimerization into a highly active form for structural and functional characterization. The main FRET-based substrates used in enzymatic assays were compiled and analyzed, as well as alternative methodologies for assessing Mpro enzymatic activity. Furthermore, the effects of assay conditions, such as buffer composition, pH, and the presence of reducing agents were addressed. The intrinsic structural features of Mpro that impact its catalytic function are discussed, including functional asymmetry in substrate binding and the positive allosteric cooperation between monomers. Overall, this review provides a critical and integrated perspective on the main experimental limitations in the production and characterization of Mpro, applicable to other proteases, contributing to the standardization of approaches and advances in the development of more effective inhibitors.

title: T-Cell Response After SARS-CoV-2 Vaccination in Patients With Hematological Malignancy.
abstract: Patients with hematologic malignancies (HM) often mount poor humoral responses to SARS-CoV-2 vaccination due to their immunocompromised status. Protection against severe COVID-19 is strongly related to cellular immunity, yet vaccine-induced T-cell responses remain incompletely characterized. We conducted a systematic review of 87 studies assessing vaccine-induced T-cell response rates in HM. Across HM subtypes, 75%-87% of studies reported T-cell response rates of at least 50%. Active disease was associated with reduced T-cell responses. These findings indicate that SARS-CoV-2 vaccination can elicit cellular immunity in HM patients, including those receiving immunosuppressive therapy, supporting continued vaccination strategies even when humoral responses are suboptimal.
authors: Catharina H. M. J. van Elssen

analysis.scope_and_question: The review focuses on T-cell responses to SARS-CoV-2 vaccination in patients with hematological malignancies (HM), particularly those with immunocompromised status. The central question is whether SARS-CoV-2 vaccination can elicit effective cellular immunity in this population, despite poor humoral responses.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review is a systematic analysis of 87 studies that evaluated vaccine-induced T-cell response rates in HM patients. The studies were selected based on their assessment of T-cell responses, and the review method involved a structured analysis of these studies to determine the overall response rates.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: Across HM subtypes, 75%-87% of studies reported T-cell response rates of at least 50%. This suggests that SARS-CoV-2 vaccination can induce significant cellular immunity in HM patients, even those on immunosuppressive therapy.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: Active disease was associated with reduced T-cell responses, indicating variability in vaccine effectiveness based on disease status. However, the evidence does not provide detailed mechanisms or long-term data on T-cell persistence.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: These findings support the continuation of SARS-CoV-2 vaccination strategies for HM patients, even when humoral responses are suboptimal. Further research is needed to explore the impact of active disease on T-cell responses and to investigate long-term immunity.

analysis.summary_en: This review evaluates T-cell responses to SARS-CoV-2 vaccination in patients with hematological malignancies (HM), a population known for poor humoral immunity. A systematic analysis of 87 studies found that 75%-87% reported T-cell response rates of at least 50%, suggesting that vaccination can elicit significant cellular immunity. Active disease was linked to reduced T-cell responses, highlighting variability in vaccine effectiveness. The results support ongoing vaccination efforts for HM patients despite suboptimal humoral responses, but further research is needed to understand the long-term implications and mechanisms of T-cell immunity in this group.

elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 本综述是对87项研究的系统分析,这些研究评估了疫苗在HM患者中诱导的T细胞反应率。研究的选择基于其对T细胞反应的评估,综述方法涉及对这些研究的结构化分析,以确定总体反应率。
elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 在不同HM亚型中,75%-87%的研究报告了至少50%的T细胞反应率。这表明,严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 疫苗接种能够在HM患者中诱导显著的细胞免疫,即使这些患者正在接受免疫抑制治疗。
elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 活动性疾病与T细胞反应降低相关,表明疫苗的效果可能因疾病状态而异。然而,现有证据并未提供关于T细胞持续性的详细机制或长期数据。
elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 这些发现支持在体液免疫反应不佳的情况下继续对HM患者实施严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 疫苗接种策略。需要进一步研究以探讨活动性疾病对T细胞反应的影响,并调查长期免疫情况。

Further research is needed to explore the impact of active disease on T-cell responses and to investigate long-term immunity.

title_zh: T细胞对严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 疫苗接种的反应在血液系统恶性肿瘤患者中的表现。
source_body_en: Patients with hematologic malignancies (HM) often mount poor humoral responses to SARS-CoV-2 vaccination due to their immunocompromised status. Protection against severe COVID-19 is strongly related to cellular immunity, yet vaccine-induced T-cell responses remain incompletely characterized. We conducted a systematic review of 87 studies assessing vaccine-induced T-cell response rates in HM. Across HM subtypes, 75%-87% of studies reported T-cell response rates of at least 50%. Active disease was associated with reduced T-cell responses. These findings indicate that SARS-CoV-2 vaccination can elicit cellular immunity in HM patients, including those receiving immunosuppressive therapy, supporting continued vaccination strategies even when humoral responses are suboptimal.

analysis_zh.scope_and_question: 本综述聚焦于血液系统恶性肿瘤(HM)患者对严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 疫苗接种的T细胞反应,特别是免疫功能低下的患者。核心问题是:尽管体液免疫反应较差,严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 疫苗接种是否能够在该人群中引发有效的细胞免疫?
analysis_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 本综述是对87项研究的系统分析,这些研究评估了疫苗在HM患者中诱导的T细胞反应率。研究的选择基于其对T细胞反应的评估,综述方法涉及对这些研究的结构化分析,以确定总体反应率。
analysis_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 在不同HM亚型中,75%-87%的研究报告了至少50%的T细胞反应率。这表明,严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 疫苗接种能够在HM患者中诱导显著的细胞免疫,即使这些患者正在接受免疫抑制治疗。
analysis_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 活动性疾病与T细胞反应降低相关,表明疫苗的效果可能因疾病状态而异。然而,现有证据并未提供关于T细胞持续性的详细机制或长期数据。
analysis_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 这些发现支持在体液免疫反应不佳的情况下继续对HM患者实施严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 疫苗接种策略。需要进一步研究以探讨活动性疾病对T细胞反应的影响,并调查长期免疫情况。

title: Aromaticity at spike position 456 affects functional immunogenicity of SARS-CoV-2 Omicron variant receptor-binding domain
abstract: The recurrent emergence of the F456L substitution in SARS-CoV-2 Omicron sublineages has been associated with immune evasion, yet its impact on vaccine-induced immune responses remains poorly understood. Using a trimeric RBD-HR subunit vaccine platform, we investigated how residue 456 influences the functional immunogenicity of the receptor-binding domain (RBD). We found that the F456L substitution markedly reduced neutralizing antibody responses against multiple SARS-CoV-2 variants, despite maintaining comparable levels of total antigen-specific IgG, indicating a selective impairment of functional immunogenicity rather than overall antigenicity. Single-cell RNA sequencing and B-cell receptor (BCR) repertoire analyses further revealed that the F456L mutation weakened germinal center responses, reduced clonal expansion, and impaired repertoire remodeling of antigen-specific B cells. Structural modeling, biolayer interferometry, and calcium flux assays demonstrated that aromatic residues at position 456 promote effective germline BCR recognition and activation. Importantly, replacing the non-aromatic leucine residue with aromatic amino acids, including tyrosine or tryptophan, restored the neutralizing antibody-eliciting capacity of the antigen. Together, these findings identify aromaticity at residue 456 as a critical determinant of RBD functional immunogenicity and demonstrate how a single amino acid substitution can reshape B-cell responses and antibody quality. This work provides important insights for rational vaccine antigen design and advances our understanding of how site-specific mutations regulate antiviral immunity.

abstract_zh: F456L取代在严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2奥密克戎亚系中反复出现,与免疫逃逸有关,但其对疫苗诱导的免疫应答的影响仍不明确。我们使用三聚体RBD-HR亚单位疫苗平台,研究了第456位残基如何影响受体结合域(RBD)的功能免疫原性。我们发现,F456L取代显著降低了针对多种严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2变体的中和抗体反应,尽管总抗原特异性IgG水平保持相当,这表明功能性免疫原性的选择性受损,而非整体抗原性。单细胞RNA测序和B细胞受体(BCR)谱分析进一步揭示,F456L取代削弱了生发中心反应,减少了克隆扩增,并损害了抗原特异性B细胞谱的重塑。结构建模、生物层干涉技术和钙离子流实验表明,第456位芳香残基促进了有效的生源BCR识别和激活。重要的是,将非芳香性亮氨酸残基替换为芳香族氨基酸(如酪氨酸或色氨酸)恢复了抗原的中和抗体诱导能力。综上所述,这些发现确定了第456位芳香性是RBD功能性免疫原性的关键决定因素,并展示了单个氨基酸取代如何重塑B细胞反应和抗体质量。这项工作为合理设计疫苗抗原提供了重要见解,并加深了我们对特定位点突变如何调控抗病毒药物免疫的理解。

title: Boosting hybrid immunity with intranasal live-attenuated or intramuscular mRNA vaccination prevents SARS-CoV-2 XBB.1.5 transmission
abstract: Rapid antigenic evolution of SARS-CoV-2 and waning immunity have reduced antibody-mediated neutralization, enabling breakthrough infections and sustained transmission despite widespread immunity. This highlights the need for variant-adapted booster vaccines. However, pre-existing immunity may influence the magnitude and specificity of immune responses induced by variant-adapted booster vaccination. Using the Syrian hamster model, we previously described a safe and efficient mucosal vaccination approach using live attenuated viruses (LAV) based on a "One-to-Stop (OTS)" codon modification strategy. Whether OTS vaccines are suitable as effective booster vaccines in the presence of pre-existing mucosal immunity remained unaddressed. Here, we modeled pre-existing hybrid immunity in Syrian hamsters using intramuscular bivalent mRNA vaccination followed by SARS-CoV-2 infection and subsequently administered heterologous intranasal OTS-LAV or intramuscular mRNA XBB.1.5 booster vaccination. Both booster strategies significantly increased XBB.1.5-binding- and neutralizing antibodies systemically and at mucosal sites. In contrast, booster vaccination left SARS-CoV-2 specific T cell frequencies unchanged. While all hybrid-immune animals were protected from disease following XBB.1.5 challenge infection, virus transmission was completely blocked only after booster vaccination and was associated with the absence of infectious virus in nasal samples. Collectively, using OTS-LAV we provide a proof of concept that intranasal LAV vaccination can effectively boost pre-existing hybrid immunity and restrict viral transmission. These findings support the use of OTS-LAV as a heterologous booster strategy against SARS-CoV-2 and demonstrate that variant-adapted booster vaccination can efficiently limit transmission, a strategy highly desired for tackling emerging respiratory infections.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the effectiveness of variant-adapted booster vaccines in preventing SARS-CoV-2 XBB.1.5 transmission in the context of pre-existing hybrid immunity. Using a Syrian hamster model, researchers administered intranasal live-attenuated or intramuscular mRNA vaccines as boosters following initial bivalent mRNA vaccination and SARS-CoV-2 infection. However, the study is limited to an animal model, which may not fully reflect human immune responses.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2的快速抗原变异和免疫力减弱降低了抗体介导的中和作用,导致突破性感染和持续传播,尽管广泛存在免疫力。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究使用叙利亚仓鼠模型来探讨在预先存在混合免疫的情况下,针对变异株的加强疫苗的有效性。
elements_zh.methods: 本研究通过肌肉内二价mRNA 疫苗接种接种后进行严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2感染,模拟了叙利亚仓鼠中的预先存在的混合免疫,并随后给予异源鼻内OTS-LAV或肌肉内mRNA XBB.1.5加强疫苗。
elements_zh.main_results: 两种加强策略均显著增加了全身和黏膜部位对XBB.1.5的结合和中和抗体水平。所有混合免疫动物在XBB.1.5挑战感染后均能防止疾病,但只有在接种加强疫苗后病毒传播才被完全阻断,并且与鼻腔样本中无传染性病毒的存在相关。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 加强疫苗未改变针对严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2的T细胞频率,突显了OTS-LAV加强疫苗对抗体反应的独特影响。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现支持将OTS-LAV作为针对严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2的异源加强策略,并证明针对变异株的加强疫苗能够有效限制传播,这对于应对新兴呼吸道感染是一种高度期望的策略。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 本研究仅限于叙利亚仓鼠模型,这可能无法完全代表人类免疫应答。证据强度较高,因为它直接证明了加强疫苗在预防传播方面的有效性。

abstract_zh: 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2的快速抗原变异和免疫力减弱降低了抗体介导的中和作用,导致突破性感染和持续传播,尽管广泛存在免疫力。这凸显了需要针对变异株的加强疫苗。然而,预先存在的免疫力可能影响针对变异株加强疫苗诱导的免疫反应的强度和特异性。我们之前使用叙利亚仓鼠模型描述了一种基于"One-to-Stop (OTS)"密码子修饰策略的减毒病毒(LAV)安全且有效的黏膜免疫增强方法。在存在预先存在的黏膜免疫力的情况下,OTS加强疫苗是否适合作为有效的增强策略仍未被解决。在此,我们通过肌肉内二价mRNA 疫苗接种接种后进行严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2感染,模拟了叙利亚仓鼠中的预先存在的混合免疫,并随后给予异源鼻内OTS-LAV或肌肉内mRNA XBB.1.5加强疫苗。两种加强策略均显著增加了全身和黏膜部位对XBB.1.5的结合和中和抗体水平。相比之下,加强疫苗未改变针对严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2的T细胞频率。尽管所有混合免疫动物在XBB.1.5挑战感染后均能防止疾病,但只有在接种加强疫苗后病毒传播才被完全阻断,并且与鼻腔样本中无传染性病毒的存在相关。总体而言,我们通过使用OTS-LAV提供了一个概念验证,表明鼻内LAV 疫苗接种可以有效增强预先存在的混合免疫并限制病毒传播。这些发现支持将OTS-LAV作为针对严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2的异源加强策略,并证明针对变异株的加强疫苗能够有效限制传播,这对于应对新兴呼吸道感染是一种高度期望的策略。

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2的快速抗原变异和免疫力减弱降低了抗体介导的中和作用,导致突破性感染和持续传播,尽管广泛存在免疫力。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究使用叙利亚仓鼠模型来探讨在预先存在混合免疫的情况下,针对变异株的加强疫苗的有效性。
analysis_zh.methods: 本研究通过肌肉内二价mRNA 疫苗接种接种后进行严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2感染,模拟了叙利亚仓鼠中的预先存在的混合免疫,并随后给予异源鼻内OTS-LAV或肌肉内mRNA XBB.1.5加强疫苗。

title: Differences between Canadian parents' attitudes toward routine, influenza, and COVID-19 vaccines for their children, and changes in vaccine hesitancy since the pandemic: A national cross-sectional comparative study.
abstract: Background Evidence suggests the COVID-19 pandemic had heterogeneous and vaccine-specific effects on parental attitudes toward childhood vaccination. A decline in vaccine confidence has been noted in some settings, however even studies reporting stable or increased confidence suggest polarized attitudes with stronger pro- and anti-vaccine views emerging concurrently. We explored differences between Canadian parents' attitudes toward childhood routine, influenza, and COVID-19 vaccination, and changes in attitudes since the pandemic. Methods In 2025 we conducted a cross-sectional national online survey of parents with children aged 0-17 years using a polling firm. Previously validated questions asked about parents' attitudes toward vaccination using the '5C' scale, capturing separate responses for routine, influenza, and COVID-19 vaccines. We assessed changes in attitudes about routine vaccination over time by comparing 5C responses from two previous surveys conducted in 2020 and 2021. We calculated proportions and 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Results Respondents (N = 1327) were proportionally representative across provinces, but not the territories. Parents were most confident in the safety of routine vaccines (71.0%, 95%CI 66.5-75.7), compared to influenza (63.7%, 95%CI 59.5-68.1) and COVID-19 (57.9%, 95%CI 53.9-62.1). The majority indicated the pandemic did not change attitudes about routine (60.8%) or influenza (63.7%) vaccination, while more than one-quarter (31.6% and 27.8%) reported that routine and influenza vaccines were more important following the pandemic. In 2025, a slightly higher proportion of parents reported low confidence in the safety and effectiveness of routine vaccines (12.7% and 9.2%, respectively), compared to 2021 (8.5% and 5.6%), and 2020 (12.2% and 6.8%). Conclusions Parental attitudes toward childhood COVID-19 vaccination differed from attitudes toward routine and influenza. Most parents reported positive or neutral impact of the pandemic on perceived importance of routine and influenza vaccines. Parents reported the highest positive attitudes toward routine vaccination mid-pandemic (2021), and parents' attitudes in 2025 were slightly less positive than in 2020 and 2021.

source_records.title: Differences between Canadian parents' attitudes toward routine, influenza, and COVID-19 vaccines for their children, and changes in vaccine hesitancy since the pandemic: A national cross-sectional comparative study.
source_records.abstract: Background Evidence suggests the COVID-19 pandemic had heterogeneous and vaccine-specific effects on parental attitudes toward childhood vaccination. A decline in vaccine confidence has been noted in some settings, however even studies reporting stable or increased confidence suggest polarized attitudes with stronger pro- and anti-vaccine views emerging concurrently. We explored differences between Canadian parents' attitudes toward childhood routine, influenza, and COVID-19 vaccination, and changes in attitudes since the pandemic. Methods In 2025 we conducted a cross-sectional national online survey of parents with children aged 0-17 years using a polling firm. Previously validated questions asked about parents' attitudes toward vaccination using the '5C' scale, capturing separate responses for routine, influenza, and COVID-19 vaccines. We assessed changes in attitudes about routine vaccination over time by comparing 5C responses from two previous surveys conducted in 2020 and 2021. We calculated proportions and 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Results Respondents (N = 1327) were proportionally representative across provinces, but not the territories. Parents were most confident in the safety of routine vaccines (71.0%, 95%CI 66.5-75.7), compared to influenza (63.7%, 95%CI 59.5-68.1) and COVID-19 (57.9%, 95%CI 53.9-62.1). The majority indicated the pandemic did not change attitudes about routine (60.8%) or influenza (63.7%) vaccination, while more than one-quarter (31.6% and 27.8%) reported that routine and influenza vaccines were more important following the pandemic. In 2025, a slightly higher proportion of parents reported low confidence in the safety and effectiveness of routine vaccines (12.7% and 9.2%, respectively), compared to 2021 (8.5% and 5.6%), and 2020 (12.2% and 6.8%). Conclusions Parental attitudes toward childhood COVID-19 vaccination differed from attitudes toward routine and influenza. Most parents reported positive or neutral impact of the pandemic on perceived importance of routine and influenza vaccines. Parents reported the highest positive attitudes toward routine vaccination mid-pandemic (2021), and parents' attitudes in 2025 were slightly less positive than in 2020 and 2021.

analysis.summary_en: This study examines differences in Canadian parents' attitudes toward routine, influenza, and COVID-19 vaccines for their children, and changes in vaccine hesitancy since the pandemic. The research highlights that parental confidence in routine vaccines remains higher than for influenza and COVID-19 vaccines. While the majority of parents reported no change in attitudes toward routine or influenza vaccination, some indicated increased perceived importance of these vaccines post-pandemic. The study also notes a slight increase in low confidence for routine vaccines in 2025 compared to 2021 and 2020. Overall, the findings suggest polarized attitudes toward vaccination, with stronger pro- and anti-vaccine views emerging concurrently. The study underscores the need for targeted research and public health strategies to address vaccine hesitancy and improve vaccination rates.

title: Supramolecular assembly and membrane anchoring alter variant-induced SARS-CoV-2 Spike conformational dynamics.
abstract: Viral surface glycoproteins function within crowded, membrane-anchored supramolecular assemblies, yet their dynamics are often inferred from soluble, engineered ectodomains. For SARS-CoV-2 Spike (S), this distinction is especially important because variant mutations evolved in the context of intact virions, not engineered trimers. Here, we combined cyclic ion mobility mass spectrometry (CIM-MS) for hydrogen deuterium exchange mass spectrometry (HDXMS) with computational weighted ensemble molecular dynamic (WE-MD) simulations to compare the conformational effects of SARS-CoV-2 mutations in two S protein constructs: soluble recombinant 2P S and full-length S displayed in virus-like particles (VLPs). Our results reveal that membrane anchoring and virion-like assembly substantially dampen global dynamic changes produced by variant mutations. In VLP S, D614G induced decreased dynamics across interprotomer contacts, whereas Omicron BA.1 mutations systematically reversed this decrease in dynamics in the S1 domain while preserving decreased dynamics near the fusion machinery. These effects are more spatially constrained than those observed in recombinant 2P S. Comparison of the 2 constructs further reveals that 2P substitutions alter native interprotomer communication. Recombinant S shows a predominantly fast-exchanging population in the receptor binding domain (RBD) hinge region, consistent with disruption of hydrogen-bonding and salt bridge networks that couple RBD motion to the trimer core. Thus, recombinant S captures important structural features of S without recapitulating the native conformational ensemble presented on virions. Together, these results show that the supramolecular context of S reshapes the conformational dynamics of variant evolution with direct implications for epitope presentation, antibody recognition, and interpretation of recombinant S structural studies.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates how supramolecular assembly and membrane anchoring influence the conformational dynamics of SARS-CoV-2 Spike protein, particularly in the context of viral variants. abstract_zh: 病毒表面糖蛋白在拥挤且膜锚定的超分子组装体中起作用,但其动力学通常是从可溶性、工程化的胞外结构域推断得出的。对于严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2刺突蛋白(S),这种区别尤为重要,因为变异体突变是在完整病毒颗粒的背景下进化而来的,而非工程化的三聚体。在这里,我们结合了循环离子迁移率质谱(CIM-MS)用于氢氘交换质谱(HDXMS)以及计算加权集合分子动力学(WE-MD)模拟,以比较变异体突变在两种S蛋白结构中的构象效应:可溶性重组2P S和在病毒样颗粒(VLPs)中展示的全长S蛋白。我们的结果表明,膜锚定和类似病毒颗粒的组装显著抑制了变异体突变引起的全局动态变化。在VLP S中,D614G变异体导致了跨亚基接触区域的动态减少,而Omicron BA.1 突变则系统性地逆转了S1结构域中的这种减少,同时保留了融合机制附近动态减少的现象。这些效应在重组2P S中更为空间受限。对这两种结构的比较进一步揭示了2P位点的替换改变了天然的亚基间通信。重组S蛋白在受体结合结构域(RBD)铰链区表现出主要的快速交换群体,这与破坏了将RBD运动与三聚体核心耦合的氢键和盐桥网络一致。因此,重组S蛋白捕捉了S蛋白的重要结构特征,但并未再现病毒颗粒上天然的构象动态集合。综上所述,这些结果表明S蛋白的超分子环境重塑了变异体进化的构象动力学,并对表位呈现、抗体识别以及重组刺突蛋白结构研究的解释具有直接影响。

analysis_zh.main_results: 结果表明,膜锚定和类似病毒颗粒的组装显著降低了变异体突变引起的全局动态变化。具体而言,在VLP S中,D614G变异体导致了跨亚基接触区域的动态减少,而Omicron BA.1 突变则在S1结构域中系统性地逆转了这种减少,同时保留了融合机制附近动态减少的现象。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者认为,刺突蛋白的超分子环境改变了变异体进化的构象动力学,这对表位呈现、抗体识别以及重组刺突蛋白结构研究的解释具有直接影响。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现为理解刺突蛋白的结构环境如何影响其动力学提供了重要见解,有助于设计更准确的诊断工具、疫苗开发以及对免疫应答到严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2变异体的理解。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 本研究的结果基于计算和实验方法,可能无法完全捕捉天然病毒颗粒的构象动力学复杂性。然而,证据是强有力的,并直接支持了关于超分子环境对刺突蛋白动力学影响的结论。

title: Differential expression of lung-homing chemokine receptors in severe COVID-19: distinct profiles between Alpha and Omicron.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Severe Coronavirus Disease 2019 (COVID-19), caused by Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome Coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2), is characterized by excessive pulmonary immune cell recruitment mediated by chemokine - chemokine receptor signaling. Variant-specific differences in lung-homing chemokine receptor expression remain insufficiently defined. METHODS: This retrospective case-control study analyzed Bronchoalveolar Lavage Fluid (BALF) samples from Intensive Care Unit (ICU) admitted patients with severe COVID-19 during the Alpha (hICU-α) and Omicron (hICU-Ο) waves, along with SARS-CoV-2 - negative controls. Messenger RNA expression of CXCR1, CXCR2, CXCR3, CCR2, and CCR6 was quantified by Real-Time quantitative Polymerase Chain Reaction (RT-qPCR). Protein expression of selected receptors was assessed by western blotting in available samples. RESULTS: CXCR1 expression was significantly increased in hICU-α patients compared with controls (p = 0.02) but not in hICU-Ο patients. CXCR2 expression was elevated in both hICU-α and hICU-Ο groups versus controls (p = 0.008 and p = 0.006, respectively) and was higher in hICU-α than hICU-Ο patients (p = 0.009). CXCR3 expression was increased in both COVID-19 groups compared with controls (p = 0.03 and p = 0.001). CCR6 expression was highest in hICU-Ο patients compared with hICU-α and controls (p = 0.04 and p = 0.001). Increased CXCR2 and CXCR3 protein expression was confirmed in hICU-Ο patients. CONCLUSIONS: Severe COVID-19 is associated with variant-specific alterations in lung chemokine receptor expression, highlighting differential immune trafficking patterns during Alpha and Omicron waves.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates variant-specific differences in lung-homing chemokine receptor expression in severe COVID-19 patients during the Alpha and Omicron waves. Using Bronchoalveolar Lavage Fluid (BALF) samples from ICU patients, the researchers quantified mRNA and protein expression levels of CXCR1, CXCR2, CXCR3, CCR2, and CCR6 via RT-qPCR and western blotting. They found that CXCR1 was significantly increased in Alpha patients but not in Omicron patients. CXCR2 and CXCR3 were elevated in both groups compared to controls, with CXCR2 being higher in Alpha patients. CCR6 was highest in Omicron patients. These results suggest that severe COVID-19 is associated with variant-specific changes in chemokine receptor expression, indicating potential differences in immune trafficking patterns. The study's findings may contribute to understanding immune responses to different SARS-CoV-2 variants and could inform future therapeutic strategies. However, the retrospective design and potential for selection bias limit the confidence in the results, though the evidence is supported by clear statistical significance.

title: Online COVID-19 Misinformation and Infodemic Governance During the Peak Pandemic Period: Scoping Review of Social Media Research From 2020 to 2022.
abstract: Abstract Background During the COVID-19 pandemic, social media platforms became major channels for public health communication and public sensemaking, but they also enabled the rapid circulation of rumors, false claims, conspiracy narratives, and misleading health information. Research on online COVID-19 misinformation expanded rapidly during the peak pandemic period, yet the evidence base was fragmented across public health, computing, communication, and information science. Objective This scoping review synthesizes empirical research on online COVID-19 misinformation on social media during the peak pandemic period from February 2020 to October 2022. It examines how misinformation was conceptualized, which platforms and public health contexts were emphasized, and how computational methods shaped the evidence base for infodemic management. Its distinct contribution is an integrated comparison of conceptual definitions, thematic and platform concentration, the computational research pipeline, and the gap between detection and actionable infodemic governance. Methods We conducted a PRISMA (Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses)-informed scoping review of empirical studies indexed in PubMed and IEEE Xplore in November 2022 using COVID-19, social media platforms, and misinformation-related terms. Eligible reports were English-language, peer-reviewed empirical studies published between February 2020 and October 2022 that analyzed social media data using computational, quantitative, or social media analytic methods; the language restriction applied to the publication, not to the underlying dataset. The final synthesis included 100 studies selected from 1688 records. Results Within the included corpus, the literature was concentrated around vaccine-related discourse, public health and social measures-related misinformation, and text-based data from X (X Corp), formerly known as Twitter. Studies commonly used misinformation detection, classification, sentiment analysis, topic modeling, and network analysis. Fewer studies examined diffusion pathways, source tracing, cross-platform movement, intervention effectiveness, or platform governance. The evidence base remains more developed for detecting and describing misinformation than for evaluating actionable responses to it. Conclusions Peak-pandemic COVID-19 misinformation research produced important computational and empirical knowledge, but it remains detection-centered and unevenly connected to public health action. Future infodemiology research should link computational outputs to intervention design, risk communication, fact-checking workflows, platform moderation, multilingual and multimodal analysis, and the evaluation of infodemic governance strategies.

title_zh: Online COVID-19 Misinformation and Infodemic Governance During the Peak Pandemic Period: Scoping Review of Social Media Research From 2020 to 2022.
source_body_en: Abstract Background During the COVID-19 pandemic, social media platforms became major channels for public health communication and public sensemaking, but they also enabled the rapid circulation of rumors, false claims, conspiracy narratives, and misleading health information. Research on online COVID-19 misinformation expanded rapidly during the peak pandemic period, yet the evidence base was fragmented across public health, computing, communication, and information science. Objective This scoping review synthesizes empirical research on online COVID-19 misinformation on social media during the peak pandemic period from February 2020 to October 2022. It examines how misinformation was conceptualized, which platforms and public health contexts were emphasized, and how computational methods shaped the evidence base for infodemic management. Its distinct contribution is an integrated comparison of conceptual definitions, thematic and platform concentration, the computational research pipeline, and the gap between detection and actionable infodemic governance. Methods We conducted a PRISMA (Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses)-informed scoping review of empirical studies indexed in PubMed and IEEE Xplore in November 2022 using COVID-19, social media platforms, and misinformation-related terms. Eligible reports were English-language, peer-reviewed empirical studies published between February 2020 and October 2022 that analyzed social media data using computational, quantitative, or social media analytic methods; the language restriction applied to the publication, not to the underlying dataset. The final synthesis included 100 studies selected from 1688 records. Results Within the included corpus, the literature was concentrated around vaccine-related discourse, public health and social measures-related misinformation, and text-based data from X (X Corp), formerly known as Twitter. Studies commonly used misinformation detection, classification, sentiment analysis, topic modeling, and network analysis. Fewer studies examined diffusion pathways, source tracing, cross-platform movement, intervention effectiveness, or platform governance. The evidence base remains more developed for detecting and describing misinformation than for evaluating actionable responses to it. Conclusions Peak-pandemic COVID-19 misinformation research produced important computational and empirical knowledge, but it remains detection-centered and unevenly connected to public health action. Future infodemiology research should link computational outputs to intervention design, risk communication, fact-checking workflows, platform moderation, multilingual and multimodal analysis, and the evaluation of infodemic governance strategies.

title: Immunization with JN.1 spike protein increases the breadth of binding and neutralizing antibodies in Syrian hamsters in an immune-history dependent manner.
abstract: With much of the world exposed to previous variants of SARS-CoV-2, testing of current COVID-19 vaccines in preclinical models should occur in the context of preexisting immunity to the virus. Here, we evaluated the immunogenicity and efficacy of a JN.1 variant spike (S) protein-based nanoparticle vaccine in Syrian hamsters nine months after three immunizations with Wuhan-1 prototype, prototype + BA.5, or XBB.1.5 variant COVID-19 vaccines. Serum was collected prior to and three weeks after the JN.1 immunization to measure antibody responses to different variants of SARS-CoV-2, including JN.1 and KP.2. To assess efficacy, age-matched naive and JN.1 vaccine-boosted hamsters were challenged with the KP.2 variant of SARS-CoV-2, and viral burden in the nasal turbinates, trachea, and lungs was measured. Three doses of the nanoparticle S protein vaccine induced long-lasting virus neutralizing antibody responses, and neutralization of the JN.1 and KP.2 variants of SARS-CoV-2 was associated with one or more doses of the XBB.1.5 vaccine. Subsequent immunization with the JN.1 variant vaccine boosted JN.1 and KP.2 specific antibody responses, however, the relative increase in titer was dependent on vaccine history and inversely correlated with JN.1 neutralizing titers prior to boosting. Following challenge, JN.1-boosted hamsters, regardless of their immune history or increase in JN.1 specific antibody response, were protected against the KP.2 variant with infectious virus titers averaging at or below the limit of detection in all tissues. The reductions in viral RNA levels correlated with pre-challenge serum antibody titers against KP.2. In conclusion, boosting with a variant SARS-CoV-2 vaccine is effective in a diverse immune landscape and protects against a related virus variant.

Serum was collected prior to and three weeks after the JN.1 immunization to measure antibody responses to different variants of SARS-CoV-2, including JN.1 and KP.2. To assess efficacy, age-matched naive and JN.1 vaccine-boosted hamsters were challenged with the KP.2 variant of SARS-CoV-2, and viral burden in the nasal turbinates, trachea, and lungs was measured. Three doses of the nanoparticle S protein vaccine induced long-lasting virus neutralizing antibody responses, and neutralization of the JN.1 and KP.2 variants of SARS-CoV-2 was associated with one or more doses of the XBB.1.5 vaccine. Subsequent immunization with the JN.1 variant vaccine boosted JN.1 and KP.2 specific antibody responses, however, the relative increase in titer was dependent on vaccine history and inversely correlated with JN.1 neutralizing titers prior to boosting. Following challenge, JN.1-boosted hamsters, regardless of their immune history or increase in JN.1 specific antibody response, were protected against the KP.2 variant with infectious virus titers averaging at or below the limit of detection in all tissues. The reductions in viral RNA levels correlated with pre-challenge serum antibody titers against KP.2. In conclusion, boosting with a variant SARS-CoV-2 vaccine is effective in a diverse immune landscape and protects against a related virus variant.

title: Persistent COVID-19 Symptoms in General Population and Healthcare Workers: Systematic Review With Meta-Analysis.
abstract: ABSTRACT Background and Aims COVID‐19 can cause persistent symptoms that continue after the infection, condition known as long COVID. This study aimed to identify the prevalence of persistent signs and symptoms of COVID‐19 in individuals with confirmed SARS‐CoV‐2 infection and among healthcare workers. Methods This is a systematic review with meta‐analysis guided by PRISMA and registered in PROSPERO (CRD42023460632). Cohort studies with a minimum follow‐up of 12 weeks after COVID‐19 infection were included. Searches were conducted in PubMed, Scopus, Embase, Scielo, and LILACS/BVS databases and gray literature, in November 2023. Rayyan was used for article selection, and pooled prevalence meta‐analysis for each symptom was conducted in R. Methodological quality was assessed using the Newcastle‐Ottawa Scale. Results A total of 2,456 studies were identified, with 59 articles included in the systematic review and 58 in the meta‐analysis, comprising 196,863 participants. The symptoms with the highest pooled prevalence (95% CI) were fatigue (0.29[0.24–0.36], 95% PI: 0.05–0.78) and dyspnea (0.16[0.12–0.22], 95% PI: 0.01–0.71). Conclusion Healthcare workers showed lower prevalence rates for some persistent symptoms (fatigue, dyspnea, cough, taste changes, and gastrointestinal symptoms) than the general population. Most studies were of fair quality. Despite the findings of a high prevalence of persistent symptoms, high heterogeneity remained a key limitation.

analysis.scope_and_question: This review investigates the prevalence of persistent symptoms—collectively termed long COVID—in individuals with confirmed SARS‐CoV‐2 infection, comparing the general population with healthcare workers.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The authors conducted a systematic review and meta‐analysis following PRISMA guidelines and registered the protocol in PROSPERO (CRD42023460632). Cohort studies with a minimum follow‐up of 12 weeks after SARS‐CoV‐2 infection were eligible. Searches were performed in PubMed, Scopus, Embase, Scielo, and LILACS/BVS, plus gray literature, up to November 2023. Rayyan was used for article selection, and pooled prevalence estimates were calculated in R. Methodological quality was appraised with the Newcastle‐Ottawa Scale.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: Across 58 studies comprising 196,863 participants, the pooled prevalence of fatigue was 0.29 (95% CI 0.24–0.36) and dyspnea 0.16 (95% CI 0.12–0.22). Healthcare workers exhibited lower prevalence rates for several persistent symptoms—including fatigue, dyspnea, cough, taste changes, and gastrointestinal symptoms—than the general population.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The analysis was limited by substantial heterogeneity among studies, and most studies were rated only as fair quality, underscoring uncertainty in the pooled estimates.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The supplied evidence does not report specific research or practice implications.

analysis.summary_en: This systematic review and meta‐analysis examined the prevalence of long COVID symptoms in the general population and healthcare workers. Using PRISMA guidelines and a PROSPERO‐registered protocol, the authors included cohort studies with at least 12 weeks of follow‐up, identified 58 studies with 196,863 participants, and assessed quality with the Newcastle‐Ottawa Scale. The pooled prevalence of fatigue and dyspnea were 29% and 16%, respectively, with healthcare workers showing lower rates for several symptoms. High heterogeneity and fair study quality limit confidence in these estimates. No explicit research or practice implications were reported in the abstract.

title_zh: Persistent COVID-19 Symptoms in General Population and Healthcare Workers: Systematic Review With Meta-Analysis.
source_body_en: ABSTRACT Background and Aims COVID‐19 can cause persistent symptoms that continue after the infection, condition known as long COVID. This study aimed to identify the prevalence of persistent signs and symptoms of COVID‐19 in individuals with confirmed SARS‐CoV‐2 infection and among healthcare workers. Methods This is a systematic review with meta‐analysis guided by PRISMA and registered in PROSPERO (CRD42023460632). Cohort studies with a minimum follow‐up of 12 weeks after COVID‐19 infection were included. Searches were conducted in PubMed, Scopus, Embase, Scielo, and LILACS/BVS databases and gray literature, in November 2023. Rayyan was used for article selection, and pooled prevalence meta‐analysis for each symptom was conducted in R. Methodological quality was assessed using the Newcastle‐Ottawa Scale. Results A total of 2,456 studies were identified, with 59 articles included in the systematic review and 58 in the meta‐analysis, comprising 196,863 participants. The symptoms with the highest pooled prevalence (95% CI) were fatigue (0.29[0.24–0.36], 95% PI: 0.05–0.78) and dyspnea (0.16[0.12–0.22], 95% PI: 0.01–0.71). Conclusion Healthcare workers showed lower prevalence rates for some persistent symptoms (fatigue, dyspnea, cough, taste changes, and gastrointestinal symptoms) than the general population. Most studies were of fair quality. Despite the findings of a high prevalence of persistent symptoms, high heterogeneity remained a key limitation.

title: Vaccination rates, facilitators and barriers for influenza, pneumococcal and SARS-CoV-2 vaccination among sepsis survivors: a Mid-German Sepsis Cohort survey
abstract: Abstract Sepsis survivors often suffer from chronic immune dysfunction, leading to frequent rehospitalization and recurrent sepsis. Vaccinations are effective in preventing common infections in sepsis survivors. However, vaccination behavior in this vulnerable population remains unknown. Prospective interviewer-administered survey performed between 04/2023 and 04/2024 among sepsis survivors in Germany. Participants were recruited from the Mid-German Sepsis Cohort (MSC) 6 to 8 years after initial inclusion. We assessed risk perception, cues to action and barriers for vaccination against influenza, pneumococci and SARS-CoV-2. Predictors for the vaccination status of each of the three infections were identified by logistic regression analyses. Among 174 survivors, vaccination rates against influenza and pneumococci rose from 57.3 to 70.7% and from 31.4 to 60.5% 3 months to 8 years post-sepsis, respectively. A total of 135 patients (77.6%) had full vaccination coverage against SARS-CoV-2 at the time of the survey. Higher age and an intermediate vs. low education increased the odds for influenza vaccination. No associations between sociodemographic indicators and the vaccination status against pneumococci and SARS-CoV-2 were found. Vaccination counselling by a general practitioner increased the odds for vaccination between 5.5-fold (influenza) and 3.2-fold (pneumococci) in the multiple regression analyses. The review of general vaccination status was associated with a 4.7-fold increase of influenza vaccination rates and 3.1-fold increase of SARS-CoV-2 vaccination rates. Among patients with at least one missing vaccination (n = 92), impaired mobility (16.8%), long waiting times in the practice (14.8%) and fear of infection in the practice (14.7%) were the most relevant barriers. There are considerable vaccination gaps in sepsis survivors. Pro-active vaccination counselling and checks of vaccination status by general practitioners may offer a great potential to increase vaccination rates and thus should be considered as an important element of sepsis aftercare.

analysis.summary_en: This review explores vaccination rates, facilitators, and barriers for influenza, pneumococcal, and SARS-CoV-2 vaccines among sepsis survivors in Germany. A prospective survey of 174 sepsis survivors, conducted between 2023 and 2024, revealed that vaccination rates for influenza and pneumococci increased over time, with 77.6% of participants having full SARS-CoV-2 vaccination coverage. The study highlights the need for proactive vaccination counseling and status checks in sepsis aftercare to address existing gaps.

elements_en.scope_and_question: Sepsis survivors often suffer from chronic immune dysfunction, leading to frequent rehospitalization and recurrent sepsis. Vaccinations are effective in preventing common infections in sepsis survivors. However, vaccination behavior in this vulnerable population remains unknown.
elements_en.evidence_base_and_review_method: Prospective interviewer-administered survey performed between 04/2023 and 04/2024 among sepsis survivors in Germany. Participants were recruited from the Mid-German Sepsis Cohort (MSC) 6 to 8 years after initial inclusion. Predictors for the vaccination status of each of the three infections were identified by logistic regression analyses.
elements_en.consensus_and_key_conclusions: Among 174 survivors, vaccination rates against influenza and pneumococci rose from 57.3 to 70.7% and from 31.4 to 60.5% 3 months to 8 years post-sepsis, respectively. A total of 135 patients (77.6%) had full vaccination coverage against SARS-CoV-2 at the time of the survey. Vaccination counselling by a general practitioner increased the odds for vaccination between 5.5-fold (influenza) and 3.2-fold (pneumococci) in the multiple regression analyses. The review of general vaccination status was associated with a 4.7-fold increase of influenza vaccination rates and 3.1-fold increase of SARS-CoV-2 vaccination rates.
elements_en.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: No associations between sociodemographic indicators and the vaccination status against pneumococci and SARS-CoV-2 were found. Among patients with at least one missing vaccination (n = 92), impaired mobility (16.8%), long waiting times in the practice (14.8%) and fear of infection in the practice (14.7%) were the most relevant barriers. There are considerable vaccination gaps in sepsis survivors.
elements_en.research_and_practice_implications: Pro-active vaccination counselling and checks of vaccination status by general practitioners may offer a great potential to increase vaccination rates and thus should be considered as an important element of sepsis aftercare.

title_zh: 脓毒症幸存者中流感、肺炎球菌和 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 疫苗接种 的发生率、促进因素和障碍:中德脓毒症 队列研究 调查
source_body_en: Abstract Sepsis survivors often suffer from chronic immune dysfunction, leading to frequent rehospitalization and recurrent sepsis. Vaccinations are effective in preventing common infections in sepsis survivors. However, vaccination behavior in this vulnerable population remains unknown. Prospective interviewer-administered survey performed between 04/2023 and 04/2024 among sepsis survivors in Germany. Participants were recruited from the Mid-German Sepsis Cohort (MSC) 6 to 8 years after initial inclusion. We assessed risk perception, cues to action and barriers for vaccination against influenza, pneumococci and SARS-CoV-2. Predictors for the vaccination status of each of the three infections were identified by logistic regression analyses. Among 174 survivors, vaccination rates against influenza and pneumococci rose from 57.3 to 70.7% and from 31.4 to 60.5% 3 months to 8 years post-sepsis, respectively. A total of 135 patients (77.6%) had full vaccination coverage against SARS-CoV-2 at the time of the survey. Higher age and an intermediate vs. low education increased the odds for influenza vaccination. No associations between sociodemographic indicators and the vaccination status against pneumococci and SARS-CoV-2 were found. Vaccination counselling by a general practitioner increased the odds for vaccination between 5.5-fold (influenza) and 3.2-fold (pneumococci) in the multiple regression analyses. The review of general vaccination status was associated with a 4.7-fold increase of influenza vaccination rates and 3.1-fold increase of SARS-CoV-2 vaccination rates. Among patients with at least one missing vaccination (n = 92), impaired mobility (16.8%), long waiting times in the practice (14.8%) and fear of infection in the practice (14.7%) were the most relevant barriers. There are considerable vaccination gaps in sepsis survivors. Pro-active vaccination counselling and checks of vaccination status by general practitioners may offer a great potential to increase vaccination rates and thus should be considered as an important element of sepsis aftercare.

title: Mitigation of imprinted antibody responses against COVID-19 in highly vaccinated older adults.
abstract: Despite higher clinical risk of severe COVID-19, contemporary data on antibody durability and breadth in older adults receiving multiple COVID-19 booster vaccines remain limited amid ongoing evolution of SARS-CoV-2 Omicron JN.1 descendants and the divergent BA.3.2 saltation variant. We studied a clinically vulnerable cohort of 43 older adults (median age = 85 years, IQR 75-88, 40% female). Using pseudotyped and surrogate virus neutralization-based assays, we demonstrate that JN.1 and KP.2 vaccinations six months apart elicit high-potency neutralization across all studied JN.1-lineage variants but not BA.3.2.2, where titers were 2-3-fold lower. Waning of serum neutralizing activity was modest between vaccine doses, suggesting sustained immunity. Importantly, the half-life of serum neutralization against Wu-1 (179 days) was substantially longer than JN.1 subvariants (43.7-70.1 days), consistent with Wu-1-specific imprinted responses. Furthermore, BA.3.2.2 neutralizing antibody half-life was prolonged at 107 days, implicating imprinted ancestral variant-targeting antibodies having some activity against BA.3.2.2. While absolute neutralization titers remained highest against ancestral Wu-1 due to multiple historical exposures, recall responses after the KP.2 vaccine revealed a shift in immunodominance. Neutralization against full-length Wu-1 spike was not boosted, whereas all JN.1 descendants and BA.3.2.2 showed significant boosts, indicating partial alleviation of immune imprinting. These data indicate that in the elderly, protective neutralizing antibody responses against recent variants of concern can be achieved, with reduction of immune imprinting and waning through biannual, strain-updated booster vaccines. Imprinted antibodies against ancestral variants may still be relevant for protection against highly immune evasive variants such as BA.3.2.2, highlighting that careful characterization of population-level COVID-19 humoral immunity remains warranted.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates antibody responses in older adults who received multiple booster vaccines against SARS-CoV-2, focusing on the durability and breadth of immunity against recent variants. The research highlights that despite the clinical vulnerability of this population, biannual, strain-updated booster vaccines can reduce immune imprinting and sustain neutralizing activity against emerging variants. The findings suggest that while ancestral variant-specific antibodies may persist, they do not fully impede responses to newer variants like BA.3.2.2. These results have implications for vaccine strategies in the elderly, emphasizing the need for updated formulations to maintain effective protection. However, the study's abstract-only nature and limited scope may restrict the depth of conclusions that can be drawn.

title: Associations between salivary HHV-6 and long COVID severity in a cross-sectional, case-control analysis.
abstract: Background Reactivation of human herpesviruses (HHVs), particularly EBV, is associated with more severe acute SARS-CoV-2 infection and the development of Long COVID (LC). Reactivation of HHVs has been previously implicated in hormonal dysregulation, which has also been observed in LC, suggesting a potential link. This study aims to examine the relationship between LC symptoms and salivary HHV DNA, cortisol, testosterone, and oestradiol levels. Methods Our cross-sectional, case-control study enrolled 45 participants with LC, and 45 age-sex-matched controls. Surveys and validated health questionnaires were used to collect demographics, medical history, and symptom profiles. Saliva was self-collected at waking, 15, 30, and 45 min, and 8 and 16 h after waking, across two consecutive days. Salivary cortisol, testosterone and oestradiol were measured, and extracted nucleic acid was tested for EBV, HSV 1/2, HCMV and HHV-6 A/B using multiplex qPCR, and for SARS-CoV-2 and RNaseP using RT-qPCR. Findings Detection of salivary EBV and HHV-6 DNA copies was highest early in the morning. There were no significant differences in salivary cortisol, testosterone, or oestradiol, or in EBV or HHV-6 DNA between the LC and control groups. However, salivary HHV-6 DNA levels were positively associated with a greater aggregated LC propensity score (r = 0.24, 95% CI = 0.02-0.44, p = 0.015, adj. p = 0.030), as well as anxiety (β = 0.69, 95% CI = 0.02-1.36, p = 0.045) and depression (β = 0.24, 95% CI = 0.05-0.42, p = 0.013) scores. Interpretation The observed correlation between salivary HHV-6 DNA and symptom severity suggests HHV-6 may contribute to post-acute disease, though mechanisms remain unclear. While we did not identify a relationship between salivary EBV DNA and LC, EBV may still play a role at earlier time points in the disease course, or in compartments not sampled in this study. These findings highlight the potential importance of HHV-6 in LC pathophysiology and underscore the need for longitudinal, multi-compartment studies of herpesvirus reactivation in LC. Funding This work was supported in part by the Else Kröner Fresenius Prize for Medical Research 2023 (to AI), the Howard Hughes Medical Institute Collaborative COVID-19 Initiative (to AI), and the Howard Hughes Medical Institute (to AI), the Polybio Research Foundation (to AI and DP) and the Steven and Alexandra Cohen Foundation (to DP). National Institutes for Health (NIH) funding sources supported AT, SB and CM.

analysis.study_design_and_population: A cross-sectional, case-control study was conducted with 45 participants diagnosed with long COVID and 45 age-sex-matched controls.
analysis.methods: Salivary cortisol, testosterone, and oestradiol were measured, and extracted nucleic acid was tested for EBV, HSV 1/2, HCMV, and HHV-6 A/B using multiplex qPCR, and for SARS-CoV-2 and RNaseP using RT-qPCR. Surveys and validated health questionnaires were used to collect demographics, medical history, and symptom profiles.
analysis.main_results: Salivary HHV-6 DNA levels were positively associated with a greater aggregated long COVID propensity score (r = 0.24, 95% CI = 0.02-0.44, p = 0.015, adj. p = 0.030), as well as anxiety (β = 0.69, 95% CI = 0.02-1.36, p = 0.045) and depression (β = 0.24, 95% CI = 0.05-0.42, p = 0.013) scores. analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The observed correlation between salivary HHV-6 DNA and symptom severity suggests HHV-6 may contribute to post-acute disease, though mechanisms remain unclear.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings highlight the potential importance of HHV-6 in long COVID pathophysiology and underscore the need for longitudinal, multi-compartment studies of herpesvirus reactivation in long COVID.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is cross-sectional, limiting causal inference, and the sample size may not be sufficient to capture all potential associations. The evidence is moderate in strength due to the observational nature of the study.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the relationship between long COVID symptoms and salivary HHV-6 DNA, cortisol, testosterone, and oestradiol levels. It enrolled 45 participants with long COVID and 45 age-sex-matched controls in a cross-sectional, case-control design. Salivary cortisol, testosterone, and oestradiol were measured, and nucleic acid was tested for HHV-6 and other herpesviruses using qPCR. The results showed a positive association between salivary HHV-6 DNA levels and a greater aggregated long COVID propensity score, as well as anxiety and depression scores. However, no significant differences were found in EBV or HHV-6 DNA between the groups. The authors suggest that HHV-6 may contribute to post-acute disease, though mechanisms remain unclear. The findings highlight the potential role of HHV-6 in long COVID pathophysiology and emphasize the need for further longitudinal studies. The study's cross-sectional design limits causal inference, and the moderate sample size may affect the strength of the conclusions.

title_zh: 横断面病例对照分析中唾液 HHV-6 与 长新冠 严重程度之间的关联。
source_body_en: Background Reactivation of human herpesviruses (HHVs), particularly EBV, is associated with more severe acute SARS-CoV-2 infection and the development of Long COVID (LC). Reactivation of HHVs has been previously implicated in hormonal dysregulation, which has also been observed in LC, suggesting a potential link. This study aims to examine the relationship between LC symptoms and salivary HHV DNA, cortisol, testosterone, and oestradiol levels. Methods Our cross-sectional, case-control study enrolled 45 participants with LC, and 45 age-sex-matched controls. Surveys and validated health questionnaires were used to collect demographics, medical history, and symptom profiles. Saliva was self-collected at waking, 15, 30, and 45 min, and 8 and 16 h after waking, across two consecutive days. Salivary cortisol, testosterone and oestradiol were measured, and extracted nucleic acid was tested for EBV, HSV 1/2, HCMV and HHV-6 A/B using multiplex qPCR, and for SARS-CoV-2 and RNaseP using RT-qPCR. Findings Detection of salivary EBV and HHV-6 DNA copies was highest early in the morning. There were no significant differences in salivary cortisol, testosterone, or oestradiol, or in EBV or HHV-6 DNA between the LC and control groups. However, salivary HHV-6 DNA levels were positively associated with a greater aggregated LC propensity score (r = 0.24, 95% CI = 0.02-0.44, p = 0.015, adj. p = 0.030), as well as anxiety (β = 0.69, 95% CI = 0.02-1.36, p = 0.045) and depression (β = 0.24, 95% CI = 0.05-0.42, p = 0.013) scores. Interpretation The observed correlation between salivary HHV-6 DNA and symptom severity suggests HHV-6 may contribute to post-acute disease, though mechanisms remain unclear. While we did not identify a relationship between salivary EBV DNA and LC, EBV may still play a role at earlier time points in the disease course, or in compartments not sampled in this study. These findings highlight the potential importance of HHV-6 in LC pathophysiology and underscore the need for longitudinal, multi-compartment studies of herpesvirus reactivation in LC. Funding This work was supported in part by the Else Kröner Fresenius Prize for Medical Research 2023 (to AI), the Howard Hughes Medical Institute Collaborative COVID-19 Initiative (to AI), and the Howard Hughes Medical Institute (to AI), the Polybio Research Foundation (to AI and DP) and the Steven and Alexandra Cohen Foundation (to DP). National Institutes for Health (NIH) funding sources supported AT, SB and CM.
