title: Association Between Acute Vulvar Ulcers and Gene-Based COVID-19 Vaccines.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: Acute vulvar ulcers have been reported following gene-based COVID-19 vaccinations, though causality remains uncertain. This study aims to examine the association between vaccination and ulcer occurrence. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This observational study analyzed vulvar ulcer cases reported to the Vaccine Adverse Event Reporting System (VAERS) from January 2002 to February 2022. Risk was estimated by comparing VAERS-reported ulcer cases with vaccine recipient data from the COVID Data Tracker. Causality was assessed using the Bradford Hill criteria. RESULTS: From 2021 to 2022, the proportion of vulvar ulcers among reported adverse events exceeded the upper control limits for the first time since 2002. Most cases (134/137, 97.8%) were linked to COVID-19 vaccines. Ad26.COV2.S had the highest relative risk (2.72 vs. BNT162b2; 95% CI: 1.17-6.30). For two-dose vaccines, the second dose posed a higher risk (dose 2 vs. dose 1: RR 3.52; 95% CI: 2.06-6.02 for BNT162b2; RR 2.40; 95% CI: 1.82-3.18 for mRNA-1273). Ulcers appeared a median of 2 days post-vaccination (IQR: 1.25-2.75) and resolved after a median of 12 days (IQR: 7-18). Adolescent females aged 12-17 years had the highest risk (RR vs. age 25-39: 4.01; 95% CI: 2.67-6.05), with a 46.0-fold increased risk (95% CI: 11.2-188.9) compared to age-matched females who received HPV vaccines. CONCLUSIONS: Vulvar ulcers were closely associated with COVID-19 vaccination, especially in adolescent females. While findings suggest a potential link, further research is warranted to determine causality.

title_zh: Association Between Acute Vulvar Ulcers and Gene-Based COVID-19 Vaccines.
source_body_en: OBJECTIVE: Acute vulvar ulcers have been reported following gene-based COVID-19 vaccinations, though causality remains uncertain. This study aims to examine the association between vaccination and ulcer occurrence. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This observational study analyzed vulvar ulcer cases reported to the Vaccine Adverse Event Reporting System (VAERS) from January 2002 to February 2022. Risk was estimated by comparing VAERS-reported ulcer cases with vaccine recipient data from the COVID Data Tracker. Causality was assessed using the Bradford Hill criteria. RESULTS: From 2021 to 2022, the proportion of vulvar ulcers among reported adverse events exceeded the upper control limits for the first time since 2002. Most cases (134/137, 97.8%) were linked to COVID-19 vaccines. Ad26.COV2.S had the highest relative risk (2.72 vs. BNT162b2; 95% CI: 1.17-6.30). For two-dose vaccines, the second dose posed a higher risk (dose 2 vs. dose 1: RR 3.52; 95% CI: 2.06-6.02 for BNT162b2; RR 2.40; 95% CI: 1.82-3.18 for mRNA-1273). Ulcers appeared a median of 2 days post-vaccination (IQR: 1.25-2.75) and resolved after a median of 12 days (IQR: 7-18). Adolescent females aged 12-17 years had the highest risk (RR vs. age 25-39: 4.01; 95% CI: 2.67-6.05), with a 46.0-fold increased risk (95% CI: 11.2-188.9) compared to age-matched females who received HPV vaccines. CONCLUSIONS: Vulvar ulcers were closely associated with COVID-19 vaccination, especially in adolescent females. While findings suggest a potential link, further research is warranted to determine causality.

title: Identification of broad-spectrum inhibitors for the cryptic binding site of SARS-CoV-2 NSP1 across multiple variants using molecular dynamics simulation
abstract: Context Non-structural protein 1 (NSP1) is a critical viral virulence factor expressed early during SARS-CoV-2 infection that facilitates host immune evasion by supressing host gene expression through its interaction with the 40S ribosomal subunit. NSP1 occludes the mRNA entry channel, thereby inhibiting translation of host transcripts while selectively permitting viral mRNA translation. Recent advances in structural biology have revealed previously unrecognized cryptic binding pocket within NSP1, expanding the repertoire of viable drug targets. In this study, we systematically investigated an allosteric pocket of NSP1 as a novel intervention strategy to disrupt NSP1-mRNA interactions. Virtual screening of FDA-approved drugs identified sorafenib as a promising allosteric inhibitor. For the broad-spectrum efficacy evaluation, sorafenib inhibitory potential against a variety of clinically relevant NSP1 mutants was tested. Detailed molecular dynamics simulations of the wild-type and mutant systems showed that sorafenib binding leads to different conformational and dynamic changes, that result in protein stabilization. Residue-level fluctuation analyses indicated that sorafenib had relatively stable interactions within the allosteric pocket even in the presence of destabilizing mutations, suggesting resilience against mutation-driven resistance. We have identified allosteric targeting as a viable approach to blocking the functional role of NSP1 in host translation shutdown. Sorafenib emerges as a promising broad-spectrum NSP1 inhibitor for additional experimental testing and development of NSP1-directed antiviral therapeutics. Methods All FDA-approved drugs were first optimized using the semi-empirical PM6 method. The optimized structures were subsequently subjected to virtual screening against the cryptic binding site of NSP1 using AutoDock. MD simulations of the selected protein-ligand complexes were carried out using GROMACSv2023. Binding free energies were estimated using the MM/PBSA method and steered molecular dynamics simulations were performed to evaluate ligand dissociation. Post-MD trajectory analyses were performed using various built-in GROMACS tools and PyMol.

analysis_en.research_question_and_background: This study aimed to identify broad-spectrum inhibitors targeting the cryptic binding site of SARS-CoV-2 NSP1, which is critical for host immune evasion by suppressing host gene expression through interaction with the 40S ribosomal subunit.
analysis_en.study_design_and_population: The study focused on the cryptic binding pocket of SARS-CoV-2 NSP1, examining its interactions with FDA-approved drugs and evaluating their inhibitory potential against various NSP1 mutants.
analysis_en.methods: FDA-approved drugs were optimized using the PM6 method, then subjected to virtual screening against the NSP1 cryptic binding site with AutoDock. Molecular dynamics simulations were conducted using GROMACSv2023, and binding free energies were estimated via the MM/PBSA method.
analysis_en.main_results: Sorafenib was identified as a promising allosteric inhibitor through virtual screening. Molecular dynamics simulations showed that sorafenib binding leads to conformational and dynamic changes in NSP1, resulting in protein stabilization.
analysis_en.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted these findings as evidence that allosteric targeting of NSP1 could effectively block its functional role in host translation shutdown, offering a novel strategy for antiviral therapeutics.
analysis_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that targeting NSP1's cryptic binding site with drugs like sorafenib could provide a broad-spectrum approach to combat SARS-CoV-2 variants, potentially informing future antiviral drug development.
analysis_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to computational methods and does not include experimental validation, which reduces the strength of the evidence to moderate.

title_zh: 利用分子动力学模拟确定严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 NSP1隐秘结合位点的广谱抑制剂
source_body_en: Context Non-structural protein 1 (NSP1) is a critical viral virulence factor expressed early during SARS-CoV-2 infection that facilitates host immune evasion by supressing host gene expression through its interaction with the 40S ribosomal subunit. NSP1 occludes the mRNA entry channel, thereby inhibiting translation of host transcripts while selectively permitting viral mRNA translation. Recent advances in structural biology have revealed previously unrecognized cryptic binding pocket within NSP1, expanding the repertoire of viable drug targets. In this study, we systematically investigated an allosteric pocket of NSP1 as a novel intervention strategy to disrupt NSP1-mRNA interactions. Virtual screening of FDA-approved drugs identified sorafenib as a promising allosteric inhibitor. For the broad-spectrum efficacy evaluation, sorafenib inhibitory potential against a variety of clinically relevant NSP1 mutants was tested. Detailed molecular dynamics simulations of the wild-type and mutant systems showed that sorafenib binding leads to different conformational and dynamic changes, that result in protein stabilization. Residue-level fluctuation analyses indicated that sorafenib had relatively stable interactions within the allosteric pocket even in the presence of destabilizing mutations, suggesting resilience against mutation-driven resistance. We have identified allosteric targeting as a viable approach to blocking the functional role of NSP1 in host translation shutdown. Sorafenib emerges as a promising broad-spectrum NSP1 inhibitor for additional experimental testing and development of NSP1-directed antiviral therapeutics. Methods All FDA-approved drugs were first optimized using the semi-empirical PM6 method. The optimized structures were subsequently subjected to virtual screening against the cryptic binding site of NSP1 using AutoDock. MD simulations of the selected protein-ligand complexes were carried out using GROMACSv2023. Binding free energies were estimated using the MM/PBSA method and steered molecular dynamics simulations were performed to evaluate ligand dissociation. Post-MD trajectory analyses were performed using various built-in GROMACS tools and PyMol.
abstract_zh: 非结构蛋白 1 (NSP1) 是 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 感染早期表达的关键病毒毒力因子,通过与 40S 核糖体亚基相互作用抑制 宿主 基因表达,从而促进 宿主 免疫逃避。NSP1 阻断 mRNA 进入通道,从而抑制 宿主 转录物的翻译,同时选择性地允许病毒 mRNA 翻译。结构生物学的最新进展揭示了 NSP1 内以前未被识别的神秘结合袋,扩大了可行药物靶点的范围。在这项研究中,我们系统地研究了 NSP1 的变构袋,作为破坏 NSP1-mRNA 相互作用的新干预策略。对 FDA 批准药物的虚拟筛选发现索拉非尼是一种有前途的变构抑制剂。为了进行广谱疗效评估,测试了索拉非尼对多种临床相关 NSP1 突变体的抑制潜力。对野生型和突变体系统的详细分子动力学模拟表明,索拉非尼结合导致不同的构象和动态变化,从而导致蛋白质稳定。残留水平波动分析表明,即使存在不稳定的 突变,索拉非尼在变构袋内也具有相对稳定的相互作用,这表明对 突变 驱动的耐药性具有弹性。我们已经确定变构靶向是阻断 NSP1 在 宿主 翻译关闭中的功能作用的可行方法。索拉非尼作为一种有前景的广谱 NSP1 抑制剂,可用于 NSP1 导向的 抗病毒药物 疗法的额外实验测试和开发。方法 所有 FDA 批准的药物首先使用半经验 PM6 方法进行优化。随后使用 AutoDock 对优化的结构进行针对 NSP1 神秘结合位点的虚拟筛选。使用 GROMACSv2023 对选定的蛋白质-配体复合物进行 MD 模拟。使用 MM/PBSA 方法估计结合自由能,并进行引导分子动力学模拟以评估配体解离。使用各种内置 GROMACS 工具和 PyMol 进行 MD 后轨迹分析。

title: Time to resolution of Long COVID symptoms and the associated factors among the people infected with SARS-CoV-2 during the 3rd wave of COVID-19 in Zambia: A prospective quantitative study
abstract: This study was conducted over 24 months (September 2021-Agust, 2023) to determine the time to resolution of Long COVID symptoms and the associated factors among people infected with SARS-CoV-2 during the 3rd wave (June - August, 2021) of COVID-19 in Zambia. Participants comprised a cohort of 303 people randomly sampled from 7 healthcare facilities from Lusaka and Southern provinces. Demographic and clinical data were collected at baseline and at a monthly interval from participants’ clinical records and interview. Descriptive analysis was conducted to summarise respondent demographic and clinical characteristics. Survival analysis (Kaplan Meier model) was conducted to determine the median time to symptom resolution, generate survival curves and the risk table. A Poisson model was fitted to compute the crude incident rate of recovery. Cox-Proportional Hazards regression analysis was conducted to determine the univariate and multivariate association between the covariates and the time to resolution of symptoms. Crude and adjusted hazard ratios, 95% confidence intervals and p-values were computed. A total of 236 events occurred during the follow- up period; the crude incidence rate was 1, 575.6 events per 1000 person years (95%CI: 1,363.2 - 1,784.4). The median time from diagnosis of Long COVID symptoms to resolution was 6 (IQR: 5-8) months. Vaccination status was significantly associated with the time to resolution of symptoms (aHR= 1.71, 95% CI: 1.02 - 2.86, p=0.04) after adjusting for age, number of children, occupation, pre-existing medical conditions, number of vaccine doses and hospital admission. Other variables did not show statistically significant association with the time to resolution of symptoms (p>0.05). These findings suggest that vaccination is associated with a shorter time to resolution of Long COVID symptoms. Netherless, causation can not be ascertained due to the observational design of the study. A study with an experimental design is needed to establish the causal relationship.

analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The study provides insights into the resolution of Long COVID symptoms and highlights the potential role of vaccination in influencing recovery time, which can inform public health strategies for managing post-COVID conditions.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the time to resolution of Long COVID symptoms and associated factors among individuals infected with SARS-CoV-2 during the 3rd wave of the pandemic in Zambia. Conducted over 24 months, it included 303 participants from seven healthcare facilities. Demographic and clinical data were collected monthly, and survival analysis, Poisson modeling, and Cox-Proportional Hazards regression were used to assess outcomes. The median time to symptom resolution was 6 months, and vaccination status was significantly associated with shorter recovery times (aHR=1.71, 95% CI: 1.02-2.86, p=0.04). Other variables did not show significant associations. The study suggests a potential link between vaccination and symptom resolution but emphasizes the need for experimental designs to confirm causality. These findings may inform public health strategies for managing post-COVID conditions.

Other variables did not show statistically significant association with the time to resolution of symptoms (p>0.05). These findings suggest that vaccination is associated with a shorter time to resolution of Long COVID symptoms. Netherless, causation can not be ascertained due to the observational design of the study. A study with an experimental design is needed to establish the causal relationship.

title: Pregnancy and iron deficiency anemia are associated with COVID-19 severity: a retrospective cohort study from Gaza.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: COVID-19 poses significant risks to pregnant women, with pregnancy recognized as a risk factor for severe disease. This vulnerability may be exacerbated by iron deficiency anemia (IDA) due to impaired immune function, reduced oxygen transport, and altered coagulation and endothelial function. METHODS: A retrospective cohort study of 271 unvaccinated, otherwise healthy women aged 18-38 with COVID-19 was conducted at Al-Shifa Hospital, Gaza (2021). Pregnant (n = 97) and nonpregnant (n = 174) groups were stratified by IDA, investigating the impact of pregnancy and IDA on the severity of COVID-19. Iron deficiency was determined by transferrin saturation levels <20% measured during acute infection, whereas ferritin levels were not available. RESULTS: Overall pregnancy was significantly associated with COVID-19 severity (p < 0.001), with pregnant women having higher odds of critical illness (OR = 4.61, 95% CI 2.27-9.39, p < 0.001) and death (OR = 5.25, 95% CI 1.91-14.44, p = 0.001) compared with moderate illness. All deaths were due to acute respiratory distress syndrome; no venous thromboembolism cases occurred. IDA was associated with COVID-19 severity in both pregnant (p = 0.015) and non-pregnant (p = 0.002) women. In a multivariable model including pregnancy, IDA was associated with higher odds of severe (OR = 3.57, 95% CI 1.97-6.48, p < 0.001), critical (OR = 2.25, 95% CI 1.09-4.64, p = 0.029), and fatal illness (OR = 7.23, 95% CI 1.96-26.74, p = 0.003) compared with moderate illness. CONCLUSION: This study suggests that among young, otherwise healthy, unvaccinated women with COVID-19, pregnancy and IDA are associated with increased COVID-19 severity. However, interpretation requires caution considering the small number of events, particularly deaths, and the assessment of iron status during acute infection using transferrin saturation alone without ferritin measurements, which limits the ability to distinguish preexisting iron deficiency from inflammation-related changes in iron metabolism.

analysis.study_design_and_population: A retrospective cohort study was conducted at Al-Shifa Hospital in Gaza from 2021, involving 271 unvaccinated, otherwise healthy women aged 18-38 with COVID-19. The study stratified participants into pregnant (n = 97) and nonpregnant (n = 174) groups based on IDA status.
analysis.methods: Iron deficiency was assessed using transferrin saturation levels <20% measured during acute infection. Ferritin levels were not available for analysis. A multivariable model was used to evaluate the association between IDA and severity of illness, including critical illness and fatal outcomes.
analysis.main_results: Pregnancy was significantly associated with increased severity of COVID-19, with pregnant women having higher odds of critical illness (OR = 4.61, 95% CI 2.27-9.39, p < 0.001) and death (OR = 5.25, 95% CI 1.91-14.44, p = 0.001) compared with moderate illness. IDA was also associated with higher odds of severe, critical, and fatal illness in both pregnant and nonpregnant women.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret that pregnancy and IDA are associated with increased severity of COVID-19, highlighting the potential impact of these factors on disease outcomes in young, otherwise healthy, unvaccinated women.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that monitoring and addressing iron deficiency in pregnant women may be important for improving outcomes in severe cases of COVID-19, particularly in resource-limited settings like Gaza.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study has limitations due to the small number of events, particularly deaths, and the reliance on transferrin saturation alone to assess iron status, which may not distinguish preexisting iron deficiency from inflammation-related changes.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the association between pregnancy and iron deficiency anemia (IDA) with the severity of COVID-19 in a cohort of 271 unvaccinated, otherwise healthy women aged 18-38 in Gaza. The results showed that pregnancy was significantly linked to higher odds of critical illness and death, while IDA was associated with increased severity in both pregnant and nonpregnant women. The authors suggest that these factors may influence disease outcomes, emphasizing the need for targeted surveillance and management. However, the study's small sample size and reliance on transferrin saturation alone to assess iron status limit the strength of the evidence, necessitating caution in interpretation.

title_zh: Pregnancy and iron deficiency anemia are associated with COVID-19 severity: a retrospective cohort study from Gaza.
source_body_en: INTRODUCTION: COVID-19 poses significant risks to pregnant women, with pregnancy recognized as a risk factor for severe disease. This vulnerability may be exacerbated by iron deficiency anemia (IDA) due to impaired immune function, reduced oxygen transport, and altered coagulation and endothelial function. METHODS: A retrospective cohort study of 271 unvaccinated, otherwise healthy women aged 18-38 with COVID-19 was conducted at Al-Shifa Hospital, Gaza (2021). Pregnant (n = 97) and nonpregnant (n = 174) groups were stratified by IDA, investigating the impact of pregnancy and IDA on the severity of COVID-19. Iron deficiency was determined by transferrin saturation levels <20% measured during acute infection, whereas ferritin levels were not available. RESULTS: Overall pregnancy was significantly associated with COVID-19 severity (p < 0.001), with pregnant women having higher odds of critical illness (OR = 4.61, 95% CI 2.27-9.39, p < 0.001) and death (OR = 5.25, 95% CI 1.91-14.44, p = 0.001) compared with moderate illness. All deaths were due to acute respiratory distress syndrome; no venous thromboembolism cases occurred. IDA was associated with COVID-19 severity in both pregnant (p = 0.015) and non-pregnant (p = 0.002) women. In a multivariable model including pregnancy, IDA was associated with higher odds of severe (OR = 3.57, 95% CI 1.97-6.48, p < 0.001), critical (OR = 2.25, 95% CI 1.09-4.64, p = 0.029), and fatal illness (OR = 7.23, 95% CI 1.96-26.74, p = 0.003) compared with moderate illness. CONCLUSION: This study suggests that among young, otherwise healthy, unvaccinated women with COVID-19, pregnancy and IDA are associated with increased COVID-19 severity. However, interpretation requires caution considering the small number of events, particularly deaths, and the assessment of iron status during acute infection using transferrin saturation alone without ferritin measurements, which limits the ability to distinguish preexisting iron deficiency from inflammation-related changes in iron metabolism.

title: Integrating Individual-Level Syndromic Surveillance Data Into Infectious Disease Modeling for COVID-19 Forecasting in Sweden: Comparative Modeling Study.
abstract: Background The COVID-19 pandemic has triggered major global challenges, highlighting the need for timely surveillance and accurate forecasting to curb disease transmission and reduce the health burden. Traditional modeling approaches usually rely on aggregated data on confirmed cases. However, testing data can be unreliable due to low availability and uptake, as well as registration delays. In Sweden, the 1177 health care helpline provides valuable syndromic surveillance data that can capture early signals of infection prior to confirmation through testing. Objective This study aims to evaluate the effect of integrating syndromic surveillance data on short-term COVID-19 forecast accuracy. Methods We developed a novel epidemiological model named SI s I c HRD (susceptible-infected suspected -infected confirmed -hospitalized-recovered-deceased), incorporating data from the 1177 health care helpline cross-linked with national registers on COVID-19 testing, hospitalizations, and deaths. In the novel model, the population with infection is divided into suspected infections (I s ; those reporting symptoms to 1177) and confirmed infections (I c ; those who tested positive). Accuracy metrics of this model are compared to a model without data from the 1177 health care helpline. To evaluate model performance across different pandemic phases between March 2 and December 31, 2020, we used a daily rolling-window approach with a 60-day fitting period to predict confirmed infections, hospitalizations, and deaths over the subsequent 30 days. Prediction performance was evaluated using mean absolute error and mean absolute percentage error (MAPE). Results The proposed SI s I c HRD model successfully captured the temporal dynamics of confirmed, hospitalized, and death cases. The model achieved a median mean MAPE of 61.6% (IQR 37.6%-79.6%) for confirmed cases, 37.5% (IQR 18.9%-57.5%) for hospitalizations and for deaths, the model achieved a median MAPE of 0.65% (IQR 0.3%-1.9%), indicating substantially higher predictive accuracy for severe outcomes compared to confirmed infections and hospital admissions. Compared to the model without syndromic surveillance data, short-term forecasting performance of the SI s I c HRD model reduced MAPE by an average of 15.7 percentage points for confirmed cases, 8.17 percentage points for hospitalizations, and 1.99 percentage points for deaths. Overall, the results demonstrate predictive stability for severe outcomes during the early phase of the pandemic. Conclusions The proposed model demonstrated predictive performance by integrating individual-level data with health care helpline syndromic data on testing and severe disease outcomes, capturing early signals from symptomatic individuals and distinguishing suspected cases from subsequently confirmed infections, leading to better forecasts of severe outcomes such as hospitalizations and deaths. This framework can support public health decision-making in future outbreaks.

title: Coronavirus health beliefs and fetal health concerns: associations with preventive health behaviors during COVID-19.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: During infectious disease outbreaks, pregnant women and their fetuses may be especially vulnerable to health risks, emphasizing the importance of preventive health behaviors (PHB). title: Impact of the COVID-19 Pandemic on Pediatric Burn Injuries: A Cross-Sectional Study at a Canadian Tertiary Pediatric Hospital.
abstract: Background During the COVID-19 pandemic, Provincial Health Orders led to many families spending more time at home. This study aimed to describe changes in the incidence, mechanisms, and severity of burn injuries for children seen at a provincial pediatric burn center during the COVID-19 pandemic. Methods Patients presenting to the Emergency Department with acute burns from 2019 to 2020 were retrospectively reviewed. Patients were grouped by time of presentation: prior to the COVID-19 pandemic (March 11, 2019 to December 31, 2019), or during the COVID-19 pandemic (March 11, 2020 to December 31, 2020). Groups were compared by demographics, burn characteristics, management, and outcomes. Results Fewer patients with burns presented to the ED during the COVID-19 pandemic ( n = 117) versus prior ( n = 132); however, during the pandemic, the proportion of all ED visits that were burn related was significantly higher ( p = .003). There were no statistically significant differences between the two groups for injury time of day, mechanism, anatomical location, and burn depth. Burn management and time to healing were comparable, although 11% more patients had plastic surgery follow-up during the pandemic ( p = .041). Conclusion The epidemiology of pediatric burn injuries did not significantly change during the COVID-19 pandemic, and access to care remained consistent. The results of this study may have implications for hospital resource allocation planning in the event of similar provincial health orders.

source_records.title: Impact of the COVID-19 Pandemic on Pediatric Burn Injuries: A Cross-Sectional Study at a Canadian Tertiary Pediatric Hospital.
source_records.abstract: Background During the COVID-19 pandemic, Provincial Health Orders led to many families spending more time at home. This study aimed to describe changes in the incidence, mechanisms, and severity of burn injuries for children seen at a provincial pediatric burn center during the COVID-19 pandemic. Methods Patients presenting to the Emergency Department with acute burns from 2019 to 2020 were retrospectively reviewed. Patients were grouped by time of presentation: prior to the COVID-19 pandemic (March 11, 2019 to December 31, 2019), or during the COVID-19 pandemic (March 11, 2020 to December 31, 2020). Groups were compared by demographics, burn characteristics, management, and outcomes. Results Fewer patients with burns presented to the ED during the COVID-19 pandemic (n = 117) versus prior (n = 132); however, during the pandemic, the proportion of all ED visits that were burn related was significantly higher (p = .003). Burn management and time to healing were comparable, although 11% more patients had plastic surgery follow-up during the pandemic (p = .041). Conclusion The epidemiology of pediatric burn injuries did not significantly change during the COVID-19 pandemic, and access to care remained consistent. The results of this study may have implications for hospital resource allocation planning in the event of similar provincial health orders.

title: Emergence of Novel Macrolide-Resistant Mycoplasma pneumoniae Sequence Type 3 Subclades in Children after COVID-19 Pandemic, Taiwan.
abstract: Post-COVID-19 pandemic Mycoplasma pneumoniae resurgences have occurred globally and have been particularly severe in Taiwan. We conducted a multicenter study to assess M. pneumoniae trends in children. Compared with the 2019 peak, 2024 data revealed a doubling of incidence (546/100,000 population), a 2.2-fold increase in intensive care unit admissions (10.9/100,000 population), and a 13.7-fold surge in central nervous system complications (6.1/100,000 population). In a 2023-2024 prospective cohort (n = 226), intensive care unit admission risk factors were neutrophils >7,000/μL (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 6.2 [95% CI 1.3-29.9]), platelets >400 × 10 3 /μL (aOR 12.5 [95% CI 2.7-57.9]), pleural effusion (aOR 9.7 [95% CI 1.6-58.1]), and central nervous system involvement (aOR 27.9 [95% CI 4.1-188.3]). Phylogenetic analysis of 698 genomes demonstrated that 4 emerging subclades replaced pre-COVID-19 lineages by mid-2024; 1 subclade was associated with severe outcomes, highlighting evolving resistant, neurotropic lineages and calling for enhanced surveillance.

title: Epidemiological characteristics and transmission dynamics of dengue in Ningbo City, China before, during, and after the COVID-19 pandemic interventions.
abstract: BACKGROUND Ningbo experienced a local dengue outbreak in 2018-2019, followed by the implementation and relaxation of COVID-19 pandemic interventions. Evidence has been limited on dengue epidemiology and the transmissibility across these periods. METHODS We analyzed routine dengue cases and mosquito surveillance data from 2017 to 2024, using descriptive analyses to assess the epidemiological characteristics, and a mathematical model was developed to estimate the basic reproduction number (R0). RESULTS A total of 266 dengue cases were reported, with no deaths. Before the pandemic interventions, 51.19% of cases were overseas-imported; no cases were reported during pandemic interventions, whereas 73.47% were domestically imported after pandemic interventions. The median age of cases was 38.50 years (IQR = 31.25-54.00), and 57.52% were unemployed, retired, or in commercial services. The onset-to-diagnosis interval shortened post-interventions (4.46 days vs. Viral typing increased post-interventions (34.59% vs. 63.27%), with 83.70% of cases identified as dengue virus-1 infections. Dengue cases were reported across all districts, with higher proportions in Haishu (27.07%) and Yinzhou (24.44%). The incidence was 2.82 per 100,000 persons. Incidence did not differ significantly by sex, but was significantly higher among individuals 15-59 years and those aged ≥60years than among those aged ≤14 years (3.18 and 3.01 per 100,000 persons, respectively, vs. 0.45 per 100,000 persons). Incidence was highest in Haishu and Jiangbei (6.90 and 4.93 per 100,000 persons, respectively). A post-intervention incidence rebound was observed, although no statistically significant differences were observed in the ≤ 14 age group, Beilun District, Ninghai County and Xiangshan County. Aedes albopictus was the only vector species. The mean Breteau Index was 16.07 (SD: 8.04) and decreased across phases, and rebounded in Jiangbei, Zhenhai, and Haishu districts. The mean BI was higher in summer compared to other seasons (p 0.95). The median R0 was higher in the outbreak years (3.46, IQR = 2.98-3.95) than years without local transmission (0.00, IQR = 0.00-0.00; p < 0.001). Median R0 was 0.00 (IQR = 0.00-0.71) over 2017-2024 due to the absence of local cases in most years. CONCLUSIONS Dengue remains non-endemic in Ningbo, and is driven primarily by imported infections rather than sustained local transmission. Despite a reduction in diagnostic delay and vector density, post-PHSM incidences rebounded, and district-level heterogeneity indicates ongoing outbreak potential. Sustained surveillance, rapid diagnosis and district-tailored vector control are critical to prevent re-establishment of local transmission.

title: SARS-CoV-2 membrane (M) protein activates TLR4 to induce an inflammatory response
abstract: ABSTRACT An excessive inflammatory response, also known as “cytokine storm,” is a major cause of severe COVID-19. Viral RNA and its structural proteins are key mediators of SARS-CoV-2-induced inflammation. While the immune sensors and host inflammatory responses induced by SARS-CoV-2 RNA and the structural proteins spike (S), envelope (E), and nucleocapsid (N) are well defined, the role of membrane (M) protein in inflammatory/antiviral response and the signaling pathway facilitating M protein-mediated immune response is not well characterized. Here, we show that SARS-CoV-2 M protein induces robust inflammatory cytokine responses in murine and human macrophages and lungs. We also show that the M protein-induced inflammatory response relies on TLR4 signaling and that MyD88 serves as the key adaptor driving inflammation, while TRIF is primarily required for the antiviral IFN response. Detailed evaluation of downstream signaling pathways highlighted the critical roles of mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAPK) molecules JNK and ERK1/2, followed by nuclear factor kappa B (NF-κB) and p38 signaling in the M protein-TLR4-mediated inflammatory response. Finally, we show that abrogation of M protein-induced ERK1/2 and p38 signaling reduced inflammatory cytokine production and rescued type I interferon production in wild-type macrophages, while inhibition of JNK and NF-κB suppressed the M protein-induced inflammatory and antiviral cytokine responses. Collectively, our results demonstrate that SARS-CoV-2 M protein induces pro-inflammatory cytokines and type I interferons via TLR4-MyD88/TRIF activation, with MAPK activation playing a dominant role, and offer specific targeting of MAPK signaling to mitigate SARS-CoV-2-induced excessive inflammation and pathology. IMPORTANCE Severe COVID-19 is often caused by an excessive inflammatory response, but the role of the SARS-CoV-2 membrane (M) protein in this process has not been well understood. We show that the M protein strongly activates inflammatory and antiviral immune responses through TLR4 signaling and identify the key signaling pathways involved. We also demonstrate that selectively targeting MAPK signaling can reduce harmful inflammation while restoring antiviral interferon responses. These findings improve our understanding of how SARS-CoV-2 causes disease and identify potential therapeutic targets to limit excessive inflammation without compromising antiviral immunity.

title: Strengthening post-market COVID-19 vaccine safety surveillance and research: An interpretive description study from Kenya, South Africa, and Canada.
abstract: Post-market vaccine safety surveillance and research are essential to detect and evaluate rare adverse events following immunization (AEFIs) not identified in pre-licensure clinical trials, such as myocarditis post-COVID-19 vaccination. AEFI surveillance infrastructure varies between jurisdictions. Factors that enable or hinder vaccine safety evaluation across diverse settings are not well understood. The study objective was to examine clinical, social, and structural/system factors that enable AEFI case identification, reporting, data and biosample collection in high-income countries (HICs) and low-and middle-income countries (LMICs). We conducted a qualitative study informed by Interpretive Description in Kenya, South Africa, and Canada. Three participant groups were recruited using purposive and snowball sampling: (1) key informants with leadership roles in AEFI surveillance and research, (2) healthcare workers, research and laboratory staff involved in vaccine safety evaluation, and (3) past participants in COVID-19 vaccine safety studies. Data were collected through semi-structured interviews and focus group discussions. Thematic analysis was conducted. Eighteen key informants, 37 healthcare workers and research staff, and 27 past research participants were enrolled. Facilitators and barriers were identified across two domains: AEFI surveillance and investigation, and vaccine safety research participation. AEFI surveillance and investigation were shaped by trust in system responsiveness, beliefs and awareness around AEFI reporting, digital innovation, and implementation gaps. Research participation was shaped by altruism and social influence, logistics and research infrastructure, and institutional policies and privacy. Facilitators for AEFI surveillance and research included established policies and procedures for surveillance, digital tools, empathic communication about AEFIs, and convenient research processes. Barriers included limitations in workforce capacity, diagnostic testing and funding (especially in LMICs), and cumbersome research approval processes. Findings underscore the need for globally harmonized standards and locally tailored strategies to support AEFI surveillance and research in LMICs and HICs that are patient/participant-centered and include sustainable investments in infrastructure and workforce capacity.

title: Interleukin signaling and iron dysregulation in SARS-CoV-2 pathogenesis and therapeutic targeting
abstract: It is crucial for individuals with high Fe levels to closely monitor their symptoms and seek medical attention if needed. This review article offers a brief yet valuable overview of how inflammation can be managed and immune cells can be activated using IL and their interactions with ACE2, TMPRSS2, and FURIN protease. It also discusses the therapeutic potential of drugs as anti-COVID agents in patients with Fe overload, presenting a new avenue for treating SARS-CoV-2 effectively. The search primarily targeted peer-reviewed English-language articles, including clinical trials and scientific reviews. Researches published through 1983 and 2025 were compiled from reference lists and different electronic databases. IL is vital for controlling inflammation and activating immune cells, playing a crucial role in coordinating the body’s immune response to infections and diseases. In patients with SARS-CoV-2 infection, regulating Fe levels through ACE2, TMPRSS2, or FURIN using pharmacological practices could be a suitable therapeutic approach to control this virus. Cytokine signaling (IL-1 to IL-6), Fe metabolism controlled by the hepcidin–ferroportin axis, immune checkpoint pathways (PD-1/PD-L1), and viral entry factors (ACE2, TMPRSS2, and FURIN) all interact intricately in COVID-19 immunopathology, which offers a conceptual framework for comprehending the complex mechanisms causing illness development and locating possible therapy targets.

title: Infection prevention in residential care homes for the elderly: insights from the antibody landscape of COVID-19 after an explosive outbreak
abstract: Abstract The immunologic landscape of COVID-19 in residential care homes for the elderly (RCHEs) after a territory-wide Omicron surge in early 2022 is informative for current infection control practice. A cross-sectional seroepidemiology survey was conducted among 676 RCHE residents in Hong Kong in 2022. The surrogate virus neutralization test showed that the median percentage inhibition against BA.2 was 46.7 overall, with the mean increasing from 8.63 in February to 54.1 in April before levelling off till November. Profiles of hybrid immunity presented higher neutralizing antibody (nAb) levels than those with CoronaVac (C) or infection (I). A generalized additive regression analysis, accounting for the time elapsed between the last immunologic exposure and blood collection, showed that recent infection profiles (CCCI, CCIC) were associated with higher nAb levels than ICCC. Pearson correlation analysis uncovered that the cross-reactivity between BA.2 and BA.4/5 diverged by serostatus. By pairing cross-sectional sera with vaccination and infection histories, this study elucidates how the immunity landscape in outbreak-prone RCHEs was shaped by immunologic exposures. The moderate post-outbreak nAb level hints at a suboptimal immunity level in RCHEs in the post-Omicron period. The findings strengthen the evidence base for retaining vaccination as an infection control strategy, and provide immunologic support for its time-dependent effectiveness.

title: Metformin at the Time of COVID-19 Infection and Risk of Long COVID: A Target Trial Emulation Study.
abstract: ABSTRACT Our objective was to evaluate metformin prescribed at the time of SARS‐CoV‐2 infection on the risk of developing Long COVID (LC) in electronic health record data. We conducted a new user analysis of metformin prescribed within 6 days of documented infection with severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS‐CoV‐2) versus experimental control: prescription for fluvoxamine, fluticasone, ivermectin, or montelukast. Inclusion criteria: a clinic visit in the 0–6 months and the 6–12 months before infection. Exclusion criteria: metformin or control within 12 months. Primary outcome: LC or death (LC/D), to address death as a competing risk, among patients prescribed drug within Days 0–6 of infection. LC was defined by diagnosis code or computable phenotype. We used entropy balancing to estimate the average treatment effect with a weighted log‐linear model. After weighting, there were 248 in the metformin and control groups; the average age was 53 (16); 16% were Black; and 16% were Hispanic. In the primary analysis, 10/248 (4.0%) in the metformin group developed LC/D versus 21/248 (8.5%) in the control group, adjusted risk ratio (aRR) 0.47 (95% CI 0.25–0.89, p = 0.02). For prescriptions on Days 0–1 relative to infection, aRR was 0.39 (95% CI 0.12–1.24); for prescriptions on Days 0–14, the aRR was 0.75 (95% CI 0.52–1.08). In this observational analysis, metformin prescribed within a week of documented SARS‐CoV‐2 infection was associated with a 53% lower risk of LC over 6 months than comparator medications. With the aRR of 0.47 (95% CI 0.25–0.89), any risk reduction between 75% and 11% is highly compatible with our data. This analysis of electronic health record diagnoses is important for the reproducibility of clinical trial results that ascertained the same outcome but via participant‐report.

title: Postmenopausal Bleeding Risk after COVID-19 Vaccination: A Population-Based Self-Controlled Case Series Study.
abstract: Purpose This study aimed to evaluate whether COVID-19 vaccination increases the risk of postmenopausal bleeding requiring hospital care. Materials and methods We conducted a nationwide population-based study using the integrated database of the Korea Disease Control and Prevention Agency COVID-19 registry and the National Health Insurance Service claims data. Women aged 56 years or older who received their first COVID-19 vaccine dose before December 2021 and were newly diagnosed with postmenopausal bleeding during the observation period were included. A self-controlled case series design was applied to compare the incidence of postmenopausal bleeding during predefined risk periods (1-30 days after each vaccine dose) with that during baseline periods within the same individuals. Incidence rate ratios (IRRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were estimated using conditional Poisson regression models. Results Among 8075792 women aged 56 years or older who received COVID-19 vaccination, 5716 were diagnosed with postmenopausal bleeding. There was no significant increase in the risk of postmenopausal bleeding within 30 days following vaccination (IRR 0.98, 95% CI 0.92-1.04). Results remained consistent in subgroup and sensitivity analyses across vaccine types, doses, and age groups. Conclusion COVID-19 vaccination was not associated with an increased risk of postmenopausal bleeding requiring hospital care. These findings provide reassuring evidence supporting the safety of COVID-19 vaccines in postmenopausal women with respect to bleeding risk.

title: Plasma Interleukin-10 Levels and IL10 Genetic Variants Are Associated With Clinical Outcomes in Patients With Severe COVID-19 Treated With Corticosteroids.
abstract: We aimed to evaluate the association between IL10 variants and plasma IL-10 levels and clinical outcomes in patients with severe COVID-19 treated with corticosteroids. We studied 944 patients with severe COVID-19 who were treated with corticosteroids. The clinical outcomes evaluated were in-hospital mortality and the requirement of invasive mechanical ventilation (IMV). The variants IL10 rs1800872, rs1554286, rs3024505, and rs3122605 were determined using TaqMan SNP assays, and IL-10 levels were measured by ELISA at the start of corticosteroid treatment (T1) and after 8 days (T2). The rs1800872-TT (p = 0.035, OR = 1.55, 95% CI = 1.03-2.33) and the rs1554286-AA genotypes were associated with IMV (p adj = 0.036, OR = 2.42, 95% CI = 1.12-5.95). IL-10 levels were higher at T1 than at T2. At T2, IL-10 levels were higher in non-survivors (15.9 vs. 7.0 pg/mL, p < 0.001) and in patients requiring IMV (9.9 vs. 5.5 pg/mL, p < 0.001). Among non-survivors, IL-10 plasma levels did not decrease at T2. The alluvial plot revealed that 51.9% of patients in the highest IL-10 tertile at T1 remained in the highest tertile at T2, with a mortality rate of 50%. IL10 rs1800872 and rs1554286 contribute to the risk of requiring IMV. Elevated IL-10 levels after corticosteroid treatment were linked to in-hospital mortality and IMV.

title: IL-6 Blockade with Clazakizumab is Associated with Low Myeloid Cell Activation and Increased Type 2 Immune Responses in Non-survivors of COVID-19.
abstract: Background IL-6 inhibitors have been associated with reduced mortality in severe COVID-19 in randomized clinical trials, but the comprehensive immunological impact of IL-6 blockade in the setting of an acute viral infection is poorly understood. Methods To gain insight into the systemic immune response to IL-6 inhibition in COVID-19, we utilized samples from patients who participated in a randomized placebo-controlled trial of clazakizumab, a direct anti-IL-6 monoclonal antibody, in severe COVID-19 in the pre-vaccine era. We applied multidimensional measurements of cytokines, chemokines, whole blood transcriptomes, and high-dimensional immune-metabolic flow cytometry to samples before and after treatment to study the changes in immune signatures after IL-6 blockade and to identify pathways associated with positive clinical outcomes. Results Clazakizumab was associated with a distinct myeloid activation signature and type 2 (T2) cytokine response. Non-survivors who received clazakizumab demonstrated a decoupling of these two clazakizumab-associated phenotypes, exhibiting the most pronounced T2 response coupled with less myeloid activation. Furthermore, elevated baseline levels of the emergency myelopoiesis related cytokine, IL-27, were strongly associated with non-survival after receipt of clazakizumab. Conclusions These findings suggest that specific biomarkers may identify patients most likely to benefit from IL-6 blockade and could lead to more personalized applications in COVID-19 and other inflammatory conditions in which IL-6 targeted therapies are in use.

Non-survivors who received clazakizumab demonstrated a decoupling of these two clazakizumab-associated phenotypes, exhibiting the most pronounced T2 response coupled with less myeloid activation. Furthermore, elevated baseline levels of the emergency myelopoiesis related cytokine, IL-27, were strongly associated with non-survival after receipt of clazakizumab. CONCLUSIONS These findings suggest that specific biomarkers may identify patients most likely to benefit from IL-6 blockade and could lead to more personalized applications in COVID-19 and other inflammatory conditions in which IL-6 targeted therapies are in use.

title: Induction of Caspase-7 Serum and P53 Gene Expression in Severe Omicron Variant SARS-CoV-2 Infection
abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic has caused significant global health issues, with the Omicron variant emerging in South Africa in November 2021. Apoptosis is a natural antiviral defense; however, in SARS-CoV-2 infection, it may paradoxically enhance viral replication, worsening the severity instead of eradicating it. This study aims to investigate viral infection by analyzing serum levels of caspase-7 and gene expression of P53 during the severe and late stages of Omicron infection, as well as their correlation with severity, inflammatory biomarkers, and blood cell counts. A case-control study involved 124 participants aged 25-69, with 74 being SARS-CoV-2 patients and 50 healthy controls. The study found that patients had significantly lower median levels of caspase-7 and P53 than healthy controls. Most patients were considered low producers of caspase-7 and P53. A caspase-7 level greater than 3169 pg/ml (area under the curve=0.790; p < 0.0001) in receiver operating characteristic curve (ROC) analysis; therefore, it is considered a good marker to predict the outcome of COVID-19 patients. The caspase-7 levels showed a significant relationship with biomarkers (ferritin, D-dimer, and blood cells). Our findings with the Omicron variant revealed low levels of caspase-7 and P53 at early infection stages and in older patients with a low Ct value (indicating a high viral load). Thus, the P53 expression induces caspase-7 production, affecting the viral load outcome and control. Further research on the relationship between the severity of Omicron SARS-CoV-2 infections and the activity level of apoptotic caspases is necessary to fully comprehend the hidden potential and characteristics of the current subject of study.

title: A Case of Recurrent COVID-19 Pneumonia Following Rituximab Therapy: Treatment Informed by a Serial Transbronchial Lung Cryobiopsy, BALF SARS-CoV-2 PCR, and the Clinical Course.
abstract: Coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) presents with diagnostic and therapeutic challenges in immunocompromised patients, particularly those receiving anti-CD20 antibody therapy. This report describes a patient with recurrent pneumonia following COVID-19 after receiving anti-CD20 antibody therapy. Two transbronchial lung cryobiopsies documented active lung injury in two clinically distinct episodes. Based on an integrated assessment of the histopathological findings, bronchoalveolar lavage fluid SARS-CoV-2 PCR results, and the clinical course, antiviral and corticosteroid therapies were administered, followed by an improvement in the clinical course. This case suggests that cryobiopsy-based histopathology, integrated with the virological findings and clinical course, may provide complementary information for treatment selection in this patient population.

title: Antigenic landscape of a highly mutated SARS-CoV-2 spike in ongoing viral evolution
abstract: The ongoing emergence of SARS-CoV-2 variants in an increasingly immune-experienced population is largely enabled by the plasticity of the Spike protein, which lies at the frontline of host immune pressure. Here, we investigated how extensive remodeling of the N-terminal domain (NTD) in Spike influences its antigenic properties. Using BA.2.87.1, a variant heavily mutated in this domain, we found that even large deletions do not substantially disrupt overall Spike structure or pseudovirus infectivity. However, our structural and binding analyses revealed that the NTD exhibits increased flexibility and that interaction with a heme–metabolite, known to facilitate the exposure of an immunodominant epitope, is lost. These conformational effects, coupled with 33 NTD mutations, compromised the ability of human convalescent antibodies to engage this domain, contributing to their reduced neutralizing capacity. Consequently, BA.2.87.1-like variants may escape recognition by the preexisting NTD-targeting antibodies, potentially reducing protection. Together, our results highlight the intrinsic adaptability of the Spike beyond the receptor-binding domain, with implications for immune escape during viral evolution.

title: Experiences and challenges of healthcare professionals in oncological surgery during the COVID-19 pandemic: A qualitative study.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: The COVID-19 pandemic posed significant challenges not only to healthcare systems but also to healthcare professionals. This study explores the experiences, perceptions, and perceived burdens of healthcare professionals involved in the care of patients undergoing oncological surgery during the pandemic, with a particular focus on clinical staff working in hospital-based care in Saxony-Anhalt, Germany. METHODS: A qualitative, interpretive-hermeneutic approach was employed using one focus group and one individual semi-structured interview. Participants were healthcare professionals involved in the care of patients undergoing oncological surgery. The focus group included 12 participants, and one additional participant took part in an individual interview. The transcripts were independently coded and analytically annotated by two researchers and systematically analyzed in an iterative process using MAXQDA. The analysis combined deductively informed codes derived from the interview guide with inductively developed codes emerging from the data. The study was reported in accordance with the Consolidated Criteria for Reporting Qualitative Research (COREQ) reporting statement. RESULTS: In September 2024, one focus group and one individual interview were conducted with a total of 13 participants, predominantly nurses and nursing assistants. Nine categories were identified. Participants described substantial emotional, professional, and organizational burdens during the COVID-19 pandemic, including stress, anxiety, increased demands, uncertainty, and difficulties in maintaining usual standards of patient care. Participants also reported challenges related to postponed or adapted oncological treatments, communication with patients under infection-control measures, postoperative care under capacity constraints, team collaboration, and the availability and use of personal protective equipment. Political measures, changing regulations, and the occupational vaccination mandate were perceived by participants as sources of uncertainty, frustration, and reduced autonomy. Despite these challenges, participants also described experiences of team cohesion and professional commitment. Participants expressed a need for clearer guidance, accessible contact persons, psychosocial support, supervision, and greater involvement in decision-making. CONCLUSION: The findings suggest that healthcare professionals involved in hospital-based oncological surgical care experienced substantial emotional, ethical, and organizational challenges during the COVID-19 pandemic. Participants' accounts indicate that pandemic preparedness should extend beyond infection control and include clear communication, consistent guidance, psychosocial support, supervision, and adequate organizational resources. Given the small, convenience-based, and predominantly nursing sample, these findings should be interpreted as context-specific accounts rather than as representative of healthcare professionals in oncological surgery as a whole.

title: Post-COVID-19 Expansion of Streptococcus pyogenes Lineages Causing Toxic Shock Syndrome, Japan, 2023-2024.
abstract: We analyzed 919 Streptococcus pyogenes isolates from laboratory-confirmed streptococcal toxic shock syndrome cases in Japan during 2023-2024. Post-COVID-19 resurgence was driven by expansion of M1 UK (49.8%) and emerging M1 13SNPs (37.4%) lineages, replacing ancestral M1 global . title: Comparing the Risk of Maternal Complications and Adverse Infant Outcomes Among Pregnancies With and Without COVID-19 in the Sentinel System.
abstract: BACKGROUND: SARS-CoV-2 infection during pregnancy may increase the risk of adverse pregnancy outcomes, but knowledge about the timing of COVID-19 infection during pregnancy on these outcomes is limited. OBJECTIVES: We implemented the CONSIGN protocol to examine the impact of COVID-19 on pregnancy-related complications and adverse infant outcomes. STUDY DESIGN: We identified eligible females with live-birth deliveries who had a COVID-19 diagnosis or a positive-confirmed test for SARS-CoV-2. Pregnancies with COVID-19 were propensity score (PS) matched 1:1 to pregnancies without COVID-19 during the 6 months prior to or during pregnancy. RESULTS: From 2020 to 2023, we identified 69 901 pregnancies with COVID-19 and 1:1 matched pregnancies without COVID-19. Most pregnancies with COVID-19 were diagnosed in the third trimester (49%, 33 979/69 901) and < 5% (1860/69 901) were classified as severe. Pregnancies with severe COVID-19 in the first trimester had a higher rate of preterm delivery, and pregnancies with severe COVID-19 in the second trimester had a higher rate of cesarean section compared to those without COVID-19. No increased risk of adverse infant outcomes was observed among 22 865 linked mother-infant pairs with COVID-19 although a slightly increased risk of low birth weight was noted among pregnancies exposed to severe COVID-19 in the third trimester. CONCLUSION: Among nearly 70 000 live-birth pregnancies with COVID-19, severe COVID-19 was associated with cesarean section and preterm delivery. No association with adverse infant outcomes was noted. Our study enabled assessment of the timing and severity of COVID-19 on adverse pregnancy outcomes, although changing treatment and prevention recommendations might impact trends of these outcomes.

title: Lessons learned from pregnant women's experiences with COVID-19 vaccination in Brazil: A qualitative study.
abstract: Abstract Objective To explore pregnant women's perceptions of COVID‐19 vaccination and factors influencing their decision making. Methods This qualitative study, part of a multinational project led by WHO and Johns Hopkins University, was conducted in Brazil between August and December 2023. In‐depth interviews were conducted with 25 pregnant women across all three trimesters of pregnancy and 25 postpartum women, exploring their knowledge, attitudes, and decision making regarding COVID‐19. Data were analyzed thematically through an iterative process until saturation, examining confidence levels, vaccination history, risk perceptions, fears of adverse events, and the influence of healthcare professionals. Based on these dimensions, distinct profiles of vaccine hesitancy were developed. Results Five profiles of COVID‐19 vaccine attitudes during pregnancy were identified among 50 pregnant and postpartum women: trust in vaccination during pregnancy ( n = 23), characterized by confidence in vaccine safety, science, and protection; need for external encouragement to vaccinate ( n = 6), mainly influenced by healthcare professionals or family; waning interest in additional doses ( n = 6), associated with low perceived risk, prior infection, or pandemic fatigue; concerns about vaccine safety or side effects ( n = 7), often linked to previous adverse reactions and insufficient information; and concerns about vaccine effects on pregnancy or the fetus ( n = 8), contributing to delayed or refused vaccination during pregnancy. Conclusion Despite overall high vaccine acceptance in Brazil, pregnancy introduced hesitations related to fetal safety, communication gaps, and trust in health information. The identification of five distinct profiles highlights lessons learned from the COVID‐19 pandemic and reinforces the need for targeted communication strategies and consistent healthcare guidance to support maternal immunization in future public health scenarios.

title: The relationship between immunological age determined by Immune Age Index (IMMAX) and response to vaccination against SARS-CoV-2
abstract: Abstract Immunosenescence contributes to reduced vaccine efficacy in aging populations, but chronological age is an imperfect proxy for the underlying immunological decline. We investigated whether the Immune Age Index (IMMAX), a validated surrogate for the IMM-AGE metric, better predicts vaccination outcomes than chronological age. Using the unique setting of primary SARS-CoV-2 vaccination in immunologically naive individuals, we analyzed anti-spike RBD antibody titers and IMMAX in 658 fully vaccinated adults, including a subgroup of 91 professional firefighters. Both chronological age and IMMAX negatively correlated with antibody titers. Notably, women exhibited IMMAX values matching those of men roughly eight years younger and correspondingly showed higher antibody responses across the entire age range, indicating a sex-based immunological advantage independent of age. In the subgroup of 353 participants vaccinated twice with BNT162b2, our analysis revealed that while antibody titers declined linearly with chronological age, they remained stable across a range of lower IMMAX values before declining beyond an equivalent-years-of-life value of about 60. Professional firefighters displayed significantly lower IMMAX scores than age-, sex-, and lifestyle-matched controls, corresponding to an immune age advantage of 8.24 years. More importantly, they also showed significantly higher antibody titers compared to matched controls. These findings establish IMMAX as a robust, readily measurable biomarker that captures individual variation in immune competence beyond chronological age.

title: Reconstruction of SARS-CoV-2 transmissibility within households in the UK Virus Watch Study
abstract: Abstract Background Households provide an ideal setting to study SARS-CoV-2 transmission modes due to the close proximity and extended exposure among members. Understanding the patterns of who infects whom during infectious disease outbreaks is crucial for implementing effective control measures globally. Combining genomic data with epidemiological insights can help clarify and infer pathways of viral spread. Methods We analyse SARS-CoV-2 whole genome sequences from 237 subjects across 162 households recruited to the Virus Watch Prospective Community Cohort Study ( n = 372 total participants). We consider minority variants as an indicator of within-host genomic diversity and incorporate these into a phylogenetic model to reconstruct the relationships between genomes, leading to a more accurate reconstruction of transmission than if only the consensus variation were used. Results Here we show that of the 73 households with multiple infected participants, both consensus and within-host phylogenetic analyses identify eight households in which one or more secondary cases appear to arise from separate community introductions rather than within-household transmission. These households are excluded from the bottleneck and within-host transmission analyses. For the remaining 65 households, including minority variants when reconstructing phylogeny allows us to infer transmission chains that are otherwise uncertain with consensus variants only. Conclusions Integrating within-host genetic diversity into a phylogenetic model alongside epidemiological data provides a robust approach to accurately identify true household transmission events, assess risk factors for infection acquisition and spread, and improve the estimation of the secondary attack rate

Understanding the patterns of who infects whom during infectious disease outbreaks is crucial for implementing effective control measures globally. Combining genomic data with epidemiological insights can help clarify and infer pathways of viral spread. Methods We analyse SARS-CoV-2 whole genome sequences from 237 subjects across 162 households recruited to the Virus Watch Prospective Community Cohort Study ( n = 372 total participants). We consider minority variants as an indicator of within-host genomic diversity and incorporate these into a phylogenetic model to reconstruct the relationships between genomes, leading to a more accurate reconstruction of transmission than if only the consensus variation were used. Results Here we show that of the 73 households with multiple infected participants, both consensus and within-host phylogenetic analyses identify eight households in which one or more secondary cases appear to arise from separate community introductions rather than within-household transmission. These households are excluded from the bottleneck and within-host transmission analyses. For the remaining 65 households, including minority variants when reconstructing phylogeny allows us to infer transmission chains that are otherwise uncertain with consensus variants only. Conclusions Integrating within-host genetic diversity into a phylogenetic model alongside epidemiological data provides a robust approach to accurately identify true household transmission events, assess risk factors for infection acquisition and spread, and improve the estimation of the secondary attack rate

title: Prospective Associations Between Older Adults' Social Connections and Trajectories of Change in Physical Activity and Psychological Well-Being During the COVID-19 Pandemic: A Parallel Process Approach.
abstract: Associations between seven social connection trajectories and changes in physical activity (PA) and psychological well-being were examined among older adults (N = 890, Mage = 65.05 years, SD = 6.91) during the COVID-19 pandemic. Six online monthly surveys were administered between October 2021 and May 2022. Latent growth curve modeling demonstrated injunctive and descriptive norms did not change over time. Social network, relatedness, stress, and negative affect decreased, and social support quantity and quality increased over time. Social participation, positive affect, and light-intensity PA changed quadratically, and moderate to vigorous PA increased steadily and then slowed over time. Changes in social participation, social network, and social support were positively associated with changes in moderate to vigorous PA and psychological well-being. Findings support theories suggesting social connections play a dynamic, multidimensional role in health behaviors and highlight the need for future research examining how social connections contribute to higher intensity PA and well-being among older adults.

title: Letter to the Editor: Coronavirus disease 2019, multisystem inflammatory syndrome, and children’s hearts: Finding answers with cardiac magnetic resonance imaging
abstract: The article refers to “Persistent long-term subclinical myocardial changes in multisystem inflammatory syndrome in children revealed by cardiac magnetic resonance and galectin-3” by OV et al published in the World Journal of Clinical Pediatrics , multisystem inflammatory syndrome in children (MIS-C) associated with coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) and its cardiovascular complications. MIS-C frequently causes cardiovascular complications, including coronary artery dilatation, low left ventricular (LV) ejection fraction, diastolic dysfunction, myocarditis, and pericardial effusion, decreases over time, usually resolving within 6-9 months after the disease onset. Echocardiographic evaluations reveal mild to moderate LV dysfunction, resolving within two weeks. Severe dysfunction normalizes after approximately 1.5 months. Global longitudinal strain proves valuable for detecting subclinical myocardial damage. Long-term effects based on cardiac magnetic resonance imaging (CMRI) data indicate the persistent myocardial edema and/or fibrosisupto12 months after the initialevent. Signs of interstitial fibrosis were found in 7.7% of patients during a one-year follow-up period. CMRI is an important additional method in the assessment of children who have experienced multisystem inflammatory syndrome in COVID-19, especially in patients with persistent symptoms or abnormal data from other cardiac findings.

title: COVID-19 Vaccination and the Risk of Migraine Chronification: A Comparative Cohort Study of Vaccinated and Unvaccinated Patients With Episodic Migraine.
abstract: Introduction Headache is among the most frequently reported adverse events after COVID-19 vaccination, and patients with migraine often fear that vaccination will worsen their disease or accelerate the transition from episodic to chronic migraine. Controlled data comparing vaccinated and unvaccinated patients with migraine are scarce. Methods We conducted a comparative prospective cohort study of 60 adults with pre-existing episodic migraine, classified at enrolment as vaccinated (n = 30) or unvaccinated (n = 30) against COVID-19, at a single neuroscience clinic in Jeddah, Saudi Arabia, and followed for 6 months. Migraine status (episodic or chronic, per ICHD-3) was assessed at 3 and 6 months. Between-group chronification was compared using Fisher's exact test with odds ratios (ORs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs); patient-level transitions were also examined. No a priori sample-size calculation was performed. Results There were no statistically significant baseline differences between groups in age (30.3 ± 5.07 vs. 30.5 ± 4.46 years; p = 0.87), sex (p = 0.78), or preventive medication (p = 0.58). Provisional chronic-frequency status was recorded in 5/30 vaccinated versus 11/30 unvaccinated patients at 3 months (OR 0.35, 95% CI 0.10-1.16; p = 0.14), and chronic migraine in 3/30 versus 6/30 at 6 months (OR 0.44, 95% CI 0.10-1.97; p = 0.47). All such transitions occurred by 3 months, with no new cases between 3 and 6 months; the confidence intervals were wide and included no difference. Conclusions In this small observational cohort, no statistically significant association was detected between COVID-19 vaccination and migraine chronification. The wide confidence intervals preclude firm conclusions regarding either harm or benefit, and larger, adequately powered studies are needed.

title: Real-world effectiveness of Paxlovid in protecting Long COVID for outpatient adult patients: A target trial emulation study from the RECOVER Initiative.
abstract: Paxlovid (nirmatrelvir/ritonavir) has been approved for use in patients who are at high risk for severe acute COVID-19 illness. Evidence regarding whether acute use of Paxlovid protects against Post-Acute Sequelae of SARS-CoV-2 infection (PASC), or Long COVID, is mixed in high-risk patients and lacking in low-risk patients. With a target trial emulation framework, we evaluated the association of Paxlovid treatment within 5 days of SARS-CoV-2 infection with incident Long COVID and hospitalization or death from any cause in the post-acute period (30-180 days after infection) using electronic health records from the Patient-Centered Clinical Research Networks (PCORnet) RECOVER repository. The study population included 497,499 SARS-CoV-2 positive patients between March 1, 2022, to February 28, 2023. For those who had at least 1 risk factor for severe COVID-19 illness, 159,659 were treated with at least one dose of Paxlovid within 5 days since infection and 272,048 were not treated with Paxlovid or other COVID-19 treatments during the acute infection period. Compared with the non-treated group, Paxlovid treatment was associated with reduced risk of Long COVID with a Hazard Ratio (HR) of 0.88 (95% CI, 0.87 to 0.89) and absolute risk reduction of 2.99 events per 100 persons (95% CI, 2.65 to 3.32). For those without documented risk factors, the associations (HR, 1.03, 95% CI 0.95 to 1.11; risk increase 0.80 events per 100 persons, 95% CI -0.84 to 2.45) were inconclusive. High-risk, nonhospitalized adult patients with COVID-19 who were treated with Paxlovid within 5 days of SARS-CoV-2 infection had a lower risk of Long COVID and all-cause hospitalization or death in the post-acute period. However, Long COVID risk reduction with Paxlovid was not observed in low-risk patients.

The study population included 497,499 SARS-CoV-2 positive patients between March 1, 2022, to February 28, 2023. Compared with the non-treated group, Paxlovid treatment was associated with reduced risk of Long COVID with a Hazard Ratio (HR) of 0.88 (95% CI, 0.87 to 0.89) and absolute risk reduction of 2.99 events per 100 persons (95% CI, 2.65 to 3.32). For those without documented risk factors, the associations (HR, 1.03, 95% CI 0.95 to 1.11; risk increase 0.80 events per 100 persons, 95% CI -0.84 to 2.45) were inconclusive. High-risk, nonhospitalized adult patients with COVID-19 who were treated with Paxlovid within 5 days of SARS-CoV-2 infection had a lower risk of Long COVID and all-cause hospitalization or death in the post-acute period. However, Long COVID risk reduction with Paxlovid was not observed in low-risk patients.

title: Is SARS ‐ CoV ‐2 Infection ( COVID ‐19) Associated With Congenital Anomalies? A Population Study of Congenital Anomaly Surveillance Data and Maternal SARS ‐ CoV ‐2 Infection in Wales
abstract: ABSTRACT Objectives Explore the relationship between maternal SARS‐CoV‐2 infection and congenital anomalies in Wales. Study Design Mixed observational epidemiological cross‐sectional and cohort. Methods Congenital anomaly prevalence data were provided by the Congenital Anomaly Register and Information Service. Two comparisons were made using these data: firstly, congenital anomaly subgroup prevalence prior to and during the pandemic at population level, and in a cohort of women with laboratory‐confirmed maternal SARS‐CoV‐2 infection compared with the population trend. Results Prevalence of congenital anomalies in Wales was lower during the pandemic (mean 365 per 10,000 in 2020–22 vs. 454 per 10,000 in 2009–19) showing stable trends. However, the mean for abdominal wall defects increased from 9.8 per 10,000 births between 2009 and 2019 to 13.9 per 10,000 births in 2020–2022, largely attributed to an increase in omphalocele. A cohort of 486 confirmed maternal SARS‐CoV‐2 infections led to 181 births affected by congenital anomalies, and the trimester of infection did not impact the adjusted odds of this occurring. Circulatory anomalies were most frequently reported, consistent with pre‐pandemic population‐level data. Urinary and cardiac anomalies were more prevalent in this cohort group than at population level. Conclusions There was no clear evidence at population‐level of an association between congenital anomalies and maternal SARS‐CoV‐2 infection in Wales. However, a potential association with specific congenital anomalies cannot be excluded. Increased omphalocele is consistent with a Europe‐wide trend that pre‐dated COVID‐19. National surveillance registries should remain vigilant.

title: Post-COVID-19 Penalty Trends Following an Injury-Prevention Rule Change in Rhode Island High School Boys' Hockey.
abstract: Background Penalty infraction minute (PIM)-based rule modifications have been implemented in youth and high school ice hockey to reduce injury risk. A prior Rhode Island Interscholastic League (RIIL) study demonstrated a reduction in game-related injuries following implementation of a statewide 2015-2016 50/70 PIM rule. The durability of these behavioral trends post-COVID-19 has not been evaluated. Purpose This descriptive epidemiologic study evaluates post-pandemic trends in penalty infraction minutes and disqualifying penalties in RIIL boys' varsity ice hockey. Methods Publicly available RIIL varsity boys' ice hockey data were reviewed for four consecutive seasons (2021-2022 through 2024-2025). Extracted variables included total rostered players, counts of players exceeding PIM thresholds (≥25, ≥50, ≥70), mean team PIM per game, goals scored, number of participating teams, and total disqualifying penalties per season. Data were summarized descriptively by season. Results Across four seasons, rostered players ranged from 479 to 540, with 21 to 25 teams competing annually. Mean team PIM per game remained stable, ranging from 8.13 to 8.83. No players accumulated ≥50 or ≥70 PIM in any season. Players accumulating ≥25 PIM ranged from 17 to 24 per season. Disqualifying penalties occurred each season (range, 5-11 per year) without a consistent directional trend. Goals scored remained proportional to participating teams. Conclusions In post-pandemic seasons, PIM distributions and disqualifying penalties remained stable, with no recurrence of high-PIM accumulations requiring suspension. These findings suggest sustained behavioral patterns following rule modifications, but cannot be interpreted as evidence of injury reduction without injury surveillance data. Continued monitoring incorporating injury outcomes is warranted.

title: Identifying phase separation modulators mediated by the SARS-CoV-2 nucleocapsid protein using a structure-based drug discovery approach.
abstract: As severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) continues to evolve through mutations and acquire resistance to existing antiviral agents, the persistence of post-pandemic infections remains a significant global health concern. To address these challenges, it is crucial to develop novel therapeutic agents that target previously unexplored viral or host mechanisms. The nucleocapsid (N) protein of SARS-CoV-2 plays a critical role in viral RNA replication and genome packaging through its ability to undergo liquid-liquid phase separation (LLPS). Targeting the condensation of N-RNA complex could potentially serve as an effective therapeutic strategy against coronavirus infections. The present study provides a successful exemplification of antiviral agent discovery by targeting the viral N protein on the basis of its structural characteristics. A total of 23 virtual screening compounds and 16 hit derivatives were prepared. Their binding affinity and antiviral activities were evaluated using surface plasmon resonance and immunofluorescence assay, respectively. The impact of these compounds on condensate formation was verified through fluorescence recovery after photobleaching, as well as the inhibition of N condensate formation in cells. Structure-based virtual screening, target protein binding affinity quantification, and cell culture-based anti-SARS-CoV-2 assays enabled the identification a hit compound, D21. Subsequent structural optimization of series I and II yielded compound II8, which exhibits stronger binding affinity for the N protein and effectively inhibits the formation of N-RNA condensates, thereby demonstrating its potential to modulate LLPS, a mechanism underlying its antiviral activity. In vivo evaluation showed that II8 displays antiviral activity in a human ACE2-expressing mouse model when administered intranasally as a pre-incubated mixture with SARS-CoV-2. Due to the pharmacokinetic profile of compound II8, further structural modifications are still required. Our findings suggest that compound II8 may serve as a localized prophylactic nasal spray, providing valuable insights for further development of LLPS modulators as next-generation antiviral agents.
