title: COVID-19 and male infertility - A review
abstract: Abstract Background: Coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19), caused by SARS-CoV-2, is a systemic illness capable of influencing the male reproductive system through fever, inflammation, oxidative stress, vascular injury and endocrine disturbance. Because spermatogenesis is temperature-sensitive and spermatozoa are vulnerable to oxidative damage, semen quality may be altered during acute infection and early recovery. Objective: This systematic review evaluates the association between COVID-19 and male reproductive function, with a focus on conventional semen parameters, sperm DNA fragmentation and oxidative stress, reproductive hormones, SARS-CoV-2 detection in semen, and the time course of recovery. Methods: Published human studies of confirmed or previous SARS-CoV-2 infection were identified through structured searches of electronic literature sources. Eligible observational studies reported at least one male reproductive outcome, including semen quality, sperm functional integrity, reproductive hormones, or viral detection in semen/testicular material. Findings were synthesised qualitatively in accordance with PRISMA 2020 reporting principles (Page et al., 2021). Results: Across the available evidence, the clearest pattern is a short-term reduction in sperm concentration, total sperm count and motility after infection, although individual studies differ in magnitude and not all report persistent abnormalities. Longitudinal and pre/post-infection studies indicate improvement over subsequent months in many men (Guo et al., 2021; Hu et al., 2022; Zhao et al., 2025). Sperm DNA fragmentation and seminal oxidative/inflammatory markers may also increase after COVID-19 (Hajizadeh Maleki and Tartibian, 2021; Yuan et al., 2025). Endocrine studies report transient reductions in testosterone or altered gonadotrophin relationships, particularly during symptomatic disease (Ma et al., 2021; Majzoub et al., 2024). SARS-CoV-2 RNA is rarely detected in semen; one early study reported positive samples, whereas most subsequent cohorts did not (Li et al., 2020; Pan et al., 2020; Ruan et al., 2021). Conclusion: COVID-19 can act as a temporary reproductive stressor in men, particularly after symptomatic or febrile illness. Current evidence supports predominantly indirect mechanisms such as fever, inflammation, oxidative stress and endocrine disturbance, rather than persistent seminal infection. The evidence is insufficient to conclude that COVID-19 commonly causes permanent infertility. When semen results are abnormal soon after infection, repeat assessment after approximately one spermatogenic cycle may help distinguish transient suppression from persistent dysfunction.

title: Antibody Positivity for Influenza A and SARS- CoV-2 Among Patients with Acute Respiratory Illness at Five Sentinel Hospitals in Rwanda
abstract: Abstract Background Serological surveillance complements molecular detection by providing evidence of previous immune exposure to respiratory viruses. However, antibody positivity does not establish the timing of exposure or the cause of the presenting illness, and hospital-based sentinel surveillance does not provide population-representative estimates. This study assessed antibody positivity for influenza A virus and SARS-CoV-2 among patients with acute respiratory illness enrolled at five sentinel hospitals in Rwanda. Methods A total of 500 participants meeting influenza-like illness or severe acute respiratory infection criteria were enrolled from January to early May 2026, with 100 participants recruited at each of five sentinel hospitals. Antibodies were detected by enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay, and logistic regression was used to assess factors associated with antibody positivity. Equal allocation across sites was used for site-level comparison rather than population-proportional sampling. Results Influenza A antibody positivity was 75.4% (377/500; 95% CI, 71.44–78.97%), SARS-CoV-2 antibody positivity was 59.0% (295/500; 95% CI, 54.64–63.23%), and dual antibody positivity was 53.4% (267/500; 95% CI, 49.02–57.73%). Antibody positivity varied across sentinel hospitals, ranging from 61.0% to 93.0% for influenza A and 37.0% to 92.0% for SARS-CoV-2 (both p < 0.001). Influenza vaccination was associated with influenza A antibody positivity (AOR 2.89; 95% CI, 1.27–6.98). Conclusion Antibody positivity for influenza A and SARS-CoV-2 was common among patients with acute respiratory illness enrolled through five sentinel hospitals in Rwanda and varied substantially between sentinel-site clinical populations. These findings describe differences within the national sentinel surveillance system and should not be interpreted as population-representative estimates of national or community-level seroprevalence.

title: Stem Cell Educator Therapy for Ex Vivo Immune Modulation of Peripheral Blood Mononuclear Cells in Patients with Long COVID.
abstract: Long COVID, generally defined as clinical symptoms persisting for 3 months or longer following severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) infection, affects multiple organs and systems. At least 400 million people globally are living with long COVID, with symptoms including persistent fatigue and brain fog. Currently, long COVID care mainly consists of symptomatic management and supportive approaches, with no validated effective treatments available that address the underlying inflammation. Stem Cell Educator (SCE) therapy is a treatment developed to modulate immune responses. This protocol describes SCE therapy and its application in patients with long COVID to evaluate safety, clinical outcomes, and immunological changes. During SCE therapy, a patient's peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMC) are collected by leukapheresis and co-cultured with adherent cord-blood-derived multipotent stem cells (CB-SC) in vitro, after which the "educated" PBMC are returned to the patient's circulation via infusion. SCE therapy has previously been evaluated in clinical studies for type 1 diabetes and other autoimmune diseases. Twenty-five patients with long COVID (15 males and 10 females) received SCE therapy. Five patients experienced mild adverse effects during apheresis, and one patient reported itching during infusion. Brain fog and fatigue disappeared in 21 of 25 patients following treatment, and most participants reported feeling refreshed, energized, and mentally clear. Flow cytometry demonstrated reductions in inflammatory markers, including interleukin-1 beta (IL-1β)-positive cells and C-X-C motif chemokine ligand 16 (CXCL16)-positive cells. These findings demonstrate the application of SCE therapy in patients with long COVID and provide preliminary clinical and immunological observations supporting further evaluation of this approach.

title: Phagocytosis of SARS-CoV-2 nucleocapsid- and RNA-containing immune complexes drives inflammatory cytokine production and endothelial dysfunction.
abstract: The aberrant inflammation that characterizes severe COVID-19 is incompletely understood. Given the persistence of SARS-Cov-2 RNA and nucleocapsid protein (N) and the presence of anti-N antibody during the course of severe infection, we investigated the role of RNA-containing immune complexes (ICs) in driving inflammation. We found that ICs consisting of SARS-CoV-2 RNA, N, and anti-N IgG1 are internalized by primary human monocytes and stimulate inflammatory cytokines and chemokines in a manner dependent on Fcγ receptors and partially dependent on toll-like receptor-8. In addition, the inflammatory response induced in monocytes by RNA-containing ICs caused endothelial dysfunction in vascularized micro-organs. Using nasopharyngeal samples from SARS-CoV-2-infected individuals, SARS-CoV-2 RNA and N were captured by anti-N monoclonal antibody in the absence of lysing reagents, indicating that SARS-CoV-2 RNA and N complexes are present outside of virions and cells. title: COVID-19 as a Natural Experiment in Virtual Oncology Care and Head and Neck Cancer Outcomes.
abstract: Objectives Oncology rapidly adopted telemedicine during COVID‐19, with limited outcome data. Prior work from our group reported the feasibility of telehealth consultations for head-and-neck cancer, one of the most challenging subsites to forego face-to-face encounters. Telemedicine remains an important mode of health care delivery, but data are lacking on cancer outcomes with entry into the treatment pathway through virtual versus conventional in-person consultations. We aimed to address the evidence gap by evaluating cancer outcomes in a homogeneous group of patients with oropharyngeal cancer (OPC) who underwent virtual new-patient consultations. Methods Prospective nonrandomized cohort study at a multistate comprehensive cancer center. The telemedicine (TELE) cohort comprised 41 consecutive radiation oncology OPC consultations from 3/2020 to 9/2020; the standard in‐person (STIP) cohort included 104 patients from 10/2019 to 9/2020 with balanced baseline clinicopathologic features. Follow‐up ended May 31, 2025 (median: 57.0 mo). Primary endpoints included 3-year outcomes: locoregional control (LRC), distant metastasis-free survival (DMFS), progression-free survival (PFS), and cancer-specific survival (CSS). The following quality-of-care metrics were evaluated: time to initiation of treatment, clinical trial enrollment, and feeding tube placement. Results There were no differences in 3-year outcomes between TELE and STIP cohorts: LRC (92.3% vs. 97.0%, P=0.50), DMFS (92.5% vs. 90.6%, P=0.65), PFS (87.5% vs. 88.6%, P=0.88), and CSS (97.4% vs. There were no differences in care quality indicators. Conclusions Telemedicine new patient oncology consultations did not compromise OPC outcomes or care quality. These findings from a pandemic-driven natural experiment support virtual oncology consultations as a viable form of patient-centered care and may encourage telemedicine outcomes studies across other specialties.

title: Bacterial epidemiology and attributable mortality of Ventilator-associated pneumonia before and after COVID-19 pandemic (2018-2021).
abstract: BackgroundVentilator-associated pneumonia (VAP) is a leading cause of morbidity and mortality in mechanically ventilated patients. The COVID-19 pandemic has profoundly modified VAP epidemiology and microbial ecology.MethodsWe conducted a prospective multicenter cohort study within the REA-REZO network (≈20% of French ICU beds), 1 January 2018-31 December 2021. All adults receiving invasive mechanical ventilation were included. VAP was defined according to ECDC criteria. Primary endpoints were VAP incidence density (per 1000 ventilation-days) and 30-day attributable mortality. Secondary endpoints included resistance patterns and pre-pandemic versus pandemic trends.ResultsAmong 98,047 patients, 12,251 patients developed VAP, with an incidence of 18.9/1000 ventilation-days. Peak incidence occurred at day 10 (29/1000 ventilation-days). Thirty-day attributable mortality was 4.9% [95% CI 3.7;6.2], rising to 7.2% [6.0;8.5] at 60 days. Gram-negative bacteria accounted for 78.0% of isolates, predominantly Enterobacterales (46%) and Pseudomonas aeruginosa (20%). Third-generation cephalosporin resistance reached 27% in Enterobacterales and 25% in P. The COVID-19 patients had a higher VAP rate (19.5% vs 9.7%, p<0.001) and mortality (36.9% vs 31.0%, p<0.001).ConclusionsVAP remains highly prevalent in French ICUs with substantial attributable mortality. The COVID-19 pandemic nearly doubled VAP incidence and worsened resistance profiles. Intensified prevention bundles during the first 10 days of ventilation and reinforced antimicrobial stewardship are critical.

title: Endoplasmic Reticulum Stress and Differential Regulation of UPR-Specific Genes in Response to SARS-CoV-2 Infection
abstract: The coronavirus spike (S) protein is folded within the lumen of the endoplasmic reticulum (ER) and can induce ER stress and the unfolded protein response (UPR). Although SARS-CoV-2 infection is known to trigger ER stress, it remains unclear how UPR-associated genes respond across different levels of viral replication. To address this question, I quantified SARS-CoV-2 subgenomic RNAs (sgRNAs) and the expression of fourteen UPR-associated genes in A549 cells, A549 cells expressing human ACE2 (A549+hACE2), and Calu-3 cells infected with SARS-CoV-2. These genes represent the three branches of mammalian UPR. Cells with limited viral gene expression exhibited transcriptional changes consistent with adaptive UPR activation, including increased expression of genes associated with the IRE1α-XBP1 pathway and ER protein-folding functions. In contrast, cells expressing abundant viral sgRNAs displayed strong induction of the PERK-associated genes ATF4 and DDIT3, together with reduced expression of several ER chaperone genes, including HSPA5, CALR, CANX, and HSP90B1. Calu-3 cells exhibited an intermediate response. These findings reveal a continuum of ER-stress responses across increasing levels of SARS-CoV-2 infection and suggest that productive viral replication is associated with selective remodeling of the UPR transcriptional program rather than uniform activation of all UPR pathways. The results shed light on the conflict between the virus and the host cell in controlling the cell fate upon viral infection.

title: Serologic Testing for Middle East Respiratory Syndrome Coronavirus and SARS-CoV-2 Cross-Reactive Immune Responses, the Netherlands
abstract: Cross-reactive SARS-CoV-2-specific antibodies could compromise the specificity of MERS-CoV serology, potentially leading to misclassification of infection history. SARS-CoV-2 exposure induced MERS-CoV antibodies primarily targeting the conserved S2 domain, with occasional neutralizing capacity. Combining MERS-CoV S1 binding with neutralization, however, limited the influence of SARS-CoV-2-induced cross-reactivity on MERS-CoV serology.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the potential for SARS-CoV-2-induced cross-reactive antibodies to affect the specificity of MERS-CoV serology in the Netherlands. It found that SARS-CoV-2 exposure led to the production of MERS-CoV antibodies primarily targeting the conserved S2 domain, with some neutralizing capacity. The researchers combined MERS-CoV S1 binding assays with neutralization tests to address this cross-reactivity. The study suggests that using combined assays can improve the accuracy of MERS-CoV serology in populations with prior SARS-CoV-2 exposure. However, the findings are based on abstract-level evidence, and the study's generalizability may be limited. The results have implications for improving serological testing methods to avoid misclassification of infection history due to cross-reactivity.

title: Temporal changes in incidence of Shoulder Injury Related to Vaccine Administration (SIRVA) after COVID-19 vaccination.
abstract: Shoulder Injury Related to Vaccine Administration (SIRVA) is a rare but potentially preventable adverse event associated with improper intramuscular (IM) injections into the deltoid muscle. This study aimed to assess temporal changes in SIRVA incidence following universal COVID-19 vaccination in Japan and to examine the associations with sex, age, and vaccine type. We analyzed publicly available passive adverse event reports from the Health Science Council in Japan between 2/17/2021 and 3/12/2023. Two SIRVA criteria (broad and narrow) were used. SIRVA cases per 1,000,000 doses and rate ratios were calculated across 9 three-month intervals. Subgroup analyses were conducted according to sex, age, and vaccine type (Pfizer or Moderna). Among the 433,538,539 vaccine doses administered, 574 (broad) and 76 (narrow) SIRVA cases were identified. The highest estimated three-month reporting incidence was 22.96 cases per 1,000,000 doses administered. The incidence of SIRVA declined over time, especially between the first and second three-month intervals. According to both criteria, the reporting incidence was twice as high in women. The highest reporting incidence was observed in individuals aged 35-39 (broad) and 60-64 years (narrow). No significant differences in SIRVA incidence were observed between the vaccine types. The temporal decline in SIRVA incidence may reflect improvements in the IM injection technique during the COVID-19 mass vaccination, but other factors including changes in reporting behavior should also be considered. Training in proper IM injection techniques, monitoring adverse events, and raising awareness of SIRVA are important to further reduce the incidence of SIRVA.

title: Detecting epidemic outbreaks with routine blood tests: A comparison of surveillance methods using COVID-19 simulations and real-world seasonal disease data
abstract: Timely detection of an epidemic outbreak is essential for implementing interventions and limiting the spread of the pathogen. The digitalization of healthcare has led to the availability of up-to-date, large-scale data on routinely tested blood parameters. This data can be used to detect the onset of an epidemic, which is particularly important when a new, previously unknown pathogen emerges for which no testing systems are available. In this study, we evaluated the effectiveness of various mathematical approaches for detecting an epidemic based on routinely collected blood test results. The evaluation was performed using both simulated and real-world data. First, we developed the BloodCovasim agent-based model, which defines the dependency of C-reactive protein (CRP) on time for each individual based on the course of their disease and simulates blood analysis. Using synthetic data from thousands of BloodCovasim simulations, we determined the characteristics of different methods of epidemic outbreak detection under controlled conditions. Second, we used the same methods but applied them to real-world data on CRP from Russia during a period of increased seasonal infectious diseases (rhinoviruses, adenoviruses, seasonal coronaviruses) associated with the back-to-school effect. Third, we compared the CRP-based detection method with methods based on a set of inflammatory biomarkers obtained from complete blood count (CBC) results. As a result, we found that the applicability of the methods depends on the volume of incoming data. With large amounts of data, they demonstrate similar results in terms of the probability of detecting an outbreak. As the number of tests decreases, detection methods based on basic statistical tests lose accuracy faster than those based on moving averages, while the AIC-based detector performs best. The use of composite biomarkers increases the probability of detecting an outbreak compared to using CRP alone. These results can help epidemiologists select mathematical approaches based on the volume of incoming data.

title: Rebound Phenotypes of Childhood Respiratory Infectious Causes After the COVID-19 Perturbation: A 29-Cause, 204-Country Mortality Atlas, 2019–2023
abstract: Background: Post-pandemic resurgence of childhood respiratory pathogens has been documented by case-based surveillance, but case counts are sensitive to testing behaviour. Whether the mortality rebound is uniform or structured is unknown. We phenotyped the 2019–2023 collapse and rebound of modelled childhood deaths from 29 respiratory infectious causes across 204 countries.Methods We assembled a country × cause panel of Global Burden of Disease Study 2023 death estimates at ages 0–19 years (26 lower-respiratory-infection aetiologies, tuberculosis, pertussis and COVID-19). For each cell we defined collapse (2019→2021), rebound (2021→2023) and net change (2019→2023), classified the 1,917 stable cells (2019 deaths ≥20; 1,800 non-COVID-19 and 117 COVID-19) into six phenotypes using declared thresholds, and handled COVID-19 separately as a peak-fade metric. Reporting follows GATHER.Findings The rebound was phenotypically structured, not uniform. Pertussis rebounded in 85 of 87 evaluable countries (98%; median +168%) yet only 32% exceeded their 2019 baseline—a rebound without overshoot, excess concentrated in sub-Saharan Africa. Influenza and respiratory syncytial virus showed a near-universal V-with-shortfall: fast rebound in 70.5% and 72.5% of countries, but median net change near −50%. Only Latin America and the Caribbean sat above baseline, marginally (+0.9%), against −17.0% in high-income countries. COVID-19 deaths faded by a median 73%, resurging in six countries, five late-exit settings. Pneumococcal rebound was uncorrelated with conjugate-vaccine coverage (ρ = 0.00).Interpretation Post-pandemic mortality rebounded as distinct, geographically structured phenotypes, not a single global wave; mortality readouts complement incidence surveillance and locate where the rebound window remains open.

Reporting follows GATHER.Findings The rebound was phenotypically structured, not uniform. Pertussis rebounded in 85 of 87 evaluable countries (98%; median +168%) yet only 32% exceeded their 2019 baseline—a rebound without overshoot, excess concentrated in sub-Saharan Africa. Influenza and respiratory syncytial virus showed a near-universal V-with-shortfall: fast rebound in 70.5% and 72.5% of countries, but median net change near −50%. Only Latin America and the Caribbean sat above baseline, marginally (+0.9%), against −17.0% in high-income countries. COVID-19 deaths faded by a median 73%, resurging in six countries, five late-exit settings. Pneumococcal rebound was uncorrelated with conjugate-vaccine coverage (ρ = 0.00).Interpretation Post-pandemic mortality rebounded as distinct, geographically structured phenotypes, not a single global wave; mortality readouts complement incidence surveillance and locate where the rebound window remains open.

title: Multi-source COVID-19 surveillance in Fujian, China: epidemiological features of two epidemic waves and public health implications
abstract: Objective Using Fujian’s multi-source Coronavirus Disease 2019 (COVID-19) surveillance system, this study compared epidemiological features and indicator associations of two successive epidemic waves to optimize epidemic surveillance and prevention strategies. Methods Multi-source surveillance data were collected from week 49 of 2022 (the week of December 7, 2022, when the 10 optimization measures were issued) to week 29 of 2023 (July 17–23, 2023) in Fujian Province, including reported COVID-19 cases, fever clinic visits, population nucleic acid testing, sentinel hospital surveillance, hospitalized severe cases, and viral variants. Descriptive epidemiology, Spearman correlation, and lagged cross-correlation analyses were adopted for data evaluation. Results The first wave showed a sharp peak pattern, with most indicators peaking around weeks 51–52/2022 and reported cases peaking at week 1/2023; the second wave exhibited a gradual peak at week 21/2023. Peak levels of the second wave were 10.7–99.9% lower across indicators, although the markedly reduced nucleic acid testing volume and changed surveillance conditions warrant cautious interpretation of cross-wave comparisons. The interval between the two epidemic peaks was about 5 months, and severe cases consistently lagged infection peaks by approximately 2 weeks. Indicators were strongly correlated, with the highest correlation between sentinel and nucleic acid positivity rates (rs = 0.92, p < 0.001); lagged cross-correlation analysis indicated that these two indicators moved essentially in synchrony. The XBB variant took approximately 4 weeks from initial local detection to predominance alongside the second epidemic peak. Conclusion The two observed epidemic peaks were approximately 5 months apart, and multi-source surveillance indicators showed high temporal concordance. However, lagged cross-correlation indicated that the indicators moved essentially in synchrony, so sentinel surveillance should be regarded as a complementary monitoring tool rather than a proven early-warning measure. The XBB variant reached predominance approximately 4 weeks after initial local detection in this episode, a descriptive observation that cannot be generalized as a validated predictive tool. These findings facilitate multi-wave epidemic preparedness and surveillance improvement.

title: Social Engagement and Cognitive Function Among Chinese Older Adults During the COVID-19 Outbreak: Gender and Urban-Rural Disparities.
abstract: ObjectivesThis study examines the association between reduced social engagement and cognitive function among older adults in China during the COVID-19 pandemic with a focus on gender and urban-rural differences.MethodsUsing China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study data, we used OLS regression to assess changes in cognitive function before and during the pandemic and their associations with changes in physical and cognitively stimulating activities.ResultsCognitive function declined across social groups, with the largest decline among urban women. Moderate physical activity was not associated with less cognitive function, whereas decreased engagement in cognitively stimulating activities was associated with greater decline.ConclusionsForms of social engagement were associated with cognitive function of older adults in distinct ways, underscoring the need for a nuanced rather than uniform interpretation. The observed differences in cognitive function by subgroups suggest a need for targeted interventions to support older populations in the post-pandemic context.

title: Diabetes–hypertension multimorbidity and admission hypoxaemia marked every in-hospital COVID-19 death during the Delta wave in a Lagos isolation unit: a retrospective case series
abstract: Abstract Background : Patient-level clinical data from sub-Saharan Africa on hospitalised COVID-19 during the Delta-driven third wave are limited. We describe the characteristics, management and outcomes of consecutive patients admitted to a dedicated COVID-19 isolation unit in Lagos, Nigeria, and identify bedside features associated with in-hospital death. Methods : Retrospective case series of all consecutive patients admitted to the COVID-19 isolation unit of the Federal Medical Centre, Ebute-Metta, Lagos, between 1 August and 30 September 2021. Infection was confirmed by rapid antigen testing and RT-PCR. Admission demographics, comorbidities, room-air oxygen saturation (SpO2), full blood count, in-hospital interventions and outcome were abstracted from the unit register. Survivors and non-survivors were compared using exact tests. Results : Fifteen patients were included (median age 57 years, range 16–81; 10 male); nine had at least one comorbidity. In-hospital mortality was 26.7% (4/15; 95% CI 7.8–55.1). All four deaths occurred in patients with coexisting diabetes and hypertension (4/4 vs 0/11 without this combination; p = 0.001), all of whom were hypoxaemic on admission (SpO2 84–89%). Mortality was 80% (4/5) among patients with admission SpO2 Conclusions : In this small series, every in-hospital COVID-19 death occurred in patients who presented with diabetes–hypertension multimorbidity and hypoxaemia. Pulse oximetry and a full blood count at admission may help identify a high-risk phenotype for early escalation in resource-limited settings. The frequent use of therapies without proven benefit underlines the need for evidence-aligned prescribing in future epidemic responses. These hypothesis-generating findings require confirmation in larger, multicentre cohorts.

title: Physicians struck-off the professional registers during COVID-19 pandemic: is their reinstatement risk-free?
abstract: On July 14, 2026, in the course of its examination of a bill concerning healthcare professions, the 12th Social Affairs Committee of the Italian Chamber of Deputies adopted an amendment providing for the reinstatement of physicians removed from the relevant professional registers by the competent medical boards during the SARS-CoV-2 pandemic. The measure was introduced on the grounds that these physicians have breached the rules of the Italian Code of Medical Ethics (ICME) by disseminating vaccine misinformation denying its effectiveness, promoting unsupported therapies, and issuing false certifications. The article highlights three relevant risks arising from this amendment. First, it violates some universally shared principles of clinical ethics as well as the provisions of the ICME in which they are embodied. In doing so, the amendment threatens the role that medical ethics plays in safeguarding the health of both individuals and the wider community. At the same time, it challenges the statutory autonomy of medical boards, which serve as subsidiary state bodies, charged, among other duties, with disciplining registrants. Second, reinstating these physicians would place an unacceptable primacy of politics over science, undermining latter’s independence and blurring the distinction between evidence-based medicine (EBM) and misinformation. Third, the reinstatement of these physicians would jeopardise public health by undermining the Italian citizens’ trust in medicine. From a moral perspective, this amendment also disrespects the memory of pandemic victims, including hundreds of physicians and nurses who died in service. The article concludes by urging health-care professionals to sustain transparent public dialogue with a view to preserve trust in medicine, warning that its erosion could severely compromise the management of future health crises, and calls on Parliament to reject the amendment in order to prevent political interests from jeopardising public health.
journal: Journal of Anesthesia Analgesia and Critical Care

title: A simple and robust approach for expression and purification of Receptor-Binding Domain (RBD) of SARS-CoV-2 spike protein from E. coli.
abstract: The Receptor-Binding Domain (RBD) of the severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) spike protein is the paramount component that is responsible for recognizing the host receptor angiotensin-converting enzyme 2 (ACE2) to initiate the membrane fusion and cell entry. RBD also serves as an important target for development of neutralizing antibodies, virus inhibitors and vaccines. Here, we developed a one-step purification protocol for getting bacterially overexpressed FLAG tagged-RBD with high yield (>20 mg/L minimal medium) and solubility (∼1 mM), which can be used for Nuclear Magnetic Resonance spectroscopy (NMR) study and structural characterization. The purified RBD retains its biological functions as demonstrated by its binding to the human ACE2 receptor and the neutralizing nanobody Ty1. This protocol provides a simple and robust method for producing RBD samples to facilitate NMR-based studies on SARS-CoV-2 for therapeutic development and understanding viral biology.

title: Membrane Association, Conformation, and Dynamics of SARS-CoV/SARS-CoV-2 Spike Fusion Peptides in Lysolipid Micelles
abstract: Fusion peptides within the coronavirus (CoV) Spike glycoprotein interact with host membranes and contribute to the structural rearrangements required for membrane fusion. Here, we investigated the upstream fusion peptide (FPu) from severe acute respiratory syndrome (SARS)-CoV and the conserved internal fusion peptide (IFP) of SARS-CoV/SARS-CoV-2 in zwitterionic and anionic lysolipid micelles using steady-state and time-resolved fluorescence, circular dichroism (CD), electron spin resonance (ESR), and molecular dynamics (MD) simulations. Both peptides strongly associated with the micellar phase, with IFP displaying higher partition coefficients and a clearer preference for negatively charged micelles. FPu exhibited pronounced environment-sensitive fluorescence changes, whereas CD revealed greater α-helical propensity for IFP and higher conformational heterogeneity for FPu. ESR showed that both peptides restricted spin-probe rotational dynamics, with broader and stronger effects in anionic micelles, particularly under acidic pH. MD simulations further indicated dynamic micelle-bound topologies in which central peptide regions were preferentially lipid-associated and less solvent-exposed, while terminal regions remained more flexible. Together, the results demonstrate that peptide affinity, conformation, bound-state topology, and perturbation of micellar dynamics are related but non-equivalent properties, highlighting the importance of membrane composition and environmental conditions in modulating coronavirus fusion-peptide interactions.

Here, we investigated the upstream fusion peptide (FPu) from severe acute respiratory syndrome (SARS)-CoV and the conserved internal fusion peptide (IFP) of SARS-CoV/SARS-CoV-2 in zwitterionic and anionic lysolipid micelles using steady-state and time-resolved fluorescence, circular dichroism (CD), electron spin resonance (ESR), and molecular dynamics (MD) simulations. Both peptides strongly associated with the micellar phase, with IFP displaying higher partition coefficients and a clearer preference for negatively charged micelles. FPu exhibited pronounced environment-sensitive fluorescence changes, whereas CD revealed greater α-helical propensity for IFP and higher conformational heterogeneity for FPu. ESR showed that both peptides restricted spin-probe rotational dynamics, with broader and stronger effects in anionic micelles, particularly under acidic pH. MD simulations further indicated dynamic micelle-bound topologies in which central peptide regions were preferentially lipid-associated and less solvent-exposed, while terminal regions remained more flexible. Together, the results demonstrate that peptide affinity, conformation, bound-state topology, and perturbation of micellar dynamics are related but non-equivalent properties, highlighting the importance of membrane composition and environmental conditions in modulating coronavirus fusion-peptide interactions.

title: Maternal Depression, Childhood Resting-State Brain Connectivity, and Adolescent Depression During the COVID-19 Outbreak.
abstract: Adolescents of mothers with a history of depression are at increased risk for developing depression themselves. These adolescents may have been especially vulnerable to depression under conditions of stress, such as the beginning of the COVID-19 pandemic. To understand the complex processes involved in the transmission of maternal depression risk to adolescent offspring in the context of stress, we examined potential mediating and moderating factors that link maternal depression history and offspring depressive symptoms, including resting-state functional connectivity (rs-FC) and mothers' depressive symptoms, in 85 adolescents during the pandemic. Adolescents' prepandemic rs-FC between the posterior and anterior cingulate cortices (PCC-ACC) moderated the association between maternal depression history and adolescents' symptoms during the pandemic, such that maternal depression history predicted adolescents' symptoms only in youths with heightened PCC-ACC rs-FC. Mothers' depressive symptoms during the pandemic mediated and moderated the link between maternal depression history and adolescents' symptoms. Mothers with a history of depression had greater depressive symptoms early during the pandemic, which were further associated with offspring depressive symptoms. Additionally, maternal depression history predicted depressive symptoms in adolescents whose mothers had lower depressive symptoms during the pandemic. Findings speak to the mediating and moderating processes in the transmission of maternal depression risk to adolescent offspring in the context of the pandemic.

title: Impact of Community Factors on Mental and Physical Health During Successive Waves of COVID-19 Pandemic in China.
abstract: This study examined how community factors impacted well-being during the COVID-19 pandemic in China. Data were collected at two time points: Time 1 (T1) in September 2021 (N = 992) when COVID-19 cases stabilized, and Time 2 (T2) in January 2023 (N = 497) during a sudden outbreak of new infected cases. At T1, perceived community safety and sense of community directly affected depression, anxiety, and physical health symptoms, with sense of community partially mediating these effects. At T2, community factors at T1 continued to impact depression, anxiety, and physical health symptoms. Sense of community at T1 partially mediated the link between community safety at T1 and mental health at T2. Higher income and older age were associated with a stronger sense of community, better perceived community safety, and improved health. Policymakers should consider the impact of community factors on well-being during health crises.

title: Impact of COVID-19 Restrictions on Estimating Causal Effects: Fluoroquinolones and Tendon Rupture.
abstract: Purpose The COVID-19 pandemic disrupted healthcare services, potentially affecting causal effect estimation using real-world data. As a case study, we replicated a cohort study using Clinical Practice Research Datalink Aurum to evaluate whether pandemic-related disruptions influenced the measured association between fluoroquinolone use and tendon rupture. Methods We included adults initiating fluoroquinolones/cephalosporins during 1 January 2006-31 March 2023. Four analyses compared treatment effect estimates using different periods for exposure and outcome ascertainment: pre-pandemic only, pre-pandemic exposure with follow-up extending through the pandemic, all available data and post-pandemic only. We estimated hazard ratios (HRs) for tendon rupture using Cox regression. Results Among 891 968 fluoroquinolone users and 895 229 cephalosporin users, fluoroquinolone users had more comorbidities than cephalosporin users in the pre-pandemic period but fewer in the post-pandemic period. Pre-pandemic analysis showed an increased risk of tendon rupture associated with fluoroquinolones (Propensity score weighted [PSW]-HR: 1.94; 95% CI: 1.46-2.59), consistent with previous evidence. Estimates using all available data were similar for the overall study period (PSW-HR: 1.91; 95% CI: 1.46-2.51) and the pre-pandemic period (PSW-HR: 1.96; 95% CI: 1.47-2.61) but were less precise during/post-pandemic period (PSW-HR: 1.57; 95% CI: 0.72-3.41) with no evidence of a period-treatment interaction (PSW-HR: 0.80; 95% CI: 0.35-1.84). Post-pandemic analysis showed very few events among cephalosporin users but not fluoroquinolone users with a larger but imprecise estimate (PSW-HR: 3.32; 95% CI: 0.62-17.72). Conclusion In this case study, there was no clear evidence that pandemic-related healthcare disruptions materially altered causal estimates, albeit with limited power to detect differences between before and during/post-pandemic effects. Studies using real-world data across the pandemic should routinely examine temporal changes in baseline characteristics and outcome incidence.

title: The estimation of population effective dose after chest CT scans for COVID-19 in Babol.
abstract: The new coronavirus that causes coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) is called severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2). Chest computed tomography (CT) scan plays a key role in the diagnosis of this disease. Due to the increase in chest CT scans because of the COVID-19 pandemic, this study aims to evaluate the population Effective Dose for chest CT scans from COVID-19 patients in Babol city. In the present study, COVID-19 patients who were referred to the radiology department of A and B hospitals and C and D imaging centers for chest CT scans between February 20, 2020, and December 22, 2021, were included in this study. Required information including volume computed tomography dose index (CTDIVOL), and dose-length product (DLP) were obtained from the Dose Report window. Then, by using this information Effective Dose and the annual per capita Effective Dose were calculated. In total, 2288 samples of this study were used to calculate the mean values of CTDIW, CTDIVOL, DLP, and Effective Dose: 7.61 mGy, 5.74 mGy, 146.61 mGy.cm, and 2.12 mSv, respectively. In one year, 44,347 patients underwent chest CT scans at hospitals A and B, as well as imaging centers C and D. The annual per capita effective dose for these patients was calculated to be 1.79 mSv. The annual per capita Effective Dose of Babol was calculated to be 0.14 mSv. This study assessed the Effective Dose received by the population from chest CT examinations of COVID-19 patients and compared these findings with previously published data. The calculated dose index values exceeded those reported for low-dose chest CT protocols, while remaining comparable to those obtained from standard CT protocols. These findings underscore the need to optimize imaging protocols to further reduce patient radiation exposure and minimize the collective dose within the community, particularly in light of the increased use of chest CT imaging during the pandemic.

Required information including volume computed tomography dose index (CTDIVOL), and dose-length product (DLP) were obtained from the Dose Report window. Then, by using this information Effective Dose and the annual per capita Effective Dose were calculated. In total, 2288 samples of this study were used to calculate the mean values of CTDIW, CTDIVOL, DLP, and Effective Dose: 7.61 mGy, 5.74 mGy, 146.61 mGy.cm, and 2.12 mSv, respectively. In one year, 44,347 patients underwent chest CT scans at hospitals A and B, as well as imaging centers C and D. The annual per capita effective dose for these patients was calculated to be 1.79 mSv. The annual per capita Effective Dose of Babol was calculated to be 0.14 mSv. This study assessed the Effective Dose received by the population from chest CT examinations of COVID-19 patients and compared these findings with previously published data. The calculated dose index values exceeded those reported for low-dose chest CT protocols, while remaining comparable to those obtained from standard CT protocols. These findings underscore the need to optimize imaging protocols to further reduce patient radiation exposure and minimize the collective dose within the community, particularly in light of the increased use of chest CT imaging during the pandemic.

title: Influence of the COVID-19 pandemic on the incidence, severity, and pathogen spectrum of acute otitis media with complications in adults.
abstract: This study aimed to investigate the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on (1) the incidence of acute otitis media (AOM) with complications, (2) the incidence and severity of complications, and (3) the spectrum of pathogens. Monocentric retrospective cohort analysis in a tertiary care and referral hospital in Switzerland. Adult patients diagnosed with complications of AOM before (pre-pandemic period: 01.01.2014 to 31.01.2020), during (pandemic period: 01.02.2020 to 31.03.2022) and after the COVID-19 pandemic (post-pandemic period: 01.04.2022 to 01.09.2024) were included. To analyze the nationwide incidence in Switzerland, data from a national hospitalization database provided by the Swiss Federal Statistical Office were used. Ninety patients were included in the cohort analysis. A significant increase in the incidence of AOM with complications was observed in our cohort from the pre-pandemic to the post-pandemic period from 1.46 to 2.60/100'000 person-years (IRR 1.78, 95% CI 1.15-2.76; p = 0.009). This finding was consistent with nationwide incidence trends. The incidence of acute mastoiditis in our cohort increased significantly from the pre-pandemic to the post-pandemic period from 0.18 to 0.69/100'000 person-years (IRR 3.77, 95% CI 1.20-12.86; p = 0.017). No significant differences in the requirement of surgical treatment or in the pathogen spectrum were observed in our cohort between periods. Our data showed a significant increase in AOM with complications following the lifting of COVID-19 isolation measures compared to pre-pandemic numbers with a shift towards more severe complications.

title: HEMATOLOGICAL AND RENAL BIOMARKERS IN CRITICALLY ILL PATIENTS WITH COVID-19 IN A BRAZILIAN ICU: A RETROSPECTIVE COHORT STUDY.
abstract: and Objectives: Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome Coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) is associated with high morbidity and mortality, especially in critically ill patients. This study aimed to evaluate the behavior of hematological and renal biomarkers and their association with mortality in brazilian ICU patients with COVID-19. This retrospective cohort study included 52 adult patients admitted to a Brazilian ICU between June 2020 and September 2021. Hematological parameters, urea, creatinine, neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR), and platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio (PLR) were assessed at admission and at the final outcome. Statistical analyses were performed in two stages: first, comparisons were made between sexes (male vs. female); subsequently, patients were stratified into survivors and non-survivors for group comparisons. Between-group analyses were conducted using the Mann-Whitney U test, with paired comparisons performed using the Wilcoxon signed-rank test. Multivariable logistic regression was used to identify independent predictors of mortality. Patients who died during hospitalization (non-survivors, n=29) showed higher levels of urea, creatinine, leukocytes, and neutrophils, and lower hemoglobin and platelet counts compared to survivors (n=23) (p<0.001). Renal and hematological alterations were independently associated with mortality. Dynamic changes in hematological and renal biomarkers are strongly associated with mortality. Serial monitoring may improve risk stratification in critically ill COVID-19 patients.

title: Potential Synergistic Association of Donepezil and Metformin With COVID-19 Mortality in Dementia Patients.
abstract: Background Older adults with dementia face markedly elevated mortality from COVID-19. Both donepezil and metformin have anti-inflammatory effects and are associated with improved outcomes in respiratory viral infections, but whether their combined use is associated with lower COVID-19 mortality remains unknown. Methods We conducted a retrospective cohort study using the National Clinical Cohort Collaborative (N3C) data enclave, including adults aged ≥65 years with primary SARS-CoV-2 infection. We evaluated the association between donepezil monotherapy (5 mg or 10 mg) and COVID-19 mortality using 1-to-1 propensity score-matched analyses. Analyses were stratified by diabetes and metformin use. Results Among patients with dementia, 30-day mortality was lower in patients receiving donepezil 5 mg compared with matched untreated controls (10.3% vs 13.2%; p = 0.00046) and similarly for 10 mg (10.3% vs 13.4%; p = 0.0014). Among patients with dementia and diabetes, donepezil-metformin use was associated with the lowest mortality, approaching levels in matched individuals without dementia or diabetes. Metformin or donepezil alone was associated with modest reductions. Among donepezil users, those with diabetes treated with metformin had lower mortality than those without diabetes (30-day: 7.6% vs 10.2%, p = 0.016; significant only after FDR correction). No significant mortality differences by diabetes or metformin use were observed among dementia patients not receiving donepezil. Conclusions Donepezil use was associated with reduced COVID-19 mortality in older adults with dementia, with findings consistent with a potential synergistic association with metformin. These findings warrant further study of cholinergic modulation, alone or with metabolic therapies, to reduce severe COVID-19 outcomes.

title: Pan-Coronavirus Molecular Surveillance in Stool Samples from Patients with Acute Gastroenteritis: SARS-CoV-2 as the Only Coronavirus Detected
abstract: Background: Coronaviruses (CoVs) are important human and animal pathogens with respiratory and gastrointestinal tropism and considerable potential for cross-species transmission. Broad molecular surveillance approaches may complement virus-specific assays by facilitating the detection of both known and potentially emerging CoVs in diverse clinical specimens. This study aimed to investigate and molecularly characterize CoVs in stool samples from patients with acute gastroenteritis using a broad-range pan-coronavirus (panCoV) RT-PCR approach and to provide baseline data relevant to future One Health surveillance. Methods: A total of 280 stool samples collected from patients with acute gastroenteritis between November 2021 and October 2022 were analyzed. Viral nucleic acids were subjected to semi-nested panCoV RT-PCR targeting a conserved approximately 600 bp region of the RNA-dependent RNA polymerase (RdRp) gene within the subfamily Orthocoronavirinae. Confirmed amplicons were characterized by Sanger sequencing and BLASTn analysis, and sequences of sufficient quality were further evaluated by phylogenetic analysis. Results: CoV RNA was detected in 20 of 280 stool samples (7.14%, 95% exact CI, 4.42–10.82%). Sequence analysis identified all 20 positive samples as SARS-CoV-2, while phylogenetic analysis of 16 high-quality sequences supported species-level identification. No endemic non-SARS-CoV-2 or zoonotic CoVs were detected by the applied assay in this cohort. In an exploratory analysis, SARS-CoV-2 RNA detection was more frequent among patients receiving chemotherapy and/or immunosuppressive treatment than among those not receiving these therapies (18.4% vs. Conclusions: Broad-range molecular screening of stool specimens from patients with acute gastroenteritis detected SARS-CoV-2 RNA, whereas no endemic non-SARS-CoV-2 or zoonotic CoVs were detected by the applied assay in this cohort. These findings provide baseline data on coronavirus RNA detection in an underexplored clinical specimen type and support the potential complementary role of stool-based molecular surveillance in future integrated One Health surveillance strategies. Detection of viral RNA alone does not demonstrate viral infectivity or fecal–oral transmission.

title: Circadian Light Amplitude and Activity Timing Associated with Mean Platelet Volume in Young Adults with Previous SARS-CoV-2 Infection
abstract: Background: / Objectives: Circadian light exposure and rest–activity timing may influence hematologic physiology through pathways involving autonomic regulation, inflammation, and vascular function. However, the relationships between objectively measured circadian exposures and platelet indices remain insufficiently characterized, particularly in young adults with previous SARS-CoV-2 infection. We investigated associations between actigraphy-derived light and activity metrics and platelet indices, and examined whether these associations differed according to previous infection status. Methods: One hundred twelve young adults (mean age 24.4±9.7 years; 74 COVID+, 38 COVID−) from Tyumen, Russia, wore wrist actigraphs with light sensors for 7 consecutive days (October–November 2023). Fasting morning complete blood counts provided platelet count (PLT), mean platelet volume (MPV), platelet distribution width (PDW), and plateletcrit (PCT). Multivariable linear regression tested associations between circadian predictors and platelet indices, adjusted for age and sex. Results: No significant associations were found between circadian metrics and PLT, PDW, PCT, or MPV/PLT ratio after FDR correction. Higher MPV was independently associated with greater normalized amplitude of blue-light exposure, earlier BLE L5 onset, earlier wake time, and earlier 24-h activity acrophase. These associations were stronger in COVID+ participants and non-significant in COVID− participants. Earlier BLE L5 and fair light hygiene were associated with higher MPV in COVID+ only. Conclusions: In this cross-sectional study, MPV, but not the other platelet indices examined, was associated with selected measures of circadian light exposure and rest–activity timing. Associations were more pronounced among participants reporting previous SARS-CoV-2 infection. These findings identify a potential link between environmental circadian patterns and hematologic phenotype that warrants further investigation in relation to vascular physiology. Longitudinal studies incorporating direct measures of platelet function and cardiovascular regulation are needed to determine the underlying mechanisms and clinical significance.

title: Functional and mechanistic characterization of SARS-CoV-2 NSP15 reveals metal-dependent regulation and inhibition by direct-binding small molecules.
abstract: The SARS-CoV-2 nonstructural protein 15 (NSP15) is a uridine-specific endoribonuclease involved in viral RNA processing and immune evasion, thereby contributing to viral pathogenesis. Although NSP15 has been structurally characterized in several studies, which report its endoribonuclease activity and regulatory features, important functional and regulatory gaps remain unaddressed, including quantitative stability, metal ion regulation, and inhibitor-binding kinetics. To address these gaps, we used an integrated approach to investigate NSP15 regulation and inhibition. Thermochemical stability studies indicated moderate NSP15 stability, with cooperative unfolding characterized by a Cm of 1.68 M urea and a Tm of ∼70°C. Urea-PAGE activity measurements revealed a strong metal ion dependence, with Mn2+ as the optimal activator and marked stimulation compared with Ca2+, Mg2+, and Zn2+. Biophysical experiments using SPR and fluorescence quenching confirmed a direct protein-ligand interaction with dissociation constants of ∼1-4 μM. Consistent with these results, the compounds inhibited endoribonuclease activity with IC50 values of ∼8-30 μM. Alanine substitution of catalytic residues H235A and H250A completely abolished cleavage, while S294A within the B1 pocket, a uridine-specificity determinant, reduced activity by 51%-67% (10-50 nM), markedly weakened inhibitor binding, and increased inhibition susceptibility. Importantly, docking and simulation studies revealed stabilized active-site dynamics driven by strong polar interactions, as evidenced by solvent-accessible surface area, hydrogen-bonding, RMSD, RMSF, and radius of gyration (Rg) analyses, underscoring the coordinated contribution of polar contacts and hydrophobic interactions in the inhibitor-bound active-site conformation. Collectively, the present work provides quantitative, mutational, and functional characterization, forming a foundation for designing NSP15-specific antivirals.

title: Does COVID-19 Vaccination Protect Against Post-COVID Cardiovascular Conditions?
abstract: Cardiovascular diseases, such as acute myocardial infarction, heart failure, and arrhythmias, have been associated with SARS-CoV-2 infection, representing an important cause of long-term morbidity and mortality. In addition to preventing primary infection, COVID-19 vaccination has emerged as a protective factor against post-COVID cardiovascular outcomes. This study aims to analyse the evidence supporting a causal relationship between COVID-19 vaccination and the prevention of post-COVID cardiovascular conditions, based on classical and contemporary epidemiological criteria, including the Bradford Hill criteria (BHC) and the sufficient component cause (SCC) model. A qualitative synthesis of the evidence was performed according to the nine BHC and the SCC model. Scientific evidence indicates that COVID-19 vaccination meets four of the nine BHC as a protective factor against post-COVID cardiovascular conditions, namely strength of association, consistency, temporality, and biological gradient. Three criteria, biological plausibility, coherence, and analogy, were partially met. Specificity and experimental evidence were not supported by the available literature. The SCC model highlights the fundamental role of vaccination as a preventive causal component. It also contributes to two criteria, strength of association and temporality, while emphasising the limitation of specificity in causal inference. COVID-19 vaccination has proven effective beyond the acute phase of the disease, with protection extending to a reduced risk of post-COVID cardiovascular conditions. Comprehensive immunisation strategies and reinfection prevention are essential to mitigate the burden of post-COVID conditions. Additional studies are needed to explore the underlying biological mechanisms, interactions, and the role of COVID-19 vaccination in preventing post-COVID complications.

title: Symptom Expectations and Subsequent Symptom Reporting Following COVID-19 Vaccination: A Prospective Naturalistic Study of Nocebo-Related Processes
abstract: Response expectancies are central to nocebo models, but naturalistic studies cannot readily distinguish expectancy-related symptom reporting from biological reactions. We tested whether pre-intervention symptom expectations prospectively predicted subsequent reports. Adults awaiting AstraZeneca or Pfizer-BioNTech vaccination in Poland completed a pre-vaccination assessment in the first half of 2021 (N = 244); 197 completed telephone follow-up about two weeks later. The primary outcome was the number of reported symptoms. A multivariable negative-binomial model adjusted for vaccine type, sex, and age. Symptom-specific logistic models were adjusted for the same covariates and controlled using the Benjamini-Hochberg false-discovery rate. Attrition-weighted and alternative-model analyses assessed robustness. The expected and reported symptom counts were positively correlated (rho = .34, 95% CI [.22, .46]). In the adjusted count model, each additional expected symptom was associated with an 11% higher expected number of reported symptoms (incidence rate ratio = 1.11, 95% CI [1.02, 1.20], p = .011). Vaccine type was not independently associated with symptom count (incidence rate ratio = 0.91, 95% CI [0.61, 1.36]). Of five symptom-specific models, only expected headache remained associated with reported headache after adjustment and false-discovery-rate correction (adjusted odds ratio = 4.06, 95% CI [1.52, 10.88], q = .027). Attrition-weighted analysis produced a similar estimate for expected symptom count. Pre-intervention symptom expectations were independently associated with later symptom reporting in a real-world medical context. The temporal ordering and adjusted analyses are consistent with nocebo-related processes, but the observational design does not establish an expectancy-induced nocebo effect.

title: Rapid Screening of Early SARS-CoV-2 Variants of Concern by Pyrosequencing
abstract: SARS-CoV-2 variants of concern (VOCs) emerged in late 2020 and were characterized by increased transmissibility, virulence, or antigenic drift. Rapid identification in diagnostic materials is essential for effective implementation of public health responses. The spike gene, essential in viral entry and immune escape, frequently harbors VOC-specific mutations. Their detection by conventional sequencing methods remains time-consuming. A nested RT-PCR-based pyrosequencing (PSQ) assay was designed targeting three mutation-dense regions of the SARS-CoV-2 spike gene. Analytical specificity was assessed using defined controls. Clinical validation involved 175 SARS-CoV-2-positive specimens from the national German acute respiratory infections (ARI) sentinel covering Alpha, Beta, and Delta variants, with different subsets of spike mutations analyzed by PSQ. PSQ generated interpretable pyrograms and enabled reliable detection of predefined VOC-associated spike mutations. Direct comparison of PSQ calls with the corresponding WGS-derived sequences showed 98.6% concordance (489/496 evaluable comparisons). The workflow enabled same-day mutation profiling directly from diagnostic material, providing rapid sequence-level information on mutations associated with increased transmissibility and immune escape. These findings demonstrate that PSQ provides rapid and reliable screening of predefined spike mutations associated with early SARS-CoV-2 VOCs. The workflow may complement whole-genome sequencing in surveillance settings where rapid mutation-level information is required. In a broader sense, the study demonstrates a data-driven approach for developing and periodically adapting targeted molecular surveillance assays as viral populations evolve.

title: Causal discovery and inference in COVID-19: A multiscale longitudinal analysis using mixtures of DAGs.
abstract: Real-world longitudinal clinical datasets present major challenges for causal discovery due to mixed variable types, temporal dependencies, treatment-selection mechanisms, missingness, and patient heterogeneity. We extended the Causal Inference over Mixtures (CIM) framework to accommodate mixed-type longitudinal data and applied it to 1,937 hospitalized patients from the Khorshid COVID Cohort. The analysis integrated admission characteristics, symptom trajectories, in-hospital treatments, laboratory measures, and short-term outcomes up to 12 weeks after discharge using mixed conditional-independence testing, bootstrap stability selection, graph-based interpretation, and follow-up outcome assessment. The recovered ancestral structures revealed clinically coherent symptom clusters at admission and persistent associations among several post-discharge symptoms, including cough, fatigue/weakness, shortness of breath, weight loss, and loss of smell. Treatment-related associations were interpreted cautiously because cumulative treatment exposure may reflect disease severity, hospitalization duration, physician decision-making, and other selection mechanisms. In particular, the observed associations involving ceftriaxone and interferon-β should be regarded as exploratory and require independent validation. Simulation studies demonstrated that CIM consistently outperformed PC, FCI, RFCI, and CCI, achieving the highest recovery accuracy and balanced accuracy while maintaining low false-positive rates and competitive computational efficiency, even in the presence of latent confounding and selection bias. These results support the feasibility and utility of the proposed framework for identifying robust structural patterns in complex longitudinal clinical data. Given the observational nature of the study, the single-cohort design, and the absence of external replication, the findings should be viewed primarily as hypothesis-generating rather than confirmatory evidence of causal effects.

title: Alcohol use and its associations with mental health across the first year of the COVID-19 pandemic.
abstract: BACKGROUND: While the COVID-19 pandemic caused major disruptions to social connections and lifestyles, many countries continued the sale of alcohol as an essential commodity. Evidence on change in alcohol use, and its association with mental health and wellbeing during the pandemic is, however, mixed and limited to initial periods of the pandemic. This study aimed to address these research gaps. METHODS: Data were drawn from the COVID-19 Risks Across the Lifespan (CORAL) Study, a three-wave longitudinal study conducted between May 2020 and April 2021. The present sample included 2,369 participants (ageM = 38.81 ± 16.94 years, range = 11-100; 90% females) from the United Kingdom, United States, and Australia. Measures included pre-pandemic alcohol use and changes in consumption frequency, quantity, drinking behaviours (e.g., drinking earlier in the day), and motivations (e.g., drinking for enjoyment) during the pandemic. General perceived stress, COVID-19-related stress, loneliness, and symptoms of depression and anxiety were also assessed. FINDINGS: Drinking frequency and quantity remained stable across the first year of the pandemic; however, non-linear age associations were found. Young individuals aged between 11 to 20 years, and mid-aged individuals aged between 50 to 70 years, had the highest probability of increased alcohol use frequency and quantity. Drinking behaviours and motivations also remained largely stable, although age- and country-specific differences emerged, potentially reflecting policy differences such as alcohol access restrictions and lockdown measures. Finally, loneliness unidirectionally predicted subsequent alcohol use quantity. CONCLUSIONS: These findings highlight the heterogeneous alcohol use patterns across age groups and countries during the pandemic, and underscore loneliness as an important public health issue with implications for alcohol misuse.

title: Discovery of 3-phenyldibenzo[b,d]furan derivatives as potent multi-stage inhibitors against SARS-CoV-2.
abstract: Since its emergence in early 2020, SARS-CoV-2 has continuously threatened human health and public safety, underscoring the persistent need for novel antiviral agents. Based on our previously identified marine natural product peniterphenyl A, we designed and synthesized 23 novel 3-phenyldibenzo[b,d]furan derivatives (T1 - T23). Their anti-SARS-CoV-2 activities were evaluated using two infection models: recombinant VSV-Venus-VSVΔG-SARS2-SΔ21 in Vero cells (rVSV-s/Vero) and transcription- and replication-competent SARS-CoV-2 virus-like particles in Caco-2-N cells (trVLP/Caco-2-N). Among them, T11 (IC50 = 5.6 and 3.1 μM), T15 (IC50 = 8.1 and 5.1 μM), and T16 (IC50 = 8.2 and 4.2 μM) exhibited moderate to potent inhibitory activities in both models. Preliminary structure-activity relationship analysis indicated that the 3-phenyldibenzo[b,d]furan scaffold serves as the core pharmacophore, with 2-OH on the B ring and 2'-Br on the C ring being favorable for activity. T15 could downregulate IL-1β mRNA expression. It had low cytotoxicity against host cells and no direct virucidal activity. Mechanistically, by targeting on the AMP-activated protein kinase (AMPK), it inhibited viral entry and almost completely blocked viral replication when added within 4 h post-infection, whereas its antiviral efficacy gradually declined as the addition was postponed. In addition, T15 dose-dependently elevated the phosphorylation levels of TBK1 and IRF3. Collectively, T15 exhibits multi-stage antiviral activity (inhibiting viral entry and early-stage of replication), along with anti-inflammatory effects and low cytotoxicity, positioning it as a promising lead candidate for anti-SARS-CoV-2 drug development. However, its detailed signaling pathway requires further elucidation.

title: COVID-19 Mortality and Vaccination Coverage Among Older Adults in Tunisia, 2020–2022: A National Descriptive and Ecological Study
abstract: Background: Older adults experienced a disproportionate burden of COVID-19 mortality, but national evidence is limited. We described COVID-19 mortality among adults aged ≥65 years (March 2020–December 2022) and vaccination coverage among adults aged ≥60 years (March 2021–December 2022). Methods: We conducted a retrospective national descriptive and ecological study using ONMNE mortality surveillance and aggregated EVAX vaccination data. We calculated mortality, age-standardized, and proportional mortality rates; vaccination coverage; dropout proportions; and no-show rates. Results: Of 29,306 COVID-19 deaths, 20,467 (69.8%) occurred among adults aged ≥65 years; 8,725 (42.6%) were aged ≥80 years and 11,463 (56.0%) were male. Cumulative mortality was 1,809.9 per 100,000, with the highest period-specific rate during Delta predominance (750.1 per 100,000). Coverage among adults aged ≥60 years was 95.4% for at least one dose, 88.3% for primary-schedule completion, and 38.4% for a third dose; cumulative uptake was 215.1 doses per 100. Coverage varied by governorate; no-show rates increased in 2022. Conclusions: Mortality was concentrated among the oldest-old and during Delta predominance. Coverage was high nationally but uneven geographically, and booster uptake and attendance declined. Targeted outreach and equitable access remain priorities.

title: Nanobodies targeting the conserved post-fusion six-helix bundle core provide protective effects against SARS-CoV-2 infection and immunopathology.
abstract: The post-fusion six-helix bundle (6-HB) of the SARS-CoV-2 spike protein is an evolutionarily constrained structural machinery essential for viral and host membrane fusion, representing a critical vulnerability for antiviral development. While peptide-based fusion inhibitors have been extensively explored, the application of nanobodies, which offer superior stability and the unique capacity to penetrate sterically restricted or cryptic epitopes, remains largely untapped for targeting this conserved fusion core. In this study, we utilized yeast surface display to engineer and isolate high-affinity nanobodies specifically directed against the post-fusion 6-HB. Two lead candidates, ML01 and ML13, exhibited nanomolar to low-micromolar binding affinities and distinct paratope specificity, as confirmed by biophysical characterization and epitope mapping. Functional evaluation demonstrated that these nanobodies exert potent neutralization of pseudotyped and authentic SARS-CoV-2 variants in vitro. Crucially, in vivo validation using a K18-hACE2 neonatal mouse model revealed that ML01 and ML13 administration significantly attenuated pulmonary transcription- and replication-competent virus-like particle (trVLP) entry, suppressed the induction of hyper-inflammatory cytokines (including TNF-α, IL-1β, IL-6, IFN-γ, and CXCL1), and mitigated severe histopathological lung injury. These findings provide a proof-of-concept that the post-fusion 6-HB is a promising target for nanobody-based therapeutic development. ML01 and ML13 emerge as resilient therapeutic candidates capable of providing a potential defense against the evolving SARS-CoV-2 landscape. Whether these nanobodies can cross-react with other coronaviruses remains to be determined.

title: Covid-19 second dose vaccine uptake and associated factors: A community-based cross-sectional study among adults in Masindi district in Uganda
abstract: While Uganda has achieved relatively high COVID-19 first dose vaccination rates, completion of the second dose remains low, particularly in Masindi district where only 44.0% of adults who were vaccinated with the first dose proceeded to receive the second dose. This shortfall threatens to undermine the achievement of herd immunity and the effectiveness of the nation’s COVID-19 vaccination campaign. This study aimed to determine the rate of second dose vaccine uptake and assess factors associated with second dose uptake among adults in Masindi district. We conducted a community-based cross-sectional study using multi-stage random sampling approach to select 637 study respondents. Data were collected using a pre-tested interviewer-administered structured questionnaire and analyzed using SPSS v26. Modified Poisson regression was used to identify independent predictors of second dose uptake. Results were reported using adjusted prevalence ratios (APRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs), with statistical significance set at p<0.05. Among adults who had received at least one dose of a COVID-19 vaccine, 44.0% had completed the two-dose vaccination schedule. Independent factors significantly associated with higher second dose uptake included high economic status (APR = 2.2, 95% CI: 1.16-3.07), urban residence (APR = 1.3, 95% CI: 1.13-1.62), high perceived risk of COVID-19 (APR = 2.0, 95% CI: 1.59-2.55), chronic illness (APR 1.9; 95% CI: 1.60-2.33), living less than 1 km from a vaccination site (APR = 2.0, 95% CI: 1.49-3.01), Shorter waiting times; under 30 minutes (APR = 1.7, 95% CI: 1.41-2.08), community/religious leaders’ support (APR = 1.7, 95% CI: 1.41-2.16), Community outreach programs (APR = 2.5, 95% CI: 1.99-3.36), and Exposure to vaccination information through radio or TV (APR = 1.5, 95% CI: 1.25–1.88). Vaccine shortages (APR = 0.4, 95% CI: 0.31-0.55), and experiencing of adverse side effects after the first dose (APR = 0.8, 95% CI: 0.71-0.97) were associated with reduced prevalence of receiving a second dose. The findings suggest that COVID-19 vaccine second dose uptake in Masindi district remains low and is associated with interconnected socioeconomic, individual, health system, and community-level factors. Interventions should consider improving access, risk communication, and engagement of community structures are needed to boost vaccine completion rates.

title: Study on the clinical outcomes of COVID-19 infection and immune responses following the third booster dose of inactivated COVID-19 vaccine in hematologic disease patients
abstract: Background Patients with hematologic diseases may have impaired immunity owing to their underlying diseases and immunosuppressive treatments. title: COVID-19-Related Disruptions and Adaptations to HIV Service Delivery in Rakai, Uganda: A Qualitative Study Among Virologically Unsuppressed People Living With HIV and HIV Care Providers.
abstract: Abstract COVID-19 pandemic restrictions disrupted HIV services globally, but few studies have explored experiences from rural Africa or experiences of virologically unsuppressed individuals who may experience heightened barriers to care. We sought to explore COVID-19-related disruptions and adaptations to HIV service delivery in rural Rakai, Uganda. We conducted qualitative, in-depth interviews with 38 people living with HIV, all with high-level viremia (≥1,000 copies/ml), and 15 HIV clinicians. We also conducted six focus group discussions with peer health workers. Findings were analyzed thematically using a team-based inductive and deductive approach. Participants described the disruptive impact of COVID-19, precipitating transportation barriers and constraints to facility access, human resource gaps, and anticipated and enacted stigma. HIV services adapted, however, through approaches such as multimonth antiretroviral treatment dispensing, intensified community-based antiretroviral treatment delivery, flexibility in working hours, and changes in service access locations. Findings can inform HIV service delivery responses to future public health emergencies.
journal: Journal of the Association of Nurses in AIDS Care

title: Cross-reactive T cell immunity against novel coronaviruses with pandemic potential, predictable from spike sequence conservation.
abstract: Widespread SARS-CoV-2 infection and vaccination have reshaped global immunity to coronaviruses. Whether this immunity extends to animal sarbecoviruses with spillover potential remains unknown. We assessed cross-reactive memory T-cell responses to spike proteins from five relevant human angiotensin-converting enzyme 2 (hACE2)-dependent sarbecoviruses and MERS-CoV in healthcare workers in the UK and Vietnam. Limited SARS-CoV-2 specific or cross-reactive responses were seen in pre-pandemic samples. However, in samples collected from vaccinated donors at 3-24 months after booster vaccination, cross-reactive T-cell responses across the hACE2-dependent sarbecoviruses were detected. There was a strong correlation between the magnitude of responses and the level of viral sequence identity. This relationship was reproduced across cohorts in the UK and Vietnam. These findings indicate that post-pandemic populations possess measurable cellular immunity to genetically related sarbecoviruses and suggest that the degree of T-cell cross-recognition can be predicted from the spike protein sequence conservation. Such data provide an immunological framework for assessing vulnerability to future sarbecovirus spillover.

title: Early Risk Stratification of COVID-19 Associated Cytokine Storm Using a Four-Cytokine Cumulative Score: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
abstract: Cytokine storm (CS) is a major immunopathological driver of severe illness and death in COVID-19, yet practical tools for its early identification remain limited. This study aimed to identify early predictive biomarkers, characterize their lead times and develop a cumulative cytokine score for early risk stratification of COVID-19-associated CS. In this single-center retrospective cohort study, 295 hospitalized patients with COVID-19 were included. Admission cytokines and inflammatory markers were analyzed. Cox proportional hazards models were used to identify predictors of CS and in-hospital mortality. Receiver operating characteristic analysis was performed to determine optimal cut-offs, and the interval between biomarker elevation above the cut-off and CS onset was defined as the early warning interval. A four-cytokine cumulative score (0-4 points; IL-6, IL-8, IL-10, TNF-α) was constructed. Internal validation was performed using 2,000 bootstrap resamples. Cytokines increased approximately 4-5 days prior to CS onset, earlier than CRP and d-dimer. In the multivariable model integrating clinical variables, a cumulative cytokine score of 3-4 was independently associated with increased CS risk (HR = 4.078, 95% CI: 1.180-14.101, p = 0.026) and higher in-hospital mortality (HR = 22.026, 95% CI: 2.569-188.846, p = 0.005). The score demonstrated good discriminative performance for CS prediction (AUC = 0.795). A cumulative cytokine score integrating multiple inflammatory pathways may offer a theoretical basis for the early auxiliary diagnosis and risk stratification of COVID-19-associated CS.

title: Interpersonal Stressors and Adolescent Mental Health During COVID-19: Investigating the Role of Loneliness.
abstract: Abstract The COVID-19 pandemic created social disruptions, leading to high levels of mental health problems for adolescents. Interpersonal stressors, such as lack of familial support, peer victimization, and discrimination, may have further exacerbated teen mental health issues. Yet, the psychological impact of interpersonal stressors and their interactive effects with high levels of loneliness remains unknown. In this pre-registered study , conducted in November and December 2020 (approximately eight months into the COVID-19 pandemic), we used a diverse sample of adolescents from across 43 U.S. states with elevated depressive symptoms (n = 2,452, ages 13–16) to examine how familial support, peer victimization, and discrimination are concurrently associated with mental health outcomes. Results indicated that perceived discrimination was the strongest standardized correlate across continuous internalizing outcomes (depressive symptoms, anxiety symptoms, and hopelessness), whereas lack of familial support was the primary correlate of suicidal ideation; if youth reported a lack of familial support, they were over three times as likely to report suicidal ideation. Loneliness significantly moderated the cross-sectional links between lack of familial support and depressive symptoms, as well as perceived discrimination and hopelessness. Simple slope probing demonstrated a distress ceiling effect: interpersonal stressors were most strongly associated with elevated distress among youth reporting low baseline loneliness, whereas youth experiencing high loneliness exhibited consistently elevated distress regardless of stressor exposure. These findings underscore interpersonal stressors and loneliness as high-priority targets for youth prevention and intervention programs, particularly during periods of widespread social disruption.
