title: Exploring "equigenesis" in the association between the natural outdoor environment, mental health and death by suicide before and during the COVID-19 pandemic: a population-based cohort study of more than 2 million records in Northern Ireland.
abstract: Recent evidence suggests that the natural outdoor environment (NOE) may mitigate socioeconomic inequalities in mental health, but it remains unclear how such associations vary between the pandemic and the non-pandemic period. Therefore, this study focused on the association between NOE and inequalities in mental health before and during the pandemic. We used a population-based cohort of individuals in Northern Ireland (NI), including more than 2 million General Practice participants from 2017 to 2022. NOE was assessed using the proportion of blue space and green space within the administrative neighbourhoods, respectively. Mental health outcomes included death by suicide, mental health-related hospital admissions and prescriptions. We applied multilevel Cox proportional hazards and logistic regressions. Further, we stratified the analysis by area-level deprivation index. The analyses were performed for the pre-pandemic (2017-2019) and during the pandemic (2020-2022), respectively. However, there is no evidence that NOE is related to a lower risk of having a mental health-related hospital admission (e.g., pre-pandemic: OR=1.053, 95% CI=0.794-1.396; intra-pandemic: OR=1.044, 95% CI=0.778-1.401). The association between NOE and mental health-related hospital admissions, as well as the association between NOE and prescriptions, was more pronounced in socioeconomically disadvantaged neighbourhoods, especially during the pandemic. However, such "equigenesis" was only observed for death by suicide before the pandemic. Therefore, NOE may mitigate socioeconomic inequalities in mental health, especially during the pandemic. Our findings demonstrate the importance of sufficient NOE to support better and more equal mental health and preparedness for future pandemics.

title: Regional Synchrony of COVID-19 Peaks and Mycoplasma Pneumoniae-Attributed Mortality Troughs and Rebounds in Children Aged 0–19 Years: a Systematic Analysis of the Global Burden of Disease Study 2023 in 204 Countries and Territories
abstract: Background: Mycoplasma pneumoniae, a leading cause of paediatric community-acquired pneumonia, nearly disappeared under COVID-19 non-pharmaceutical interventions and re-emerged with a delay relative to other respiratory pathogens. Whether its timing tracks national and regional COVID-19 waves has not been quantified globally. Methods: From the Global Burden of Disease Study 2023 Results Tool we extracted, for 204 countries and seven GBD super-regions, deaths and disability-adjusted life years (DALYs) at ages 0–19 years from lower respiratory infections attributable to Mycoplasma pneumoniae (2019–2023) and deaths and incident cases of COVID-19 (2020–2023; 2019 set to zero by definition). For each geography we located the COVID-19 peak year, the Mycoplasma trough (minimum 2020–2023) and the post-trough rebound maximum, computed the peak-to-peak interval, and tested Spearman correlations between COVID-19 peak intensity and trough depth or rebound amplitude, with lagged z-score cross-correlations and alternative COVID-19 calibres (all-ages deaths; 0–19-year incidence) as sensitivity analyses. Results: Globally, Mycoplasma-attributed deaths at ages 0–19 years fell from 27,388 in 2019 to a trough of 22,711 in 2021 (−17.1%) and partially recovered to 26,366 in 2023 (−3.7% versus 2019), while paediatric COVID-19 deaths peaked at 147,850 in 2021. The modal interval from the COVID-19 peak to the Mycoplasma rebound peak was +2 years in five of seven super-regions and in 115 of 204 countries (56%; median 2 years). COVID-19 peak intensity showed no significant correlation with trough depth or rebound amplitude (|r| ≤ 0.21; p ≥ 0.09). Because rebound maxima fell in 2023—the final data year—in six of seven super-regions, the +2-year interval is partly a right-censoring artefact. The pattern strengthened under all-ages COVID-19 mortality (64% of countries at +2 years), shifted to +1 year under 0–19-year incidence, and was unchanged under the DALY calibre. Conclusions: Paediatric Mycoplasma-attributed mortality troughs followed COVID-19 mortality peaks with a modal two-year lag, consistent with suppression and delayed re-emergence under pandemic interventions, but with no detectable intensity gradient. The timing signal is robust to all-ages mortality calibration, calibre-dependent for incidence, and bounded by right-censoring at 2023; continued surveillance is required to observe complete rebound cycles.

title: A Tailored Sequencing Approach for Identifying SARS-CoV-2 Variants in Challenging Samples from Mink
abstract: High-throughput sequencing (HTS) is an essential tool for genomic surveillance of infectious agents, including SARS-CoV-2 in farmed mink. However, sample quality varies, hindering high-quality sequencing results. In this study, six mink-origin SARS-CoV-2-positive samples were sequenced using two hybrid-capture methods (commercial and custom) and a shotgun metagenomic approach. All methods consistently identified SARS-CoV-2 variants. The metagenomic approach yielded the lowest mapping rate (up to 0.35%), breadth of coverage (97–100%), depth of coverage (9–932×), and mean mapq (30–59), and one sequence did not meet the quality criteria. In contrast, both hybrid-capture methods achieved higher mapping rates (47–99%), breadth of coverage (99.9–100%), and depth of coverage (508–115,846×). The custom hybrid-capture approach was selected because of its superior coverage uniformity, the lowest number of ambiguous bases (N), adjustability to low RNA levels and degraded material, and streamlined laboratory workflow. To further evaluate its applicability, it was applied to 35 clinical samples collected as part of routine genomic surveillance. This method generated sequencing data with high mapping rates (median 95%), depth of coverage (median 13,238×), breadth of coverage (median 100%), and mean mapq (median 60). These findings demonstrate that the custom hybrid-capture approach is a useful tool for genomic surveillance of SARS-CoV-2 in mink-origin samples.

title: Revised estimates of types and duration of long COVID symptoms based on claims records from 245 million US patients.
abstract: COVID-19 has been reported to cause multisystem effects lasting years [Z. Topol, Science 383, 830-832 (2024)]. These findings are primarily based on cohort studies comparing test-positive COVID-19 patients to controls without known COVID-19 infection, tested or untested [M. 30, 1564-1573 (2024)]. However, such comparisons can be biased by the reasons people were tested. Using 14.4 billion insurance claims from 244.7 million US patients, we find that most long-term effects attributed to COVID-19 by unrestricted control designs likely reflect bias due to selective testing of individuals with non-COVID conditions, causing long-term effects of those conditions to be misattributed to COVID-19. We removed this bias by analyzing only tested individuals, comparing test-positive to test-negative patients. Across 614 clinical outcomes followed over 2 y, the test-based design resulted in 83.5% fewer symptoms being attributable to COVID-19 between 30 to 119 d after infection (43 attributable symptoms vs. 262 for the unrestricted control design), a 98.2% reduction at 120 to 359 d (5 vs. 286), and a 100% reduction at 360 to 719 d (0 vs. The unrestricted control design also attributed unrelated outcomes (e.g., firearm injuries) to COVID-19 at a high rate, whereas the testing-based design did not. The test-based control design may modestly underestimate some effects. This study does not indicate that symptoms beyond one year are not genuine but that their attributability to COVID-19 is uncertain.

title: Family-Related Language in Bullying Discourse on Reddit before and after the COVID-19 Pandemic: An Analysis of Online Narratives.
abstract: This study aims to analyze how family-related language in online bullying discourse changed from before to after the COVID-19 pandemic. We assess the semantic similarity of familial terms (such as "parent," "child," "sister," and "brother") to the word "bullying," and the emotions expressed in sentences containing these terms, before and after the pandemic. We obtained 8,720 posts on subreddit r/Bullying between January 1, 2015, and December 31, 2022. Using a word embedding technique, we extracted keywords similar to "bullying" each period and compared them with a focus on familial terms, and we classified the emotions of family-mentioning sentences using a pretrained classifier. We identified four keywords ("child," "niece," "sister," and "parent") that were semantically similar to "bullying" before the onset of the COVID-19 pandemic. After the pandemic, a larger set of family terms (son, sister, brother, child, cousin, daughter, and parents) appeared among these keywords, although only some of them were retrieved consistently across repeated model estimations with different random seeds. Emotion differences were smaller and less consistent, with only three terms showing changes that survived correction for multiple comparisons. Because co-occurrence of family terms with bullying language cannot separate posts describing bullying by a family member from posts in which family members appear as supporters or advice-seekers, we treat these results as evidence about family-related language within bullying discourse rather than about the incidence of family bullying. The findings are consistent with, but do not distinguish between, a change in family dynamics during the pandemic and an increased willingness to disclose family experiences online. They suggest that platforms hosting anti-bullying discussion may benefit from surfacing family violence resources when family terms co-occur with bullying language.

title: SARS-CoV-2 Evolution in Critically Ill Patients with Prolonged Infections Requiring Intubation or ECMO
abstract: The outbreak of SARS-CoV-2 in December 2019 and the ensuing global pandemic raised critical questions about the virus's capacity for rapid adaptation to environmental conditions. In this study, we investigated viral evolution in critically ill patients suffering from severe lung failure. From November 2020 to December 2022, respiratory samples were collected from a total of 41 patients upon admission to the intensive care unit at the University Hospital Regensburg, Germany, and during the course of treatment (median interval: 15 days; range: 6 to 42 days). The samples were analyzed for genomic alterations using next-generation sequencing. Detected changes were correlated with clinical, virological, immunological, and therapeutic parameters using both univariate and multivariate logistic regression analysis. Seventeen of 41 patients (41%) developed amino acid substitutions in non-structural proteins (nsp) 2, 3, 4, 10, 14, and 15, as well as in open reading frames 3a and 8, and within the spike and nucleocapsid proteins over the course of the study. Notably, 20 of 27 observed changes represented reversions to the Wuhan-1 wild-type genome, including eight at position 323 of the polymerase nsp12. Statistically significant factors associated with the occurrence of mutations included younger age, prolonged stay in the intensive care unit, ECMO and catecholamine treatment, development of thrombosis, extended virus replication period, and infection with the Delta variant (p<0.05). In contrast, treatment with remdesivir was negatively correlated with the emergence of mutations. Epitope mapping revealed that the humoral immune response was unlikely to be the main driver of viral evolution in vivo. Thus, the likelihood of genomic alterations in severely ill patients increases with both disease severity and duration of virus replication. The frequent observation of reversions to the wildtype genome suggests that the virus preferentially replicates in inflamed and poorly ventilated areas of the lungs – an effect that may be further amplified by the presence of pulmonary embolism. Furthermore, replication appears to be suppressed by the administration of remdesivir. These findings highlight that integrating antiviral strategies into the clinical management of severely ill patients may limit the emergence of potentially novel mutations.

title: Significant hypercapnia as an initial manifestation of COVID-19 without typical symptoms in chronic cervical spinal cord injury: A case series.
abstract: Context Few reports have described how Coronavirus Disease 2019 (COVID-19) presents in patients with long-standing high cervical spinal cord injury (SCI). This case series suggests that clinically significant hypercapnia may be an early manifestation of COVID-19 in this population, even without classic respiratory symptoms or marked oxygen desaturation, potentially delaying recognition of ventilatory failure. Findings We describe two men with chronic C4 ASIA Impairment Scale (AIS) A. Case 1: A 76-year-old vaccinated man developed drowsiness, confusion, and headache without cough or fever. Room-air oxygen saturation was 90-95%, and inflammatory markers did not clearly indicate infection. Arterial blood gas (ABG) showed new-onset, clinically significant hypercapnia (pH 7.306, PaCO2 62.4 mmHg, PaO2 77.3 mmHg). He required endotracheal intubation and intensive care unit (ICU) care; COVID-19 was subsequently confirmed and remdesivir was administered. Tracheostomy was later performed after unsuccessful ventilator weaning. Case 2: A 70-year-old unvaccinated man reported chest discomfort without cough or fever, then developed confusion. Room-air oxygen saturation remained 94-95%. ABG showed respiratory acidosis with new-onset, clinically significant hypercapnia (pH 7.304, PaCO2 59.4 mmHg, PaO2 76.7 mmHg). He also required intubation, mechanical ventilation, ICU care, and tracheostomy after COVID-19 was confirmed; he was treated with remdesivir and corticosteroids. Conclusion/clinical relevance These cases suggest that hypercapnia may be an early and potentially critical manifestation of COVID-19 in chronic high cervical SCI, without typical respiratory symptoms or marked hypoxemia. Clinicians should assess CO2 retention in this vulnerable population to avoid delayed diagnosis and deterioration.

title: Power, Ideology, and Institutional Betrayal: The Intensive Care Unit Experiences of Bereaved Families during COVID-19.
abstract: In this qualitative study conducted in Israel, the authors explored the experiences of family members (N = 19) who lost a loved one to COVID-19 following hospitalization in intensive care units (ICUs). In particular, the authors examined how bereaved individuals perceived their interactions with ICU staff, institutional policies, and power dynamics within healthcare settings. Semistructured interviews with the 19 participants revealed recurring themes of struggle, perceived injustice in medical decision making, enforced patient isolation, and a resulting erosion of trust in the healthcare system. These experiences shaped not only the bereavement process but also participants' perceptions of fairness, care, and institutional responsibility, often culminating in a sense of institutional betrayal. Alongside these challenges, some participants described moments of compassionate care and meaningful communication. The authors argue that these findings underscore the importance of transparent communication, psychosocial support, and trauma-informed care in ICU settings, particularly during times of crisis.

title: Prevalence of burnout in physiotherapists during the COVID-19 pandemic: systematic review and meta-analysis
abstract: This study aimed to obtain a pooled estimate of the prevalence of burnout in physiotherapists during the COVID-19 pandemic and to explore differences between low- and middle-income countries (LMICs) and high-income countries (HICs). A systematic search was conducted on six databases, from December 2019 to June 2026. Two reviewers independently extracted data from the included studies and assessed the risk of bias using a modified version of the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale. The pooled prevalence was calculated through meta-analysis of proportions with 95% confidence interval (CI). Prevalence of overall burnout and of its three dimensions of emotional exhaustion (EE), depersonalization (DP), and reduced personal accomplishment (PA) was estimated. A total of 23 studies was included and 19 was used for meta-analyses. Pooled prevalence (95% CI) estimate of 18% (9–35), higher than usually observed pre-COVID. The pooled prevalence of the three MBI components was: EE, 46% (35–57); DP, 46% (21–73), and low PA, 34% (13–64), and tended to be higher in LMICs, although the difference between LMICs and HICs were statistically significant only for EE. The findings indicate a substantial prevalence of burnout among physiotherapists during the COVID-19 pandemic. However, substantial heterogeneity and differences in burnout definitions across studies should be considered when interpreting these estimates. To prevent burnout, special attention should be given to healthcare professionals’ wellbeing during exceptional events such as the COVID-19 pandemic. Systematic review registration PROSPERO , CRD420251029422.

title: Hand sanitizer recalls during the COVID-19 pandemic: a descriptive analysis of regulatory records from Canada, Nepal, Singapore and the USA
abstract: Background: Alcohol-based hand sanitizers were central to infection prevention during the COVID-19 pandemic. The abrupt rise in global demand fueled the emergence of substandard and unregulated products. Government regulatory bodies around the globe responded to this issue by tightening quality control and enforcing stringent limits on contaminants. This study aimed to descriptively analyze the reasons for, and timing of hand sanitizer recalls and safety warnings between 2020 and 2024. Methodology: We extracted publicly available records from the national regulators of Canada, Nepal, Singapore, and the USA. The database was analyzed by country, year, and reason for recall to identify the recall patterns and regulatory practices. Results: We identified 1044 recalled products in Canada (277), Nepal (39), Singapore (26), and the USA (702). Major reasons for recall were administrative reasons such as non-compliance, nonresponse to the regulator, and unregistered or unauthorized sale (43.9%) followed by contamination with hazardous chemicals such as methanol, acetaldehyde, and benzene (37.4%) and subpotent ethanol or isopropanol (15.6%). Two-thirds of the recall records were from the USA followed by Canada, Nepal, and Singapore. While most of the recalls were announced during the first year of COVID-19, the recalls did not follow a temporal trend. Conclusion: The recall records showcased product hazard risks during the pandemic, highlighting its global impacts. The recalls in each of the four countries may have missed other substandard hand sanitizer products. This underlines the importance of strict monitoring and public awareness for product safety. The recall records discussed in this paper describe regulatory activity and should not be read as the prevalence of substandard hand sanitizers. Robust emergency regulatory frameworks, rapid analytical verification, and distributed yet strictly monitored certified production systems may help reduce public health risks due to hand sanitizers in the future.

Two-thirds of the recall records were from the USA followed by Canada, Nepal, and Singapore. While most of the recalls were announced during the first year of COVID-19, the recalls did not follow a temporal trend. Conclusion The recall records showcased product hazard risks during the pandemic, highlighting its global impacts. The recalls in each of the four countries may have missed other substandard hand sanitizer products. This underlines the importance of strict monitoring and public awareness for product safety. The recall records discussed in this paper describe regulatory activity and should not be read as the prevalence of substandard hand sanitizers. Robust emergency regulatory frameworks, rapid analytical verification, and distributed yet strictly monitored certified production systems may help reduce public health risks due to hand sanitizers in the future.

title: Clinical case analysis of orbital inflammatory pseudotumor with COVID-19 infection
abstract: Abstract Objective To compare the proportion of orbital inflammatory pseudotumor (OIP) among orbital disease cases during the peak of the COVID-19 Omicron wave (December 2022–January 2023) with the corresponding periods of the preceding three years, and to characterize the clinical features of OIP in patients with recent COVID-19 infection. Methods 62 patients diagnosed with orbital diseases from December 2022 to January 2023 were enrolled as the study group. The control group comprised OIP patients from the same months in the previous 3 years. Comparative statistical analysis and descriptive analysis were used to explore the clinical features of OIP. Results The study group had 13 cases (20.97%) of OIP, significantly higher than that of the control group ( P < 0.05). Six cases occurred in the right eye, and seven cases in the left eye, with eight males and five females, aged 16–65. All cases had acute onset clinical features including eyelid swelling (61.54%), conjunctival hyperemia and chemosis (61.54%), ocular motility disorders (53.85%), eye pain (46.15%), diplopia (46.15%), proptosis (23.08%), ptosis (15.38%), and decreased vision (7.69%). OIP was confirmed through ocular ultrasound, orbital CT, and MRI scans. Glucocorticoid therapy resulted in excellent treatment outcomes. Conclusions The proportion of OIP among orbital disease cases presenting to our hospital increased significantly from December 2022 to January 2023 compared with the corresponding periods of the preceding three years, featured with a single-eye onset, no significant difference between the eyes, a slightly higher incidence rate in males than females, and middle-aged prevalence. Patients had acute onset symptoms including eyelid swelling, conjunctival hyperemia and chemosis, ocular motility disorders and eye pain. Glucocorticoid therapy was effective. Considering the study group was relatively small, it requires further research to provide more reliable evidence.

title: Adverse Birth Outcomes Associated With SARS-CoV-2 Infection Among Pregnant Women With and Without HIV: A Longitudinal Cohort Study.
abstract: Background COVID-19 and HIV infection are independently associated with increased risk of adverse pregnancy outcomes. However, there is limited evidence on the effect of SARS-CoV-2 infection during pregnancy in sub-Saharan Africa, particularly among women living with HIV (WLWH). Setting Two antenatal clinics in southern Malawi (2018-2022). Methods We conducted a prospective cohort study of singleton pregnancies enrolled at 20-36 weeks gestation. SARS-CoV-2 infection was determined through serologic testing at enrollment and delivery. Participants were enrolled based on HIV status and viral suppression: (1) WLWH with detectable viral load (VL), (2) WLWH with undetectable VL, and (3) HIV-negative women. We used a multivariable logistic regression with adjustment for confounding to evaluate the effect of SARS-CoV-2 alone or in combination with HIV infection on the following adverse birth outcomes: low birth weight (LBW), preterm birth, small-for-gestational-age (SGA), and stillbirth or early neonatal death. Results Among 905 pregnant women, 29% tested positive for SARS-CoV-2, 87% of infections were mild or asymptomatic. Overall, SARS-CoV-2 infection was significantly associated with SGA births (adjusted OR [aOR]: 1.49, 95% CI: 1.03 to 2.13) but not associated with other adverse outcomes. Among WLWH, SARS-CoV-2 was significantly associated with increased odds of LBW (aOR: 2.07, 1.10 to 3.91) and SGA births (aOR: 1.73, 1.01 to 2.91). The effect of SARS-CoV-2 infection among WLWH did not differ based on VL. Conclusions SARS-CoV-2 infection during pregnancy was associated with adverse birth outcomes, particularly among WLWH. These findings underscore the need for integrated antenatal care and targeted infection prevention strategies for pregnant women with HIV in high-burden settings.

title: Using iterative agentic retrieval-augmented generation to refine the risk of infection from social contexts during the COVID-19 pandemic: Development and Evaluation Study
abstract: Background: Contact tracing is crucial to limit pathogen transmission and to gather epidemiological data. However, despite machine learning optimizations, it remains time-consuming. Large language models have been used for infection risk prediction, but no existing application converses with a user to adapt its risk estimates. Objective: We aimed to develop an iterative retrieval-augmented generation conversational framework to predict coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) infection risk from textual social data. The conversational agent aims to gather personalized risk factors based on descriptions of social interactions. Methods: We trained a long short-term memory (LSTM) model to predict the risk of COVID-19 infection from 19,434 textual descriptions of social interactions, collected during the pandemic in the Leuven student community, in Belgium. We integrated this model into a Llama3.3-based conversational framework that iteratively gathers additional social information that may represent a risk of infection. We evaluated the framework using large language model (LLM)-as-a-judge metrics and by comparing its risk assessment in different social contexts. Results: Based solely on social interaction data, a fine-tuned RobBERT model predicted infection risk with an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (ROC AUC) of 0.73. It performed similarly to an LSTM model and a logistic regression on term frequency-inverse document frequency (TF-IDF) features, which both achieved a ROC AUC of 0.72. These three models slightly outperformed a Quantized Low-Rank Adaptation (QLoRA)-fine-tuned Mistral NeMo model (ROC AUC = 0.69). Llama3.3 performed well in our framework: the predicted infection risk converged often, and it asked fewer redundant questions than the smaller models (Mistral 7B, Gemma3 12B). In addition, the framework showed the ability to stratify, by risk of infection, synthetic users who had different types of social interactions. Conclusions: Combining simple language models with large language models can refine individual infection risk from contact tracing data in a high-circulation context. Our conversational framework may help optimize contact tracing by highlighting social contexts with a high risk of infection.

title: Biopsychosocial versus purely biological explanation for persistent physical symptoms following COVID-19: An experimental study with lay participants and healthcare professionals.
abstract: This study aims to compare changes of attitudes regarding the causation, evolution, and treatment for persistent physical symptoms following COVID-19 after lay participants and healthcare professionals receive medical explanations presenting either a purely biological or a biopsychosocial account of symptoms. Participants completed an online questionnaire assessing their views on underlying physical and mental causation, chronicity, disability and annoyance of symptoms, required examinations, and appropriate treatments. Lay participants rated their feelings of offence and anxiety associated with symptoms, while healthcare professionals their feelings of competence and willingness to care for a patient with persistent physical symptoms following COVID-19. All participants were allocated alternatingly to watch a standardized video with distinct accounts: either purely biological or biopsychosocial. -tests were used to compare representations after explanations. A total of 208 lay participants (mean age: 42; 74% women) and 104 healthcare professionals (mean age: 42; 68% women) were included. The two explanations were efficient in changing beliefs about mental and physical causation of persistent physical symptoms following COVID-19 in both participants' groups. Compared to the purely biological explanation, the biopsychosocial explanation increased feelings of offence while at the same time decreasing lay participants' views that symptoms are chronic and disabling and increasing views that symptoms can be improved with CBT and physical exercise therapy. In healthcare professionals, the biopsychosocial explanation increased feelings of competence and belief that symptoms can be improved with CBT. A standardized biopsychosocial video explanation may help promoting integrative care. Results suggest that explaining the biopsychosocial approach can modulate healthcare professionals' and lay people's attitudes towards persistent physical symptoms following COVID-19. Future research should investigate how explaining the biopsychosocial approach can be further improved to promote more sustained changes in attitudes over time.

title: The relationship between the oral health status and COVID-19 and Influenza infections
abstract: Abstract A relationship has been reported between oral hygiene and influenza infection. Coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) and influenza are major respiratory virus infections. The oral cavity may act as both an entry site and reservoir for these viruses. The present study examined the role of oral health in SARS-CoV-2 infection through epidemiology and histopathology. A prospective observational study was also conducted to investigate whether good oral hygiene habits contribute to the prevention of respiratory viral infections. In the epidemiological study using data from health/dental check-ups and the Japanese National Health Insurance database, a multivariate analysis identified poor oral hygiene as an independent risk factor for the onset of COVID-19. A histopathological analysis revealed that the expression of the angiotensin-converting enzyme 2 (ACE2) receptor and furin in the gingival epithelium was higher with than without inflammation. The prospective observational study comparing two groups with different oral hygiene habits suggested that good oral hygiene practices with interdental brushes and mouthwash prevented the onset of COVID-19 and influenza. Collectively, these results indicate that poor oral hygiene contributes to the onset of COVID-19 infection by increasing ACE2 and furin expression. Furthermore, improvements in oral hygiene may prevent the onset of COVID-19 and influenza.

title: Disparities in type 2 diabetes incidence trends during the COVID-19 pandemic in Sweden: a register-based population study.
abstract: Background The COVID-19 pandemic profoundly affected health care provision for chronic diseases, including type 2 diabetes. However, its effects on type 2 diabetes incidence remain poorly understood, particularly how they differ between population groups, which has not yet been examined in a Swedish context. We aimed to investigate trends in type 2 diabetes incidence in Sweden from 2016 to 2022, and to explore whether potential changes in type 2 diabetes incidence associated with the COVID-19 pandemic varied by sex, age, or migration status. Methods Quarterly incidence rates of new-onset type 2 diabetes were calculated from individual-level register data for a dynamic population consisting of all adults (age ≥ 18 years) in Sweden during 2016-2019 (pre-pandemic) and 2020-2022 (pandemic). Incidence rate ratios (IRRs) for each pandemic year were modelled in multivariable Poisson regression analysis using the pre-pandemic years as reference, adjusted for age, sex, migration status, season, and long-term annual trend. Stratified and interaction analyses were performed based on age, sex, and migration status. Results Overall, the incidence of type 2 diabetes showed an increasing underlying linear trend of 3.6% (IRR 1.036, 95% CI 1.028, 1.045) between 2016 and 2022. During the pandemic (2020-2022), the overall type 2 diabetes incidence decreased by 6% relative to the underlying linear trend (IRR 0.94, 95% CI 0.91, 0.97). The decrease was strongest in 2020 (IRR 0.90, 95% CI 0.87, 0.94) compared to 2021 (IRR 1.03, 95% CI 0.99, 1.06) and 2022 (IRR 0.95, 95% CI 0.91, 0.99). The decline in type 2 diabetes incidence in 2020 was most pronounced among individuals 65 years and older and in the native-born Swedish population. Conclusions During the first year of the COVID-19 pandemic in Sweden, a decline in incidence of type 2 diabetes was observed that varied in magnitude by sex, age, and migration status. This finding may reflect differential but transient changes in health-seeking behaviour during the initial phases of the pandemic. Our results underscore the challenges of maintaining continuous health care for non-communicable diseases during a major health crisis in society, highlighting the need to ensure equitable access for vulnerable groups such as older persons.

title: Impact of Covid-19 Pandemic on Nigerian Capital Market: The Imperative of Testing the Efficacy of Efficient Market Hypothesis
abstract: In this paper we reviewed the efficacy of Efficient Market Hypothesis (EMH) on the outbreak of Covid-19 on Nigerian Capital Market. The EMH is a theory based on informational efficiency by the capital markets owing to their quick and instantaneous incorporation of new information. The study tested the market in two parameters: to confirm the randomness (efficiency of the market) using run-test, and to confirm the effect of Covid-19 protocols on some economic fundamentals using regression analysis. The result of the run-test of the daily Nigerian capital market data (April, 2020 to July 2020) revealed randomness within the period under review. The regression analysis however revealed significant relationship between the markets and some economic fundamental indicators (inflation and international price of crude oil) of the economy. The paper concluded that the Nigerian Capital Markets revealed randomness signifying a weak form of EMH as news about the Corona Virus was incorporated slowly but not instantaneously during the period under review, and hence, the pandemic did affect the market. The study also posited that EMH can be tested and validated not only from economic or finance point of view but also from public health view of the outbreak of Corona Virus. The paper recommended that policy makers in the country should devise a proper hedging mechanism to be put in place to mitigate any unforeseen negative market reactions in future as a result of any health pandemic.

title: Severe Thrombocytopenia Induced by Re-Exposure to Piperacillin/Tazobactam: A Case Report in Critically Ill Patient With COVID-19.
abstract: Drug-induced thrombocytopenia is a condition where certain medications can significantly reduce the platelets in the blood. This can increase the risk of bleeding and bruising. We reported a case of a 73-year-old woman with multiple comorbidities who was admitted to the hospital with COVID-19. Upon admission, the patient received multiple antibiotics, including Piperacillin/Tazobactam. In the following days, she developed severe thrombocytopenia upon re-exposure to Piperacillin/Tazobactam. Other causes of thrombocytopenia were systematically excluded. After discontinuing the Piperacillin/Tazobactam and administering intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIG), the thrombocytopenia resolved. A Naranjo Adverse Drug Reaction Probability Scale score was calculated and indicated a probable (i.e., 6 points) adverse drug reaction. This case underscores the importance of considering Piperacillin/Tazobactam as a potential cause of severe thrombocytopenia in critically ill patients, even in the presence of confounding factors such as COVID-19. To our knowledge, this is a rarely reported presentation in a patient with a recent COVID-19 infection. Further studies are needed to clarify the relationship between COVID-19 and drug-induced thrombocytopenia.

title: Long COVID burden in healthcare workers: a 12-month survey of 771 cases
abstract: Long COVID syndrome represents a significant public health concern, with healthcare workers constituting a population at particularly high risk of SARS-CoV-2 infection and subsequent persistent symptoms. To evaluate the prevalence of Long COVID syndrome in healthcare employees of IRCCS Policlinico San Matteo Foundation over a four-year time window from the pandemic onset. An anonymous survey was conducted among healthcare workers with documented SARS-CoV-2 infection since February 2020. Long COVID syndrome was defined as persistent symptoms lasting beyond 12 weeks from the acute infection, extending to 12 months or more. The Fisher exact test and the McNemar test were used to compare prevalences between groups and over time, respectively. Unsupervised learning techniques were used for identifying patient aggregation. Among 771 respondents (response rate 41.41% of employees with previous SARS-CoV-2 infection), the overall Long COVID syndrome cumulative prevalence (participants experiencing symptoms at any time point) was 27.9% (215/771; 95% CI: 24.7–31.2%), with point prevalence decreasing over time: 26.0% (95% CI 23.0–29.0%) at 3 months, 20.0% (95% CI 17.0–23.0%) at 6 months, and 16.0% (95% CI 14.0–19.0%) at 12 months post-infection. Significant associations were found with job position ( p = 0.004), with nurses showing the highest prevalence (35.0%). Fatigue, joint and muscle pain, concentration troubles, and memory difficulties emerged as the most persistent symptoms over time. Long COVID syndrome affects more than one-quarter of healthcare workers with previous SARS-CoV-2 infection, with symptom persistence demonstrating a gradual decline over time. These findings have important implications for occupational health management and workforce planning in healthcare settings.

title: Phase-Specific Changes in Korean Adolescents' Health Behaviors and Mental Health Across COVID-19 School Closure and Reopening.
abstract: Background The COVID-19 pandemic disrupted school routines, but health changes during school reopening remain unclear. This study examined phase-specific changes in health behaviors and mental health among Korean adolescents. Methods Nationally representative Korea Youth Risk Behavior Survey data (2018-2024) were analyzed across pre-pandemic, pandemic, transition, and post-pandemic phases. Outcomes included health risk behaviors, diet and physical activity, obesity, and mental health indicators. Weighted prevalence estimates and logistic regression models were used. Results The analytic sample included 376,066 adolescents (51.8% boys). Current smoking declined from 6.4% (95% CI, 6.1-6.7) pre-pandemic to 3.8% (3.6-4.0) post-pandemic, whereas breakfast skipping increased from 34.5% (34.0-34.9) to 41.6% (41.1-42.0). Although moderate-to-vigorous physical activity exceeded its pre-pandemic level post-pandemic, obesity prevalence increased from 10.9% (10.7-11.2) to 12.2% (11.9-12.5). Suicidal ideation decreased during the pandemic but peaked at 14.0% (13.6-14.5) during transition. Implications for school health policy, practice, and equity During reopening, schools should strengthen healthy meal and physical activity programs, sustain substance-use prevention, and ensure equitable access to mental health screening and referral. Conclusions Recovery was uneven across health domains, identifying school reopening as a critical prevention window requiring sustained, phase-specific intervention.

title: Examining the academic physician workforce in the United States: work patterns, demographic characteristics, and COVID-19 effects.
abstract: Purpose Academic physicians play an essential role in training the next generation of physicians and delivering care. However, few empirical studies compare academic and nonacademic physicians. This exploratory study examined differences in demographic and training characteristics, work patterns, and COVID-19 work effects. Method Data from the Association of American Medical Colleges' 2022 National Sample Survey of Physicians were collected from May to November 2022 and analyzed. US academic physicians were classified using 2 definitions: (1) academic affiliation (faculty appointment at a medical school or affiliation with an academic health center or teaching hospital) and (2) faculty appointment at a medical school. Three domains were examined: (1) demographic and training characteristics, (2) work patterns, and (3) COVID-19 work effects. Results Among 5834 physicians, 2659 (45.6%) were academically affiliated physicians, and 2028 (34.8%) were physicians with a faculty appointment. Minimal differences in demographics and training background exist. More academically affiliated physicians were moderate telehealth users (1011 [38.0%] vs 1002 [31.6%]; P Conclusions Differences in work patterns and patient populations distinguish academic from nonacademic physicians. Findings highlight the unique contributions and practice models of academic physicians and can inform tailored strategies to support physicians' well-being, optimize care delivery, and guide workforce planning.

title: Design and Evaluation of Next-Gen Inhibitors Targeting SARS-CoV-2 3CL Protease Clinical Variants
abstract: Abstract The 3C-like protease (3CLpro), also known as main protease (Mpro), is currently the target of the commercially available drugs nirmatrelvir and simnotrelvir which are used to treat SARS-CoV-2 infections. Global sequencing efforts of clinical isolates of SARS-CoV-2 from infected patients treated with nirmatrelvir have identified several 3CLpro clinical variants that are potentially drug resistant. Two variants, E166 and S144, have been widely studied and confirmed to have drug resistance in vitro. Using the Coronavirus 3D database, we identified and characterized ten additional SARS-CoV-2 3CLpro clinical variants deemed likely to render drug resistance. Of these, we identified a new variant, V186G, as being highly drug resistant, i.e., 116-times, 44-times, and 25-times more resistant to nirmatrelvir, simnotrelvir, and the inhibitor GRL-051-22, respectively, than the wild type. The V186G variant also displayed a 23-fold decrease in dimerization affinity. Surprisingly, no changes in drug resistance or dimerization affinity were observed for the V186F or V186I variants. X-ray structures of WT, V186G, V186F, M165I, M49I, and T190I in complex with the inhibitor GRL-051-22 were determined at resolutions between 1.3 Å and 1.9 Å revealing only small structural changes associated with any of the variants, e.g., <1.5 Å in the S2 loop of the V186G variant. Structure-based design was then used to overcome SARS-CoV-2 V186G 3CLpro drug resistance, producing the compound GRL-157-23 which is 6.5-times more potent against the V186G variant compared with the wild type. Structure–activity data for six designed compounds and their interactions with the ten variants revealed an important crosstalk between the SARS-CoV-2 3CLpro S2 and S4 subsites that plays a key role in the kinetic activity and inhibition of these variants. These results demonstrate that it is possible to design and optimize drug scaffolds that target 3CLpro variants to overcome potential drug resistance.

title: BACTEREMIA IN HOSPITALIZED PATIENT WITH COVID-19: INCIDENCE AND RISK FACTORS
abstract: The aim of the study is to assess the incidence and risk factors of bacteremia in hospitalized patients with COVID-19 during different periods of the pandemic. The study included 11203 patients diagnosed with COVID-19 who were hospitalize in Minsk City Clinical Infectious diseases Hospital, from 1 June 2021 to 30 June 2023. The incidence of bacteremia and risk factors associated with its development in conditions of competing risks were assessed using Cox cause-specific regression models. Statistical analysis was performed in R 4.3.4. The study included 11203 patients, of whom 1496 patients had 2971 blood culture tests. The cumulative incidence of bacteremia was 0.86 % during the COVID-19 pandemic before the Omicron variants and 1.63 % during the period of prevalence of SARS-CoV-2 Omicron variants. The predominant etiology was K. pneumoniae (31,7 %), S. Respiratory failure – HR 3.69 [95 % CI 2.18–6.25], p < 0.01, obesity – HR 3.04 [95 % CI 1.83-5.06], p < 0.01, age – HR 1.04 [95 % CI 1.02–1.07], p < 0.01, male gender – HR 1.94 [95 % CI 1.17–3.20], p < 0.01 were associated with bacteremia incidence in pre-Omicron SARS-CoV-2. During Omicron variants, bacteremia incidence was associated with the presence of liver disease – HR 4.26 [95 % CI 2.37–7.67], p < 0.01, respiratory failure – HR 3.72 [95 % CI 2.14–6.44], p < 0.01, COPD – HR 5.11 [95 % CI 1.50–17.40], p < 0.01. Antibacterial therapy before admission was not associated with incidence of bacteremia – HR 0.86 [95 % CI 0.51–1.16], p = 0.58 pre-Omicron; HR 1.07 [95 % CI 0.52-2.18], p = 0.86 during Omicron). Incidence of bacteremia increased almost two-fold during SARS-CoV-2 Omicron predominance. Risk factors for bacteremia in the pre-Omicron period included respiratory failure, obesity, male gender, and age, while in the Omicron period, risk factors were liver disease, respiratory failure, and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease. Antibacterial treatment before admission was not associated with in-hospital bacteremia incidence.

title: Depression-Anxiety Comorbidity Across Sex During COVID-19: An Evaluation of Partial Invariance with Invariance Partial Pruning
abstract: Depression and anxiety co-occur so frequently that comorbidity is more prevalent than the occurrence of either in isolation. The conventional latent-variable perspective offers limited insight into comorbidity because its inherent causal assumptions overlook causal relations among observable symptoms that are meaningful for explaining comorbidity. At the same time, comorbidity studies based on the network perspective have largely relied on cross-sectional data, which cannot capture the dynamic nature of mental disorders, or on two-wave panel data, which does not separate between- and within-variance and biases the estimation of dynamic processes. Therefore, we present a dynamic network analysis of depression-anxiety comorbidity with the panel graphical vector autoregressive model, using invariance partial pruning to consider possible network structural differences between biological sex. Results revealed the central role of fear in predicting depressive moods and anhedonia as a possible explanation of comorbidity. Anxiety symptoms temporally preceded depression symptoms. In the contemporaneous networks, nervousness and fear were connected to depressive mood. Furthermore, worry and rumination were more associated with depression, whereas beliefs about the uncontrollability of worry and threat monitoring were more associated with anxiety. No sex difference was discovered.

title: Changing patterns of diagnostic testing in children with asthma: evidence of redistribution, overuse, and recovery after the COVID-19 pandemic.
abstract: Background Real-world implementation of diagnostic strategies in pediatric asthma remains heterogeneous, and the long-term impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on diagnostic practice patterns is incompletely understood, particularly in middle-income countries. Guideline-recommended objective testing (e.g. spirometry) is inconsistently applied in pediatric asthma worldwide, and whether the COVID-19 pandemic produced a transient disruption or a lasting restructuring of diagnostic practice across testing domains remains unclear. We aimed to characterize longitudinal trends in diagnostic testing among children with asthma, examining pre-pandemic trajectories, COVID-associated changes, and post-pandemic recovery. Methods We conducted a nationwide population-based interrupted time-series study using Colombia's mandatory healthcare registry (2015-2024). Asthma encounters were identified using ICD-10 codes (J45-J46). Diagnostic procedures were classified into nine clinically defined domains. Diagnostic intensity was calculated as tests per 100 asthma encounters. Segmented regression estimated pre-pandemic trends, immediate 2020 level changes, and post-pandemic slope modifications. Results A total of 1,954,680 asthma encounters generated 117,324 diagnostic tests. Pre-pandemic trajectories diverged across domains. Pulmonary function testing (PFT) declined before 2020 (IRR 0.80; 95% CI 0.74-0.86) but showed a significant immediate increase in 2020 (IRR 1.42; 95% CI 1.28-1.57) and sustained post-pandemic acceleration (IRR 1.17; 95% CI 1.09-1.26). Imaging and sleep studies exhibited sharp pandemic-associated declines with partial or full recovery. Cardiopulmonary testing demonstrated marked pre-pandemic expansion (IRR 1.96). Conclusions Pediatric asthma diagnostic practice underwent domain-specific restructuring rather than uniform disruption, consistent with a process of diagnostic redistribution across testing domains. Post-pandemic intensification of PFT may reflect improved adherence to objective diagnostic confirmation, whereas persistent contraction in selected domains warrants continued monitoring.

Diagnostic intensity was calculated as tests per 100 asthma encounters. Segmented regression estimated pre-pandemic trends, immediate 2020 level changes, and post-pandemic slope modifications. Results A total of 1,954,680 asthma encounters generated 117,324 diagnostic tests. Pre-pandemic trajectories diverged across domains. Pulmonary function testing (PFT) declined before 2020 (IRR 0.80; 95% CI 0.74-0.86) but showed a significant immediate increase in 2020 (IRR 1.42; 95% CI 1.28-1.57) and sustained post-pandemic acceleration (IRR 1.17; 95% CI 1.09-1.26). Imaging and sleep studies exhibited sharp pandemic-associated declines with partial or full recovery. Cardiopulmonary testing demonstrated marked pre-pandemic expansion (IRR 1.96). Conclusions Pediatric asthma diagnostic practice underwent domain-specific restructuring rather than uniform disruption, consistent with a process of diagnostic redistribution across testing domains. Post-pandemic intensification of PFT may reflect improved adherence to objective diagnostic confirmation, whereas persistent contraction in selected domains warrants continued monitoring.

title: Social Media Identity Statements and Study Burnout Among University Students: A Secondary Analysis of the Helsinki COVID-19 Survey
abstract: Abstract Background: Associations between social media and well-being depend on what is measured. A public University of Helsinki survey contains six statements about social-media identity, similarity, and trust, alongside study-burnout items. This secondary analysis examined their cross-sectional association. Methods: The Autumn 2020 public CSV contained 1,603 records. We calculated the mean of the six documented social-media statements and a nine-item study-burnout score following the source team’s OSB9 scoring syntax. Complete cases for both scores, age group, and gender formed the analysis sample (n = 1,399). We fitted ordinary least squares regression with HC3 robust standard errors, adjusting for age group and gender. Results: Mean social-media statement score was 3.29 (SD = 1.12; response range 1–7), and mean study burnout was 3.29 (SD = 1.34; item range 1–6). The social-media score had a small negative bivariate correlation with burnout (r = −0.026). In the adjusted model, a one-point higher statement score was associated with 0.074 points lower burnout (B = −0.074, HC3 95% CI −0.138 to −0.009); model R2 was 0.070. Conclusions: The observed association was small and cross-sectional. The six statements do not measure time spent, frequency of use, or problematic use, and their construct validity is not established in the public documentation. The result should therefore be interpreted as an exploratory association between a documented statement index and study burnout, not as evidence that social-media use changes student well-being.

title: Effects of Telerehabilitation on Quality of Life, Physical Capacity, and Symptom Burden Within the Post-COVID-19 Condition: Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.
abstract: Background Post-COVID-19 condition (PCC) is characterized by persistent symptoms and functional limitations that impair quality of life, and rehabilitation is an important component of its management. Because access to conventional face-to-face rehabilitation may be limited, telerehabilitation has emerged as an accessible alternative. However, the effectiveness of telerehabilitation across clinical outcomes remains uncertain, and the influence of different delivery modes is not well understood. Objective This study aimed to evaluate the effects of telerehabilitation on health-related quality of life (HRQoL), physical capacity, and symptom burden in adults with PCC, and to determine whether delivery mode (synchronous, asynchronous, or hybrid) modified these effects. Methods Seven databases (PubMed, Cochrane Library, Web of Science, Scopus, Embase, EBSCO, and PEDro) were searched for randomized controlled trials published from January 2020 through December 2025. Eligible trials enrolled adults with PCC and compared telerehabilitation with usual care or another control condition. The primary outcome was HRQoL; secondary outcomes included functional capacity assessed by the 6-minute walk test and sit-to-stand test, dyspnea, fatigue, and symptoms of anxiety and depression. Risk of bias was assessed using the Cochrane Risk of Bias 2 tool. Mean differences or standardized mean differences (SMDs) with 95% CIs were pooled using random-effects models with the Hartung-Knapp-Sidik-Jonkman adjustment. Heterogeneity was quantified using I2 and τ2, with 95% prediction intervals reported where estimable. Certainty of evidence was evaluated using the GRADE (Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation) approach. Results A total of 22 randomized controlled trials involving 2294 participants were included. Telerehabilitation was associated with significant improvements in HRQoL (SMD 1.26, 95% CI 0.07-2.45; P=.04), dyspnea (SMD 1.95, 95% CI 0.60-3.31; P=.005), and functional aerobic capacity (6-minute walk test : mean difference 77.79 meters, 95% CI 30.44-125.14; P=.001). Fatigue was also significantly reduced (SMD 0.89, 95% CI 0.16-1.62; P=.02), but no significant effects were observed for lower-limb strength (sit-to-stand test: SMD 0.55, 95% CI -0.15 to 1.25; P=.12) or symptoms of anxiety and depression (SMD 0.12, 95% CI -0.13 to 0.38; P=.36). No significant differences between delivery modes were observed for HRQoL (P=.93), functional aerobic capacity (P=.29), or dyspnea (P=.16). A significant subgroup difference was observed for lower-limb strength (P=.02). Conclusions Telerehabilitation may improve quality of life, aerobic capacity, and symptom burden in PCC and offer an accessible option for post-COVID rehabilitation, although the certainty of evidence was generally limited. Asynchronous delivery appears feasible for general reconditioning, whereas its benefit for lower-limb strength and the value of synchronous supervision remain uncertain. Trial registration PROSPERO CRD42023490863; https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD42023490863.

title: Diabetes educators' experience of care delivery to clients during the COVID-19 pandemic: a qualitative descriptive study.
abstract: Objectives With social distancing and limitations on face-to-face interactions during the COVID-19 pandemic, diabetes educators had to adapt their practices by implementing telehealth appointments as the primary mode of care delivery. The aim of the study was to explore diabetes educators' experiences of engaging with people who have diabetes during the COVID-19 pandemic. The research question was: What were diabetes educators' experiences of delivering care to clients during the COVID-19 pandemic? Methods A qualitative descriptive methodology using semi-structured interviews was used. Individual interviews were conducted during December 2023 and March 2024 with diabetes educators who provided care in Australian hospitals or communities during the pandemic. Interviews were audio recorded, and data were analysed using reflexive thematic analysis. Results Nine diabetes educators participated in interviews. Interview themes were: (1) challenges experienced in provision of diabetes care, with sub-themes including fear and avoidance behaviour, social isolation and mental health issues, and challenges faced by diabetes educators; and (2) adaptations in diabetes care, with sub-themes including transition to telehealth and face-to-face education as a supplement. Conclusion This study revealed insights into challenges and opportunities of telehealth and/or remote care delivery for people with diabetes during the pandemic, highlighting the need for adaptations in diabetes care. Future practice strategies should consider adoption of a more integrated healthcare delivery model that incorporates telehealth and/or remote services.

title: COVID-19 lockdown duration and transitions in family intergenerational support patterns: Evidence from the China Family Panel Studies
abstract: Abstract The family is the primary informal insurance mechanism through which economies buffer individual and aggregate risks, yet whether a major crisis activates intergenerational mutual aid or, instead, weakens intergenerational ties through physical isolation and resource strain remains unclear. Existing studies mostly examine changes in a single support dimension in isolation, or the simple before-versus-after correlation, and often rely on small, short-run samples, leaving the overall effect of the shock on the configuration of intergenerational support poorly understood. Using four waves (2016–2022) of the China Family Panel Studies (CFPS), we first classify intergenerational support into four cross-wave comparable patterns—Reciprocal, Filial-support, Interactive, and Detached—through latent class analysis, and then apply a multi-group difference-in-differences design to identify the causal effect of lockdown intensity on transitions between support patterns, its dynamic path, and its heterogeneity by household resources. We find that prolonged lockdowns shift households away from one-way support or detachment toward two-way reciprocity: the effect increases in lockdown intensity, is concentrated in the most strictly locked-down regions, and raises the post-pandemic probability of being Reciprocal by about 4.8 and 5.1 percentage points on average. The effect is delayed, being close to zero in the shock year (2020) and significant only by 2022. The shift toward reciprocity is widespread across income groups, whereas transitions into Filial-support are highly concentrated among low-income households. Overall, a major public-health shock triggers an adaptive reconfiguration of intergenerational support patterns, but its direction, lag, and form depend on shock intensity and household resources; the family, as an informal safety net, is resource-asymmetric, all the more so for vulnerable households. JEL Classification: J12; D19; I18; J14

title: The Impact of malaria and intermittent preventive treatment of malaria on vaccine responses and susceptibility to SARS-CoV-2 infection
abstract: Background: Vaccine-induced immune responses vary substantially across populations, with evidence of reduced immunogenicity in rural African settings. Malaria has been proposed as a potential contributor through its immunomodulatory effects, yet its impact on vaccine responses and SARSCoV-2 infection remains incompletely understood. This thesis aimed to investigate the effects of malaria, and of its prevention through intermittent preventive treatment (IPT), on unrelated vaccine responses and susceptibility to SARS-CoV-2. Methods: Four complementary studies were conducted. First, a systematic review and meta-analysis synthesised prior evidence on the effects of malaria infection and treatment on responses to unrelated vaccines. Second, a randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial evaluated the effect of malaria IPT with dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine (DP) on immune responses to BCG, yellow fever, oral typhoid, HPV, tetanus, and diphtheria vaccines. Third, within the same trial, the effect of IPT on SARS-CoV-2 seroprevalence and on immune responses to the BNT162b2 mRNA COVID-19 vaccine was assessed. Finally, a longitudinal study nested within a birth cohort examined whether early life-course malaria exposure influenced SARS-CoV-2 seroepidemiology during the first two years of the COVID-19 pandemic. Results: The systematic review demonstrated that malaria infection was associated with reduced responses to some vaccines, particularly pneumococcal, meningococcal, and Haemophilus influenzae type B vaccines (SMD 0.34, 95% CI 0.07 to 0,60). Malaria preventive treatment partially reversed these effects (SMD 0.07, 95% CI -0.01 to 0.16). The pooled estimate indicated an overall reduction in vaccine responses associated with malaria exposure (SMD 0.15, 95% CI 0.05 to 0.26). In the clinical trial, DP reduced malaria prevalence from 64% to below 6% during follow-up but had no significant effect on peak vaccine responses, although it modestly improved persistence of yellow fever vaccine-induced immunity. As this was a secondary outcome, it should be interpreted cautiously. DP also enhanced BNT162b2 vaccine-induced responses but did not reduce pre-vaccination SARS-CoV-2 seroprevalence. In the longitudinal study nested within the birth cohort, SARS-CoV-2 seroprevalence increased rapidly within 12 months, and there were no consistent associations with malaria exposure. Conclusions: This thesis suggests that malaria infection may impair vaccine responses. Although chemoprevention does not always reverse this effect, it improved the durability of yellow fever vaccine responses and enhanced humoral responses to COVID-19 mRNA vaccination. Neither chemoprevention nor early life-course malaria exposure was associated with SARS-CoV-2 seroprevalence. Further studies should examine how malaria exposure influences the durability of vaccine-induced immunity.

title: Fabrication of a monoclonal antibody-based electro-immunosensor to detect SARS-CoV-2 nucleocapsid antigen.
abstract: The nucleocapsid protein is one of the major structural proteins of the SARS-CoV-2 virus, which has caused the COVID-19 pandemic. Due to their high abundance in the host circulation system, post-early infection, and their participation in other cyclic events that support viral survival, they exert control over the viral life cycle within the host. Thus, assessing these protein levels in serum can serve as an early diagnostic tool for COVID-19 infections. In the current study, monoclonal antibodies (mAbs) targeting recombinantly produced NCoV2 (rNCoV2) antigen have been developed, characterized, and assessed for their immunodiagnostic potential by indirect ELISA, sandwich ELISA, and further integrated into electro-immunosensor platforms. Hybridomas secreting anti-rNCoV2 mAbs were obtained by fusion of mouse myeloma Sp2/0 cells with rNCoV2 antigen-immunized murine splenocytes using a chemical fusion agent. Hybridoma clones PAb8E8c3-G8 of isotype IgG2A and PBa1-A2 of isotype IgG1, both bearing ĸ light chains, were further developed and assessed for their diagnostic potential, as they have shown a stable growth pattern and the desired antibody response against the rNCoV2 antigen. The lowest concentration of antigen detected by both mAbs with confidence was 7.81 ng/well. Of the two, mAb PAb8E8c3-G8 was selected for mAb-based electro-immunosensor fabrication. A simple label-free GCE-carbon black-based electro-immunosensor was fabricated and enhanced with L-Cys/AuNP, onto which the mAb was immobilized. The integrated mAb electro-immunosensor could efficiently detect the rNCoV2 antigen, with LOD and LOQ values of 4.618 pg/mL and 15.24 pg/mL, respectively. Thus, in this study, we have generated mAbs against the rNCoV2 antigen, which have shown better diagnostic potential in terms of specificity and sensitivity.

source_records.abstract: The nucleocapsid protein is one of the major structural proteins of the SARS-CoV-2 virus, which has caused the COVID-19 pandemic. title: Judicial reasoning in critical care allocation under scarcity in Brazil during COVID 19 based on an empirical analysis of 223 ICU related decisions
abstract: Abstract Background The COVID-19 pandemic placed exceptional pressure on intensive care unit (ICU) capacity in Brazil and brought courts into direct contact with decisions about scarce life-sustaining resources. Methods We conducted an empirical legal study combining structured case-level reanalysis with qualitative documentary analysis of 223 ICU-related judicial decisions identified within a broader corpus of 585 COVID-19 health-litigation cases. Exact linkage between supplementary appendices recovered decision type and procedural class for 209 cases (93.7%) and decision date for 204. Headnotes were systematically coded using nine prespecified binary indicators capturing constitutional rights, clinical necessity, regulation or queue considerations, scarcity or capacity constraints, equality or priority among patients, executive competence or judicial deference, transfer or referral, private-sector cost or reimbursement, and structural capacity or governance. title: Influence of Urban Form, Weather and Population on Outdoor Airborne Infection Risk: Implications in Greater London for SARS-CoV-2
abstract: Abstract Although airborne infectious disease transmission outdoors is possible, particularly in densely built urban areas with limited ventilation, the role of urban morphology and neighborhood climate heterogeneity in modulating the risk remains poorly quantified. We couple an urban climate model (SUEWS) and a modified Wells-Riley framework to develop a transferable neighborhood-scale approach for mapping outdoor airborne infection risk across morphologically diverse neighborhoods, factoring in urban form, population distribution and meteorologically driven viral infectivity decay. We demonstrate this framework by applying it to SARS-CoV-2 in Greater London. Considering outdoor urban ventilation alone, estimated risk follows a diurnal cycle and peaks at night. Including population distribution, daytime risk in busy commercial centers is up to 7.23 times higher than nighttime. Infectivity decay from ultraviolet B (UVB) exposure reduces risk by 35–45% in less dense areas and up to 99% in high built-density neighborhoods. Despite this mitigation, the highest risks persist in high-rise, high-workplace-density districts (e.g., City of London and Westminster), while lower-rise areas (e.g., Lambeth and Croydon) exhibit reductions exceeding 90%. For SARS-CoV-2, these findings demonstrate strong intraurban heterogeneity in outdoor airborne infection risk in Greater London. More broadly, the transferable framework supports high-resolution mapping to inform targeted, place-based public health interventions.

title: Simultaneous detection of influenza and SARS-CoV-2 on an AI-nanopore multiplex platform.
abstract: Seasonal influenza and SARS-CoV-2 co-circulate and present overlapping symptoms, creating demand for rapid multiplex diagnostics beyond the sensitivity limits of antigen tests and the infrastructure requirements of nucleic acid amplification tests. Here we report NanoMux, an amplification-free diagnostic platform that couples a solid-state nanopore with attention-based multiple-instance learning (Attention-MIL) to classify clinical saliva samples from their nanopore event streams. Each measurement is treated as a "bag" of unlabeled translocation events dominated by endogenous nanoparticles, while only a sparse subset contains virus like signatures. Attention-MIL learns to weight informative events during bag-level prediction, enabling robust classification in highly contaminated clinical matrices where conventional machine learning baselines degrade. In a three-class setting (SARS-CoV-2, influenza, and healthy controls), Attention-MIL achieved a macro F1 of 0.781, substantially outperforming a gradient-boosting baseline (0.327). Under diluted conditions, the LightGBM model exhibited a more gradual decline in accuracy than the Attention-MIL model, demonstrating greater robustness for low-concentration specimens. NanoMux establishes a physics-based, reagent-minimal route to rapid multiplex respiratory virus screening and provides a model framework for extracting sparse pathogen signals from noisy nanopore recordings.

title: Comparative analysis of the development of oral language as a cognitive process constitutive of learning in child cohorts exposed to COVID-19 lockdown
abstract: This study analyzes oral language development as a constitutive cognitive process of learning in child cohorts exposed to COVID-19 confinement. A mixed-method, comparative, and correlational approach is proposed with a sample of 60 children distributed across three cohorts: pre-, during-, and post-pandemic. Exposure to the pandemic context is examined through questionnaires and interviews with parents and caregivers, while language development is assessed through PLON-R, systematic observation, and pedagogical records. The theoretical review and available contextual evidence suggest variations in morphosyntactic, semantic, and pragmatic performance associated with reduced social interaction, disrupted routines, and lower communicative stimulation. The study provides an analytical basis for understanding the relationship among confinement, language, and learning, and for supporting educational and psychopedagogical interventions in post-pandemic contexts.
journal: Journal of Systems and Educational Management

title: Epidemiología del SARS-CoV-2 en la práctica odontológica: transmisión, carga viral salival y bioseguridad Epidemiology of SARS-CoV-2 in dental practice: transmission, salivary viral load and biosafety
abstract: Objetivo: sintetizar la evidencia sobre la transmisión del SARS-CoV-2 en la práctica odontológica, la carga viral salival y las medidas de bioseguridad. Método: revisión sistemática con síntesis narrativa en PubMed y SciELO (2012-2025); se incluyeron 15 estudios. Resultados: la saliva y los aerosoles de los procedimientos odontológicos son vías relevantes de transmisión. La detección molecular del virus en saliva respalda su papel como reservorio y como muestra diagnóstica. Los colutorios antisépticos reducen el virus in vitro, pero su efecto clínico sobre la carga viral salival es limitado. El triaje, la protección personal, el control de aerosoles y la teleodontología fueron las medidas centrales. Conclusión: la bioseguridad debe mantenerse como norma permanente.

title: Finding Effective Vaccine Distribution Strategies: A Retroactive Study of COVID-19 in New York City
abstract: During the early stages of the COVID-19 pandemic, the United States was under-prepared, facing a shortage of personal protective equipment, hospital beds, and vaccines, and difficulties with allocating resources like vaccines across communities. Some communities received too few vaccine doses, while others received too many. To explore this problem, we used records of COVID-19 vaccine distribution allocations to simulate the effect of different roll-out strategies on the COVID-19 outbreak in New York City, one of the hardest hit cities. We find that targeting doses uniformly or targeting them towards susceptible communities or low income communities all lead to lower case counts compared to the actual roll-out. Our findings aim to help epidemiology and public health experts in the event of future outbreaks of a similar nature and scale as COVID-19.

To explore this problem, we used records of COVID-19 vaccine distribution allocations to simulate the effect of different roll-out strategies on the COVID-19 outbreak in New York City, one of the hardest hit cities. We find that targeting doses uniformly or targeting them towards susceptible communities or low income communities all lead to lower case counts compared to the actual roll-out. Our findings aim to help epidemiology and public health experts in the event of future outbreaks of a similar nature and scale as COVID-19.

title: Which spontaneous breathing trial should be used to reproduce post-extubation respiratory effort in COVID-19-related ARDS? A multicenter randomized crossover study.
abstract: Background Spontaneous breathing trials (SBT) guide extubation decisions in intensive care unit (ICU), predicting the respiratory effort required by the patient after extubation. Different SBTs exist and should be adapted to critical illness. Viral pneumonias such as COVID-19 combine lung injury, sepsis-induced systemic inflammation, and encephalopathy, making classification challenging. The objective was to assess which SBT could be used to reproduce postextubation respiratory effort in COVID-19-related acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) patients. Methods In this multicenter randomized crossover study, COVID-19-related ARDS patients mechanically ventilated at least 24 hours and ready for extubation underwent 3 different 15-minute SBT at random order: pressure support ventilation of 7-cmH2O with positive end-expiratory pressure (PEEP) of 0-cmH2O (PSV7PEEP0), PSV 0-cmH2O with PEEP 0-cmH2O (PSV0PEEP0) and T-piece trial. At baseline, end of each SBT, and 20 minutes after extubation, surrogates of respiratory effort were measured: esophageal pressure-time-product (PTPes), PTPes per minute (PTPes.min), swing esophageal pressure (SwingPes), and SwingPes per minute (SwingPes.min). Results Sixty measurements of respiratory effort from 12 patients were analyzed. Median PTPes.min increased from 193.8 [170.8-227.2] cmH2O.s/min at baseline to 236.6 [192.1-313.6] after extubation, with no significant differences between SBTs and postextubation. SwingPes and SwingPes.min were lower during PSV7-PEEP0 than after extubation, with median paired differences of 4.7 (95% CI 0.6-9.8) and 115.3 (95% CI 4.8-297.8), but these differences did not remain significant after correction for multiple comparisons. Conclusion No SBT modality differed significantly from post-extubation respiratory effort, suggesting that none could be excluded in COVID-19-related ARDS patients.

title: Exploring the role of self-concept in predicting aggressive behaviour among Indonesian adults during the COVID-19 pandemic
abstract: Abstract Aggressive behaviour remains a pervasive global social problem with enduring and intergenerational consequences. Although self-concept has been widely examined as a predictor of aggression in child, juvenile, and young adult populations, research focusing on adults across a broad age range—particularly within multicultural Asian contexts—remains limited. Furthermore, no previous studies have applied a multivariate approach to examine this issue comprehensively. Therefore, the present study investigates both univariate and multivariate associations between self-concept and aggressive behaviour across a broad age range and gender categories among Indonesian adults. Using a cross-sectional design conducted during the COVID-19 pandemic, a period characterized by heightened psychosocial stress and increased interpersonal conflict, data were collected from 326 adults aged 19–76 years via an online survey employing two validated Indonesian instruments: the Berzonsky-Fitts Self-Concept Scale and the Buss Aggression Scale. The results revealed a significant negative association between self-concept and aggressive behaviour, indicating that higher self-concept is associated with lower levels of aggressive behaviour. Gender-specific analyses further demonstrated meaningful differences in the multidimensional correlations results. These findings confirm that self-concept is a salient predictor of aggressive behaviour in Indonesian adults. Enhancing self-concept may help mitigate aggression across diverse age and gender groups, particularly during periods of societal stress. The study provides important implications for developing targeted prevention and intervention strategies in health, educational, and community settings. Future research should incorporate broader biopsychosocial variables to deepen the understanding of aggressive behaviour in adulthood.

title: Psychoeducational Challenges of Dyslexic Children During the COVID-19 Pandemic: A Systematic Review.
abstract: Dyslexic students faced psychological and educational challenges during the COVID-19 pandemic and online learning, including increased anxiety, low self-esteem, reduced reading interest, limited access to educational technologies, insufficient teacher support, and difficulties with reading fluency and concentration. Examining these challenges is crucial for implementing effective measures and enhancing post-pandemic learning. This study investigates the psycho-educational challenges of dyslexic children during the pandemic, highlighting the need for targeted interventions to support them in current and future contexts. This systematic review identified relevant articles through electronic searches of PubMed, Wiley, Scopus, Web of Science, Google Scholar, and ScienceDirect, supplemented by the snowballing technique, which involved examining the bibliographies of retrieved references. The study identified two main categories of challenges for dyslexic children: psychological (mental health, emotional well-being, behavioural issues, parental stress) and educational (socioeconomic status, technology access, special educational needs, teacher support, remote learning difficulties) affecting children with learning disabilities. The research results show that dyslexic children faced various psychological and educational difficulties identified in this review during the COVID-19 pandemic. Therefore, targeted, evidence-based strategies-such as teacher training, family-school collaboration, adaptive learning technologies, and psychological support-are needed to mitigate these challenges in the post-pandemic period.
