title: GLOW-CRISPR: A G-Quadruplex Loop-Engineered Optical Workflow Combined with CRISPR-Cas12a System for SARS-CoV-2 Detection
abstract: Abstract SARS-CoV-2 remains a serious public health threat, highlighting the need for rapid and accessible nucleic-acid diagnostics for decentralized testing. CRISPR-Cas systems are promising platforms for viral diagnostics because of their high specificity and compatibility with isothermal workflows. However, many CRISPR-based assays still rely on labelled reporters, dedicated fluorescence instrumentation, or single-mode outputs that increase cost and limit field deployment. Herein, we developed a label-free GLOW-CRISPR assay (a G-quadruplex loop-engineered optical workflow combined with the CRISPR-Cas12a system) to detect SARS-CoV-2. The assay provides fluorescence and colorimetric readouts in separate endpoint workflows through loop-engineered G4 reporters. Upon recognition of the SARS-CoV-2 target, activated Cas12a cleaves the loop-engineered G4 reporters, thereby suppressing both fluorescence and colorimetric signals. Using optimized conditions, the GLOW-CRISPR assay achieved limits of detection of 7.7 nM and 2.9 nM for fluorescence and colorimetric readouts, respectively. It also showed no detectable cross-reactivity with non-target respiratory viruses and correctly classified patient-derived nasopharyngeal samples in concordance with RT-qPCR results. Collectively, these results establish G4 loop engineering as a general strategy for label-free CRISPR-Cas12a signal transduction without probe labelling or specialized instrumentation. By expanding optical readout flexibility while reducing assay cost and complexity, the GLOW-CRISPR assay provides a practical framework for decentralized molecular diagnostics in resource-limited settings.

title: Mortalidade por COVID-19 no Brasil: determinantes socioeconômicos segundo faixas etárias COVID-19 mortality in Brazil: socioeconomic determinants across age groups Mortalidad por COVID-19 en Brasil: determinantes socioeconómicos según grupos de edad
abstract: Introdução: A mortalidade por COVID-19 é maior em populações idosas, mas os determinantes entre diferentes faixas etárias permanecem pouco compreendidos em países com desigualdades sociais marcantes. Objetivo: Avaliar a associação entre desigualdades socioeconômicas, disponibilidade de atenção primária e mortalidade por COVID-19 segundo faixas etárias no Brasil em 2020. Métodos: Estudo ecológico de base populacional com dados do Ministério da Saúde e do Instituto Brasileiro de Geografia e Estatística (IBGE). Foram analisadas as taxas de mortalidade em três grupos etários (<30, 30–59 e ≥60 anos) nos 26 estados e no Distrito Federal, por meio de modelos de Regressão Binomial Negativa ajustados pelo tamanho da população. Resultados: A mortalidade variou significativamente entre estados e faixas etárias. Maior desigualdade de renda (Índice de Gini) associou-se a maior mortalidade em todas as faixas etárias (p<0,05), enquanto maior disponibilidade de equipes de atenção primária esteve associada a menor mortalidade (p<0,05). Conclusões: As desigualdades sociais se associaram a maior mortalidade por COVID-19 no Brasil, reforçando a necessidade de políticas públicas equitativas e do fortalecimento da atenção primária à saúde.

title: A SARS-CoV-2 entry inhibitor trimerizes to lock the spike protein in a closed conformation
abstract: Abstract The SARS-CoV-2 spike protein binds its receptor ACE2 to initiate target-cell infection. To engage ACE2, at least one of the three receptor-binding domains (RBDs) of the spike must adopt the up orientation. Here, we describe S22, a potent, bioavailable, and non-toxic inhibitor of BA.2 and all subsequent Omicron variants. Cryo-EM analyses showed that S22 assembled as a trimer in the central cavity of the spike apex, stabilizing all three RBDs in the down orientation, thereby preventing ACE2 association. Binding studies, especially those using mixed S22-sensitive and -resistant spikes, imply a cooperative assembly of three S22 molecules with three RBDs, resulting in an unusually slow S22 off-rate. Consistent with its slow dissociation and favorable pharmacokinetics, S22 suppressed viral replication and inflammation in the lungs of XBB.1.5-infected female mice. Thus, S22 potently inhibits Omicron entry through a distinct mechanism whereby a small compound assembles cooperatively as a trimer to stabilize spike in an inactive conformation.

title: Factors associated with COVID-19 severe illness leading to hospitalization in Bangladesh: a matched case-control study
abstract: A retrospective matched case-control study included 250 patients hospitalized with severe COVID-19 and 250 age- and sex-matched controls who did not require hospitalization. Data on 48 variables were collected from both the cases and controls using a structured questionnaire via retrospective telephone interviews. Univariable conditional logistic regression was initially performed to identify variables associated with severe illness. Variables with p ≤ 0.10 were included in the multivariable model to identify factors independently associated with severe illness. Whole-genome sequencing (WGS) was performed as an exploratory analysis on virus samples from five purposively selected case-control pairs to assess whether unique viral mutations were associated with severe outcomes. Having multiple (≥2) comorbidities (adjusted odds ratio = 2.5, 95% confidence interval: 1.4–4.4, p = 0.001) and attempting oxygen supplementation at home during the illness (adjusted odds ratio = 6.3, 95% confidence interval: 2.7–15.1, p < 0.001) were associated with higher odds of severe COVID-19 leading to hospitalization. In contrast, indoor physical exercise during the illness was associated with lower odds of severe illness (adjusted odds ratio = 0.3, 95% confidence interval: 0.2–0.5, p < 0.001). title: DESENVOLVIMENTO DE VACINAS PARA COVID-19: UMA REVISÃO COM ÊNFASE NAS REAÇÕES ADVERSAS
abstract: The study aimed to systematize information and critically contextualize the history and challenges of vaccine development, focusing primarily on serious adverse reactions in light of the COVID-19 pandemic and the ChAdOx1 nCov-19 immunobiological. To this end, an integrative literature review was conducted, outlined by a search for scientific articles and bibliographies across major national and international electronic repositories. The descriptors used for the search were: SARS-CoV-2, COVID-19, history, immunization, vaccines, vaccine development, ChAdOx1 nCov-19, BNT162b2, adverse effects, and thrombosis, as well as their respective English translations. The findings externalize and reinforce that such occurrences do not compromise the efficacy and safety of vaccines; rather, they drive technological refinement, the improvement of surveillance, and a deeper understanding of immune-mediated mechanisms. Consequently, the development of immunizers and new public health strategies are strengthened, contributing to the control and prevention of infectious diseases.

title: Iron Dysregulation During Severe COVID-19: Longitudinal Evidence from Hospitalized Patients
abstract: Background/Objectives: The COVID-19 pandemic underlined the critical role of iron homeostasis in infections, particularly in those cases where hyperinflammation, fueled by massive elevation in cytokines such as IL-6, TNF-α, and IL-8, triggered acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS), progressive multiorgan failure and heightened mortality. This extreme immune response aggravates systemic iron imbalance and eventually triggers a vicious cycle in which the inflammatory state fuels the impaired iron metabolism, thereby contributing to disease severity. The main goal of this work was to disentangle the relationships between inflammation and iron metabolism in a cohort of well-characterized patients hospitalized for severe COVID-19. Methods: This study evaluated 389 patients hospitalized with COVID-19 pneumonia in a medical ward at Verona University Hospital. Complete clinical parameters, inflammatory, and iron-related markers’ trends were analyzed over time during hospitalization (admission (T0), 1 week (T1), and 2 weeks after (T2)). Subjects were grouped by disease severity during hospitalization. Results: High-severity cases showed significantly higher concentrations of IL-8, IL-6, IL-10, hepcidin, and ferritin at baseline. Hepcidin correlated strongly with inflammatory markers and was a predictor of COVID-19 severity (p = 0.014). Despite a gradual decrease, hepcidin levels remained significantly higher in patients with a more serious form of the disease across time points. Conclusions: Our findings underscore the clinical utility of iron-related markers in COVID-19 management and the relevance of their assessment in clinical settings for better patient stratification.

title: Effect of HLA Class II polymorphism on susceptibility to SARS-CoV-2 infection and severity of the infection process
abstract: Previous studies have revealed a potential role of gene variants in the main histocompatibility complex, which regulates the expression of human leukocyte antigen molecules ( HLA ) in the course of coronavirus infection (COVID-19). The aim of our study was to evaluate the relationships between HLA polymorphism and COVID-19, as well as the severity of the infection process in patients from the Western Siberia. 260 patients with COVID-19 were examined two months after their convalescence. The comparison group included 372 residents from the Novosibirsk Region. Genotyping of the alleles and allele groups was performed using PCR test-systems (DNA-Technology, Moscow, Russia). The IBM SPSS Statistics 23 and Harlequine 3.5.2 were used for statistical processing. An increase in DRB1*15; DQA1*01:02 alleles and decreased frequency of DRB1*03; DQA1*01:03; DQB1*05:03 were detected in COVID-19 patients versus control group. After Bonferroni correction, the mentioned differences retained only for DQA1*01:02 . Three haplotypes were identified, which differed between the groups without Bonferroni correction. DRB1*07,15; DQA1*01:02,0201 and DQB1*02,06:02-08 frequency prevailed in patients versus control group. DRB1*07,15-DQB1*02,06:02-08; DQA1*01:02,02:01-DQB1*02,06-02-08 , and DRB1*07,15DQA1*01:02,02:01-DQB1*02,06:02-08 combinations prevailed in COVID-19 patients against control group. The DRB1*07,11; DRB1*11,15 genotypes, and several allelic combinations ( DRB1*07,11-DQA1*02:01,05:01; DRB1*11,15-DQA1*01:02,05:01; DRB1*11,15-DQB1*03:01,06:02-08, DRB1*11,15-DQA1*01:02,05:01DQB1*03:01,06:02-08 ) were present only in patients with severe disease. Prevalence of DRB1*11, DRB1*07,11 and DRB1*07,11-DQA1*02:01,05:01 was higher in the combined group (severe plus moderate course) of the disease versus the group of patients with mild disease. The results obtained make a definite contribution to clarifying the role of HLA gene polymorphism in COVID-19 not only in Western Siberia, but also in the entire Russian Federation. Further research is required, with increasing the sample size, thus reaching statistical significance, when correcting for the multiplicity of alleles.

title: Did the COVID-19 vaccination during pregnancy impact obstetric outcome?
abstract: Background: The COVID-19 wave hit the world in 2019-20. However, vaccination for covid in pregnant women was still a light behind the wall. Gradually it was accepted and the vaccination was introduced for pregnant women also. This article helps to know the effect of the two commonly used COVID-19 vaccines on obstetric outcome. Aim was to study the safety of COVID-19 vaccination on pregnant women by analyzing its impact on course and outcome of pregnancy. Methods: This was a cross-sectional study including 427 pregnant women and aims to study the safety of COVID-19 vaccination on pregnant women by analyzing its impact on course and outcome of pregnancy. Results: Of the total number of women who received the vaccination, 258 (60.4%) received both the doses and 169 (39.6%) received only a single dose of vaccine. In terms of pregnancy outcomes, 30 (6.56%) had abortion and the remaining 427 of them continued the pregnancy up to 3rd trimester. Out of 427, 421 delivered liveborn infants. 6 IUDs and 10 spontaneous first trimester abortions were documented in our study. No fetal anomalies were identified in our study group. The incidence of FGR and oligohydramnios was 0.5%. 0.9% of the mothers developed GDM. Preterm deliveries were noted in 15.2%. 8 cases (1.9%) had meconium-stained amniotic fluid at birth. 63.9% had a normal vaginal delivery and remaining 36.1% underwent LSCS. No significant changes were observed with respect to the birth weight of babies among vaccinated women. NICU admissions were noted for preterm care, birth hypoxia and hyperbilirubinemia. However, no serious neonatal morbidity was noted. Conclusions: The study has not demonstrated any untoward effects on the course of pregnancy nor the fetus at birth, due to receiving covid vaccines. Thus, it can be safely considered during pregnancy.
journal: International Journal of Reproduction Contraception Obstetrics and Gynecology

title: Determination of the Mechanisms of Substrate Specificity of SARS-CoV-2 Papain-like Protease Through Structural and Biochemical Studies
abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic was caused by Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome Coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2), and despite advancements in antivirals and vaccine development, SARS-CoV-2 remains a virus of concern. An avenue worth exploring is targeting the viral papain-like protease (PLpro) and 3C-like protease (Mpro), but to date, only the latter has FDA-approved therapeutics. PLpro is an essential protease for viral replication, with a primary role in processing viral polypeptides and a secondary role as a deubiquitinating and deISGylating enzyme. PLpro’s removal of poly-ubiquitin and ISG15 from target proteins enables the virus to evade the cellular immune response. Structurally K48-linked di-ubiquitin (Ub2) consists of two ubiquitin units connected via an isopeptide bond, which can be processed by PLpro. ISG15 is structurally similar to di-ubiquitin, consisting of two ubiquitin-like domains connected by an uncleavable linker along the backbone. Exploring how PLpro discriminates between ISG15 and Ub2 binding will provide structural insights for drug design aimed at disrupting the processing of these tags. In this work, nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) spectroscopy and a variety of biochemical techniques were used to investigate how PLpro recognizes and processes substrates. As a result of this work, PLpro has been shown to exhibit dual-domain recognition of ISG15 and Ub2 and prefers occupation of both S1 and S2 sites for effective cleavage of substrate from the target. PLpro also requires the free C-terminal tail of the substrate to enter the active site, thereby undergoing a conformational change that stabilizes interactions within the S1 site. This work further established that strong binding to PLpro may not be required for the protease to process the substrate. As a result of the work in this thesis, a deeper understanding of how PLpro structurally recognizes substrates is provided, offering a framework for developing therapeutics that more efficiently target PLpro activity. Likewise, this work contributes foundational insights into how other PLpro variants of current and future coronaviruses may interact with substrates.

Likewise, this work contributes foundational insights into how other PLpro variants of current and future coronaviruses may interact with substrates.

title: Strategi Kampanye Komunikasi Publik Satgas Covid-19 Nasional dalam Penanganan Covid-19
abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic in Indonesia generated significant impacts on public health and the national economy, reflected in rising confirmed cases, economic contraction, and increasing unemployment resulting from physical distancing policies. These conditions required society to adapt to new behavioral norms through structured and effective public communication. This study aims to analyze the public communication campaign strategy implemented by the National COVID-19 Task Force in managing the pandemic and to identify the supporting and inhibiting factors influencing its implementation. The research employed a qualitative approach within a constructivist paradigm using a case study design. Data were collected through in-depth interviews with the public communication division and community members and were analyzed interpretatively. The findings indicate that the campaign strategy was systematically designed with informative and persuasive objectives to enhance public awareness and encourage behavioral change. Messages were science-based and delivered by credible communicators with authentic voices. Furthermore, stakeholder mapping was conducted to strengthen collaborative support, contributing to the development of active and sustainable public participation in pandemic management.

title: Severe Immune-Mediated Steroid-Refractory Thrombocytopenia in a Patient With COVID-19
abstract: Coronavirus disease 19 (COVID-19) has been associated with a wide variety of clinical signs and symptoms involving the respiratory, cardiovascular, and hematopoietic systems.Few cases of severe thrombocytopenia secondary to COVID-19 have been reported.COVID-19 can cause thrombocytopenia through mechanisms of disseminated intravascular coagulation (DIC), immune thrombocytopenic purpura (ITP), thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura (TTP), deep venous thrombosis (DVT), pulmonary embolism (PE), autoimmune hemolytic anemia (AIHA), and bone marrow suppression.We present a case of a 65-year-old man who was recently diagnosed with lung cancer, presented with shortness of breath and cough, and was diagnosed with COVID-19.He was noted to have an abrupt platelet drop from 500,000 cells per mm3 to counts <2.Laboratory workup showed lactate dehydrogenase (LDH), bilirubin, and haptoglobin within normal limits and no evidence of schistocytes in the peripheral blood smear, but severe thrombocytopenia.His condition remained steroid-refractory.He was initiated on intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIG) by hematology, with subsequent improvement in platelet count to normal.COVID-19 is known to cause thrombocytopenia by various mechanisms.In patients with multiple risk factors, the risk of thrombocytopenia increases further.This patient had a diagnosis of rapidly progressing lung cancer, which puts him at risk of DIC, DVT, and PE, causing consumptive coagulopathy.He also had right-sided lung infiltrates and was initiated on empiric bacterial coverage with IV vancomycin and IV piperacillin-tazobactam, which may cause drug-induced thrombocytopenia.Bacterial pneumonia/sepsis also puts him at risk of thrombocytopenia, predominantly by consumption.When several etiologies for thrombocytopenia are possible, careful assessment of clinical findings, laboratory data, and temporal relationships is required to determine the most probable diagnosis.

title: Tracking the Medico-Legal Recognition of Occupational COVID-19 in Italy: A Nationwide Repeated-Snapshot and Sensitivity Analysis of Workers’ Compensation Claims, 2020–2023
abstract: In Italy, occupational SARS-CoV-2 infection entered the accident-at-work system through a distinctive medico-legal framework. We examined whether the positive-disposition proportion differed from contemporaneous non-COVID injury claims and changed as administrative series matured. We harmonized 3,129,447 records from the Italian National Institute for Insurance against Accidents at Work (INAIL) and combined them with 32 national occupational COVID-19 reports. Repeated snapshots assessed completed 2020 and 2021 series; same-cut-off analyses compared COVID-19 with reconstructed non-COVID claims for 2020–2022. Published positive-disposition proportions rose from 87% to 89% for 2020 claims and from 66.5% to 74% for 2021 claims. At 30 April 2023, proportions were 89%, 74%, and 70% for COVID-19 versus 62.85%, 63.42%, and 59.15% for non-COVID claims, yielding differences of 26.15, 10.58, and 10.85 percentage points. All tested rounding and insurance-management scenarios retained positive differences. Denominator sensitivity was greatest in 2021, where the reference difference reached zero after the exclusion of 94.8% of communication/franchise records; the reference tipping point was not reached within 0–100% exclusion in 2020 or 2022. These are administrative outcomes at specified cut-offs; the more recent event years had less time to mature. Positive-disposition proportions should, therefore, be interpreted jointly with claim composition, denominator specification, and administrative follow-up when comparing compensation statistics and planning surveillance for future occupational epidemics.

title: Study of COVID-19 outcomes in patients with rare diseases in Germany [SCOPE-RD], part 2
abstract: Abstract Background People with rare diseases often require continuous and specialized medical care. The COVID-19 pandemic has strained healthcare systems worldwide, but only limited data is available on its specific impact on patients with rare diseases. The aim of this study was to assess the burden of the pandemic on people with rare diseases in Germany, identify gaps in their healthcare, and provide a foundation for future strategies to support this vulnerable group during pandemics. Methods A retrospective, representative cross-sectional analysis was conducted using statutory health insurance (SHI) claims data from approximately 4.9 million insured individuals between 2017 and 2022. Patients with rare diseases were identified based on specific ICD-10-GM codes. Results The study presents initial results regarding mortality, disease burden, healthcare resource utilization, and healthcare costs associated with patients with rare diseases with and without SARS-CoV-2 infection. A total of 14,912 patients with rare diseases were identified, of whom 2,378 (16%) contracted COVID-19 between 2020 and 2022. Patients with COVID-19 incurred higher healthcare costs, particularly in 2020 and 2021, with average costs nearly twice as high as those without COVID-19. Healthcare resource utilization, including hospitalizations and emergency visits, was higher in the COVID-19 group. Additionally, these patients exhibited increased psychological stress and a higher need for pain medication. Conclusion Within the analyzed cohort, patients with rare diseases who contracted COVID-19 showed higher mortality, disease burden, healthcare resource utilization, and healthcare costs than those who did not. As this descriptive analysis included no external comparator group, the findings characterize the burden of COVID-19 within the population of people with rare diseases, in the context of published data on the general population and people with chronic diseases, rather than establishing an effect specific to rare diseases in general. They nonetheless underline the vulnerability of this group and the need for tailored strategies in future pandemics.

title: Obstructive sleep apnea and long COVID syndrome: a scoping review of current evidence in adults
abstract: Background Obstructive Sleep Apnea (OSA) is a prevalent sleep disorder characterized by intermittent hypoxia and sleep fragmentation, contributing to systemic inflammation and autonomic dysfunction. Long COVID refers to persistent symptoms following acute COVID-19 infection. Emerging evidence suggests an association between OSA and persistent post-COVID-19 symptoms, potentially mediated by overlapping biological pathways; however, the direction and causality of this relationship remain uncertain. Aim This scoping review aimed to examine the current evidence regarding the different associations between OSA and Long COVID in adults, summarize the reported clinical findings, and explore the proposed pathophysiological mechanisms linking OSA and Long COVID. Methods Following PRISMA-ScR guidelines, PubMed, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science, Cochrane Library, Google Scholar, and ClinicalTrials.gov were searched for studies published between 2020 and 2026. Eligible studies included observational studies, clinical trials, and reviews involving adults with OSAand/or Long COVID syndrome. Two independent reviewers screened studies, extracted data, and synthesized findings thematically. Results Of 184 identified records, 11 studies met the inclusion criteria. Evidence suggested different associations between OSA and Long COVID across the included studies. Proposed mechanisms included intermittent hypoxia, systemic inflammation, autonomic dysregulation, sleep fragmentation, and circadian disturbance; however, these mechanisms were not consistently measured across studies. Reported Long COVID manifestations among patients with OSA included fatigue, respiratory impairment, cognitive dysfunction, and cardiovascular complications. Evidence regarding the impact of OSA treatment on Long COVID outcomes was limited. Conclusions Current evidence suggests an association between OSA and Long COVID, although the nature and direction of this association vary across studies. However, the evidence remains limited and heterogeneous. Further longitudinal studies are needed to clarify this relationship and determine whether effective OSA management can improve Long COVID outcomes.

title: Anesthesia complications in COVID-19 positive pediatric patients: Results from a rapid literature review and meta-analysis
abstract: Children are less likely to experience severe COVID-19-related complications compared to adults, they are still an understudied, vulnerable population. Given the unique challenges posed by COVID-19 in pediatric patients, effective perioperative management is essential to mitigate potential complications and ensure safe anesthesia practices. In this manuscript, the objective was to produce a systematic literature review with meta-analysis to increase the understanding of current research to help guide anesthesiologists in perioperative management. Our analysis of the literature identifies respiratory complications as a primary concern for patients undergoing anesthesia while infected with COVID-19. Three databases were searched and screened for reviews and there were 939 combined articles found. These databases are large collections of published scientific articles which were sorted through using keywords which allowed us to find and analyze these articles. After the databases were screened there were a number of articles which worked within our criteria which were looking for pediatric anesthesia patients during the beginning of the pandemic and their complications. The odds ratio was calculated for each paper to generate an overall combined effect size, heterogeneity, and publication bias. After screening and removing duplicates, 10 articles were included for further review, and 6 were eligible for meta-analysis. Their combined effect size was 3.71 (CI 2.45, 7.24, p = 0.05), heterogeneity I2=0.76, and funnel plot for publication bias demonstrated right skew. Our results show there is a statistically significant increase in modest COVID-19 complications in pediatric patients from anesthesia. These modest complications include respiratory events, use of vasopressors, cardiac, SIRS, and unplanned escalations of care. Clinically insignificant results may have been missed due to publication bias in our study. While we found statistically significant results showing an increase in pediatric complications, it is possible that clinically insignificant results could add even more to this topic so we concluded that larger, more robust, studies need to be conducted.

title: Detection profiles and co-detection patterns of respiratory pathogens in hospitalized patients with acute respiratory infections after the COVID-19 pandemic in Nantong, China
abstract: Respiratory-pathogen circulation may have changed after relaxation of coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) control measures. We characterized the pathogen spectrum, clinical-site distribution, age-specific patterns, co-detection patterns, and seasonality among hospitalized patients with acute respiratory tract infections (ARTIs) in Nantong, China. This retrospective cross-sectional study included 5,808 patients hospitalized with ARTIs at the Affiliated Hospital of Nantong University between December 2023 and December 2025. Respiratory specimens collected at admission were tested for 16 pathogens using multiplex real-time quantitative polymerase chain reaction. Pathogen detection was compared by infection site, age group, and season. False discovery rate correction, multivariable logistic regression, and Cochran-Armitage trend tests were applied as appropriate. At least one pathogen was detected in 3,129 of 5,808 patients (53.87%). Single and mixed detections occurred in 2,103 (36.21%) and 1,026 (17.67%) patients, respectively. Klebsiella pneumoniae , Staphylococcus aureus , and Haemophilus influenzae were the most frequently detected bacterial targets. After false discovery rate correction, Mycoplasma pneumoniae , adenovirus, human metapneumovirus, H. influenzae , parainfluenza virus type III, and influenza B virus were more frequently detected in lower than upper respiratory tract infections (all q < 0.05). In adjusted analyses, M. influenzae remained associated with lower respiratory tract infections. pneumoniae detection peaked among children aged 6–17 years (30.92%, 81/262; P-trend < 0.001). Among patients with mixed detections, bacterial-bacterial pairs were most frequent, particularly S. Influenza A virus showed a marked winter peak (21.31% vs. 1.20–2.54% in other seasons; q < 0.001). Hospitalized patients in eastern China showed frequent bacterial-target detection, age-related heterogeneity, and distinct seasonal patterns. The school-age peak in M. pneumoniae and the winter peak in influenza A virus support age- and season-informed surveillance. Because molecular detection cannot distinguish active infection from colonization, bacterial findings should be interpreted alongside clinical, culture, and biomarker data.

title: How Did COVID-19 Affect Urban Slums?
abstract: Abstract During the COVID-19 pandemic, slum settlements received significant attention for their vulnerabilities. To mitigate risks of disease transmission and containment measures, experts called for community-driven solutions. But such approaches frequently neglect pre-existing structures of local leadership in these settlements. How did India’s slum leaders respond to the pandemic? What factors shape their success in helping residents? To answer these questions, we conducted a phone survey of 321 slum leaders in two north Indian cities during India’s stringent 2020 national lockdown. Our survey reveals striking continuities with pre-pandemic politics. Slum leaders persist in their problem-solving roles but tilt efforts toward pandemic response activities. Their effectiveness in doing so remains informed by the same factors that shape efficacy during “normal times,” notably their education and degree of embeddedness in party networks. Finally, pre-pandemic disparities in slum-level infrastructural development shape how much residents must depart from social distancing guidelines to secure essential services.

title: ‘Reaching and Teaching’: Understanding the Supercomplexity of Primary Teachers’ Work in an Area of High Social Deprivation During the COVID-19 Pandemic
abstract: Abstract This chapter explores the supercomplexity of primary teachers’ work in four northern English schools serving communities of high social deprivation during the COVID-19 pandemic. Based on a multiple case study, it shows how teachers’ safeguarding, pastoral and welfare roles expanded during the pandemic, requiring sustained family engagement amid overlapping social, economic and digital disadvantage and in response to shifting policy guidance. Framed by Barnett’s (2000a) notion of supercomplexity, the analysis identifies five overlapping themes: evolving definitions of vulnerability, mediating learning through homes, the emotional labour of care, rapid pedagogical and organisational adaptation and re-evaluation of educational aims beyond high-stakes accountability. While teachers demonstrated remarkable adaptability; developing hybrid provision, restructuring Early Years pedagogy and prioritising wellbeing, the moral weight of this labour remained largely unrecognised in policy. This chapter argues for teacher education and system design that centre adaptability, relational care and professional judgement, positioning teachers as co-constructors of educational meaning and essential agents in building resilience for future crises.

source_records.title: ‘Reaching and Teaching’: Understanding the Supercomplexity of Primary Teachers’ Work in an Area of High Social Deprivation During the COVID-19 Pandemic
source_records.abstract: Abstract This chapter explores the supercomplexity of primary teachers’ work in four northern English schools serving communities of high social deprivation during the COVID-19 pandemic. Based on a multiple case study, it shows how teachers’ safeguarding, pastoral and welfare roles expanded during the pandemic, requiring sustained family engagement amid overlapping social, economic and digital disadvantage and in response to shifting policy guidance. Framed by Barnett’s (2000a) notion of supercomplexity, the analysis identifies five overlapping themes: evolving definitions of vulnerability, mediating learning through homes, the emotional labour of care, rapid pedagogical and organisational adaptation and re-evaluation of educational aims beyond high-stakes accountability. While teachers demonstrated remarkable adaptability; developing hybrid provision, restructuring Early Years pedagogy and prioritising wellbeing, the moral weight of this labour remained largely unrecognised in policy. This chapter argues for teacher education and system design that centre adaptability, relational care and professional judgement, positioning teachers as co-constructors of educational meaning and essential agents in building resilience for future crises.

title: Widening the Gap? The Impact of COVID-19 Restrictions on Education for Students With Special Educational Needs and Disabilities in an English Special School
abstract: Abstract This study explores how COVID-19 restrictions impacted on the provision of education for children and young people with special educational needs and disabilities (SEND), from the point of view of four parents and the headteacher at a special school in the North of England. Thematic analysis of the data through Bronfenbrenner’s bioecological theory and Biesta’s domains of education contextualised the effects of school closures and policies on the people and systems that students engage with, as well as how they both interact with one another. While existing research has largely examined the impact of school closures and remote learning, this case study highlights the critical role of specialist provision in supporting families and maintaining student wellbeing. Findings reveal how the pandemic exacerbated existing inequalities and exposed the marginalisation of SEND learners within policy and practice. The study calls for a radical reframing of education through a social model of disability, advocating for inclusive environments and pedagogies. Although focused on only one special school, insights offer valuable lessons for mainstream and specialist settings alike. Wellbeing must be embedded in educational policy and practice to better support all learners moving forward.

title: Reimagining Secondary Schools as a Result of the COVID-19 Pandemic: A Qualitative Study
abstract: Abstract This chapter reports the findings of a qualitative study that set out to examine the experiences and priorities of English state-funded secondary schools during the COVID-19 pandemic. It considers how historical and contemporary policy eras have shaped the capacities of schools to respond to the challenges posed by the pandemic. Research took place within three schools with different types of governance: an inner-city new build that is part of a multi-academy trust, a Faith School and a Maintained School. It purposively recruited staff across a range of roles (senior leader, teaching and non-teaching support) to gain a complete picture of school approaches. Findings were as follows: going into the pandemic, each school identified challenges around staff recruitment, budgetary pressures, social deprivation and an increasing special educational needs and disabilities register. In the early days of school closure, schools utilised their existing pastoral structures to support children and families with varying degrees of success. As the pandemic evolved, all staff found themselves taking on new activities outside of their remit, which enabled a better understanding of the families and communities that they served. The authors conclude that in taking almost total responsibility for the welfare of pupils and their families during the pandemic, participating schools – whatever their governance – continued to resist neoliberal-driven educational policy that focuses purely on the classroom and excellent teaching. Learning from the pandemic suggests that there is a strong case to re-imagine schools as integral to communities and furthermore, that there is an appetite to achieve this.

title: Method to evolution's model of the epidemic of the Covid-19. A case's illustration
abstract: Introduction: At present they yield different mathematical models to describe the evolution of the epidemic of the Coronavirus, however the realized predictions do not characterize themselves for the desired precisions, and at times, they had been applied models of continuous, probabilistic processes, still when we know that they have an operation with data, which represent a discontinuous phenomenon of behavior (of finite leaps), aspect that affects the approximations of the real development of the epidemic of the new Coronavirus. Aims to: they develop a mathematical algorithm for the prediction of the epidemic of the Covid-19 through mathematical quantitative and qualitative models in compliance with humanity's needs according to the evolution of the paradigms. Methods: Theoretical methods are used: analysis and synthesis, induction and deduction, abstraction and concretion, and the logical historical method. Revision of reports of studies. Construction of function curves and their reasons for change. Mathematical methods, procedures and algorithms are applied, as well as the focuses of the clinical and epidemiologic methods. Results: The empirical methods applied are framed mainly in the observation of the records of the experimental data, the bibliographic review, in order to deepen the problem and obtain information on the main difficulties that affect the research process, and the published reports, from of the search for methods and procedures. The document review method is used, through books, and articles referring to the topic epimics evolution about experimental and statistics data in the Scielo, DOAJ, Latindex, Google Scholar Databases, Elsevier, among others. A method of work is designed, which makes easy the analysis of the quantitative real registered data to characterize the evolution of the epidemics. The May 6, 2021 is illustrated by means of the yielded information in Israel, as from the December 14, 2020. Conclusions: An alternative constitutes the mathematical designed algorithm that it assures the tracking and the control of the epidemics, as well as the performance of the data recollected to understand, explaining and interpreting essential features, from the topologic point of view, which represent the global tendencies of growth, decrease, and the cycle of epidemic attenuation.

title: Interleukin-1β in peripheral blood of pregnant women with mild and moderate course of acute SARS-CoV-2 infection
abstract: Pregnant women are susceptible to SARS-CoV-2 infection due to physiological features of the immune system. The aim of our study was to evaluate the levels of interleukin-1β (IL-1β) in peripheral blood of pregnant women during SARS-CoV-2 infection with mild to moderate forms of the disease. We examined 60 pregnant women with COVID-19, including 14 women in the 1st trimester, 17 in the 2nd trimester, and 29 in the 3rd trimester. The comparison group consisted of 20 pregnant women without clinical and laboratory signs of acute respiratory infections. IL-1β concentrations were determined in serum using ELISA technique. Statistica 10.0 (StatSoft, USA) was used for statistical data processing. The significant error level was considered to be p < 0.05. The study results showed higher levels of IL-1β in blood of SARS-CoV-2-infected pregnant women compared to pregnant women without clinical and laboratory evidence of acute respiratory infections (p = 0.005). COVID-19 is characterized by a decreased IL-1β level in blood during the 3rd trimester of gestation as compared to the 1st trimester (p = 0.01). Pregnant women with COVID-19, compared with pregnant women without detectable signs of acute respiratory infections, had higher levels of red blood cells (p = 0.043), total protein (p = 0.006), direct bilirubin (p = 0.02), high-sensitivity C-reactive protein (p < 0.001), ferritin (p = 0.016), prothrombin time (p = 0.018) and blood clotting INR values (p = 0.013). COVID-19 in pregnant women is associated with lower levels of lymphocytes (p = 0.004), serum iron (p < 0.001) and transferrin (p = 0.003), transferrin saturation coefficient (p = 0.026) and total iron-binding capacity of blood serum (p = 0.021). IL-1β in SARS-CoV-2-infected pregnant women had an inverse correlation with biochemical and coagulation blood parameters: transferrin (p = 0.006), total iron-binding capacity of serum (p = 0.03), latent iron-binding capacity of serum (p = 0.009), fibrinogen (p = 0.002). IL-1β in the blood of SARS-CoV-2-infected pregnant women is associated with the level of direct bilirubin (p = 0.045) in moderate COVID-19, C-reactive protein (p = 0.047) and alanine aminotransferase (p = 0.024) in mild forms of the disease. Moderate COVID-19 in pregnant women is associated with a decreased leukocyte counts (p = 0.038), and an increase in prothrombin time (p = 0.046). Thus, a relationship was established between the concentration of IL-1β in blood, blood coagulation and biochemical parameters in women with COVID-19 at different stages of pregnancy, as well as dependence on the clinical severity of COVID-19.

title: The COVID-19 Pandemic as an Institutional Stress Test: University Management in Four Latin American Countries
abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic required universities to reorganize teaching and student services when campus access was restricted. This exploratory study examines whether reported university management practices were associated with enrollment change. University leaders in Colombia, Ecuador, Peru, and Venezuela completed a survey between November 2021 and January 2022, rating eight management domains before and during the pandemic. Descriptive analyses included 105 institutional survey records. Enrollment analyses used 74 institutions in Colombia and Ecuador with usable student counts for 2019 and 2023. Separate regression models examined each pre-pandemic management domain, accounting for baseline institutional size, country, and perceived risks. Additional analyses examined relative enrollment change and compared institutions with different levels of reported management implementation during the pandemic. Enrollment increased by an average of 2935 students, although the median increase was considerably smaller, at 328 students. None of the eight management domains showed a statistically significant association with enrollment change after adjustment. Differences across implementation categories were also not statistically significant after correction for multiple comparisons. These findings did not establish a clear association between the measured management practices and enrollment change in this sample. Retrospective reporting and limited information on institutional circumstances constrain interpretation. The study contributes evidence on university management in a region where institutional data remain scarce. Prospective research should examine how specific practices relate to student retention, progression, and access to services, which would provide a more direct basis for assessing educational continuity during future disruptions.

title: Explaining the Factors Influencing Cyberbullyin g among Secondary School Students in the Post-COVID-19 Era: A Systematic Review
abstract: Background : Cyberbullying among secondary school adolescents, particularly in the context of social and cultural transformations following the COVID-19 pandemic, has become a significant challenge for mental health systems and educational settings. The aim of this study was to identify and synthesize the factors influencing cyberbullying among secondary school students in the post-pandemic era. Methods : This study is a systematic review with an analytical approach conducted in accordance with the PRISMA 2020 guidelines. A comprehensive systematic search was performed in both national and international databases between 2019 and 2026. After screening and quality assessment of the studies, 16 relevant articles were included in the final analysis. Data were categorized and analyzed into four main domains, including individual, family, socio-cultural, and technological factors. Results : Findings indicated that cyberbullying is a multifactorial phenomenon influenced by variables such as gender, neurodevelopmental disorders, quality of family support, school climate, cultural values

title: Understanding Poverty Dynamics and Household Vulnerability in Urban Slums of Purulia (India) across the Pre and Post COVID-19 Periods
abstract: Abstract COVID-19 has intensified urban poverty, disproportionately impacting informal workers, migrants, and slum dwellers due to job losses, reduced incomes, and limited access to social safety nets. The pandemic underscored structural inequalities such as inadequate housing, healthcare, and education. Assessing its impact is crucial to identifying vulnerable populations, designing targeted relief measures, and promoting sustainable urban development. This study evaluates the impact of COVID-19 on poverty dynamics across slums in Purulia, India, comparing pre- and post-pandemic periods through a questionnaire survey. ANOVA and a multinomial logit (MNL) model are used to examine variations in poverty among different worker groups and identify key influencing factors. Findings revealed significant disparities in poverty metrics such as the headcount ratio (HCR) and poverty gap ratio (PGR). Slums like Sufalpally and Bhagabandhpara exhibited the highest PGR (0.010 and 0.008, respectively). Peri-urban and mixed-development slums had higher HCR and PGR, while urban core slums like Bhagabandhpara showed pronounced income inequality. During the pandemic, over 50% of households in Sufalpally were classified as poor, followed by Sekrapara, Simuldanga, and Kasaimahalla. The study also highlighted substantial occupational shifts, with chronically poor households predominantly engaged in manual labour. Key factors influencing poverty dynamics included household monthly income, education level, and employment status. Addressing slum poverty is vital to mitigate vulnerabilities, improve access to essential services, and reduce urban inequalities, contributing to equitable pandemic recovery and resilient urban systems.

title: COVID-19 in the Village
abstract: Abstract This chapter examines why frontline health workers played such uneven roles in India’s rural COVID-19 response. Focusing on Accredited Social Health Activists, Anganwadi workers, and Auxiliary Nurse Midwives, it conceptualizes frontline workers as hybrid actors positioned between local communities and the state. Drawing on interviews with workers and officials, a multistate survey, and grassroots video documentation, the chapter shows that pandemic responses rose or fell with hybrid actors’ social standing and institutional support. Many frontline health workers were doubly constrained—by weak backing from state agencies and by entrenched inequalities of caste, class, and gender—leaving them exposed, overburdened, and unable to deliver reliable care or welfare. Others were doubly empowered, combining bureaucratic authority with community trust, and so were able to mobilize resources, enforce public health measures, and extend assistance more equitably. The chapter argues that inequalities affecting frontline workers are a central but overlooked feature of crisis response and identifies the conditions under which local intermediaries might reduce, rather than reproduce, social exclusion.

title: Evaluation of Gene Xpert Xpress System for Detecting SARS-CoV-2 in Suspected Clinical Samples
abstract: Background: The emergence of SARS-CoV-2 caused a global COVID-19 pandemic, necessitating rapid and accurate diagnostic tools, especially in resource-limited settings. Materials and methods: This cross-sectional study evaluated the diagnostic performance of the fully automated Gene Xpert Xpress SARS-CoV-2 assay compared to conventional real-time RT-PCR (Gold standard) using nasopharyngeal swabs from 105 suspected COVID-19 patients at BITID, Bangladesh from December 20 to December 21. Results: Of the 105 samples, 65 (61.9%) were RT-PCR positive and 40 (38.1%) were negative. The Gene Xpert Xpress detected 62/65 positives (sensitivity 95.4%) and 32/40 negatives (Specificity 80.0%) yielding an overall accuracy of 89.5%. Discordant results were mainly attributed to differences in limit of detection and Ct value interpretation. Conclusion: The Gene Xpert Xpress system demonstrated high sensitivity, rapid results (~45 minutes) minimal training requirements and suitability for decentralized settings, making it a valuable tool for timely SARS-CoV-2 detection and clinical decision-making in emergency situations and low-resource environments. IAHS Medical Journal Vol 9(1), June 2026; 4-8

title: Dual-Format Plasmonic Biosensors for the Detection of SARS-CoV-2 and the Oxidative Stress Biomarker sNOX2-dp
abstract: Abstract The integrated surveillance, combining wastewater-based epidemiology (WBE) with clinical biomarker detection, is a game-changer approach to give a big-picture view of human health in large areas. In the present study, we introduce and evaluate 2 plasmonic biosensing architectures specifically designed for detecting two analytical targets relevant for integrated surveillance: the SARS-CoV-2 Spike protein and the sNOX2-derived peptide (sNOX2-dp). The former is an analytical target for SARS-CoV-2 virus in different matrices; the latter is a biomarker of oxidative stress. It is one of the physiological responses to SARS-CoV-2 infection, crucial for SARS-CoV-2-positive individuals with severe symptoms or thrombotic complications. The two distinct biosensing architectures are plasmonic optical transducers based on gold nanorods (AuNRs), functionalized with monoclonal antibodies. They are designed to recognize and quantify SARS-CoV-2 Spike protein or sNOX2-dp from the shift of AuNR longitudinal plasmon band wavelength. For both the analytical targets, we realize and characterize AuNR-based optical probes in two distinct configurations: on a solid support (AuNR arrays) and as colloidal dispersion (AuNR bioconjugates). After screening AuNR array and bioconjugate-based sensors as a function of morphology and preparation conditions, we assess their quantitative detection performance for the respective targets. Array-based sensors exhibited lower limits of blank compared to their colloidal counterparts, both toward the SARS-CoV-2 Spike protein (0.39 ng mL−1) and toward sNOX2-dp (0.96 μg mL−1), however bioconjugates exhibited specificity and fast response time. A head-to-head comparison highlights AuNR arrays as optimal for high sensitivity and cost-efficient environmental and clinical monitoring, whereas AuNR bioconjugates enable faster and specific analytical response suitable for point-of-care applications. Overall, this adaptable plasmonic platform bridges WBE and clinical diagnostics, enabling scalable infectious disease surveillance and prevention across a wide concentration range.

title: Genome-scale eCLIP mapping of SARS-CoV-2 RNA interactions with NSP8, NSP12, and N reveals regulatory sites
abstract: Abstract The global impact of the COVID-19 pandemic highlights the need for a deeper understanding of SARS-CoV-2 replication. Although the essential roles of the RNA-dependent RNA polymerase (NSP12), primase (NSP8), and nucleocapsid (N) proteins are established, their contact points with the full-length viral RNA genome during active infection require further characterization. Here, we used enhanced crosslinking and immunoprecipitation (eCLIP) to map direct interactions of NSP8, NSP12, and N across the SARS-CoV-2 genome during live virus infection at early and late stages of replication. We mapped NSP8 and NSP12 binding to the 5′ and 3′ ends of positive- and negative-sense RNA, consistent with their roles in viral replication, transcription, and translation. We also observed an NSP12 binding site within the conserved Y1 domain of NSP3 that modulates RNA and protein abundance. In addition, N binds the 5′ untranslated region (UTR), supporting a role in translational regulation early in infection, and associates with the frameshift element, where it modulates ribosomal frameshifting. Together, these findings map SARS-CoV-2 RNA–protein interactions across the viral genome and delineate specific regulatory regions for potential antiviral intervention.

title: Rural–Urban Gaps in Working From Home During COVID ‐19
abstract: ABSTRACT The coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID‐19) pandemic exposed and intensified the long‐standing geographic divide in access to digital infrastructure and flexible work arrangements. Using 25 months of data from the Current Population Survey (May 2020–May 2022), this study examines how working from home (WFH) due to the pandemic differed between rural and urban workers and whether these differences varied by employment characteristics and industry. We find a large and persistent rural–urban WFH gap due to the COVID‐19 pandemic that remains even after accounting for worker, job, household, and contextual factors. Full‐time workers, wage workers, and those employed in high‐WFH industries were more likely to work remotely overall. However, rural workers in these categories were less likely to WFH. Interaction models and predicted probabilities show that rural full‐time workers experienced less pandemic‐related WFH than their urban counterparts, and the rural–urban gap in Finance was slightly more pronounced than expected based on rurality or industry alone. Patterns among the self‐employed showed a consistent rural disadvantage. These findings suggest that broadband access is necessary but not sufficient for enabling remote work in rural areas; the structure of rural labor markets also limits the feasibility of WFH. Documenting both the persistence and variation in this pandemic‐specific rural WFH gap shows how digital infrastructure and job composition jointly shaped remote work opportunities during the pandemic.

title: The Role of Artificial Neural Networks Techniques in the Fight Against COVID-19: A Review
abstract: This review presents an overview of the current public health emergency and the development of Artificial Neural Network techniques incorporation with medical imaging, such as chest computed tomography images and chest X-rays. Recent observations suggest that many medical researchers are increasingly employed modern computational methods to combat the spread of coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) worldwide. These methods can be divided into six directions of focus: screening, detection, diagnosis, classification, drug repurposing, and disease prediction & forecasting. This research suggests critical reviews and summarizes key studies that analyze the techniques used in these six directions of combating COVID-19, which include hybrid Artificial Neural Network models, cross-dataset validation, and integrating these technologies into clinical practice. It provides a comprehensive survey of the effect of Artificial Neural Networks in healthcare during the COVID-19 pandemic. Various Artificial Neural Network techniques have been used to enhance and expedite COVID-19 diagnostics, ultimately aiming to reduce the severity of symptoms through early detection and assessment of infection rates. In the literature retrieval process for this review, 130 research papers were taken; from this collection of papers, 10 papers that did not contain useful information were excluded, and 120 papers very relevant to our review analytics were included. This research was divided according to its direction of work; the relevant studies were sourced from multiple citation databases, including Elsevier, ScienceDirect, Google Scholar, Springer, ResearchGate, and IEEE Preprints. The review concluded that among the 120 studies related to Covid-19, 62.5% utilized Convolutional Neural Network models, 9.2% employed Recurrent Neural Networks, 7.5% used Support Vector Machines, 3.3% applied Radial Basis Functions, and 17.5% implemented various other types of machine learning models.

title: Estrategias de rehabilitación en pacientes con secuelas respiratorias post COVID-19 en América Latina. Rehabilitation Strategies for Patients with Post-COVID-19 Respiratory Sequelae in Latin America
abstract: The sequelae of COVID-19 have had a profound effect on the health of millions of patients, causing problems ranging from respiratory alterations and muscle weakness to psychological disorders. These sequelae are highly heterogeneous and negatively affect multiple biological systems, although dyspnea is a frequent symptom. The objective of our study was to analyze the impact of rehabilitation strategies in patients with post-COVID-19 respiratory sequelae in the southern region of Manabí. Strategy: A descriptive study with a documentary design was conducted through a systematic literature review. Results: The results show that dyspnea was the most frequently reported symptom, appearing in six of the ten studies analyzed. After dyspnea, decreased lung capacity, persistent cough, and functional alterations in the respiratory system were also found. Some of the most common strategies include early mobilization, breathing exercises, therapeutic education, progressive physical training, respiratory physiotherapy, pulmonary rehabilitation, muscle strengthening, and bronchial hygiene techniques. Conclusion: These results support the application of personalized and early respiratory rehabilitation protocols as part of the comprehensive care of patients with post-COVID-19 sequelae, particularly in healthcare facilities in southern Manabí.

title: TRATAMENTO JURÍDICO DA MIGRAÇÃO VENEZUELANA NO BRASIL DURANTE A PANDEMIA DE COVID-19: FRONTEIRAS, NÃO DEVOLUÇÃO E ACESSO A DIREITOS EM RORAIMA THE LEGAL TREATMENT OF VENEZUELAN MIGRATION IN BRAZIL DURING THE COVID-19 PANDEMIC: BORDERS, NON-REFOULEMENT AND ACCESS TO RIGHTS IN RORAIMA TRATAMIENTO JURÍDICO DE LA MIGRACIÓN VENEZOLANA EN BRASIL DURANTE LA PANDEMIA DE COVID-19: FRONTERAS, NO DEVOLUCIÓN Y ACCESO A DERECHOS EN RORAIMA
abstract: O artigo analisa em que medida as restrições migratórias e sanitárias adotadas pelo Brasil durante a pandemia de COVID-19 foram compatíveis com a Constituição Federal, a Lei de Migração, a Lei de Refúgio e os parâmetros interamericanos de direitos humanos, com atenção à fronteira de Pacaraima e ao estado de Roraima. Desenvolve-se pesquisa qualitativa, exploratória, bibliográfica e documental, mediante análise de legislação, portarias interministeriais editadas entre março de 2020 e abril de 2022, documentos da Defensoria Pública da União, atos do Tribunal de Justiça de Roraima, jurisprudência do Superior Tribunal de Justiça, relatórios da Comissão Interamericana de Direitos Humanos e artigos científicos indexados. Os resultados demonstram que a proteção sanitária constituía finalidade legítima, mas não autorizava exclusões baseadas em nacionalidade, retirada compulsória automática, impedimento genérico de solicitação de refúgio ou supressão do devido processo. A diferenciação expressa aplicada a pessoas provenientes da Venezuela e a interrupção prolongada das vias de regularização ampliaram vulnerabilidades documentais, sociais e institucionais. Conclui-se que a resposta estatal deveria ter combinado controle epidemiológico, avaliação individualizada, não devolução, assistência jurídica, regularização migratória e serviços públicos interculturais, sem converter a emergência sanitária em mecanismo permanente de seleção migratória.

title: Prevalence of Stress, Anxiety and Depression Among Home-Isolation COVID-19 Patients in Kathmandu Valley, Nepal
abstract: COVID-19 resulted in a dedication to both physical and mental health, with infected people experiencing home isolation as the main impact. The coronavirus outbreaks, together with COVID-19 pandemic research, show that people who experience isolation while they fear disease spread and face uncertainty with misinformation face increased stress, anxiety, and depression symptoms. The study measured stress, anxiety and depression symptoms among home-isolated COVID-19 patients in Kathmandu Valley. The research used a cross-sectional study design to examine 425 COVID-19 patients who were in home isolation throughout Kathmandu Valley. The researchers collected data through telephone interviews between 30 April and 21 May 2021 using the Nepali version of the Depression Anxiety Stress Scales-21 (DASS-21). The researchers used descriptive statistics to identify stress, anxiety and depression, and Pearson Product Moment Correlation was used to examine relationships between psychological variables (i.e., stress, anxiety and depression) and multiple linear regression analysis to find demographic factors that predict psychological outcomes. The participants had stress (66.8%), anxiety symptoms (57.2%), and depression symptoms (33.2%). Participants showed severe or extremely severe symptoms for stress at a rate of 14.8% and for anxiety at 10.0% and for depression at 6.0%. The researchers found a positive correlation between stress, anxiety, and depression, while the strongest relationship existed between anxiety and depression, which resulted in a correlation coefficient of r = 0.805 and a statistical significance of p < 0.01. The researchers found that age and education level were supporting factors for stress levels, while age, gender, income level and education level predicted anxiety and depression levels. The psychological distress level among home-isolated COVID-19 patients in Kathmandu Valley reached a significant level. Home-isolation and pandemic response strategies need to include mental health screening together with telephone counselling and accurate risk communication and targeted psychosocial support.

title: Self-DNA-induced inflammation and related clinical manifestations: Lessons from coronavirus disease 2019
abstract: In 2020, the author proposed the hypothesis that free DNA present in the cytoplasm or circulating blood may induce severe coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19), which is consistent with multiple specific clinical phenotypes reported during the COVID-19 outbreak.At that time, only a few months after the pandemic was first reported, the majority of the proposed associations and mechanistic insights regarding DNA sensors, their pathways and related biomarkers in COVID-19 had not yet been published.To date, a large number of population-based and fundamental studies have indicated that DNA sensor-mediated immune responses are involved in disease progression.This review synthesizes recent evidence to support the author's hypothesis that the self-DNA axis acts as a common driver of many pathways promoting inflammatory responses and inducing multiple organ damage in COVID-19, thereby affecting disease prognosis.This work may modestly contribute to the improved understanding of the potential role of self-DNA in severe and sustained inflammation, and elucidate its association with relevant clinical manifestations in multiple fatal infectious diseases.

title: COVID-19 immune history and post-PRP injection reactions in knee osteoarthritis
abstract: Background: Intra-articular platelet-rich plasma (PRP) is a widely used orthobiologic treatment for knee osteoarthritis (OA). Whether COVID-19 vaccination history or prior SARS-CoV-2 infection influences local post-injection reactions has not been studied. Methods: This exploratory retrospective cohort study included 57 patients who underwent 166 intra-articular PRP injection sessions for knee OA (March 2024–January 2026). Two per-patient outcomes were defined: pain rate (proportion of sessions with VAS pain>0) and swelling rate (proportion of sessions with recorded swelling). Patients with a single injection and no follow-up were excluded. Four Spearman correlations between vaccination dose count, prior infection count, and both outcomes were computed with bootstrapped 95% BCa confidence intervals (1,000 samples) and Holm correction applied across the four p values. Subgroup analyses used the Kruskal-Wallis test. The analytical sample comprised 40 complete cases. Results: All quantitative variables except age were non-normally distributed (Shapiro-Wilk p 0) occurred in 20 of 72 assessed sessions (27.8%); swelling in 8 of 75 (10.7%). No febrile reactions were documented. Conclusions: Prior SARS-CoV-2 infection count showed a directional inverse association with post-PRP swelling rate that did not survive Holm correction for multiple comparisons. These findings are exploratory and hypothesis-generating only, and do not support clinical recommendations at this stage.

title: Riesgos laborales en profesionales de la salud bucal durante la pandemia de COVID-19: revisión sistemática Occupational risks among oral health professionals during the COVID-19 pandemic: a systematic review
abstract: Objetivo: sintetizar la evidencia sobre los riesgos laborales de los profesionales de la salud bucal durante la pandemia de COVID-19 y las medidas propuestas para controlarlos. Método: revisión sistemática con síntesis narrativa en PubMed y SciELO (2012-2025); se incluyeron 15 estudios: revisiones, ensayos clínicos, estudios transversales y retrospectivos. Resultados: el riesgo biológico por aerosoles, gotas y contacto estrecho fue el principal riesgo descrito, seguido de las exposiciones a sangre y punzocortantes y del riesgo psicosocial, con agotamiento profesional y percepción elevada de riesgo. Las medidas incluyeron triaje, equipos de protección, control de aerosoles y colutorios previos al procedimiento. Conclusión: la pandemia aumentó y diversificó los riesgos laborales en odontología, por lo que se requieren protocolos permanentes de bioseguridad y de protección de la salud mental.

title: COVID-19 in the States
abstract: Abstract This chapter analyzes how the COVID-19 pandemic tested democratic capabilities at the subnational level. It argues that the crisis exposed not only core dimensions of state capacity but also the relational forms of power needed to secure public cooperation in highly unequal societies. It shows that national-level analyses overlook these dynamics by focusing narrowly on formal democracy and fixed bureaucratic resources, whereas the subnational level better captures how state agencies interact with civil society to coordinate high-touch health and welfare responses. It explains why state governments in India became the central actors during the pandemic and how political competition, state–society relations, and local institutions shaped state performance in health and welfare responses. These factors were key in mobilizing resources, inducing compliance, and mitigating inequalities. In doing so, the chapter demonstrates that subnational democratic capabilities are critical both for crisis response and for strengthening equitable state action more broadly.

title: Travel Intention and Avoidance Among Generation Z During the COVID-19 Pandemic: A Behavioural Segmentation Study in Greece
abstract: This study examines holiday-related attitudes and heterogeneous behavioural responses among Greek Generation Z during the COVID-19 pandemic. The data originate from a broader cross-sectional survey of 2364 respondents conducted in Greece during May–July 2020; the present cohort-specific secondary analysis focuses on the 1287 Generation Z respondents, of whom 701 (54.5%) intended to take holidays and 586 (45.5%) did not. Principal component analysis was used to identify attitudinal dimensions separately for the two groups, hierarchical and k-means cluster analysis was used to derive behavioural segments, quadratic discriminant analysis was used to examine internal classification consistency, and exploratory Pearson chi-square tests were used to examine between-cluster demographic associations, with effect sizes and correction for multiple testing. Among travel-intending respondents, three factors emerged: entertainment out of the hotel, eating in the hotel, and personally organised entertainment activities; the corresponding segments were Ambivalent, Bon Viveurs, and Audacious. Among travel-avoiding respondents, the main factors concerned the perceived effectiveness of COVID-19 prevention measures, economic reasons, and other family reasons; the corresponding segments were Conscious, Provident, and Opportunists. By examining the two travel-intention groups within the same questionnaire-defined age cohort, the study identifies distinct combinations of leisure preferences, perceived safety concerns, economic constraints, and family considerations that are not separately resolved in the earlier, age-heterogeneous analyses of the parent survey. These exploratory findings concern stated intentions during the COVID-19 period rather than subsequent observed travel behaviour.

title: Experimental Screening and Kinetic Characterization of Natural SARS-CoV-2 3CLpro Inhibitors with Cell-Based Antiviral Evaluation
abstract: The SARS-CoV-2 main protease (3CLpro) is a key antiviral target essential for viral replication. In this study, a fully experimental screening of a 384-compound natural product library was performed using an optimized FRET-based assay to identify SARS-CoV-2 3CLpro inhibitors. Twenty-four compounds showing >50% inhibition at 25 μM underwent dose–response analysis, revealing several low-micromolar inhibitors. Six lead compounds were further characterized through steady-state kinetic analysis, demonstrating competitive, uncompetitive, mixed-type, and possible irreversible inhibition mechanisms, together with Ki determination. To establish their biological relevance, eight selected compounds were subsequently evaluated in Vero E6 cells for cytotoxicity and antiviral activity against the SARS-CoV-2 Omicron variant. RT-qPCR analysis revealed moderate reductions in viral RNA levels for several compounds under non-cytotoxic conditions, supporting a correlation between enzymatic inhibition and antiviral activity. Overall, this study provides a comprehensive experimental dataset for natural SARS-CoV-2 3CLpro inhibitors and highlights promising hit compounds for future antiviral development.

title: A matched-cohort study of treatment-requiring autoimmune rheumatic diseases after COVID-19
abstract: Post-coronavirus disease-2019 (COVID-19) symptoms can resemble autoimmune and inflammatory rheumatic diseases (AIIRDs), and claims-based studies using diagnosis codes alone may misclassify transient or uncertain diagnoses. The combination of an AIIRD diagnosis and initiated disease-relevant therapy may more accurately identify patients requiring treatment. We aimed to determine whether a history of COVID-19 was associated with a higher 1-year incidence of treatment-requiring AIIRDs compared to matched individuals without COVID-19. We conducted a matched cohort study using the nationwide JMDC Claims Database in Japan, including inpatient, outpatient, and pharmacy data, from July 1, 2019, to August 31, 2023, with 12 months of observation after the index month. Individuals with confirmed COVID-19 and at least 12 months of claims data after the index month were matched 1:1 to individuals without COVID-19 on age, sex, severe-disease risk factors, and Charlson Comorbidity Index; individuals with COVID-19 or AIIRDs in the previous 6 months were excluded. The matched cohorts included 770,498 participants each, and the matched analysis population included 764,454 participants per group. The primary outcome was incident treatment-requiring AIIRD within 12 months, defined by an AIIRD diagnosis code plus initiation of immunosuppressants and/or disease-specific medications. The secondary outcome was AIIRD-related hospitalization. Risk differences and risk ratios with 95% confidence intervals were estimated. Among 1,528,908 participants, incident treatment-requiring AIIRDs occurred in 1,591 individuals (0.21%) with COVID-19 vs. 817 (0.11%) in those without COVID-19 (risk difference, 0.101% points [95% CI, 0.089–0.114]; risk ratio [RR], 1.95 [95% CI, 1.79–2.12]). AIIRD-related hospitalization occurred in 283 individuals (0.037%) with COVID-19 vs. 15 (0.002%) in those without COVID-19 (risk difference, 0.035% points [95% CI, 0.031–0.039]; RR, 18.87 [95% CI, 11.22–31.71]). In diagnosis-specific analyses, notably, risks were higher for rheumatoid arthritis (RR, 1.92 [95% CI, 1.71–2.15]), Sjögren’s syndrome (RR, 1.49 [95% CI, 1.24–1.79]), and antineutrophil cytoplasmic antibody-associated vasculitis (RR, 4.90 [95% CI, 2.48–9.67]). This study revealed a higher 1-year incidence of treatment-requiring AIIRDs and markedly higher AIIRD-related hospitalization associated with COVID-19. These findings support clinical vigilance for inflammatory rheumatic disease requiring treatment after COVID-19.

AIIRD-related hospitalization occurred in 283 individuals (0.037%) with COVID-19 vs. 15 (0.002%) in those without COVID-19 (risk difference, 0.035% points [95% CI, 0.031–0.039]; RR, 18.87 [95% CI, 11.22–31.71]). In diagnosis-specific analyses, notably, risks were higher for rheumatoid arthritis (RR, 1.92 [95% CI, 1.71–2.15]), Sjögren’s syndrome (RR, 1.49 [95% CI, 1.24–1.79]), and antineutrophil cytoplasmic antibody-associated vasculitis (RR, 4.90 [95% CI, 2.48–9.67]). This study revealed a higher 1-year incidence of treatment-requiring AIIRDs and markedly higher AIIRD-related hospitalization associated with COVID-19. These findings support clinical vigilance for inflammatory rheumatic disease requiring treatment after COVID-19.
