title: Reconsidering the COVID-19 pandemic as a global mental health crisis
abstract: Early in the COVID-19 pandemic, concerns were raised about a potential global mental health crisis, particularly among groups presumed to be vulnerable, such as healthcare workers (HCWs) and individuals with pre-existing mental disorders. These concerns were largely based on evidence from previous epidemics and expectations of widespread psychological consequences resulting from prolonged exposure to health threats and societal disruption. However, as longitudinal evidence accumulated, a more nuanced picture emerged, revealing substantial variation in mental health responses. This challenged the assumption that pandemic-related stressors would uniformly lead to adverse mental health outcomes and highlighted the need to better understand differences in exposure to stressors and in mental health outcomes between and within populations. This dissertation examined mental health during the COVID-19 pandemic among HCWs and individuals with pre-existing mental disorders, with the aim of understanding how mental health outcomes were shaped by the interplay between pre-existing vulnerabilities and pandemic-related stressors. Mental health in these populations was considered relative to the general population, providing broader context for interpreting patterns of risk and resilience. Chapters two to four focused on HCWs across multiple countries. In a Dutch cohort, worries about infection were consistently linked to poorer mental health, whereas most objective pandemic-related stressors showed no association. Perceived adequacy of personal protective equipment was linked to better mental health, underscoring the importance of perceived safety and control. A multinational study involving more than 32,000 HCWs across 22 countries demonstrated that women reported poorer mental health than men and were more frequently exposed to pandemic-related stressors, including insufficient protective equipment, stigma, discrimination and lower collegial support. These findings suggested that occupational roles and broader structural inequalities may partly explain gender disparities in mental health. Findings from the same multinational cohort additionally indicated that greater trust in the workplace and government was associated with a lower likelihood of depressive symptoms, underscoring the importance of institutional trust during large-scale crises. Importantly, while this pattern was observed across countries, its strength varied substantially between national settings, suggesting that the relevance of institutional trust is shaped by national and organisational contexts. Chapters five and six examined individuals with pre-existing mental disorders. Longitudinal analyses incorporating pre-pandemic measurements showed that mental health trajectories during the pandemic were predominantly characterised by stability or improvement rather than deterioration, both among individuals with pre-existing mental disorders and in the general population. Sociodemographic characteristics were more strongly associated with symptom trajectories than most pandemic-related stressors. A literature review across psychiatric disorders revealed considerable heterogeneity in outcomes. While symptom worsening was most common in eating disorders and contamination-related obsessive-compulsive symptoms, many other disorders showed stable or improving trajectories. Moreover, individuals with more chronic or severe pre-pandemic symptom profiles often exhibited stable or improving trajectories, indicating that a high pre-pandemic symptom burden was not invariably associated with adverse mental health outcomes during the pandemic. The final chapter integrated these findings within psychological and ecological frameworks. Across populations, heterogeneity emerged as the central pattern, with substantial variation observed even among groups typically considered vulnerable. The findings suggest that differences in subjective appraisals, individual characteristics and broader social and structural conditions contribute to divergent mental health responses in the face of similar stressors. Vulnerability is therefore better understood as a dynamic and context-dependent process rather than a fixed characteristic of specific populations. Overall, this dissertation indicates that the COVID-19 pandemic is best understood not as a crisis with uniformly detrimental mental health effects, but as a context in which mental health outcomes varied considerably according to the interaction between pre-existing individual and structural vulnerabilities and pandemic-related stressors.

title: Exploring Topics Trending on Twitter Amid the COVID-19 Pandemic
abstract: Twitter (X) served as an important venue for public discourse during the COVID-19 pandemic, including conversations occurring alongside major contemporaneous news events. This study descriptively compares prospectively collected COVID-19-centric Twitter data from four news-event days: the 2020 U.S. Presidential Election, the Pfizer-BioNTech vaccine efficacy announcement, the U.S. Capitol takeover, and the opening day of the second Senate impeachment trial of Donald J. A consistent search strategy using “COVID,” “COVID19,” or “coronavirus” was applied across all four collection periods. Social network analysis, lexicon-based sentiment analysis, word-frequency analysis, term frequency–inverse document frequency (tf-idf), bigram analysis, and word co-occurrence analysis were used to compare network structure and textual patterns. The four topic days differed in user-network organization, sentiment patterns, distinctive vocabulary, and word relationships. Vaccine News displayed comparatively positive sentiment patterns, whereas Capitol Takeover exhibited the strongest negative cumulative AFINN sentiment trend. Event-related vocabulary also emerged within the COVID-19-centric conversations, while Second Impeachment showed less distinct event-specific lexical differentiation. Together, the findings demonstrate the utility of combining complementary computational methods to descriptively characterize short-term social-media discourse across contrasting contemporaneous news contexts.

title: Adherence to Subcutaneous Immunotherapy (SCIT) During the COVID-19 Pandemic: The Impact of Anxiety and Depression
abstract: Objective: Allergen immunotherapy (AIT) is a cornerstone treatment for IgE-mediated allergic diseases and adherence to subcutaneous immunotherapy (SCIT) is essential for achieving optimal therapeutic outcomes. We aimed to evaluate SCIT adherence, identify the primary causes of treatment interruption, and investigate the relationship between anxiety/depression and SCIT adherence during the COVID-19 pandemic. Materials and Methods: This retrospective observational study included 191 patients underwent SCIT at a university allergy and immunology clinic between February 2021 and January 2022. Data were collected through structured face-to-face questionnaires assessing demographic characteristics, treatment duration, allergen type, comorbidities, SCIT interruption status, reasons for interruption, and symptom exacerbation. We evaluated the psychological status via the Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale (HADS). Results: The mean age of participants was 35.9 ± 11.2 years, and 52.9% were female. A total of 70 patients (36.8%) interrupted SCIT during the pandemic. Analysis by allergen type revealed a statistically significant difference between pollen and mite groups (p < 0.001), whereas no significant differences were observed between venom and pollen or mite groups. Significant differences were identified between patients treated for ≤1 year and those receiving longer treatment durations (p < 0.05). However, no significant difference was found between treatment durations of 1–2 years and ≥3 years. These findings suggest that treatment duration has a more pronounced impact within the first year, while outcomes tend to converge with longer treatment periods. The most common reasons for treatment interruption were access difficulties (52.9%) and fear of infection (35%). Conclusion: Approximately one-third of patients discontinued SCIT treatment during the COVID-19 pandemic, primarily due to access-related challenges. Female gender and mite allergen immunotherapy were associated with higher rates of non-adherence.

title: Impacto de las secuelas respiratorias y cardiovasculares post COVID-19 en poblaciones vulnerables. Impact of post-COVID-19 respiratory and cardiovascular aftereffects on vulnerable populations.
abstract: Introducción: La condición post COVID-19 puede generar manifestaciones persistentes que afectan principalmente los sistemas respiratorio y cardiovascular, limitando la recuperación funcional y la calidad de vida, especialmente en poblaciones vulnerables. Objetivo: Identificar las secuelas respiratorias y cardiovasculares posteriores al COVID-19 en pacientes vulnerables. Material y Métodos: El tipo de estudio que presentamos es de revisión con enfoque descriptivo y diseño documental. Se realizaron Artículos originales, revisiones bibliográficas, revisiones sistemáticas, meta análisis y documentos científicos, publicados entre el año 20 22 al 20 26, en idioma español, inglés y portugués. Resultados: Las principales secuelas respiratorias reportadas fueron disnea, tos seca o persistente, sensación de falta de aire, baja tolerancia respiratoria, fatiga cansancio, intolerancia al ejercicio físico, atrapamiento de aire, neumonía secundaria y fibrosis pulmonar. Cardiovasculares: miocarditis, Arritmias, insuficiencia cardiaca congestiva, dolor en pecho, palpitaciones, pericarditis y eventos tromboembólicos. Asimismo se pudo apreciar que la edad mayor a 60 años, hipertensión arterial, Diabetes mellitus, obesidad, tabaquismo, estancia hospitalaria prolongada y poco acceso a controles luego del alta son factores relacionados a tener secuelas posteriores a presentar el virus. Conclusiones: Las secuelas por el pasar COVID deben ser evaluadas por un control clínico estrecho, rehabilitación pulmonar y control cardiovascular que permitan tener un mejor pronóstico de vida en pacientes de riesgo.

title: Factores psicológicos y estrés post pandemia COVID-19 en adultos de América Latina. Psychological factors and stress after the COVID-19 pandemic in adults in Latin America.
abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic brought about consequences extending beyond the health crisis itself, particularly affecting the mental health of the adult population in Latin America—a region where structural inequalities and healthcare deficiencies exacerbated the emotional impact of lockdowns, economic uncertainty, and the fear of infection. This study aimed to identify and analyze the psychological factors linked to stress levels experienced by adults in the region following the health emergency, utilizing a systematic literature review conducted in accordance with PRISMA guidelines. The process began with 543 records identified in databases such as PubMed, SciELO, and Elsevier, from which 30 publications covering the 2022–2026 period were selected. Findings revealed that anxiety, depression, emotional fatigue, and post-traumatic stress were the predominant manifestations, associated with social isolation, economic instability, academic and work-related overload, and low socioeconomic status. Resilience and family support served as protective factors against these manifestations. The study concludes that post-pandemic stress has a multifactorial origin and that its effects can persist over time, highlighting the need to strengthen public mental health policies for the adult population.

title: Inflammatory response and mortality indices in patients hospitalized with COVID-19 in Lima, Peru
abstract: Introduction Indices derived from hematological parameters have been proposed as simple tools for estimating severity and mortality in patients with coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19); however, their independent relationship with mortality remains uncertain in hospital environments in Peru. Methods An observational, analytical, and cross-sectional study was carried out on 116 adult patients hospitalized with confirmed COVID-19, treated at the Guillermo Almenara Irigoyen National Hospital (Lima, Perú). The association between inflammatory response (neutrophil/lymphocyte index, platelet/lymphocyte index, and lymphocyte/C-reactive protein index) and intrahospital mortality was evaluated via log-binomial regression, adjusting for clinical covariables and demographics. Results The mortality rate was 9.5% (11/116). In the bivariate analysis, the platelet/lymphocyte index was associated with mortality (raw prevalence ratio: 5.34; 95% confidence interval: 1.09–26.11); however, it did not maintain an independent association following adjustment (adjusted prevalence ratio: 2.80; 95% confidence interval: 0.31–25.71). In the multivariable model, age demonstrated a consistent association with mortality (adjusted prevalence ratio: 1.12; 95% confidence interval: 1.06–1.18), and orotracheal intubation was positively associated with the outcome (adjusted prevalence ratio: 6.88; 95% confidence interval: 1.13–41.99). Conclusion In the study, age was the main factor associated with mortality, while the evaluated inflammatory indices did not demonstrate any independent relationship with mortality in the adjusted regression model; thus, their utility would be complementary within multifactorial clinical risk models.

title: A relação entre a COVID-19 e o aumento de novos casos de diabetes tipo 1: relato de caso
abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic has had effects beyond the respiratory system, including an increased risk of type 1 diabetes mellitus (T1DM) associated with SARS-CoV-2 infection. This case report describes a young female patient with no previous history of diabetes or autoimmune diseases who presented with the classic clinical manifestations of T1DM following coronavirus infection. The patient reported polyuria, polydipsia, and weight loss several weeks after the infection. Laboratory tests were subsequently performed to confirm the diagnosis, and insulin therapy was initiated. This case supports the hypothesis that SARS-CoV-2 may trigger T1DM, possibly through pancreatic injury mediated by the interaction between the virus and angiotensin-converting enzyme 2 (ACE2), an enzyme expressed in the pancreas. Despite the suggested association, the literature has methodological limitations, including the retrospective nature of studies and the difficulty of controlling for genetic and environmental factors. The establishment of a Global Registry of COVID-19-Associated Diabetes may provide more robust data to further investigate this association.

title: Multipathway Biomarker Profiling of Immunothrombosis in Moderate and Severe COVID-19
abstract: Background/Objectives: Coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) is associated with immunothrombosis involving endothelial dysfunction and coagulation activation. We aimed to compare biomarkers spanning multiple immunothrombotic pathways between patients with moderate and severe COVID-19 at baseline and according to clinical outcome. Secondary analyses compared biomarker levels at days 3 and 7. Methods: This prospective observational study included 42 hospitalized patients with COVID-19 enrolled between April 2020 and January 2021, comprising 21 with moderate and 21 with severe disease. Biomarkers of coagulation, endothelial dysfunction, endogenous anticoagulant pathways, fibrinolysis, and extracellular vesicle-mediated activity were measured at baseline and on days 3 and 7. The prespecified ventilation/death composite included invasive mechanical ventilation already ongoing at baseline or initiated subsequently and/or death by day 28. Results: Seventeen patients (40.5%) met the composite criterion, including 12 patients already receiving invasive mechanical ventilation at baseline. At baseline, severe disease was associated with higher D-dimer (1.74 [0.87–3.67] vs. 0.68 [0.46–0.94] μg/mL FEU), free tissue factor pathway inhibitor (TFPI; 55.00 [38.00–109.00] vs. 16.00 [14.00–29.00] ng/mL), extracellular vesicle-associated tissue factor activity (EV-TF; 28.86 [13.61–48.72] vs. 5.00 [5.00–5.70] fM), and extracellular vesicle-associated plasmin generation capacity (EV-PGC; 93.36 [41.60–303.10] vs. 24.50 [16.14–35.74] fM; all p < 0.01). Exploratory ROC analyses further illustrated the separation of these biomarker distributions between the predefined clinical groups. Conclusions: Severe COVID-19 and unfavorable outcomes were associated with baseline differences in biomarkers spanning several immunothrombotic pathways, some of which remained detectable at days 3 and 7. Interpretation of the marked TFPI elevation is limited by differences in heparin exposure between severity groups. These exploratory findings require confirmation in larger cohorts, and their incremental value beyond routine clinical assessment remains untested. Outcome analyses largely reflected baseline severity, with only five subsequent events.

title: Assessment of the Association between Myocarditis (New-onset Heart Failure) and COVID-19 and COVID-19 Vaccination
abstract: Introduction: Myocarditis is a rare but significant cardiovascular complication that may occur after receiving COVID-19 vaccines, particularly in younger individuals. The majority of cases have been reported after receiving mRNA-based vaccines, while inactivated and viral vector-based vaccines have been associated with fewer occurrences. Despite this, myocarditis is much more common and results in a poorer prognosis following COVID-19 infection. However, the relationship between myocarditis post-vaccination and its potential mechanisms remains unclear due to limited information. Methods: This study investigated patients with myocarditis (new-onset heart failure) who had received the COVID-19 vaccine and those who had been infected with COVID-19 between March 2021 and March 2023 in Farshchian Cardiovascular Hospital in Hamedan. The data was analyzed using Stata version 14 software and Python. Results: Among 146 myocarditis patients, unvaccinated individuals had higher rates of hypertension, diabetes, obstructive pulmonary disease, and substance abuse, and exhibited more severe cardiac issues like mitral regurgitation and ventricular dysfunction. Vaccinated patients had better lab results and fewer severe symptoms. A model identified advanced age and cardiovascular dysfunction as key mortality risks, suggesting vaccination may mitigate severe cardiac complications and improve outcomes. source_records.title: Assessment of the Association between Myocarditis (New-onset Heart Failure) and COVID-19 and COVID-19 Vaccination
source_records.abstract: Introduction: Myocarditis is a rare but significant cardiovascular complication that may occur after receiving COVID-19 vaccines, particularly in younger individuals. The majority of cases have been reported after receiving mRNA-based vaccines, while inactivated and viral vector-based vaccines have been associated with fewer occurrences. Despite this, myocarditis is much more common and results in a poorer prognosis following COVID-19 infection. However, the relationship between myocarditis post-vaccination and its potential mechanisms remains unclear due to limited information. Methods: This study investigated patients with myocarditis (new-onset heart failure) who had received the COVID-19 vaccine and those who had been infected with COVID-19 between March 2021 and March 2023 in Farshchian Cardiovascular Hospital in Hamedan. The data was analyzed using Stata version 14 software and Python. Results: Among 146 myocarditis patients, unvaccinated individuals had higher rates of hypertension, diabetes, obstructive pulmonary disease, and substance abuse, and exhibited more severe cardiac issues like mitral regurgitation and ventricular dysfunction. Vaccinated patients had better lab results and fewer severe symptoms. A model identified advanced age and cardiovascular dysfunction as key mortality risks, suggesting vaccination may mitigate severe cardiac complications and improve outcomes. title: Political Spillovers from COVID-19 Vaccine Manufacturers to Prescription Drug Acceptance
abstract: Do associations with COVID-19 vaccine manufacturers change willingness to take a new prescription drug by political background? The experiment compares a generic U.S. drugmaker (control), Pfizer (T1), and Pfizer identified as a COVID-19 mRNA vaccine manufacturer (T2). We hypothesize that those on the left will be more willing to take drug and perceive drug to be safe and effective, but that this will be shifted by experimental condition.

title: Chinese Responses to COVID-19
abstract: Abstract This chapter probes the lessons that China had learned and failed to learn during the COVID-19 pandemic. It begins by examining China’s learning from SARS and explains how SARS became the primary historical analogy for China’s COVID response in the first two months of the pandemic. The chapter then offers a historical analysis of the four phases of China’s pandemic response and identifies what was learned at the end of each phase. It argues that the most important—and problematic—lesson for the Chinese leadership was the Wuhan lockdown and its perceived effectiveness in suppressing virus transmission. Finally, it evaluates Chinese lessons in light of the propositions advanced in Chapter 2 by paying special attention to the Wuhan lockdown lesson and the zero-COVID policy it engendered.

title: Comparative Evaluation of the Inactivation of SARS-CoV-2 and Human Coronavirus 229E against Sodium Hypochlorite
abstract: Introduction: Surface disinfection is one of the important non-pharmaceutical intervention measures that help prevent the spread of Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome Coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2). Disinfectants with an efficacy claim against Human Coronavirus strain 229E (HCoV-229E) have been used for the disinfection of SARS-CoV-2; however, the comparative susceptibility of these two viruses to chemical disinfection has not been well defined. To address this, laboratory data were generated to compare the level of inactivation of human coronaviruses HCoV-229E and SARS-CoV-2 to a common antimicrobial agent, sodium hypochlorite (NaOCl), on a hard non-porous surface. Methods: A hard surface-based Quantitative Method (QM) was used to evaluate the viral inactivation efficacy by three treatments of NaOCl against HCoV-229E and SARS-CoV-2. For each treatment, viral inoculum containing soil load was applied onto a stainless steel carrier and dried. The inoculated carrier was exposed to NaOCl or a control fluid and held for five minutes. Following the exposure time, a neutralizer was added, and the sample was serially diluted and inoculated onto host cells to determine the number of infective units. The resulting Log10 of the density for control and treated carriers was used to generate Log10 reduction (LR) values for comparative statistical evaluation. Results: The mean LR ± standard error (SE) for HCoV-229E was 0.96 ± 0.09 (n=10) at 500 ppm NaOCl, 2.41 ± 0.15 (n=10) at 1,000 ppm NaOCl, and 4.54 ± 0.13 (n=10) at 1,500 ppm NaOCl. The mean LR ± SE for SARS-CoV-2 was 0.91 ± 0.24 (n=4) at 500 ppm NaOCl, 1.96 ± 0.26 (n=4) at 1,000 ppm NaOCl, and 4.23 ± 0.16 (n=4) at 1,500 ppm NaOCl. Both viruses were significantly responsive to the increasing concentrations of NaOCl. HCoV-229E had slightly higher mean LRs compared to SARS-CoV-2 at each NaOCl concentration; however, these differences were not statistically significant (p ≥ 0.067). Regression analysis using a linear mixed effects model (LMM) also indicates that the susceptibility of HCoV-229E and SARS-CoV-2 to NaOCl is comparable. Discussion: Understanding the antimicrobial tolerance of viruses can enhance public health response to viral infections. By determining the tolerance, the most appropriate antimicrobial agent can be chosen to disinfect surfaces contaminated with viral particles. Disinfection of highcontact surfaces can reduce the amount of fomite transmission and limit outbreaks. Conclusion: The data suggest that HCoV-229E and SARS-CoV-2 are statistically comparable in their susceptibility to NaOCl treatments.

title: Quasi-Periodic SEIR Modeling of COVID-19 incidence under vaccination dynamics
abstract: This work investigates the use of time-varying parameters in SEIR epidemic models to describe the temporal evolution of COVID-19 incidence data. Three models are considered: the classical SEIR model with constant parameters, a SEIR model incorporating a quasi-periodic effective progression rate, and an extended SEIR model that additionally includes a periodic vaccination function. The proposed approach is motivated by the observation that epidemic dynamics are influenced by multiple temporal factors acting at different scales, including behavioral changes, public health interventions, environmental variability, and vaccination campaigns. Model parameters were estimated from COVID-19 incidence data corresponding to the third epidemic wave in Jalisco, Mexico, using a differential evolution optimization algorithm. The results show that introducing temporal variability in the effective progression rate improves the agreement between the model and the reported data. Furthermore, the inclusion of a vaccination mechanism yields a substantial reduction in the fitting error. The proposed framework demonstrates that quasi-periodic and periodic parameterizations provide a flexible and effective approach for capturing complex epidemic dynamics and improving the description of observed incidence patterns.
journal: International Journal of Modern Physics C

title: Beyond Infection Control: Multidimensional Unmet Needs and Health-System Gaps During the COVID-19 Pandemic in India—A Convergent Mixed-Method Study
abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic created widespread disruptions extending beyond infection-related health concerns, affecting economic stability, nutrition, mental health, education, social well-being, and access to essential healthcare. This study examined multidimensional unmet needs and health-system gaps experienced by adults in India during the COVID-19 pandemic, assessed associations between selected sociodemographic characteristics and major unmet needs, and integrated quantitative and qualitative findings to contextualize pandemic-related vulnerabilities and health-system disruptions. A convergent mixed-method design was employed. Quantitative data were collected through a web-based cross-sectional survey between December 2021 and January 2022 using convenience and snowball sampling, with 958 adults completing the survey. A structured questionnaire assessed unmet needs across eight domains: economic, nutritional, social, spiritual, mental health, preventive, childcare, and healthcare. Descriptive statistics and Pearson’s chi-square tests examined unmet needs and associations with psychological stress, job or salary disruption, children’s learning difficulties, and difficulty accessing routine healthcare. Twenty information-rich open-ended responses were purposively selected for inductive thematic analysis, and findings were integrated through side-by-side comparison. title: Growth and neurodevelopmental outcomes of infants born to mothers with covid-19 during pregnancy
abstract: Aims: To evaluate the impact of intrauterine SARS-CoV-2 exposure on infant growth and neurodevelopment by comparing anthropometric measurements and Denver Developmental Screening Test II (DDST-II) results between infants born to mothers with COVID-19 during pregnancy and unexposed controls. Methods: This retrospective case-control study included 40 term infants born to mothers with confirmed COVID-19 during pregnancy and 40 term infants born to mothers without COVID-19. Well-child follow-up records from July 2020 to July 2022 were reviewed. Demographic characteristics, anthropometric measurements, and DDST-II results were analyzed. Results: The groups were comparable regarding demographic characteristics, birth weight, gestational age, and sex (all p>0.05). In the study group, 45% of mothers had COVID-19 during the third trimester. At one month, head circumference, length, and weight percentiles were similar between groups. At six months, head circumference below the third percentile was more common in the exposed group (22.2% vs. 3.6%, p=0.045), whereas length and weight percentiles did not differ. No significant differences were observed in anthropometric measurements at nine months. DDST-II showed age-appropriate neurodevelopment in 39 infants in each group; one infant in the exposed group had a suspicious result and one control infant had an abnormal result. Conclusion: Prenatal SARS-CoV-2 exposure was not associated with significant differences in infant growth or neurodevelopment during the first year of life. Larger prospective studies with longer follow-up are needed to determine long-term outcomes.
journal: Journal of Controversies in Obstetrics & Gynecology and Pediatrics

title: Eosinophil-driven immunopathology exacerbates SARS-CoV-2 pneumonia in an OVA-induced airway allergy mouse model
abstract: ABSTRACT Asthma is an allergic airway disease characterized by distinct immune environments that can alter host responses to respiratory viral infections; however, its impact on coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) severity remains unclear. To investigate how allergic airway inflammation affects severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2)-induced pneumonia, we used an ovalbumin (OVA)-induced airway allergy mouse model and infected mice with QHmusX, a mouse-passaged SARS-CoV-2 strain that causes severe acute pneumonia. Compared with phosphate-buffered saline-treated controls, OVA-sensitized mice exhibited persistent weight loss, a shift toward prominent alveolar involvement by viral infection, increased inflammatory cell infiltration, and higher histopathological scores, despite comparable viral burden. Enhanced apoptosis and increased numbers of CC10-positive epithelial cells indicated pronounced epithelial injury and repair responses in allergic mice. The post-infection decline in tissue eosinophils, together with histological evidence of eosinophil degranulation and lung cytokine profiling, was associated with amplified inflammatory and granulocyte-associated mediator responses in the airways. To define the functional contribution of eosinophils, we depleted eosinophils using an anti-interleukin-5 monoclonal antibody. Eosinophil depletion improved weight recovery, attenuated lung inflammation, and reduced CC10-associated repair responses without altering viral load. These findings demonstrate that airway allergy exacerbates SARS-CoV-2-induced pneumonia through eosinophil-mediated immunopathology and identify eosinophils as key contributors to disease severity. Targeting eosinophilic inflammation may therefore represent a potential therapeutic strategy for allergic individuals with COVID-19. IMPORTANCE Airway allergy profoundly alters host immunity; however, its impact on coronavirus disease 2019 severity remains unresolved. Using an ovalbumin-induced airway allergy mouse model, we show that pre-existing allergic airway inflammation exacerbates severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2)-induced pneumonia despite comparable viral burden. Allergic mice exhibited rapid eosinophil degranulation accompanied by extracellular eosinophil cationic protein deposition, amplified inflammatory mediator responses, and increased epithelial injury. Depletion of eosinophils with anti-interleukin-5 improved weight recovery and lung pathology without measurably affecting viral burden, supporting a pathogenic role for eosinophils in disease exacerbation. These findings indicate that the allergic airway environment can redirect the pulmonary response to SARS-CoV-2 infection and promote immunopathology independently of increased viral replication. The study provides a mechanistic framework for understanding how active allergic inflammation may contribute to severe viral pneumonia and supports further evaluation of eosinophil-targeted therapies in selected clinical contexts.

title: “I Would Prefer That They Would Be With Me”: Motivations, Roles, and Financial Realities of Informal Child Care Providers During the COVID-19 Pandemic
abstract: During the COVID-19 pandemic, working parents increasingly relied on informal child care networks as formal programs closed or restricted enrollment and health concerns grew. This study draws on surveys and interviews with 19 Illinois family, friend, and neighbor (FFN) providers supported by the Illinois Child Care Assistance Program (CCAP) to examine caregiving motivations, stressors, and access to supports. Findings show FFN providers often continued care without CCAP due to family obligation and to support parental employment. They frequently provided care beyond the scope of formal child care, including flexible hours, care for older children, and COVID-related assistance. Despite these expanded roles and risks, supports remained limited. Providers more often relied on the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP) and other public assistance rather than provider-specific programs, which they viewed as oriented toward licensed providers or those with greater financial need.

title: Unveiling the Satisfaction of Home-Based Learning During the Covid-19 Pandemic: An In-Depth Online Interview
abstract: Online home-based learning was introduced during the COVID-19 pandemic to ensure that students did not fall behind in the syllabus. This qualitative phenomenological study aims to explore satisfaction with home-based learning during the pandemic. Twenty-three adolescents who had undergone home-based learning in Selangor were interviewed during online in-depth interviews from December 2021 to March 2022. A semi-structured interview guide was adapted from the literature review, and the interviews were video recorded, transcribed verbatim, and anonymized. Transcripts were analyzed thematically using a framework approach, and NVivo 12 was used to expedite coding during data analysis. Three themes emerged as determinants of satisfaction: social norms, perceived usefulness, and perceived ease of use. A study found that students are dissatisfied with home-based learning, struggle to adapt to it, and have difficulty complying with school SOPs. Home-based learning can become a negative experience for adolescents, especially when connectivity is unstable, which can lead to frustration and disappointment and disrupt their preferred learning methods. Boys experienced greater difficulties and were less satisfied with home-based learning than girls. Thematic analysis indicated that adolescent satisfaction was higher before the pandemic. Future researchers should consider the same studies among students from different economic backgrounds. Some limitations of the study include internet connectivity issues during the interview, environmental disturbances, and difficulty interpreting nonverbal gestures. Finally, the online teaching method should be realigned and tailored to students’ expectations to enhance learning satisfaction.

title: A conceptual model for the governance of the health system in Iran; a qualitative study after the COVID-19 pandemic
abstract: The governance of the health system has a significant impact on the performance of the health system and the achievement of sustainable health goals. However, conceptualizing its constituent elements is challenging, and there is no consensus regarding its dimensions and measurement tools. This research amid to redefine the governance of the health system in Iran after the COVID-19 pandemic and design a conceptual model for health system governance in the Iranian context. This qualitative study was conducted in 2023. The participants included 22 health system managers with at least five years of managerial experience, as well as policymakers and scientific experts familiar with health system governance in Iran. Data were collected through semi-structured interviews using purposive sampling, followed by snowball sampling until data saturation was reached. Questions focused on the concepts and dimensions of health system governance. All interviews were audio-recorded and transcribed verbatim. Subsequently, meaning units were identified, coded, and categorized based on similarities and patterns. Themes were then extracted and analyzed using the content analysis method. Analysis of the participants’ experiences yielded eight main themes and 25 sub-themes. The main themes were policy and planning, rules and regulations, communication and coordination, organization, information systems, effective leadership, monitoring and evaluation, and stakeholder participation. Governance enhances the resilience and capacity of the health system to address challenges and crises, a need that has become more evident following the COVID-19 pandemic. Strengthening elements such as policy and planning, effective and efficient resource organization, interdepartmental collaboration, and stakeholder participation is crucial. To minimize conflicts and redundancies among health system stakeholders and to optimize the utilization of existing resources, it is recommended to review and redefine their roles and responsibilities.

title: The UGBC Library’s Experiences across the Pre-, During-, and Post-COVID-19 Timelines
abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic resulted in a wave of disruptions worldwide and its effect on the higher education systems significantly impacted their service units, among them being their academic libraries.This study discusses the transformation of the University of Guyana Berbice Campus (UGBC) Library operations and services across three phases: periods.This study utilises a content analysis, a qualitative research approach to discuss the UGBC Library's experience before, during and after the COVID-19 pandemic.Among the findings are that prior to the pandemic, the library was heavily dependent on traditional modes of operations, with the face-to-face services, the physical resources, and integrated minimal digital applications into its operations.In the face of the pandemic, although the abrupt and forced response to remote operations exposed various weaknesses, it also accelerated digital adoption and resulted in forward thinking and innovative work behaviour.During the pandemic timeline, the library first adopted full online operations, then gradually incorporated the hybrid service delivery model, pulling together both the physical and digital service modalities.Library operations in the post covid period can be described as being a continuation of the hybrid service model.The study concludes that despite the challenges brought about by the COVID-19 pandemic, the UGBC Library utilised the experience as an opportunity to transform its services and build greater resilience for the future.Some future recommendations for the UGBC Library include adopting a flexible work schedule, strengthening the hybrid service model, improving ICT infrastructure, and engaging in continuous Professional Development (PD) activities.

title: Hopelessness among Healthcare Workers during the COVID-19 Pandemic: Experiences and Perceptions
abstract: Background: COVID-19 has globally challenged health systems and created profound psychosocial consequences for healthcare workers. Hopelessness, as a negative future expectation, may emerge alongside fear, anxiety, and burnout. This study aimed to examine hopelessness levels among healthcare workers during the COVID-19 pandemic and to identify associated factors based on their experiences and perceptions.Methods: The research group consisted of all employees at an education and research hospital. Data were collected from 562 personnel (48.2% of active staff). The data collection tools included a questionnaire and the Beck Hopelessness Scale. Statistical analyses included descriptive statistics, independent samples t-test, one-way ANOVA with Bonferroni/Tamhane post-hoc tests, and stepwise multiple linear regression model.Results: The mean age was 35.8±8.8 years, and the mean length of service was 9.1±8.3 years. Of the participants, 61.2% were female, 30.8% were doctors, and 27.0% nurses. Nearly one-third had worked in COVID-19 units, one-third had been infected, and more than half had directly cared for COVID-19 patients. In bivariate analyses, smoking, workplace reassignment, direct care of patients with COVID-19, and perceiving colleagues’ knowledge as insufficient were associated with higher hopelessness. In the multivariable model, female gender, chronic illness or disability, a mixed work schedule, psychological impact, the belief that the pandemic could not be controlled, and pessimistic expectations about returning to normal life remained independently associated with hopelessness.Conclusion: Hopelessness is a critical psychological concern among healthcare workers in pandemic disasters. Early recognition of vulnerable groups and institutional support to reduce uncertainty, provide adequate Personal Protective Equipment, and regulate shift work are essential to strengthen workforce resilience. These findings highlight the need to integrate psychological well-being into pandemic preparedness and occupational health policies.

title: A Spatiotemporal Dynamic Immune Landscape of the COVID-19 Hamster Lung [M]
abstract: Although SARS-CoV-2-mediated inflammation has attracted global health concerns since 2019, its pulmonary immunopathology is not fully understood. Here we generated a comprehensive cellular and molecular landscape of healthy and COVID-19 hamster lungs at different timepoints after infection, using single-cell RNA sequencing and spatial transcriptomic sequencing to map the entire progression of COVID-19. We found SARS-CoV-2 could infect naive T cells and induced cell death to decrease T cell number at the early stage of COVID-19. Besides, we observed the activation and depletion of tissue resident myeloid cells after infection, the accumulation of Isg12+Cst7+ neutrophils and Il10+Spp1+M2-like macrophages to clean up virus and resolve inflammation. Finally, we identified Trem2+AM and Fbp1+AM subsets during the resolution stage of COVID-19. Our study provided spatiotemporally-resolved insights into the lung cells transcriptome, identified distinct tissue regions of viral infection, lung injury, repair and remodeling.

title: Impact of COVID-19 on adolescent mental health in Albania
abstract: Purpose The COVID-19 pandemic has profoundly disrupted adolescent mental health worldwide. Yet, the extent and sociodemographic distribution of self-perceived psychological impact of COVID-19 among adolescents in transitional postcommunist countries of the Western Balkans has not been systematically reported. This study aims to assess the magnitude and sociodemographic correlates of self-perceived mental health impact of COVID-19 among adolescents in Albania. Design/methodology/approach This was a school-based cross-sectional study conducted in Albania in 2022, including a nationwide representative sample of 5,454 adolescents aged 11–15 years (around 52% girls; overall response rate: 96%). Data on self-perceived mental health impact of COVID-19 and sociodemographic characteristics were collected. Binary logistic regression was used to assess the association of COVID-19’s mental health impact with adolescents’ sociodemographic factors. Findings About 35% of Albanian adolescents reported negative or very negative COVID-19’s mental health impact (37% in girls vs 33% in boys, p < 0.01). Irrespective of the other sociodemographic characteristics, girls and older adolescents were significantly more likely to perceive negative mental health impact of COVID-19. Conversely, no associations were evident for place of residence (urban/rural), parental employment or family affluence. Originality/value This study evidenced a substantial mental health impact of the COVID-19 pandemic perceived among Albanian adolescents, with female gender and older age emerging as independent correlates of negative appraisal. The findings emphasize the need for targeted mental health strategies and the importance of integrating psychosocial support into broader public health responses in transitional settings.

title: Middle East Respiratory Syndrome Coronavirus (MERS-CoV) Transmission at The Camel-Human Interface in Saudi Arabia
abstract: MERS-CoV remains a zoonotic threat, primarily from dromedary camels. Despite over a decade since its discovery, transmission risks and asymptomatic infections remain poorly understood. Saudi Arabia, accounting for 84% of globally reported human cases, faces surveillance challenges and limited behavioural data due to social sensitivities, hindering targeted interventions. This thesis investigated MERS-CoV transmission pathways at the camel–human interface and among humans, focusing on asymptomatic infection, occupational exposure, social mixing, and potential cross-reactivity with SARS-CoV-2. A cross-sectional study was conducted in Riyadh and Qassim (Dec 2022–Mar 2024) across camel–human interface settings: festivals, markets, abattoirs, enclosures, racetracks, and clinics. It included 475 humans and 406 camels. Human participants included camel owners with non-occupational contact; herders and trainers with occupational exposure in open-air settings; abattoir workers; and veterinary staff. Samples from both species were tested for MERS-CoV RNA and antibodies. Social contact and behavioural data were collected to identify risk factors and mixing patterns. MERS-CoV RNA was detected in 4 of 475 humans (0.8%)—all asymptomatic or mildly symptomatic—using rRT-PCR (Ct ≤40)–probable detection–, and in 101 of 406 camels (24.9%) (Ct ≤37). Antibodies were detected in 166 humans (34.9%) and 372 camels (91.6%). Positivity was highest among abattoir and veterinary workers, with adjusted odds ratios of 3.1 [95% CI: 1.6–6.5] and 2.7 [95% CI: 1.1–8.1], respectively compared with the nonoccupational-group. No evidence of cross-reactivity with SARS-CoV-2 was found. Universal SARS-CoV-2 immunity and lack of a non-exposed control group limited this investigation. No SARS-CoV-2 RNA or antibodies were detected in camels. MERS-CoV test positivity varied across camel–human interface settings and occupational groups. Detection of asymptomatic infections among camel-exposed individuals suggests that symptom-based surveillance may underestimate human infection. Enhanced surveillance and targeted occupational health measures in high-risk settings, particularly abattoirs and veterinary services, could improve MERS-CoV prevention and control.

title: Containment, social protection, and confidence in public institutions and government: Global evidence from 144 countries during the COVID-19 pandemic
abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic required governments to balance restrictive containment policies with measures to mitigate their socioeconomic consequences, raising questions about the relationship between these policy responses and public confidence and trust. Existing research has largely examined containment and economic support separately, often within individual countries or during the pandemic's initial months. We constructed a global country-level panel by integrating administrative policy data with survey measures of public confidence from the Gallup World Poll, covering 144 countries from 2006 to 2023. Using regression models with country and pre-pandemic year fixed effects, this study examined how changes in institutional and government confidence were associated with lockdown trajectories (sustained low-level, rapidly easing, and sustained high-level) and the scale, breadth, and composition of social protection responses. We found that countries following sustained high-level lockdown trajectories generally experienced less favorable changes in confidence than those following rapidly easing trajectories. Under sustained high-level lockdowns, greater social protection spending and a larger number of social protection measures were generally associated with more favorable changes in confidence. Income protection spending was more positively associated with institutional confidence than job protection spending under sustained high-level lockdowns, but this distinction was not supported for government confidence or trust. These findings highlight the importance of considering containment and social protection jointly and suggest that income protection may be particularly relevant to institutional confidence during prolonged restrictions, with broader implications for governing large-scale crises. source_records.title: Containment, social protection, and confidence in public institutions and government: Global evidence from 144 countries during the COVID-19 pandemic
source_records.abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic required governments to balance restrictive containment policies with measures to mitigate their socioeconomic consequences, raising questions about the relationship between these policy responses and public confidence and trust. Existing research has largely examined containment and economic support separately, often within individual countries or during the pandemic's initial months. We constructed a global country-level panel by integrating administrative policy data with survey measures of public confidence from the Gallup World Poll, covering 144 countries from 2006 to 2023. Using regression models with country and pre-pandemic year fixed effects, this study examined how changes in institutional and government confidence were associated with lockdown trajectories (sustained low-level, rapidly easing, and sustained high-level) and the scale, breadth, and composition of social protection responses. We found that countries following sustained high-level lockdown trajectories generally experienced less favorable changes in confidence than those following rapidly easing trajectories. Under sustained high-level lockdowns, greater social protection spending and a larger number of social protection measures were generally associated with more favorable changes in confidence. Income protection spending was more positively associated with institutional confidence than job protection spending under sustained high-level lockdowns, but this distinction was not supported for government confidence or trust. title: Understanding the uneven geography of Britain’s economic inactivity crisis since Brexit and the COVID-19 pandemic
abstract: This paper extends the concept of regional resilience to address economic inactivity as a key economic outcome, and to consider health and demography as sources of regional vulnerability and resilience. Economic inactivity in Great Britain rose sharply following Brexit and the COVID-19 pandemic, but in geographically uneven ways. Results indicate that changes to local economic inactivity are strongly associated with changes to health and ageing of the labour force, but not with changes to immigration linked to Brexit. In previous economic crises, local economic inactivity has risen in response to contractions in labour demand. In contrast, the current economic inactivity crisis has its roots in supply-side shocks to labour supply, chiefly driven by the COVID-19 pandemic and labour force ageing, although Brexit may have affected some rural economies.

title: Spatiotemporal Variability of Aerosols over Ghana: Changes Associated with the COVID-19 Period
abstract: Exposure to fine particulate matter (PM2.5) is a leading environmental health risk in West Africa, yet long-term characterization of aerosol variability in Ghana is constrained by sparse surface monitoring. Here we combine aerosol optical depth (AOD) from the Moderate Resolution Imaging Spectroradiometer (MODIS) on the Terra and Aqua satellites (2010-2022), the daily, 1 km2 Gridded Africa Surface Pollution (GRASP) PM2.5 data set (2010−2021), surface PM2.5 observations (2021), precipitation records, and HYSPLIT backward trajectories to characterize aerosol variability across the coastal, forest, and northern zones of Ghana, with emphasis on changes associated with the COVID-19 period. AOD and PM2.5 peak during the Harmattan dry season (November−February), when more than 86% of air masses arriving at Accra, Kumasi, and Tamale originate over the Sahara and Sahel. Daily PM2.5 exceeded the World Health Organization (WHO) 24-h guideline of 25 μg m−3 on 75-93% of days in 2021, with Harmattan peaks above 400 μg m−3 in Tamale. MODIS AOD was significantly correlated with GRASP PM2.5 at all three cities (R2 = 0.67−0.91, p < 0.001), and AOD decreased exponentially with monthly precipitation (R2 = 0.81). Relative to the 2010-2019 baseline, mean PM2.5 in 2020 decreased by 13.7% in Accra, 8.3% in Kumasi, and 3.6% in Tamale, with larger reductions of 33.6% and 28.4% in Accra and Kumasi during the March 30-April 20 partial lockdown. Our findings demonstrate the value of integrating satellite and gridded surface data sets to support air quality management and geographically targeted interventions in Ghana.

title: Comparative silane surface functionalization strategies for enhanced Bloch surface wave biosensing of anti-SARS-CoV-2 antibodies
abstract: Surface functionalization plays a decisive role in the performance of biosensors, as it governs the efficiency and stability of biomolecule immobilization at the sensor interface and, consequently, the overall performance of the biosensing platforms. In this work, we present a comparative study of three organosilane chemistries — APTES, APDMS, and CPTES — applied to a SiO2-terminated 1D photonic crystal able to sustain Bloch surface waves and designed to operate as optical biosensors in both label-free and fluorescence-enhanced modes. Each chemistry was evaluated through a standardized label-free protocol based on the interaction between immobilized SARS-CoV-2 spike protein and its corresponding antibodies, enabling quantitative assessment of binding efficiency, nonspecific adsorption, and signal repeatability. CPTES exhibited the most favorable balance between specific signals, reduced variability, and low nonspecific adsorption. The three chemistries were subsequently tested in fluorescence mode for the detection of anti-SARS-CoV-2 IgG antibodies in human serum, demonstrating the suitability of BSW-enhanced fluorescence for rapid serological analysis. Overall, the study identifies CPTES as the most robust and reproducible functionalization strategy among the three investigated for BSW biosensing and highlights the potential of the platform for fast, sensitive detection of clinically relevant antibodies.

title: Influence of COVID-19 Lockdown on Atmospheric Nitrate Sources and Chemistry in the Northeastern US
abstract: Abstract The outbreak of COVID-19 and subsequent lockdowns caused widespread restrictions on human activities. This presented a unique opportunity to track atmospheric chemistry changes under rapid emission reductions. Using stable nitrogen (δ15N) and triple oxygen isotopes (δ18O and Δ17O) of particulate nitrate (pNO3) collected from 2019 to 2020 in the northeastern US, combined with 0-D box-model simulations, we investigate the response of atmospheric nitrate chemistry during the COVID-19 lockdown period (March 2020) in the northeastern US. Triple oxygen isotope measurements indicate that emission reductions altered the relative contributions of NOx oxidation pathways, with a shift toward the NO2 + OH pathway and a reduced contribution from N2O5 hydrolysis. This shift was consistent with the modeled increase in OH concentrations and the observed and modeled decrease in O3 during the COVID-19 lockdown, which limited N2O5 formation and subsequent heterogeneous nitrate formation. Moreover, nitrogen isotope-constrained sensitivity analysis suggests that a reduction of approximately 40(±10)% in transportation NOx emissions relative to the annual emission inventory estimates may be required to reproduce the observed decrease in δ15N(pNO3) during the COVID-19 period. These findings highlight the utility of isotopes to detail the complex interactions between emission reductions, atmospheric oxidation chemistry, and secondary aerosol formation. Understanding these interactions is critical for effectively determining air pollution mitigation strategies and testing air-quality models, particularly under rapidly evolving emission conditions associated with energy transitions and policy interventions.

title: Hospital-acquired COVID-19 and deep vein thrombosis in orthopaedic inpatients: a retrospective cohort study in a resource-constrained setting
abstract: Background: Hospital-acquired COVID-19 presents a distinct challenge in orthopaedic care within low- and middle-income country (LMIC) settings, where prolonged isolation, delayed mobilization and system constraints increase immobilization-related morbidity. Unlike high-income settings that emphasize respiratory outcomes, LMIC orthopaedic inpatients appear to face a disproportionate burden of thromboembolic complications, particularly deep vein thrombosis (DVT). Methods: A retrospective cohort study was conducted at a South Indian teaching hospital between January 2020 and December 2025. Orthopaedic inpatients with RT-PCR–confirmed COVID-19 were categorized as having nosocomial or community-acquired infection based on timing of diagnosis. Demographic data, injury and treatment characteristics, immobilization duration, comorbidity burden, thromboprophylaxis use and vitamin D status were analysed. DVT was diagnosed using duplex ultrasonography and multivariable logistic regression identified independent predictors. Results: Of 217 patients (median age 48 years; 68.2% male), 68 developed nosocomial COVID-19. Hospital-acquired infection was associated with significantly longer hospital stay and immobilization. Overall DVT incidence was 11.1%, with a higher prevalence in nosocomial compared with community-acquired cases (19.1% vs. Nosocomial infection, immobilization exceeding seven days and vitamin D deficiency independently predicted DVT. In-hospital mortality did not differ between groups. Conclusion: Hospital-acquired COVID-19 significantly increases DVT risk among orthopaedic inpatients in LMIC settings, driven primarily by prolonged immobilization. Preventive strategies should prioritize early mobilization, optimized isolation workflows and correction of modifiable risk factors to reduce avoidable thromboembolic morbidity.
journal: International Journal of Research in Orthopaedics

title: Low-dose prednisolone and B vitamins for post-COVID-19 syndrome in Germany: the PreVitaCOV randomised clinical trial.
abstract: Background Post-COVID-19 syndrome is burdensome and not yet adequately treatable, with persistent symptoms including fatigue, dyspnoea, and cognitive impairment. The Pan American Health Organisation recommends rigorous evaluation of potentially beneficial interventions. We investigated the efficacy and safety of prednisolone and vitamins B1, B6, and B12 in patients with post-COVID-19. Methods This randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled phase 3 trial (2 × 2 factorial design) was conducted in adults with post-COVID-19 at three university sites in Germany. Adult patients with persistent symptoms after a documented SARS-CoV-2 infection ≥12 weeks ago and without acute COVID-19, major comorbidities, pregnancy or breastfeeding, prior intensive care treatment for COVID-19, recent use of trial drugs, or potentially interacting concomitant medications were included. From January 13, 2023 until July 25, 2024 participants were randomly assigned to 28 days of once-daily oral treatment with prednisolone (20 mg on days 1-5, 5 mg on days 6-28), B vitamins (thiamine nitrate [B1], 100 mg, pyridoxine hydrochloride [B6] 50 mg, and cyanocobalamin [B12] 500 μg), prednisolone and B vitamins, or placebo. The primary outcome was change in overall symptom severity from baseline to day 28, assessed in the intention-to-treat population (participants who received at least one dose of study drug) at the first follow-up visit after randomisation with a customised Patient-Reported Outcomes Measurement Information System (PROMIS) total T-score. A change of ≥3 points was considered clinically meaningful. Efficacy was assessed using a pre-specified factorial analysis of the main effects of prednisolone and B vitamins. Safety was assessed by analysing frequency and severity of adverse events in all randomised patients (safety population). This completed trial is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT05638633). Findings Of 2498 patients assessed for eligibility, 323 were randomised and 310 patients had evaluable data for the outcomes. The mean age was 44 (standard deviation (SD) 13) years, 200 participants were women. The mean change in PROMIS T-score was -4·3 (SD 5·1) with prednisolone, -3·2 (SD 5·0) with B vitamins, -4·5 (SD 4·5) with prednisolone plus B vitamins, and -2·9 (SD 4·6) with placebo. The adjusted mean difference between participants treated with prednisolone and those not treated was -1·4 points (95% confidence interval (CI), -2·5 to -0·4; p = 0·008), driven primarily by the change in the fatigue subscore (-6·4 points, p < 0·001). B vitamins showed no statistically significant or clinically meaningful difference compared with no B vitamins (adjusted mean difference (MD), -0·1 points; 95% CI, -1·2 to +1·0; p = 0·85). Adverse events were equally distributed between groups, with no study-drug-related serious adverse events. Interpretation This trial showed a statistically significant short-term reduction in symptom severity in the five dimensions of the PROMIS score in patients with post-COVID with low-dose prednisolone. However, the effect did not reach the prespecified threshold for clinical relevance. Further research is needed to confirm the efficacy of prednisolone and to determine the optimal dose and treatment duration while balancing benefits against longer-term adverse effects. Funding German Federal Ministry of Research, Technology and Space, Vogel Stiftung Dr. Eckernkamp, Hevert-Arzneimittel GmbH & Co.

title: Mathematical modeling and analysis of the impact of booster vaccination on COVID-19 eradication
abstract: In last two decades, people battled with three coronaviruses, namely Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome (SARS) in November 2002; Middle East Respiratory Syndrome (MERS) in 2012 and finally the devastating SARS-CoV-2 infection or COVID-19 pandemic in December, 2019. Though the pandemic is now under control, we need to know whether it is completely eradicated or not. For this purpose, we have formulated a mathematical model incorporating three doses of corona vaccine and studied the impact of these vaccines on the disease dynamics. In our study, we have sought the conditions for eradication of the virus from the environment. To understand the consistency of the model, we have studied first its positivity and boundedness. Then we have carried out its steady-state analysis. The stability of the COVID-free equilibrium (CFE) and COVID-endemic equilibrium (CEE) points has been analyzed with the help of the basic reproduction number [Formula: see text], which is derived by the next-generation matrix approach. Further, this model has been validated by real data reported from India and estimated model parameters. Most effective model parameters are found by sensitivity analysis. Our findings show that first and second doses of COVID vaccines are not sufficient for eradication of the disease from the population, but the third (or booster) dose is able to control the disease if no comorbidity is considered.

title: Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on critically ill patients in a pediatric emergency department
abstract: La pandemia por COVID-19 modificó la actividad de los servicios de urgencias pediátricos (SUP). Sin embargo, existe escasa información sobre su impacto en pacientes críticos en urgencias. El objetivo de este trabajo fue analizar el efecto de la pandemia en la afluencia, características clínicas y gravedad de estos pacientes en un SUP. Análisis retrospectivo de un registro prospectivo de pacientes críticos menores de 14 años atendidos en un SUP entre 2011 y 2024, definidos como aquellos que ingresaron en cuidados intensivos o fallecieron en urgencias. Se compararon cuatro periodos: pre-pandemia, alarma, post-alarma y post-pandemia. Se registraron 714.202 episodios, siendo 1.459 (0,2 %) pacientes críticos; 46 (3,2 %) fallecieron. Durante el periodo de alarma disminuyó la afluencia de pacientes críticos (1/4,8 días vs 1/3,5 en pre-pandemia), aunque aumentó su tasa respecto al total de consultas (1/394 vs 1/518 episodios). Se redujo la patología respiratoria (25 % vs 44,1 %), y aumentaron las infecciones bacterianas invasivas (20,5 % vs 12,8 %) y las lesiones no intencionadas (23,9 % vs 13 %). La mayor afluencia se registró en el periodo post-alarma (1/2,8 días). La mortalidad difirió entre periodos, aumentando durante la alarma y disminuyendo en el periodo post-alarma, mostrando diferencias significativas (p = 0,044), aunque con un tamaño de efecto pequeño (V de Cramer 0,084, IC 95 %: 0,01-0,13). La pandemia por COVID-19 modificó la afluencia y perfil de pacientes críticos atendidos en urgencias pediátricas, sin asociación con mayor gravedad, pero con variaciones de mortalidad de pequeña magnitud. Estos hallazgos pueden ayudar a planificar la atención al paciente crítico en futuras crisis sanitarias.

title: Did the COVID-19 Pandemic Change the Clinical Presentation and Management of Paediatric IgA Vasculitis? A Multicentre Retrospective Cohort Study
abstract: Objectives: Immunoglobulin A vasculitis (IgAV) is the most common systemic vasculitis in children and is frequently preceded by a respiratory or gastrointestinal infection. The COVID-19 pandemic affected the epidemiology of infections across multiple paediatric conditions and was accompanied by changes in hospitalization criteria, therapeutic practice, and healthcare organization. The aim of this study was to compare the clinical presentation and treatment of IgAV in children before and after the onset of the COVID-19 pandemic. Methods: We retrospectively analysed the medical records of 160 patients aged 0–18 years who were hospitalized for IgAV between 2015 and 2023 at three paediatric centres in the Lodz region. Patients were divided into two temporal groups: group hospitalized between 2015 and 2020 (n = 82) and group hospitalized between 2021 and 2023 (n = 78). Demographic data, length of hospitalization, disease severity, renal involvement, and treatment were compared between the groups. Results: Patient age did not differ significantly between the groups (7.2 ± 3.82 vs. 6.8 ± 3.55 years; p = 0.469). The mean length of hospitalization decreased from 10.2 ± 4.78 to 7.9 ± 3.18 days (p < 0.001). The proportion of patients classified as having severe IgAV was lower in the 2021–2023 group than in the 2015–2020 group (9.0% vs. Urinary abnormalities during hospitalization were observed in 16.7% of patients in the 2021–2023 group and in 40.2% of patients in the 2015–2020 group (p < 0.001). After the onset of the pandemic, antibiotics and etamsylate were used significantly less frequently, whereas the frequency of glucocorticoid treatment did not change significantly. Conclusions: Compared with the 2015–2020 period, children hospitalized with IgAV in 2021–2023 had shorter hospital stays, lower CRP concentrations, and less frequent urinary abnormalities, while antibiotics and etamsylate were used less frequently. The proportion of patients classified as having severe disease was also lower, although this difference was attenuated in sensitivity analysis. These temporal differences may reflect changes in infection epidemiology, clinical practice, and healthcare organization after the onset of the COVID-19 pandemic. However, the available data do not allow a direct relationship with SARS-CoV-2 infection to be established.

title: COVID-19-INDUCED REACTIVATION OF SPOROTRICHOSIS LEADING TO RAY AMPUTATION: A RARE CASE REPORT
abstract: Sporotrichosis is an infection caused by the dimorphic fungus Sporothrix schenckii, acquired through contamination of the wound by the fungi. While cutaneous forms are most common, osteoarticular involvement is rare and usually seen in immunocompromised individuals. We present a case of chronic monoarthritis of the proximal interphalangeal joint in a 36-year-old immunocompetent nurse, previously treated with itraconazole after fungal culture confirmed Sporothrix schenckii infection. Following a COVID-19 infection, the patient experienced recurrence of the arthritis, with progressive joint destruction despite ongoing antifungal therapy. Surgical debridement was performed, but worsening symptoms ultimately necessitated ray amputation of the affected digit. Postoperatively, the patient regained good hand function with minimal limitations and reported an improved quality of life at 1-year follow-up. This case highlights the diagnostic challenges of osteoarticular sporotrichosis, the potential for COVID-19 to induce reactivation of latent fungal infections through immune dysregulation, and the importance of a multimodal approach including surgery in refractory cases to preserve function.
journal: Journal of Istanbul Faculty of Medicine / İstanbul Tıp Fakültesi Dergisi

title: Rehabilitación respiratoria y funcional temprana tras neumonía asociada a COVID-19 en una persona mayor: estudio de caso con ejercicios progresivos en sedestac
abstract: Functional recovery after COVID-19-associated pneumonia may be limited by dyspnea, muscle weakness, chest pain, deconditioning, and loss of autonomy, particularly in older adults after prolonged hospitalization. This study aimed to describe the application and clinical-functional course of a progressive respiratory and functional exercise system in a woman older than 65 years during the early post-discharge phase. A descriptive single-case design with 30-day follow-up was conducted using clinical-functional observation, analysis of ventilatory mechanics, and graded motor tasks performed in a seated position. The participant had controlled hypertension and hypercholesterolemia and, after approximately 21 days of hospitalization, presented chest pain, occasional cough, fatigue, perceived breathing difficulty, and reduced muscle strength. The intervention comprised four progressive upper-limb tasks intended to promote scapulothoracic mobility, thoracic expansion, postural control, and muscular activation related to ventilatory mechanics. At day 20, an observationally favorable course was documented in movement tolerance and perceived breathing capacity; by day 30, greater functional autonomy and no reported episodes of breathlessness during usual activities were recorded. These observations must be interpreted cautiously because they derive from a single case and were not supported by standardized physiological outcomes. Current evidence supports individualized pulmonary rehabilitation after COVID-19, while emphasizing the need to rule out exertional desaturation, cardiac impairment, and post-exertional symptom exacerbation before exercise training. For future replication, the protocol should include objective monitoring, validated functional tests, symptom scales, and explicit stopping criteria. The case contributes a feasible low-resource sequence for early functional progression while highlighting the methodological and safety requirements necessary for stronger clinical inference.

title: The impact of COVID-19 and influenza on the development of obstetric complications and pregnancy outcomes
abstract: The decline in the birth rate recorded in Russia in the early 2000s exacerbated depopulation trends. Since 1993, the country has experienced a steady natural population decline due to a combination of socioeconomic factors and pregnancy complications. Transient immunosuppression during pregnancy increases women’s susceptibility to infections, the most significant of which are influenza and COVID-19. To assess the impact of viral diseases—influenza and COVID-19—on pregnancy outcomes, as well as the incidence of obstetric complications in pregnant women who had influenza or COVID-19, using Penza as an example. Materials and methods. A retrospective analysis of the medical records of 1.754 pregnant women in Penza from 2020 to 2025 was conducted. Two observation groups were formed: the study group (n=877) with laboratory-confirmed COVID-19 or influenza, and the control group (n=877) without infectious diseases. The control group was matched by paired matching based on age, gestational age, and parity. The groups were comparable in baseline characteristics (p>0.05). Infectious diseases significantly increase the odds of developing pregnancy complications (odds ratio 5.66; 95% confidence interval 3.92—8.18). Influenza is associated with a higher risk of complications than COVID-19: general complications were 3.84 times more common (95% CI 2.26—6.49), preterm birth was 3.84 times more common (95% CI 2.18—6.70), and the risk of early reproductive loss was 3.81 times higher (95% CI 1.21—10.20). Influenza during pregnancy poses a greater risk to pregnancy than COVID-19, increasing the risk of complications by 3.8—5.7 times. The most severe complication is preterm birth. These data support the need for further research to evaluate the effectiveness of influenza vaccination as a potential method for reducing the incidence of obstetric complications.

title: Recurrent mild SARS-CoV-2 infection affects the lung-brain axis in wild type and Alzheimer’s mice
abstract: The lung-brain axis, describing the complex communication between the respiratory and central nervous systems (CNS), has gained attention due to the increasing number of individuals experiencing long-term neurological symptoms following respiratory infections. Since the emergence of Coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19), caused by the severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2), millions of individuals have developed persistent symptoms collectively known as long-COVID. Among these, cognitive impairment, fatigue, and ‘brain fog’ are frequently reported. Clinical observations also suggest that SARS-CoV-2 infection may increase the risk of developing neurodegenerative conditions such as Alzheimer’s disease (AD). However, the biological mechanisms linking repeated respiratory infections and brain pathology remain poorly understood. In this study, we investigated how recurrent respiratory infection with distinct SARS-CoV-2 variants affects brain health in wild type and AD mice. Hereto, wild type and knock-in App NL−G−F Alzheimer mice, crossed into a K18-hACE2 background, were infected sequentially with two antigenically distinct variants of SARS-CoV-2 to mimic the repeated exposure experienced by many individuals during the pandemic. Two weeks after the second viral exposure, we observed no notable changes in the number or reactive state of microglial cells and astrocytes, the brain's key immune cells. In contrast, we observed a hippocampal consistent reduction in synaptic integrity in infected mice. In AD mice, repeated infection also led to increased accumulation of amyloid plaques, a hallmark of AD pathology. Our findings indicate that repeated mild SARS-CoV-2 infections can impair neuronal function and worsen brain pathology in a susceptible mouse model. This work highlights the importance of the lung-brain axis in understanding the long-term neurological consequences of respiratory viral infections and suggests that individuals at risk for neurodegenerative diseases may be particularly sensitive to repeated viral exposure.

title: ANTIVIRAIS ORAIS NO TRATAMENTO DA COVID-19: EFICÁCIA CLINICA, SEGURANÇA E MECANISMOS DE AÇÃO
abstract: A COVID-19, causada pelo SARS-CoV-2, impulsionou o desenvolvimento de estratégias terapêuticas capazes de reduzir a replicação viral e a progressão da doença, especialmente em indivíduos com maior risco de evolução para formas graves. Considerando a necessidade de tratamentos precoces e a disponibilidade de diferentes antivirais, torna-se relevante compreender as diferenças entre seus mecanismos de ação, eficácia clínica e perfil de segurança. Objetiva-se analisar as evidências disponíveis sobre eficácia, segurança e mecanismos de ação dos principais antivirais orais utilizados ou investigados no tratamento da COVID-19, com ênfase em nirmatrelvir/ritonavir, molnupiravir e favipiravir. Para tanto, procede-se a uma revisão narrativa da literatura, mediante busca de estudos publicados em português e inglês nas bases PubMed, SciELO e ScienceDirect, priorizando publicações relacionadas ao tratamento antiviral da COVID-19. Desse modo, observa-se que o nirmatrelvir/ritonavir apresenta evidências clínicas mais consistentes para redução de hospitalização e morte em pacientes com maior risco de progressão quando administrado precocemente, enquanto o molnupiravir apresenta benefício mais limitado e importantes restrições de segurança. O favipiravir, por sua vez, apresenta resultados clínicos heterogêneos e ausência de benefício consistente. Conclui-se que a utilização dos antivirais deve ser individualizada, considerando risco de progressão, momento do tratamento, contraindicações e interações medicamentosas.
