title: Neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio as a prognostic marker of disease severity and in-hospital mortality in hospitalized patients with COVID-19: a retrospective Saudi cohort study
abstract: Coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) can cause a wide range of health issues, from relatively mild symptoms to severe life-threatening conditions. It’s important to identify patients predisposed to adverse clinical outcomes so that their care can be managed better. The neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR), which is an inexpensive and highly accessible biomarker of systemic inflammation, has been suggested as a way to predict how someone with severity of COVID-19. This present study investigated the utility of NLR in prediction of COVID-19 disease severity and in hospital death in Saudi Arabia. This study included COVID-19 patients hospitalized at King Fahd Specialist Hospital in Buraydah, Qassim, Saudi Arabia, from April to December 2021. Patients’ data including age, gender, comorbidities, lab test results, hospital stay length, and outcome (death or recovery) were gathered from patients’ electronic records. Data were analyzed using regression and survival analysis. A total of 204 patients who were hospitalized were included in the study, and out of these, 56 patients (which is 27.5%) had critical illness. Critical patients were much older than non-critical cases (72.7 ± 13.4 years versus 61.9 ± 18.8 years, P < 0.001), with higher levels D-dimer, aspartate aminotransferase, total bilirubin, lactate dehydrogenase, and amylase. The NLR was much higher in dead cases compared to survivors (the middle value was 7.2 versus 4.3, with a P-value of 0.002). Furthermore, higher NLR values were recognized in critical patients and those in the intensive care unit, with no statistical significance. The ROC analysis showed that the NLR had only a moderate ability to predict in-hospital mortality, with an AUC of 0.638 and the best cutoff value at 5.01.It also showed a similar but slightly lower ability to predict disease severity, with an AUC of 0.581 and the best cutoff value at 6.2. NLR was independently associated with in-hospital mortality in multivariable logistic regression, but not with critical disease severity. However, NLR did not retain an independent association with time-to-death in the fully adjusted Cox proportional-hazards model. NLR is a low-cost, and easily available marker of inflammation that could help to assess a patient’s risk early on, especially when used together with other clinical information and lab tests. More research is needed, especially large studies involving multiple centers, that use detailed analysis of several factors to better confirm how useful this is in predicting outcomes.

title: The Impact of COVID-19 Pandemic on Health Consumption: A Comparative Analysis of the United States, China, and India
abstract: Due to the COVID-19 pandemic, the global healthcare consumption patterns have been significantly changed. This has resulted in accelerating digital healthcare adoption, increasing health awareness, and promoting preventive healthcare behaviors. This study is aiming for examining how the pandemic’s influences have reshaped healthcare consumption in the United States, China, and India by using the five indicators: healthcare spending, digital healthcare, preventive healthcare, pharmaceutical demand, and mental healthcare. By using secondary data analysis, this research applies correlation analysis, Healthcare Consumption Change Index (HCCI), and elasticity analysis for evaluating the healthcare transformation patterns. The findings have suggested that all three countries were experiencing healthcare market expansion after COVID-19, but their development paths were different. The United States has revealed huge improvements in healthcare efficiency and digital service adoption. Chinese market has shown broader healthcare modernization supported by digital infrastructure. India has experienced rapid digital healthcare growth driven by accessibility needs. The study mainly concludes that COVID-19 accelerated the transition from traditional treatment-based healthcare toward a more preventive, digital, and consumer-centered healthcare model.
journal: Advances in Economics, Management and Political Sciences

title: Performance of the hotel industry in post-COVID-19 Tanzania: A case of Arusha City Council
abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic disrupted the global hotel industry, and hotels in Arusha City, Tanzania, have shown only partial recovery well after the pandemic formally subsided. Anchored in the Theory of Consumer Behaviour and the Agile Supply Chain Theory, this study assessed the performance of the hotel industry in Arusha City in the post-COVID-19 period, examining performance before, during, and after the pandemic, and identifying the challenges hindering full recovery. A convergent parallel mixed-methods design was adopted, combining questionnaires administered to 181 hotel employees (145 fully completed and retained for the descriptive analyses), semi-structured interviews with seven hotel managers, and two focus group discussions across seven hotels. Quantitative data were analysed descriptively and through a chi-square test of association using IBM SPSS Statistics, while qualitative data were analysed using a reflexive thematic approach. The findings show that before the pandemic hotels recorded high revenue, strong guest turnout, and stable employment; during the pandemic guest numbers, revenue, and employment collapsed and several hotels closed temporarily; and in the post-pandemic period, despite health protocols, business innovation, and staff training, the industry still records slow recovery linked to financial constraints, the slow return of customers, and shortages of skilled staff. A chi-square test showed a statistically significant association, not a causal relationship, between pandemic-related effects and current hotel performance (χ2(1, N = 181) = 6.495, p = .011, φ = .19, a small-to-moderate effect). Hotel owners are encouraged to invest cautiously in digital technologies, while government and other stakeholders provide financial support, favourable policies, and skills training to strengthen sector resilience; because the present data are perceptual and retrospective, these recommendations should be verified through more direct, longitudinal evidence.
journal: JOURNAL OF TOURISM CULINARY AND ENTREPRENEURSHIP (JTCE)

title: Design Trade-Offs between Target Binding and Self-Association Revealed by De Novo SARS-CoV-2 Binders
abstract: Abstract De novo protein binders have emerged as a powerful platform for molecular recognition, yet achieving high affinity while maintaining favorable biophysical properties remains a major challenge. Here, using the SARS-CoV-2 receptor-binding domain (RBD) as a model target, we generated two de novo protein binder design campaigns that deliberately imposed different trade-offs between binding and monomeric behavior, and benchmarked them against a set of experimentally validated binders. Through integrated experimental and computational analyses, we show that binder design is constrained by two distinct failure modes that require different optimization strategies. None of the 22 original designs showed measurable binding to the RBD, with one class remaining monomeric but failing to achieve sufficient target binding, while the other had more competent binding interfaces but exhibited excessive surface hydrophobicity that promoted self-association. By integrating AlphaFold-based predictions, molecular dynamics simulations, docking analyses, and surface aggregation propensity (SAP) calculations, we establish complementary computational signatures that distinguish these failure modes and reveal their underlying structural determinants. Guided by these insights, we prospectively redesigned a representative failed binder by reducing noninterface hydrophobicity while preserving folding and binding interface quality. Experimental characterization by SEC-MALS, surface plasmon resonance, and circular dichroism confirmed that the redesigned variants were stable monomers and acquired low μM binding affinities. Together, our results define the mechanistic trade-offs between binding and self-association in de novo protein binder design and provide a framework for diagnosing and rationally overcoming common design failure modes.

source_records.title: Design Trade-Offs between Target Binding and Self-Association Revealed by De Novo SARS-CoV-2 Binders
source_records.abstract: Abstract De novo protein binders have emerged as a powerful platform for molecular recognition, yet achieving high affinity while maintaining favorable biophysical properties remains a major challenge. Here, using the SARS-CoV-2 receptor-binding domain (RBD) as a model target, we generated two de novo protein binder design campaigns that deliberately imposed different trade-offs between binding and monomeric behavior, and benchmarked them against a set of experimentally validated binders. Through integrated experimental and computational analyses, we show that binder design is constrained by two distinct failure modes that require different optimization strategies. None of the 22 original designs showed measurable binding to the RBD, with one class remaining monomeric but failing to achieve sufficient target binding, while the other had more competent binding interfaces but exhibited excessive surface hydrophobicity that promoted self-association. By integrating AlphaFold-based predictions, molecular dynamics simulations, docking analyses, and surface aggregation propensity (SAP) calculations, we establish complementary computational signatures that distinguish these failure modes and reveal their underlying structural determinants. Guided by these insights, we prospectively redesigned a representative failed binder by reducing noninterface hydrophobicity while preserving folding and binding interface quality. Experimental characterization by SEC-MALS, surface plasmon resonance, and circular dichroism confirmed that the redesigned variants were stable monomers and acquired low μM binding affinities. Together, our results define the mechanistic trade-offs between binding and self-association in de novo protein binder design and provide a framework for diagnosing and rationally overcoming common design failure modes.

title: Secuelas respiratorias persistentes después de COVID-19: factores asociados y estrategias de recuperación. Persistent respiratory sequelae after COVID-19: associated factors and recovery strategies.
abstract: Introducción: Las secuelas respiratorias posteriores a la infección por SARS-CoV-2 constituyen un problema de salud pública, manifestándose principalmente mediante disnea, fatiga y alteraciones pulmonares que afectan la calidad de vida. Objetivo: Analizar los factores asociados a la persistencia de estas secuelas y las estrategias de recuperación más efectivas. Metodología: Se realizó una revisión bibliográfica sistemática bajo los lineamientos PRISMA, mediante la búsqueda en Dimensions AI, seleccionando 31 artículos publicados entre 2022 y 2026. Resultados: Las secuelas más frecuentes fueron disnea, fatiga y disminución de la DLCO. La edad avanzada, comorbilidades, estancia en UCI y ventilación mecánica prolongada se asociaron con mayor persistencia. Los biomarcadores inflamatorios y la rehabilitación pulmonar multidisciplinaria mostraron utilidad en el seguimiento y recuperación. Conclusión: El abordaje integral mediante monitoreo clínico, biomarcadores y rehabilitación pulmonar puede favorecer la recuperación y mejorar la calidad de vida de los pacientes post-COVID-19.

title: LINKING SUSTAINABILITY PERFORMANCE TO STOCK RESILIENCE DURING AND AFTER COVID-19 CRISIS: EVIDENCE FROM SOUTHEAST ASIA
abstract: Background: The COVID-19 pandemic severely disrupted markets. While sustainability performance measured by ESG scores theoretically buffers against shocks, its efficacy in emerging markets with nascent sustainability frameworks remains underexplored. Method: We analyze a balanced panel of 1,395 observations from 279 non-financial Southeast Asian firms (2020–2024). Using OLS, lagged, and fixed effects models, we compare the impact of sustainability performance on stock resilience during the 2020–2022 and post-pandemic (2023–2024) periods. Findings: Sustainability performance (ESG scores) significantly enhanced stock resilience during the pandemic. However, this protective effect dissipated post-pandemic. Results confirm a statistically significant improvement in overall resilience following the crisis, as investors redirected their focus toward traditional financial fundamentals such as profitability and leverage. Conclusion: Sustainability performance acts as situational crisis insurance. Its risk-mitigation value is highly salient during systemic uncertainty but diminishes under stable market conditions. Novelty/Originality of this article: Unlike prior single-phase studies in developed economies, this research provides longitudinal evidence on the dynamic, state-dependent nature of sustainability performance across crisis and recovery phases within Southeast Asia’s early-stage ESG landscape.

title: Lecciones de las pandemias de influenza y de COVID-19 para la odontología: revisión sistemática
abstract: Objetivo: sintetizar las lecciones de los brotes históricos de influenza y de la pandemia de COVID-19 aplicables a la atención odontológica. Método: revisión sistemática con síntesis narrativa en PubMed y SciELO (2012-2025); se incluyeron 15 estudios: revisiones sistemáticas y narrativas, ensayos clínicos y documentos de análisis histórico. Resultados: la pandemia de 1918 mostró el valor de proteger al personal sanitario y la de 2009, el de los diagnósticos moleculares y del uso planificado de los antivirales. En odontología, la COVID-19 obligó a controlar los aerosoles, reforzar la bioseguridad, priorizar la atención urgente, evaluar colutorios antisépticos y atender el agotamiento profesional. Conclusión: la preparación odontológica exige protocolos permanentes de bioseguridad y planes de continuidad asistencial.

title: Human Mobility Networks and COVID-19 Prediction: a Feature-aware Weighted Preferential Attachment approach and a Case Study for New York State
abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic was a global health crisis and, as such, became an important research topic in epidemiology and population health sciences. Significant research has been carried out related to the prediction of COVID-19 cases and the prevention of its spread utilizing many different methods, including both network analysis and machine learning. However, combining results from network-based link prediction methods and machine learning-based models to make COVID-19 case predictions has not been widely explored. For example, no one has used Weighted Preferential Attachment results, which provide pairwise scores (like the exact numbers of people moving around) between nodes (locations in human mobility networks), as direct inputs to machine learning models to make predictions. Is this a valid approach? In this study, we used the scores from a feature-aware Weighted Preferential Attachment model as a set of indicators to predict county-level COVID-19 cases for New York State with statistics and machine learning models. Meanwhile, we fed the same group of models with another set of indicators, the raw numbers (i.e., the exact numbers of people moving between counties), and compared the results. As is the norm when comparing two indicators, we tested them on a fixed set of models. Results show that the former outperformed the latter across different models in our spatiotemporal task, and as such, using the former is a valid approach in this scenario. In general, our work provides a framework and creates a novel pipeline to predict new COVID-19 cases.

title: Evaluation of Carbon-Dots (CDs) as Antiviral Candidates Against SARS-CoV-2 Using a Chemical Crosslinking Method
abstract: The chemical crosslinking method has been effective in previous studies for interaction-based drug screening. Although CDs have been widely explored as antiviral candidates, studies that use chemical crosslinking to select effective CDs against SARS-CoV-2 remain limited. To address this gap, this study uses chemical crosslinking to test CDs as antiviral compounds. The objective of this study is to screen and determine the potential of CDs as candidate antiviral compounds for inhibiting the dimerization of the SARS-CoV-2 N-CTD protein using a chemical crosslinking method. Recombinant SARS-CoV-2 N-CTD protein was expressed, purified, and precipitated for compound testing with chemical crosslinking. The concentration ranges used in the dimerization inhibition testing were 0-2,000 ppm (pyrrolic-N CDs) and 0-6,000 ppm (pyridinic-N, graphitic-N, and nuciferine-derived CDs). The study’s results show that CDs have the potential to inhibit dimerization of the SARS-CoV-2 N-CTD protein. Among the four compounds tested, pyrrolic-N CDs showed the best inhibitory potential, as they inhibited dimerization at the lowest concentration (2,000 ppm), had the smallest percentage of dimer bands to total protein, and achieved the highest dimerization inhibition efficiency. However, further research, including in vitro and in vivo tests, is needed to comprehensively evaluate the potential of pyrrolic-N CDs.

title: Temporal changes in pediatric respiratory syncytial virus and adenovirus positivity across COVID-19-related periods: A six-year retrospective cohort study
abstract: Objective: To describe temporal changes in respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) and adenovirus positivity among children tested across three COVID-19-related periods.Methods: This single-center retrospective cohort study included 8,253 children aged 0–18 years who underwent concurrent RSV and adenovirus antigen testing for suspected acute respiratory infection from January 2018 through June 2023. Periods were defined as pre-pandemic (January 2018–February 2020), restrictive pandemic (March 2020–May 2021), and post-restriction (June 2021–June 2023). Positivity proportions were compared by period. Unadjusted odds ratios (ORs) were calculated from period-specific counts using the pre-pandemic period as reference.Results: RSV was detected in 266 children (3.2%) and adenovirus in 612 (7.4%). RSV positivity was 1.5% (55/3,785) pre-pandemic, 1.2% (13/1,055) during restrictions, and 5.8% (198/3,413) post-restriction. Relative to the pre-pandemic period, the odds of RSV positivity did not differ during restrictions (OR 0.85, 95% CI 0.46–1.55) but were higher post-restriction (OR 4.18, 95% CI 3.09–5.65). Adenovirus positivity was 8.8%, 10.2%, and 5.0%, respectively; corresponding ORs were 1.18 (95% CI 0.94–1.48) and 0.54 (95% CI 0.45–0.66).Conclusion: Among clinically selected children who were tested, RSV and adenovirus positivity followed different temporal patterns. These unadjusted associations should not be interpreted as causal effects of specific public-health measures because seasonality, testing practices, and healthcare-seeking behavior may have differed across periods.

title: Persistent exertional dyspnea following mild COVID-19: potential association with diaphragm impairment
abstract: Background Persistent exertional dyspnea is a common symptom in long COVID, and routine cardiopulmonary testing is often unrevealing. The underlying mechanisms remain incompletely understood. Although exertional dyspnea has been linked to diaphragm weakness among hospitalized individuals, studies using state-of-the-art respiratory muscle assessment in non-hospitalized cohorts are lacking. Objective This study investigated the role of respiratory muscle function in exertional dyspnea in non-hospitalized patients after mild COVID-19 infection. Methods 25 outpatients with persistent dyspnea were assessed at a median 24 months after mild COVID-19 infection. Evaluations included pulmonary function testing, 6-minute walk test, echocardiography, twitch transdiaphragmatic pressure (TwPdi) following cervical magnetic stimulation of the phrenic nerve roots, and diaphragm ultrasound. Diaphragm parameters were compared with those of a healthy control group (3:1 matched for age, sex, BMI, and comorbidities). Main results Routine blood results, pulmonary function testing or echocardiography showed no clear alternative explanation for dyspnea at the group level. However, COVID-19 individuals exhibited significantly lower diaphragm strength (expressed in TwPdi) than controls (p=0.02), with results varying across dyspnea subgroups (overall ANOVA p-value = 0.009). A negative correlation was observed between TwPdi and dyspnea expressed on mBorg scale (r = -0.67, 95% CI -0.84 to -0.37, p < 0.001). Signs indicating potential structural alterations were observed in post-COVID patients, with significantly reduced diaphragm thickness at functional residual capacity (FRC) and total lung capacity (TLC) compared to controls (p = 0.02 and p < 0.001). Conclusions Persistent exertional dyspnea after mild COVID-19 is associated with diaphragm weakness and structural changes despite normal cardiopulmonary findings, supporting a key role for respiratory muscle impairment as a potential contributor to dyspnea in long COVID despite initial mild infection.

title: Fatigue, Hypertension, Dizziness, Anxiety, Depression, Musculoskeletal and Sleep Disorders, and Cardiac Arrhythmia: A Patient with Post-COVID-19 Condition in Dental Practice: 1-Year Follow-Up
abstract: This letter describes a 1-year follow-up of a 67-year-old female patient with a broad spectrum of post-COVID-19 manifestations, including cardiac arrhythmia and anxiety, which severely delayed her dental treatment. It outlines critical clinical considerations for dentists and oral-maxillofacial surgeons, emphasizing the management of anticoagulant therapy, hypertensive thresholds, and psychological barriers to ensure safe dental care.

title: Framing the unseen: COVID-19 through the eyes of a broadsheet and a tabloid
abstract: This study compares COVID-19 news framing in UK broadsheet The Guardian and tabloid The Sun during the outbreak’s first week (27 January − 3 February 2020). A content analysis of 86 articles, using an integrated framework of generic and pandemic-specific frames, reveals both convergences and divergences. Both newspapers shared human interest and attribution of responsibility among their top frames. However, The Guardian prioritized economic consequence (35%), while The Sun relied predominantly on fear/scare-mongering (30%). Notably, the same ethnicization frame served opposite functions: The Sun reinforced stigma, whereas The Guardian challenged prejudice. These findings challenge strong tabloidization claims by howing that substantive broadsheet–tabloid differences persist, and that frame frequency alone is insufficient for comparative analysis when the same frame serves different discursive functions across outlets. The study offers practical implications for responsible health journalism, particularly regarding the handling of ethnicization and threat narratives in crisis reporting.

title: Immunogenetic regulation of organ crosstalk in long COVID
abstract: Long COVID represents a heterogeneous, multisystem condition arising from the incomplete resolution of acute SARS-CoV-2 infection. Rather than an organ-restricted disorder, accumulating evidence indicates that long COVID is driven by persistent immune dysregulation shaped by immunogenetic susceptibility, endothelial injury, and pathological organ crosstalk. Current understanding of the genetic variables linked to viral entry, autoimmunity, cytokine imbalance, and interferon signalling abnormalities that cause tissue dysfunction and chronic inflammation is limited. Immunothrombosis and endothelial dysfunction are key processes that connect immunological activation to microvascular damage and compromised tissue perfusion. A comprehensive systems biology framework examines organ-specific symptoms across the neurological, gastrointestinal, renal, metabolic, and cardiopulmonary systems. We also note that two important causes of fatigue and exercise intolerance are mitochondrial dysfunction and metabolic reprogramming. source_records.title: Immunogenetic regulation of organ crosstalk in long COVID
source_records.abstract: Long COVID represents a heterogeneous, multisystem condition arising from the incomplete resolution of acute SARS-CoV-2 infection. Rather than an organ-restricted disorder, accumulating evidence indicates that long COVID is driven by persistent immune dysregulation shaped by immunogenetic susceptibility, endothelial injury, and pathological organ crosstalk. Current understanding of the genetic variables linked to viral entry, autoimmunity, cytokine imbalance, and interferon signalling abnormalities that cause tissue dysfunction and chronic inflammation is limited. Immunothrombosis and endothelial dysfunction are key processes that connect immunological activation to microvascular damage and compromised tissue perfusion. A comprehensive systems biology framework examines organ-specific symptoms across the neurological, gastrointestinal, renal, metabolic, and cardiopulmonary systems. We also note that two important causes of fatigue and exercise intolerance are mitochondrial dysfunction and metabolic reprogramming. We conclude by outlining multi-omics integration and biomarker discovery, emphasising the necessity of interdisciplinary approaches to improve long-term outcomes in long COVID.

title: Organización comunitaria del cuidado en barrios populares de Argentina en el contexto de pandemia por COVID-19 Community Organization of Care in Popular Neighborhoods of Argentina in the Context of the COVID-19 Pandemic Organização comunitária do cuidado em bairros populares da Argentina no contexto da pandemia de COVID-19
abstract: In this article we analyze how the COVID-19 pandemic along with the preventive isolation measures implemented by national states exacerbated gender and socioeconomic inequalities in Latin America, especially in relation to the social organization of care in poor neighborhoods in Argentina. We focus on the crucial role played by socio-community organizations in the provision of care and food assistance during the crisis. We analyze 26 territorially-based social organizations in seven regions of the country. We used a data sheet and surveys to develop a description based on a quantitative approach and attempt to link the characteristics of the organizations with the type of service they offer, the sources and amount of resources available to them, as well as their relationship with the different levels of the State. Finally, we highlight how the context of the socioeconomic and health crisis has made visible the importance of community care and the need to shift it from the private sphere to a public and collective responsibility.

title: Facing the unforeseen: coping, meaning in life, fear of death, and their associations across the COVID-19 pandemic and the early phase of Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine—a repeated cross-sectional study in independent Hungarian samples
abstract: The coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) pandemic and Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine represent unprecedented global stressors with substantial consequences for mental health. A repeated cross-sectional study was conducted in three independent Hungarian samples before COVID-19 ( N = 249), after the second wave of COVID-19 ( N = 265), and during the early phase of Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine ( N = 148) to examine differences in meaning in life, coping competencies, and fear of death, as well as in the relationships among these constructs. The outbreak of the invasion during data collection provided a unique opportunity to examine these constructs during its early phase. Compared with the post-COVID sample, lower descriptive levels of fear of death were observed following the outbreak of Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine. Lower levels of several coping resources, particularly sense of coherence and social competencies, together with the greater relevance of search for meaning, were among the key findings associated with these unforeseen stressors. Stronger associations between coping and meaning in life were identified, while the association between presence of meaning and search for meaning became stronger following the outbreak of the invasion. Network analyses further suggested a closer integration of meaning-related processes with fear of death and coping resources, although these patterns should be interpreted cautiously given the limited stability of the network estimates. The findings suggest that exposure to successive unforeseen large-scale stressors may be associated with the reorganization of meaning-related processes and coping resources. The patterns observed following the outbreak of the war may be interpreted within the framework of distal defense processes described by the terror management theory, although these mechanisms were not directly assessed in the present study. The results suggest that longer-term existential anxiety processes and their delayed psychological and social consequences should be considered when developing mental health interventions. These findings may contribute to the refinement of healthcare interventions across multiple levels and cultural contexts in preparation for current and future crises.

title: Physical and psychological impacts of COVID-19 pandemic on children
abstract: Objectives: The coronavirus disease-2019 (COVID-19) infection has affected the lives of all strata of society since its beginning. To control the spread of the disease, a lockdown was imposed. During this time, there was a substantial increase in the usage of gadgets and reduction in outdoor activities because of online studies that resulted in serious the mental health issues, especially in the paediatric population. Material and Methods: To study the effect of the COVID-19 pandemic on screen time, playtime and behaviour of the students, the study was conducted on 153 subjects of 4–18 years age group attending the outpatient department, over a period of 3 months. A questionnaire format of ten questions was framed that was asked from the children or from their parents/guardians. This study included questions such as time spent on online classes, self-study or study with parents and gadgets used for the online classes. Results: Most of the children were students of classes upper kinder garden and I, comprising 19.0% and 18.3%, respectively. Females outnumbered males in the study. Weight gain was observed in 43.8%, and signs of irritability were observed in 68.0% of the children. Weight gain showed a statistically significant correlation with the duration of online classes, indoor and outdoor playtime with p-values of 0.044, <0.005 and 0.005, respectively. There was also a statistically significant correlation between change in behaviour with outdoor playtime and sleep timings with p < 0.005 and 0.019, respectively. Conclusion: This study concluded that there was a significant increase in screen time and a decrease in outdoor play activities during the time of COVID-19 pandemic with a statistically significant correlation with the weight gain and change in behaviour of the children.

title: BİST İMALAT İŞLETMELERİNİN COVID-19 PANDEMİSİNE FİNANSAL TEPKİSİ: PANEL VERİ ANALİZİ
abstract: Bu çalışmanın amacı, küresel bir sağlık ve finansal kriz niteliği taşıyan Covid-19 pandemisinin, Borsa İstanbul (BİST) imalat sanayinde faaliyet gösteren işletmelerin finansal performansları üzerindeki etkilerini ampirik olarak ortaya koymaktır. Araştırma kapsamında, BİST İmalat sanayinde işlem gören işletmelerin pandeminin etkilerinin en net yaşandığı 2019 ve 2020 yıllarına ait çeyreklik finansal veriler kullanılmış; değişkenler arasındaki ilişkiler Panel Veri Analizi yöntemiyle incelenmiştir. Analiz sonuçları, Covid-19 pandemisinin işletmelerin aktif kârlılığı üzerinde anlamlı ve negatif bir etkiye sahip olduğunu göstermektedir. Bununla birlikte, pandeminin işletmelerin aktif kârlılıkları üzerindeki olumsuz etkisinin, satış rakamları düşük olan işletmelere kıyasla, yüksek satış hacmine sahip işletmeler üzerinde çok daha belirgin ve şiddetli olduğu tespit edilmiştir. Elde edilen bulgular, kriz dönemlerinde yüksek ciro ve büyük ölçekli operasyonel yapıların her zaman finansal bağışıklık sağlamadığını, aksine yüksek satış hacmine sahip işletmelerin ani talep ve tedarik şoklarına karşı daha kırılgan olabileceğini göstermektedir. Bu doğrultuda, imalat sanayi firmalarının kriz dönemlerinde finansal esnekliklerini artırmaya yönelik stratejiler geliştirmeleri önerilmektedir.
journal: Uluslararası İktisadi ve İdari İncelemeler Dergisi

title: A Universidade de Brasília na pandemia de Covid-19
abstract: Objetivo: descrição e análise das estratégias implementadas no enfrentamento da pandemia de Covid-19 na Universidade de Brasília (UnB), identificando as principais ações e medidas adotadas e analisando os desafios enfrentados na tomada de decisões, bem como avaliando os impactos gerados. Métodos: trata-se de pesquisa documental com análise de conteúdo de documentos oficiais disponíveis nos sites institucionais e federais para identificar as ações e as estratégias adotadas pela gestão durante a pandemia de Covid-19. Resultados: ações importantes incluíram a criação de comitês para elaboração do plano de contingência, planejamento e viabilização de pesquisa e inovação para o enfrentamento da pandemia, além de coordenação das ações de readequação administrativa e acadêmica. Atividades presenciais foram substituídas por domiciliares. Guias de biossegurança e de retomada das atividades foram elaborados. Conclusões: os resultados demonstraram a adaptação da UnB ao contexto, reorganizando estrutura e processos para garantir a continuidade das atividades e proteger a comunidade. A criação de ambientes favoráveis ao ensino à distância, assim como ações de vigilância e assistência à saúde, e medidas de controle tiveram papel fundamental na resposta eficaz. Palavras-chaves: Vigilância em saúde pública. Preparação para pandemia.

title: Prevalence of Musculoskeletal Symptoms in Post-COVID-19 Patients
abstract: Background: Coronavirus disease 2019 can affect several body systems, and musculoskeletal symptoms may persist after recovery from the acute infection. Pain and other musculoskeletal complaints can create additional challenges during the post-COVID-19 recovery period. Objective: To determine the frequency and distribution of musculoskeletal symptoms among post-COVID-19 patients. Methodology: This observational cross-sectional study was conducted from June to September 2021 after ethical approval from the Lyallpur Institute of Management Sciences, using purposive sampling to recruit 120 individuals with previous COVID-19 infection, of whom 70 met the eligibility criteria. Participants were aged 30 to 55 years, had recovered from COVID-19 with a negative test, reported musculoskeletal symptoms, and had manual muscle testing grades 1–3, while smokers, those with autoimmune conditions, those >55 years, and participants still positive or under quarantine were excluded. Data were collected through a demographic form, self-developed screening questionnaire, 0–5 verbal pain scale, Musculoskeletal Health Questionnaire, and Standardised Nordic Musculoskeletal Questionnaire, administered through face-to-face interviews. The Musculoskeletal Health Questionnaire assessed overall musculoskeletal health (0–56), while the Nordic Questionnaire identified symptoms across different anatomical regions. Descriptive statistics, including frequencies, percentages, and appropriate measures for numerical variables, were used to summarize demographic characteristics, pain intensity, Musculoskeletal Health Questionnaire scores, and musculoskeletal symptoms. Results: Of the 70 participants, 50 (71.4%) reported very severe pain, 14 (20%) reported the worst possible pain, and 6 (8.6%) reported severe pain. Neck and shoulder symptoms were reported by all participants (100%), followed by upper-back symptoms (98.6%) and lower-back symptoms (94.3%). Knee symptoms were reported by 81.4% of participants, while ankle, elbow, and wrist symptoms were reported by 68.6%, 57.1%, and 54.3%, respectively. Hip symptoms were reported by 42.9% of participants. Conclusion: Musculoskeletal symptoms were frequently reported among the post-COVID-19 patients included in this study, particularly in the neck, shoulder, upper-back, and lower-back regions. These findings highlight the importance of assessing musculoskeletal complaints during post-COVID-19 follow-up. Larger prospective studies incorporating objective functional assessments are needed to determine symptom progression and rehabilitation needs.

Neck and shoulder symptoms were reported by all participants (100%), followed by upper-back symptoms (98.6%) and lower-back symptoms (94.3%). Knee symptoms were reported by 81.4% of participants, while ankle, elbow, and wrist symptoms were reported by 68.6%, 57.1%, and 54.3%, respectively. Hip symptoms were reported by 42.9% of participants. Conclusion: Musculoskeletal symptoms were frequently reported among the post-COVID-19 patients included in this study, particularly in the neck, shoulder, upper-back, and lower-back regions. These findings highlight the importance of assessing musculoskeletal complaints during post-COVID-19 follow-up. Larger prospective studies incorporating objective functional assessments are needed to determine symptom progression and rehabilitation needs.

title: Prognostic Value of the Veno-Arterial Carbon Dioxide Difference in COVID-19-Associated Acute Hypoxemic Respiratory Failure: A Retrospective Cohort Study
abstract: Background/Objectives: In acute hypoxemic respiratory failure, hyperventilation and alterations in oxygenation can influence CO2 kinetics via the Haldane effect, potentially modifying the venous-to-arterial carbon dioxide partial pressure gradient (PvaCO2) irrespective of tissue perfusion, thereby complicating its prognostic significance. This study assessed the predictive importance of PvaCO2 in critically ill patients experiencing acute respiratory failure linked to COVID-19. Methods: This retrospective bicentric study included critically ill patients with hypoxemic COVID-19 (PaO2/FiO2 100–200 mmHg), and mild (>200 mmHg)—a stronger exploratory signal related to ICU mortality was observed in moderate hypoxemia; however, the formal interaction did not reach statistical significance (Pinteraction = 0.075). Conclusions: Early PvaCO2 was not significantly associated with ICU death within 28 days in patients with predominantly hypoxemic respiratory failure without major baseline circulatory shock. Exploratory subgroup analyses suggested that its association with outcome may vary according to arterial and central venous oxygenation. This hypothesis warrants targeted evaluation in future prospective studies.

title: Multimodal physiological determinants of persistent dyspnea nearly four years after COVID-19 hospitalization
abstract: Dyspnea is a frequent and disabling symptom following COVID-19 and may persist despite preserved pulmonary and cardiac function. The physiological mechanisms underlying persistent dyspnea at long-term follow-up remain incompletely characterized. We conducted a cross-sectional analysis nested within a prospective cohort of COVID-19 survivors evaluated 41–47 months after hospitalization. Participants with identifiable structural cardiopulmonary disease were excluded based on comprehensive pulmonary function testing and echocardiography. Dyspnea was assessed using the modified Medical Research Council (mMRC) scale and analyzed as both a binary (mMRC ≥ 2) and ordinal outcome. Inspiratory muscle weakness was defined as concomitant reductions in maximal inspiratory pressure and sniff nasal inspiratory pressure (< 70% predicted). A standardized multimodal assessment included respiratory and peripheral muscle function, ultrasonography, functional capacity testing, and fatigue evaluation. Associations were examined using hierarchical logistic and ordinal regression models. Among 270 participants, clinically relevant dyspnea (mMRC ≥ 2) was present in 34.4%. In multivariable hierarchical models, dyspnea was independently associated with inspiratory muscle weakness (OR 8.86, 95% CI 6.33–12.41), along with female sex, obesity, higher fatigue burden, respiratory muscle ultrasound abnormalities, and reduced peripheral muscle strength. Model discrimination improved stepwise across hierarchical models, reaching an AUC of 0.89 for dyspnea. Dyspnea severity showed graded associations with respiratory muscle dysfunction, peripheral muscle impairment, reduced functional capacity, and fatigue. Inspiratory muscle weakness (23.4%) was characterized by a distinct muscular profile involving diaphragmatic and parasternal intercostal abnormalities together with reduced peripheral muscle mass and strength. Hierarchical models predicting inspiratory muscle weakness also demonstrated strong discriminative performance, with AUC up to 0.92. Nearly four years after hospitalization, persistent dyspnea remains common among COVID-19 survivors without structural cardiopulmonary disease and is associated with a multidimensional physiological profile. Respiratory muscle dysfunction, integrated with peripheral muscle impairment and fatigue, represents a key correlate of long-term dyspnea.

title: Determinants of Community Compliance With COVID 19 Health Protocols in Indonesia: An Integrative Literature Review
abstract: Background: Community compliance with health protocols was essential during the early COVID 19 pandemic. Understanding its determinants may inform preparedness for future respiratory outbreaks. Objectives: This integrative literature review synthesized Indonesian evidence on factors associated with community compliance with COVID 19 preventive protocols. Methods: Google Scholar was the documented search source. Of 31 initially identified records, 16 remained after restriction, and six studies met eligibility criteria. Eligible studies examined community compliance with preventive protocols and provided accessible full text. Findings were synthesized descriptively using a Health Belief Model informed framework. Results: Across six studies, compliance was associated with cognitive factors, including knowledge, awareness, perceived threat, and perceived barriers; motivational and social factors, including attitudes, concern, motivation, and social environment; and structural factors, particularly facility availability. Findings varied across study settings, suggesting that compliance reflected interactions among individual perceptions, social influences, and environmental opportunities. Conclusions: Community compliance during the early pandemic was associated with interconnected cognitive, motivational, social, and structural factors. These findings provide contextual lessons for designing integrated health promotion strategies and strengthening preparedness for future respiratory outbreaks.

title: Spontaneous Tumor Bleed with Subarachnoid Hemorrhage in Conus Ependymoma with COVID-19 and Dengue Co-Infection—A Case Report
abstract: Abstract Spinal subarachnoid hemorrhage (SAH) is a rare complication of dengue-associated thrombocytopenia. Hemorrhagic manifestations have also been infrequently reported with coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) infections. However, the clinical implications of COVID-19 and dengue coinfections remain poorly understood and may be severe. We report the case of a 32-year-old man with COVID 19 and dengue coinfection complicated by severe thrombocytopenia, who subsequently developed an acute-onset neurological deficit below the L1 level. Magnetic resonance imaging demonstrated spontaneous spinal SAH, and the patient underwent decompressive surgery with simultaneous platelet transfusion support. Histopathological examination of the clot tissue unexpectedly revealed an underlying ependymoma. Following decompression, platelet correction, and structured rehabilitation, the patient showed gradual neurological recovery and regained the ability to walk. This case highlights that thrombocytopenia-related intraspinal hemorrhage should be considered a rare but important cause of acute neurological deficit in patient with COVID-19 and dengue coinfection. It also emphasizes the importance of maintaining a high index of suspicion for underlying intraspinal pathology and obtaining tissue diagnosis when feasible.

title: Provision of cross-border reproductive care in Czechia during the COVID-19 pandemic: a population-based study
abstract: Cross-border reproductive care (CBRC) is shaped by legal frameworks, costs, the quality of care, access constraints and socio-cultural preferences. The COVID-19 pandemic disrupted access to assisted reproductive technology services through lockdowns, travel restrictions and shifting regulations, thus rendering CBRC unstable and affecting access unevenly across countries. This study evaluates changes in the volume and structure of CBRC in Czechia during 2016–2021, focusing on the COVID-19 period (2020–2021), and identifies those origin countries that exhibited the most pronounced changes in demand. A population-based quantitative study of all the assisted reproduction cycles initiated in Czechia between 2016 and 2021, excluding egg donation. Employing anonymised individual data obtained from the National Registry of Assisted Reproduction, 231,363 ART cycles entered the analysis, of which 93,834 (41%) were cycles sought by women who visited Czechia for infertility treatment. A time-series approach based on year-on-year relative changes was applied to capture the temporal dynamics. The pre-COVID trend (2017–2019) for 26 source countries was summarised applying geometric mean growth rates, whereas the COVID years 2020 and 2021 were analysed as distinct periods. Cross-border reproductive care represents an important component of the provision of assisted reproduction in Czechia. Assisted reproduction cycles declined by 2% during the pandemic with concern to the domestic population, whereas CBRC decreased by 27%. Although declines were recorded for most countries, increases in demand were registered for other states. While the COVID-19 pandemic markedly reduced the overall volume of CBRC provided in Czechia, country-specific trajectories suggest that structural factors in the origin countries appear to continue to shape cross-border demand and treatment choices. From the policy perspective, the results underline the importance of expanding equitable and liberal access to national health system-provided reproductive healthcare. The barriers presented by national systems act to shift the demand for treatment abroad, which fuels CBRC and increases the financial, medical, legal and psychosocial risks faced by couples.

title: Constructing a work management model for outsourced personnel in medical institutions during the COVID-19 epidemic
abstract: During the COVID-19 pandemic, outsourcing non-core services like cleaning, security, and logistics allowed healthcare facilities to focus on patient care. In Taiwan, the Ministry of Health and Welfare’s guidelines ensured outsourced staff were properly trained to minimize infection risks, supporting epidemic control. Our hospital’s “Epidemic Response Command System” highlighted the critical role of outsourced personnel in maintaining operational continuity, enabling medical staff to focus on patient care. Outsourcing was essential for supporting logistics and operations, ensuring the smooth functioning of the hospital while healthcare professionals focused on direct patient care. Simultaneously, stringent auditing mechanisms were established to enable outsourced colleagues to perform tasks within a safety-controlled framework. Emphasis was placed on prioritized and enhanced management for personnel engaged in cleaning, transportation, and access security, including personnel segregation and diversion management. In-depth on-site training by infection control nurses covered cleaning, disinfection operations, health management, and counseling mechanisms. It was executed meticulously, given the paramount importance of operations auditing in infection control and epidemic prevention effectiveness. The COVID-19 pandemic highlighted the need for stricter infection control. Reducing outsourced personnel ensures standardized hygiene protocols, better staff protection, and reduced legal risks, improving overall healthcare response. In future planning for specialized units, medical institutions should consider minimizing outsourced personnel or implementing measures, such as enhancing salary and benefits, for dedicated on-site staff.

title: Association of Vitamin D Deficiency with COVID-19 Susceptibility and Severity in Hospitalized Children: A Case–Control Study
abstract: Background: Vitamin D exerts immunomodulatory and anti-inflammatory effects that may influence outcomes of viral respiratory infections, including COVID-19. However, pediatric data remain limited. This study examined the relationship between serum 25-hydroxy-vitamin D [25(OH)D] levels and susceptibility to and severity of COVID-19 among hospitalized children in Iran. Methods: In this retrospective case–control study, 63 children (0–16 years) with RT-PCR-confirmed COVID-19 admitted to Firouzabadi Hospital, Tehran (2019–2021) were compared with 68 age- and sex-matched historical controls hospitalized two years before the pandemic for non-respiratory conditions. Moreover, historical controls were used to avoid pandemic-era confounding due to widespread supplementation and asymptomatic infection. Demographic, clinical, and laboratory data including 25(OH)D, C-reactive protein (CRP), lymphocyte count, and need for pediatric intensive-care-unit (PICU) admission-were also extracted. Statistical analysis employed non-parametric tests with P-value < 0.05 as significant. Results: Vitamin D deficiency (<20 ng/ml) occurred in 61% of cases versus 14% of controls (P<0.001). Mean 25(OH)D levels were lower in cases (18.6±9.6 ng/ml) than controls (43.4±25.3 ng/ml, P<0.001). PICU-admitted patients showed lower vitamin D than non-PICU patients (13.8±6.4 vs 19.7±9.9 ng/ml, P=0.035). Conclusions: Vitamin D deficiency was strongly associated with COVID-19 susceptibility but not with in-hospital severity. Therefore, routine screening and correction of vitamin D deficiency may be a cost-effective preventive strategy for pediatric populations.

title: Anxiety, depression and perceived stress among nursing students and their family members in the post-COVID-19 setting: a cross-sectional study in Barranquilla, Colombia
abstract: Introduction: During the first year of the COVID-19 pandemic, the global prevalence of anxiety and depression rose by about 25%, with women and young people most affected. Now that the emergency phase is over, it is necessary to know the mental health status of university students' families, a group that is rarely measured directly. Objective: To describe the levels of anxiety, depression and perceived stress among nursing students and their family members, and to explore their relationship with age, gender, socioeconomic stratum and religion. Methods: Quantitative, descriptive, cross-sectional study with non-probability convenience sampling. Thirty-nine people aged 17 to 79 took part: third-semester nursing students at Universidad Metropolitana de Barranquilla and their family members. The GAD-7, the PHQ-9 and the 10-item Perceived Stress Scale (PSS-10) were administered. Associations were tested with the chi-square test and, because of the small cell counts, with an exact test estimated by Monte Carlo simulation.Results: Of the participants, 67% were women, 31% were aged 17 to 25, 49% belonged to socioeconomic stratum 2 and 87% were Catholic. Absence of symptoms and mild levels predominated. Mild anxiety was the most frequent category among those aged 17 to 25 (66.7%), and 25% of those aged 44 to 52 had severe anxiety. The chi-square test suggested an association between age and anxiety (p = 0.046), but the exact test did not confirm it (p = 0.080). No other variable was significantly associated with anxiety, depression or stress. Conclusions: Participants mostly showed mild or no symptoms, with no significant differences by sociodemographic variables. The cross-sectional design and the sample size do not allow these levels to be attributed to the pandemic, but the cases of severe anxiety and moderately severe depression among middle-aged family members warrant follow-up of family mental health in the post-pandemic period.

title: FORMATIVE PROCESS OF GRADUATE STUDENTS IN NURSING IN THE CONTEXT OF COVID-19
abstract: Objective: to report the experience of remote teaching in an academic master’s degree course during the covid-19 pandemic. Methods: this is a descriptive study, experience report type, experienced from October to December 2020 in a mandatory subject of the Postgraduate Program in Nursing of a Public University in the state of Pará. Results: The educational activities took place synchronously and asynchronous, from virtual classes and texts for reading, all of that was possible by the use of educational technological strategies in the experienced pandemic scenario. Remote teaching required students and teachers to adapt to the new classroom routine in their homes, adapting the study environment and appropriate equipment for this context. Even with the challenges faced, the establishment of the remote learning process added skills among those involved, improvement of tools and digital transformation of the conventional classroom. Conclusion: remote teaching was efficient and provided opportunities for pedagogical mediations, promoting collaborative learning among students. It also revealed the need for training for those involved in the process.

title: Multi-Scale In Silico Discovery of Potent SARS-CoV-2 RdRp Inhibitors
abstract: In this study, hybrid compounds containing 1,3-thiazolidin-4-one and benzene sulfonohydrazide moieties were evaluated against severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) RNA-dependent RNA polymerase (RdRp) using in silico methods. Molecular docking showed binding energies between -5.5 and -6.6 kcal.mol-1, with compound 7, displaying affinities comparable to remdesivir. Molecular dynamics (MD) simulations indicated greater stability for the Z isomer, while the E isomer reached similar stability over time. Density functional theory (DFT) analyses revealed that the Z isomer has a higher dipole moment and a smaller highest occupied molecular orbital–lowest unoccupied molecular orbital (HOMO–LUMO) energy gap, suggesting increased reactivity. Condensed Fukui function analysis further indicated that the nitro group represents the main electrophilic and reduction-prone region, while the 1,3-thiazolidin-4-one–sulfonohydrazide framework contributes to nucleophilic and radical reactivity in an isomer-dependent manner. ADME profiling and metabolite prediction indicated favorable pharmacokinetics, including low lipophilicity, high polarity, and an acceptable safety profile. Overall, these findings highlight the 1,3-thiazolidin-4-one–benzene sulfonohydrazide scaffold as a promising framework for RdRp inhibition and identify compound 7 as a strong candidate for further optimization and experimental validation.

ADME profiling and metabolite prediction indicated favorable pharmacokinetics, including low lipophilicity, high polarity, and an acceptable safety profile. Overall, these findings highlight the 1,3-thiazolidin-4-one–benzene sulfonohydrazide scaffold as a promising framework for RdRp inhibition and identify compound 7 as a strong candidate for further optimization and experimental validation.

title: Post Acute Sequelae of COVID 19: A Prospective Observational Study
abstract: The aim was to evaluate sequelae of COVID-19 on CXR and HRCT thorax in young and middle-aged patients. This was a prospective observational study comprising a total number of 58 COVID cases from November 2020 to October 2022. The baseline scan during the active phase of the disease was collected followed by CT scan done 3 to 24 months later. 30 patients had mild disease, 15 had moderate and 13 had severe disease during the active phase of the disease (based on CT severity score - out of 25). 39.66% patients showed post- acute-infection sequelae of COVID. Fibrosis was the predominant sequelae observed in 21 patients- mild in10, moderate in 9 and severe in 2. Fibrosis was more common with advancing age in the age group of 41-50 years (61% had fibrosis). The majority of the patients (60%) showed complete clearance of the acute changes in the lung. Post COVID lung fibrosis was found approximately in 36 % of patients, predominantly in patients with moderate to severe disease.
journal: International Journal of Science and Research (IJSR)

title: Perceived Body Weight and Food Choice Motives among Malaysian Adults: Comparative Study between the Pandemic and Endemic Phases of COVID-19
abstract: Background: The COVID-19 pandemic significantly disrupted dietary patterns, food purchasing behaviors, and food choice motives. This study aimed to examine differences in perceived body weight and food choice motives between the pandemic and endemic phases and to investigate the associations between the motives among a sample of adults residing in Selangor, Malaysia. Methods: A cross-sectional study was conducted among 318 adults aged 18–55 years recruited in Selangor using a convenience sampling approach in year 2022. Data on perceived body weight were gathered using a single-item scale, and food choice motives were assessed via a validated 38-item Food Choice Questionnaire. During the pandemic, body weight and height were self-reported, while measurements during the endemic phase were taken by trained researchers. Results: The proportion of participants classified as obese rose from 41.2% during the pandemic to 50.6% in the endemic phase. Approximately, half of the respondents misperceived their body weight in both phases (47.8% and 46.9%, respectively). Food choice motives shifted significantly, with religion, price, and convenience being most influential during the endemic phase, compared to mood, religion, and price during the pandemic. However, perceived body weight was not significantly associated with food choice motives in either phase. Conclusion: This study offers important insights into the evolving nature of food choice motives and body weight perception across two key phases of the COVID-19 pandemic, with implications for designing public health interventions promoting healthier dietary behaviors and accurate weight perception in Malaysian adults.
journal: Journal of Nutrition and Food Security

title: Peak-Weighted Calibration of Implemented Integer-Order, Caputo, and Atangana–Baleanu–Caputo Schemes for Simultaneous COVID-19 and Influenza Transmission
abstract: COVID-19 and influenza may produce overlapping waves, yet an overall least-squares fit need not represent their high-activity weeks well. We compare implemented integer-order, Caputo, and Atangana–Baleanu–Caputo (ABC) discrete schemes for a common ten-compartment transition structure with seasonal transmission and external influenza input. The schemes are calibrated with ordinary mean-normalized weighted least squares (J1) and a peak-weighted objective (J2). We fit the first 66 of 83 weekly observation pairs and assess the remaining 17 weeks. ABC gives the smallest training peak root-mean-square error for both series under either objective. Within ABC, J2 reduces COVID-19 and influenza training peak errors by 9.50% and 42.98%, respectively, relative to its J1 fit. Integer order achieves the smallest ordinary loss and lower temporal validation error. The autonomous disease-free and conditional invasion thresholds characterize the underlying unforced vector field, not the fitted seasonal system. These findings support peak-weighted calibration for retrospective high-activity reconstruction in these data, but they do not establish superior future-peak prediction.

title: Nutrition Status and Health-Related Quality of Life of Individuals Post COVID-19: A Retrospective Cross-Sectional Study
abstract: Aim: Persistent symptoms following COVID-19 may adversely affect nutritional status and health-related quality of life. This study evaluated these outcomes and their associations with pulmonary function and clinical characteristics.Material and Methods: This cross-sectional retrospective study included 200 ICU-hospitalized COVID-19 patients (June 2020–December 2022) who later attended outpatient follow-up. Hospitalization and post-discharge data were obtained from institutional electronic systems and HSYS. Statistical analyses were conducted using SPSS 27.0, with p 60 years and those with chronic diseases. Overall, 89.0% of participants had normal nutritional status, 10.0% were at risk of malnutrition, and 1.0% were classified as malnourished. Participants with normal nutritional status had significantly higher EQ-VAS scores than those who were at risk of malnutrition or malnourished (p=0.020).Conclusion: Post-COVID-19 individuals exhibited reductions in both nutritional status and quality of life, underscoring the importance of long-term monitoring and targeted follow-up, particularly among high-risk groups.

title: Global logistics priorities before and after COVID-19: A multi-criteria assessment of logistics performance index dimensions across income groups
abstract: This study examines changes in global logistics priorities by comparing the relative importance of the six Logistics Performance Index (LPI) dimensions across income groups in the 2018 and 2023 evaluation periods. A fixed common panel of 134 countries is classified into high-, upper-middle-, lower-middle-, and low-income groups to ensure comparability between the two periods. Criterion weights are determined using three objective weighting methods, LODECI, LOPCOW, and SITDE, and integrated through arithmetic averaging. Countries are then ranked using the ALPAS method. The findings reveal different weighting patterns across income groups and periods. International shipments remain the highest-weighted dimension in the high-income group, while customs retain the highest weight in the lower-middle-income group. In the upper-middle-income group, tracking and tracing remains the highest-weighted dimension in both 2018 and 2023, although its weight decreases from 0.201 to 0.184. The most notable change is observed in the low-income group, where the weight of timeliness decreases from 0.160 to 0.112, while international shipments gain relative importance and tracking and tracing retains the highest weight despite declining from 0.213 to 0.191. Country rankings also show both stability and substantial movements within each income group. Comparisons with AROMAN, CRADIS, MABAC, and MAIRCA, together with scenario-based sensitivity analysis, indicate that the main ranking structure is highly stable. The integrated-ALPAS rankings also show strong agreement with the official World Bank LPI rankings. Overall, the findings indicate that the relative importance of LPI dimensions varies across income groups and evaluation periods, supporting a more context-sensitive interpretation of logistics performance and providing a basis for income-group-specific policy and managerial priorities.
journal: International Journal of Business and Economic Studies

title: The COVID-19 Pandemic as a Natural Experiment: Advancing the Understanding of Stress, Rhythm Dysregulation, and Mental Health in Healthcare Workers
abstract: Few events in recent history have forced clinicians and researchers to rethink mental health quite like COVID-19. In this commentary, we reflect on something that struck us while reading the work of Cantone et al. : the pandemic, for all its devastation, created a kind of unplanned observational window, a chance to study, at population scale, what happens when stress and rhythm disruption hit at the same time. Healthcare Workers (HCWs) were at the epicentre of this. They didn't just witness the crisis; they absorbed it, shift after shift, for months. What the data show is that their depressive symptoms and rhythm instability were not random; they appear systematically linked, and at levels one would more typically associate with mood disorder research. We discuss these findings through the lens of DYMERS (Dysregulation of Mood, Energy, and Social Rhythms Syndrome), a heuristic transdiagnostic construct that, in our view, captures something that standard categorical diagnoses tend to miss: the subthreshold, fluctuating psychopathology that sits just below the threshold of formal diagnosis but causes real impairment. The pandemic may not have created these vulnerabilities, but it may well have sharpened our ability to see them.
journal: Clinical Practice & Epidemiology in Mental Health

title: Pre-hospital emergency care for patients with suspected stroke during the COVID-19 pandemic: a retrospective analysis from the Ústí nad Labem Region
abstract: Purpose is to evaluate the impact of the first year of the COVID-19 pandemic on selected temporal and organizational parameters of prehospital emergency care for patients with suspected stroke in the Ústí nad Labem Region by comparing system performance before and during the pandemic. Materials and Methods. A retrospective observational study was conducted using data from the Electronic Patient Record system of the Ústí nad Labem Region Emergency Medical Service. Patients with suspected stroke (ICD-10 codes I60–I64) treated between March 2019 and February 2021 were included. Two 12-month periods were compared: pre-pandemic (March 2019–February 2020) and pandemic (March 2020–February 2021). Primary outcomes were dispatch call-processing time, response time, and on-scene time. Statistical analyses were performed in R (version 4.5.1) using the Wilcoxon rank-sum test, chi-square test, and two-proportion test (α = 0.05). A total of 1.783 emergency calls were analysed (917 pre-pandemic, 866 pandemic). No significant differences were found in the number of patients (p = 0.488), median age (73 years; p = 0.785), or distribution of calls by time of day (p = 0.598). During the pandemic, median response time increased from 11:03 to 11:57 (p < 0.001), while dispatch call-processing time increased from 2:44 to 2:58 (p < 0.001). On-scene time remained unchanged at 22:00 minutes (p = 0.362). The prehospital emergency care system remained resilient during the COVID-19 pandemic. Although dispatch and response times increased slightly, stable on-scene times indicate effective adaptation of emergency medical teams. Dispatch centres appear to be the most vulnerable component of the prehospital stroke care pathway and should be prioritised in future emergency preparedness planning.

title: Indian National Health Protection Scheme and COVID-19: Response and Lessons Learnt
abstract: The coronavirus (COVID-19) has placed the entire planet in an unprecedented state of misery, with innumerable medical catastrophes, countless deaths, and significant mental strain. The Ayushman Bharat-Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (AB-PMJAY), a government-funded health insurance program launched by the Government of India a year before the COVID-19 pandemic, aimed to provide total financial security for vulnerable and disadvantaged families against medical emergencies. This study investigates the response of this program to COVID-19 management in India, with its allocation of Rs. 5 lakh per family per year for secondary and tertiary-level medical care. This qualitative study examines both the positive and negative experiences of beneficiaries, as identified through thematic analysis. It also seeks to capture the impact of this initiative using social justice theory, a strength-based approach, and systems theory. The study included ten purposely selected respondents from COVID-19-affected beneficiary households in Dakshina Karnataka and attempted to comprehend the benefits and shortcomings of AB-PMJAY's response to COVID-19 through their narratives. This study's findings revealed a mixed reaction. While access to quality healthcare, a sense of contentment, reduced out-of-pocket expenditure, and reduced mental agony were the positive experiences acknowledged, the individual/system drawbacks reported by respondents included lack of support systems, bureaucratic delays, infrastructure constraints, lack of awareness, and incomplete coverage.

title: Left Behind Places and Regional Resilience to COVID-19 Shock in Europe
abstract: Current turbulent times pose challenges not only for countries, but also-and above all-for regions within them. However, economic resilience of left behind places is still underexplored, especially in the light of entrenched regional disparities. The aim of this paper is to investigate the nexus between regional development and economic resilience across 898 European NUTS 3 regions during the COVID-19 pandemic. To go beyond the GDP-based approach, we construct a multidimensional "left behindness" index. Our findings show that left-behind places, as identified through this multidimensional approach, were relatively more successful in resisting the immediate pandemic shock, while more developed regions demonstrated a stronger recovery capacity. The analysis also highlights that international trade, industrial specialization and the share of public employment acted as determinants of these divergent resilience trajectories. The results suggest that policymakers should adopt a differentiated strategy by strengthening the resistance of more advanced regions and enhancing the recovery capacity of left behind places to reduce persistent regional disparities.

title: COVID-19 EM AMBIENTE PSIQUIÁTRICO: UMA ANÁLISE TRANSVERSAL DA CONTENÇÃO DA TRANSMISSÃO E AVALIAÇÃO DOS CASOS CONFIRMADOS EM UM HOSPITAL PÚBLICO NO PERÍODO DE 2020 A 2023
abstract: Este estudo sistematizou o plano de contenção adotado por um hospital psiquiátrico da rede pública de saúde para prevenir a propagação do vírus no ambiente hospitalar, descrevendo também as características sociodemográficas, clínicas e laboratoriais dos pacientes com covid-19 que internaram no período de 2020 a 2023. Trata-se de um estudo transversal composto de uma avaliação documental das estratégias de contenção adotadas e dos registros em prontuário médico realizados na internação psiquiátrica. Foram calculadas frequências com medidas de tendência central e de dispersão na análise descritiva para avaliar as características sociodemográficas, clínicas e laboratoriais e análises bivariadas para avaliar o risco de os pacientes manifestarem sintomas da covid-19. Nas análises foram utilizados o Teste Chi-Quadrado de Pearson, Teste Exato de Fisher, Teste Exato de Fisher Generalizado, Teste t-Student e o Teste de Wilcoxon para um nível de significância estatística 0,05. Medidas de associação foram determinadas pelo Coeficiente de Cramer V e cálculo de Odds ratio. Foram avaliados 251 pacientes. title: Metaphors and the COVID-19 pandemic
abstract: This chapter explains why and how metaphor played a central role in communication about COVID-19 during the years of the pandemic. I begin by defining metaphor from the perspective of Conceptual Metaphor Theory. I then provide an overview of research on metaphors and the pandemic, focusing on a selection of studies that take a linguistic (including multimodal) perspective, and/or that investigate responses to linguistic stimuli. Conventional metaphors to do with War, Journey, Sports, and Natural Disaster are discussed alongside creative metaphors such as the description of heroism during the pandemic as acting like a hedgehog. I then focus on the metaphor of the pandemic as a series of ‘waves’, and show how even this highly conventional metaphor was used creatively for a variety of rhetorical purposes under the communicative pressures caused by the pandemic. I conclude by looking ahead at directions for future research.

title: Trajectories of mental health and well-being across healthcare workers during COVID-19 pandemic: a Swiss longitudinal study
abstract: This longitudinal study examined the trajectories of healthcare workers’ mental health from the first to the second COVID-19 wave (May 2020–December 2020) in a Swiss tertiary hospital, and their association with individual and organizational factors. For each mental health outcome (depression, anxiety, peritraumatic stress, and well-being), a separate analysis identified two trajectories: one with higher, persistent levels of symptoms and one that was resilient, with low-level symptoms. The persistent trajectory comprised about 25%–30% of participants for anxiety, depression and peritraumatic stress and 47% for well-being; because the classifications were outcome-specific, membership differed across outcomes (about 15% of participants were on a persistent trajectory for all four outcomes and 46% resilient for all four). We found that women, nurses, caregivers, non-managerial employees, and frontline COVID-19 workers were more likely to follow a persistent trajectory. Organizational risk factors were a high workload and an irregular work schedule. These results provide a basis for implementing risk-adapted prevention measures and resilience-promotion programs to protect health workers from the impact of major crises. Future research should address the needs of vulnerable health workers to provide evidence-based health promotion.

title: Urban Exodus After COVID-19? Internal Migration Trends Pre- and Post-pandemic in Germany
abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic has been linked to increased net migration gains in suburban, peri-urban, and rural areas, at the expense of larger cities, contributing to suburbanization in many Western countries. Post-pandemic trends are less understood, but recent evidence indicates a return to pre-pandemic levels of internal migration intensity. This study examines internal migration trends in Germany in the aftermath of the COVID-19 pandemic, drawing on comprehensive flow data from 1991 to 2024. We analyze migration patterns across four urban-rural categories to assess the destinations of different age groups. The results indicate that net migration losses in the large cities continue to be driven by young adults. The pre-pandemic trend of sub- and counterurbanization persists during and after the pandemic, largely due to stable urban-to-rural migration by family movers. However, the second-most densely populated areas, “urban counties”, emerge as the winners in the internal migration trends across the urban-rural continuum.

title: Unequal recovery of health facility visits in hospitals and township health centres after COVID-19 disruption in Henan Province, China, 2014–2024: a time-series study
abstract: Background The COVID-19 pandemic disrupted health service utilisation worldwide. Its long-term effect remains uncertain, especially after the major adjustment of China’s COVID-19 control policies at the end of 2022. Evidence is also limited on whether recovery differed between hospitals and township health centres (THCs). The research aimed to evaluate the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic and its ending on health facility visits in hospitals and THCs in Henan Province from 2014 to 2024. Methods Monthly aggregate data on total health facility visits in hospitals and THCs in Henan Province from January, 2014, to December, 2024, were obtained from the health statistics system. The observation period was divided into the pre-pandemic period (2014–2019), the pandemic period (2020–2022), and the post-pandemic period (2023–2024). A Quasi-Poisson regression model was trained with data from 2014 to 2018. The residual series from the Quasi-Poisson model was then modelled using an LSTM neural network. Data from 2019 were used as the validation set to compare the predictive performance of the Quasi-Poisson model and the Quasi-Poisson-LSTM hybrid model. The final model was used to generate counterfactual predictions for 2020–2024, and relative differences between observed and predicted values were calculated with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Key results In 2024, hospitals and THCs in Henan Province recorded 423 million health facility visits. During 2014–2019, the EAPC in per-person visits was 5.0% (95% CI 3.8–6.1) overall, with a faster increase in hospitals (6.5%, 5.8–7.3) than in THCs (2.2%, −0.5 to 5.0). Over 2014–2024, the EAPC increased to 4.4% (3.0–5.8) in THCs, whereas it decreased to 4.8% (3.8–5.9) in hospitals. The Quasi-Poisson-LSTM model had lower prediction error than the Quasi-Poisson model alone for total visits (RMSE 42.7081 vs. 51.7871; MAE 34.2020 vs. Counterfactual predictions showed that total visits were 14.7% (95% CI 13.2–16.2%) lower than expected in 2020, 4.8% (2.8–7.0%) lower in 2021, and 6.8% (4.3–9.3%) lower in 2022. In 2023 and 2024, total visits returned to near-expected levels, with non-significant relative differences of −1.4% (−4.4% to 1.7%) and 2.3% (−1.2% to 6.0%), respectively. However, facility-specific patterns diverged. In 2024, hospital visits remained 6.0% (3.9–9.5%) below expected levels, whereas THCs visits were 39.7% (20.8–45.0) above expected levels. Conclusion The COVID-19 pandemic had divergent effects on health facility visits in hospitals and THCs in Henan Province. Although total visit volume had returned to the expected level in the post-pandemic era, hospital-based visits remained persistently below expected levels, while THCs showed substantial excess use. These findings suggest that care-seeking patterns might have shifted structurally in the post-pandemic era.
