title: Pregnant Women With COVID‐19 Hospitalised in a Maternity Ward: Infection Severity, Mothers' Physical Status, and Sick Leave
abstract: ABSTRACT Objective To compare the severity of COVID‐19 infection in pregnant women hospitalised in a maternity ward and to investigate whether severity affected physical status and sick leave in the postpartum period. Methods This registry study retrieved data from Sahlgrenska University Hospital's COVID‐19 Registry (SU‐COVID Registry) and the Swedish Social Insurance Agency. In total, data from 178 patients ≥ 18 years of age and hospitalised in a maternity ward between 1 March 2020 and 31 March 2022 were included. Results Most women had mild disease (mild 66.3%) followed by moderate (28.7%) and severe (5.1%) disease ( p < 0.001). There were no significant differences regarding physical status measured as walking capacity or activities of daily living (ADL) capacity at admission and on discharge according to COVID‐19 severity. There was no significant difference across groups according to COVID‐19 severity in terms of how many participants were on postpartum sick leave (mild 15.3%, moderate 13.7%, and severe 33.3%; p = 0.319) nor regarding mean (SD) days of postpartum sick leave mild (7.2 [42.3]), moderate (6.8 [21.5]), and severe (24.8 [39.2]); p = 0.383). Conclusion Two‐thirds (66.3%) of women with COVID‐19 infection hospitalised in a maternity ward had a mild COVID‐19 infection. Furthermore, walking and ADL capacity were unchanged from hospital admission to hospital discharge. A low percentage of women were on sick leave during the first year after hospital discharge and there were no significant differences according to the severity of the COVID‐19 infection.

title: Minecraft as a site of memory and collaborative learning during the COVID-19 pandemic
abstract: The emergence of cyberspace has reshaped how societies remember, as networked environments redefine space, participation and social interaction. Personal memory becomes more public and collaborative in networked environments, as memory processes shift from predominantly two-dimensional media such as photographs, drawings and texts to more immersive three-dimensional spatial environments in cyberspace. As the world undergoes rapid technological change, it also points to the need to rethink methods of education. Exploring the intersection between virtual space, creativity and memory, this research examines how a group of university students responded to the loss of their physical campus during COVID-19 by recreating their school in Minecraft. Through the Minecraft School project, this paper demonstrates how digital environments can function as sites of collective memory and foster innovative thinking through four modes of learning: game as memory palace, game as dream, game as interaction and game as remediation.

title: Determining the Effects of the COVID-19 Pandemic on Family Life in Turkey
abstract: Aim: This study aimed to examine perceived changes in family life and levels of family tension and distress during the COVID-19 pandemic in Türkiye. Materials and Methods: Participants were recruited using a non-probability sampling method. An a priori sample-size calculation conducted using G-Power indicated that at least 469 participants were required based on the prespecified statistical assumptions. A total of 631 participants were included. Data were collected using a questionnaire assessing socio-demographic characteristics, the Family Tension Index, and the Family Distress Index. Results: Among the participants, 58.5% stated that their family economy, 65.9% their family routine, 76.1% their social relationships, and 71.8% their sleep patterns were affected by the pandemic. Additionally, 38.3% reported negative changes. Furthermore, 18.7% stated that domestic violence had emerged, and 88.1% reported an increase in technology use. The mean Family Tension Index score was found to be 23.12 ± 16.31, and the mean Family Distress Index score was 11.73 ± 10.04. A statistically significant relationship was found between the Family Tension Index and having an extended family, having an income lower than expenses, being divorced, and having a disabled or chronically ill family member (p < 0.05). Similarly, Family Distress Index scores were significantly higher among divorced individuals and those with a disabled or chronically ill family member, and differed significantly according to income status (p < 0.05). Conclusion and Recommendations: The findings revealed that the COVID-19 pandemic had numerous negative effects on the lives of family members, the fundamental unit of society. Overall, the results demonstrate that the pandemic made existing economic, social, and psychosocial vulnerabilities more visible, strengthened the factors determining intra-family tension and distress levels, and played a decisive role in shaping family functioning.

title: Impacto de la COVID-19 en los servicios y las políticas de salud de América Latina
abstract: Objetivo: analizar el impacto de la COVID-19 en los servicios de salud pública de América Latina y las políticas adoptadas. Método: revisión sistemática con síntesis narrativa en PubMed y SciELO (2012-2025); se incluyeron 15 estudios. Resultados: la pandemia interrumpió los servicios esenciales de rutina, incluidas la atención materna y odontológica, y amplió vulnerabilidades previas de sistemas fragmentados y desiguales. Las respuestas incluyeron la reorganización de servicios, la telesalud, la protección de las cadenas de suministro, medidas no farmacológicas y planes de vacunación con prioridades distintas. La recuperación fue parcial. Conclusión: la pandemia evidenció la fragilidad de los sistemas de salud latinoamericanos y la necesidad de políticas que garanticen la continuidad de la atención esencial.

title: Exploring deepened anxiety during the COVID-19 transition to online teaching and learning: Coping strategies within and beyond communities of practice in rural universities of South Africa and Uganda
abstract: The rapid increase in anxiety among teaching professionals before and after the COVID-19 pandemic has given university lecturers and students around the globe the motivation to explore ways to deal with anxiety as a key mental health issue, which has caused increased psychological and affective discomfort among both categories of population. In this study, the researchers explored how lecturers and students responded to the increased anxiety caused by a sudden, unexpected transition from traditional teaching and learning strategies to online delivery modes. Seventy participants, drawn from one Ugandan and one South African rural university, were purposively selected, and data were collected through in-depth interviews and focus group discussions. Thematic analysis of data, together with verbatim narratives, was used. The findings of this study reveal that communities of practice were the most widely adopted strategy to reduce and subsequently alleviate anxiety, in addition to physical activities, seeking mental health services, strengthening relationships among faculty, support staff and students, and training in online pedagogies. The recommendations highlight the need to frequently train students and lecturers on Learning Management Systems. This study highlights how community of practice (COP) systems and emerging support mechanisms can ease anxiety during online learning in rural universities, offering insights to guide policy and improve lecturer and student well-being and success in South Africa, Uganda, and similar contexts.
journal: Journal of Education and Learning Technology

title: Exploring the Challenge of Emotional Labor for Women Higher Education Leaders During the COVID-19 Pandemic
abstract: Abstract The COVID-19 pandemic significantly intensified the emotional labor experienced by women in higher education leadership. This chapter explores the unique burdens these leaders faced during the pandemic, including managing institutional responses, supporting community well-being, and maintaining their own emotional stability. Drawing from qualitative insights, it examines the impact of the pandemic on leadership practices and underscores the urgent need for systemic support structures that recognize and respond to the emotional demands placed on women in academic leadership.

title: Estrés, ansiedad y depresión asociados a la conducta alimentaria en estudiantes universitarios durante la pandemia de la COVID-19
abstract: La pandemia de la COVID-19 afectó significativamente la salud mental y nutricional de los estudiantes universitarios. Objetivo: Analizar cómo el estrés, la ansiedad y la depresión se asocian a la conducta alimentaria en estudiantes universitarios durante la pandemia de la COVID-19. Métodos: Se realizó un estudio transversal analítico. La muestra se obtuvo mediante muestreo aleatorio simple. Los datos se recolectaron con un cuestionario en línea. Se evaluaron estrés, ansiedad y depresión, con la escala DASS-21, y la conducta alimentaria con el Índice de Alimentación Saludable (Healthy Eating Index, HEI). Para el análisis se aplicaron pruebas bivariadas y modelos de regresión lineal multivariada ajustados por posibles factores de confusión y se consideró una significancia de p < 0,05. Resultados: Se incluyeron 366 estudiantes (mediana de edad: 20 años), con predominio femenino (72,1%). La prevalencia de estrés, ansiedad y depresión fue 53,8%, 74,5% y 62,3%, respectivamente, y más del 99% presentó hábitos alimentarios no saludables o que requerían cambios. El estrés se asoció con mayor frecuencia de conductas alimentarias no saludables y con menores puntajes del Índice de Alimentación Saludable (HEI; p < 0,001); la ansiedad y la depresión también mostraron asociaciones negativas. Se observaron correlaciones inversas entre el HEI y estrés (r = −0,18), ansiedad (r = −0,14) y depresión (r = −0,16). En modelos ajustados, las tres condiciones se asociaron independientemente con reducciones del HEI. Conclusiones: El estrés, la ansiedad y la depresión se asociaron significativamente con la conducta alimentaria en estudiantes universitarios durante la pandemia de la COVID-19.

title: Analysis of Covid 19 Pandemic on the Travel Behavior of Commuters in Igboora
abstract: The study viewed at global Coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic as is taking an excessive sway on all areas of the normal life of individuals worldwide as well as their travel behavior. Nations have been effected various methods that focus on checking social contacts and reducing in this way the spread of the virus and its swift blowout transversely throughout the world necessitated the introduction of travel restriction policies by the federal and state governments of Nigeria. It was done to abridge the stretch out of the noxious diseases.This paper sought to examine the travel behaviour of scorning travellers in Igboora,oyo state Nigeria amidst the travel restriction policy during the lock down. About 400 questionnaires were administered to commuters travelling within the 440 square kilometers of igboora in Oyo State. The study was Analysed using descriptive statistics and chisquare test for independence between the categorical data made available for this study. The findings of the study displayed that there was significant variation in travel behavior of commuters in Igboora, Oyo State at 0.05% level of significance using contingency tables. Also, there was statistically significant level of depence of commuters’ socio-demographic characteristics on modal split and trip destination.
journal: INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF SOCIAL SCIENCES AND MANAGEMENT RESEARCH

title: Mental well-being during the COVID-19 pandemic and its antecedents of crafting, work and home demands and resources: longitudinal profile analyses in Germany, Switzerland and Austria
abstract: The uncertainty of the COVID-19 pandemic and limited resources to manage blurred work-life boundaries during remote work, have impacted many employees’ mental well-being to varying degrees. In this study, we used latent profile analysis to identify the number and type of subgroups of the longitudinal patterns of mental well-being over the course of two and a half years, among 585 employees in Germany, Switzerland and Austria. We also examined whether demands, resources, and crafting strategies across work and non-work domains, increased the likelihood of belonging to a subgroup with different levels of mental well-being. Our findings revealed three subgroups (high, medium, low well-being) of relatively stable mental well-being over time, with the majority in the medium profile (N = 232, 39.66%). During the pandemic compared to the pre-pandemic period, employees with higher home developmental possibilities, mental home demands and home social support were more likely to belong to higher mental well-being subgroups. During the pandemic, off-job crafting only predicted differences between high versus medium mental well-being, whereas pre-pandemic, it predicted belonging to higher than lower well-being across all subgroups. Meanwhile, colleagues’ support no longer predicted belonging to specific subgroups during the pandemic as it did pre-pandemic. In sum, our results highlight the importance of both work, and especially the non-work domain, for preserving mental well-being during the pandemic and beyond. Organizations are encouraged to support work-life balance and boundary management through family support and flexible policies, as these may employees’ mental well-being during and beyond the crisis.

title: El aprendizaje que dejó la pandemia COVID-19: técnicas innovadoras en la docencia en Enfermería en El Salvador.
abstract: Introducción: Al inicio, durante y post pandemia Covid-19, los sistemas educativos enfrentaron desafíos que estremecieron los procesos de enseñanza a nivel internacional y nacional, las consecuencias alcanzaron todos los niveles educativos y principalmente la docencia en enfermería. Objetivo: Analizar el aprendizaje que dejó la pandemia Covid-19 en la docencia en Enfermería en El Salvador. Participantes y métodos: Se trató de un estudio cuantitativo, transversal, no experimental, descriptivo, realizado en una muestra de 34 docentes de enfermería que laboran en instituciones de Educación Superior. Se utilizó un cuestionario estructurado, centrado en dimensiones sociodemográficas, educativas y técnicas de enseñanza, con 24 ítems tipo Likert, 4 opciones de respuesta 1 = De acuerdo, hasta 4 = muy de acuerdo, y preguntas dicotómicas SI o No, ad hoc, validado por expertos, el análisis estadístico de validación alfa de Cronbach de 0.9. Los datos fueron analizados a través del programa SPSS. Resultados: Se observó el 79,4% (27) de los docentes de instituciones educativas no estaban preparados para enfrentar desafíos de la pandemia COVID, el 17,6% (6) de docentes no se capacitó durante la pandemia, sin embargo, existió la necesidad de innovar procesos educativos en las plataformas online, actualmente vigentes. Conclusión: La formación de enfermería durante la pandemia evidenció desafío para los docentes en garantizar el aprendizaje en el uso de técnicas de enseñanza en la modalidad virtual que superó la brecha de décadas pasadas. La resiliencia de los docentes en adaptarse a los cambios fue un reto en las instituciones de Educación Superior.
journal: Revista Científica de la Escuela Universitaria de las Ciencias de la Salud

title: CSR as a Systemic Buffer Against External Disruption: Panel Evidence on COVID-19 Resilience and Firm Performance in Korean-Listed Firms
abstract: Background: Whether corporate social responsibility (CSR) helps firms withstand external disruption, and how any advantage evolves as a shock unfolds, remains unresolved. Drawing on stakeholder theory, conservation of resources theory, and a systems-resilience perspective, we set out two competing predictions for the acute phase of COVID-19: an insurance-based loss-mitigation view and a resource-premium view. Methods: We use a balanced panel of 100 KOSPI-listed non-financial firms observed annually from 2016 to 2024 (900 firm-year observations) and estimate two-way fixed-effects difference-in-differences and event-study models, classifying firms by pre-crisis (2016–2019) CSR and clustering standard errors by firm. Results: Firms with higher pre-crisis CSR show a positive return-on-assets differential that appears in 2020, is statistically clear from 2021, and persists through 2024 without attenuating, although the recovery-phase differential is not statistically larger than the acute-phase differential. Each ESG sub-dimension is associated with the post-COVID-19 differential when examined separately, but only governance remains so when all three are included jointly. Conclusions: The estimates describe differential performance trajectories associated with pre-crisis CSR status rather than causal effects, and the design cannot identify the mechanism. The persistence pattern is somewhat more consistent with a resource-premium than a loss-mitigation view.

title: Antecipação da vacinação contra a COVID-19 no Brasil e suas regiões: análise por modelagem SIRV
abstract: Introdução: A oportunidade do início da vacinação constitui fator relevante no controle de epidemias. Objetivo: Estimar o impacto de uma antecipação hipotética de 15, 30, 45 e 60 dias da vacinação contra a COVID-19 nos casos e óbitos no Brasil e em suas cinco regiões. Metodologia: Estudo de modelagem epidemiológica com dados secundários do Ministério da Saúde e utilização de modelo compartimental SIRV, com proteção parcial por vacinação e infecção prévia. As projeções foram comparadas com séries de referência nacionais e regionais. Resultados: No Brasil, a antecipação de 15 dias resultou em redução projetada de 8.513.037 casos e 121.836 óbitos. A antecipação de 60 dias correspondeu a 20.865.096 casos e 330.157 óbitos a menos. No cenário de 60 dias, a redução regional de casos foi estimada em 3.647.495 no Nordeste, 1.289.197 no Norte, 2.140.585 no Centro-Oeste, 8.865.353 no Sudeste e 4.334.953 no Sul. Conclusão: Nos cenários simulados, maior antecipação vacinal foi acompanhada por maior redução estimada de casos e óbitos. Os resultados dependem das premissas da modelagem e não constituem estimativas causais observacionais.
authors: Ricardo de Sá Alencar e Moraes
journal: Brazilian Journal of Implantology and Health Sciences

Metodologia: Estudo de modelagem epidemiológica com dados secundários do Ministério da Saúde e utilização de modelo compartimental SIRV, com proteção parcial por vacinação e infecção prévia. As projeções foram comparadas com séries de referência nacionais e regionais. Resultados: No Brasil, a antecipação de 15 dias resultou em redução projetada de 8.513.037 casos e 121.836 óbitos. A antecipação de 60 dias correspondeu a 20.865.096 casos e 330.157 óbitos a menos. No cenário de 60 dias, a redução regional de casos foi estimada em 3.647.495 no Nordeste, 1.289.197 no Norte, 2.140.585 no Centro-Oeste, 8.865.353 no Sudeste e 4.334.953 no Sul. Conclusão: Nos cenários simulados, maior antecipação vacinal foi acompanhada por maior redução estimada de casos e óbitos. Os resultados dependem das premissas da modelagem e não constituem estimativas causais observacionais.

title: The Influence of Governance Conditions and Extreme Events on Salaries in Argentina: Establishing Subsidies by Decree‐Laws, Currency Devaluations, and Covid‐19
abstract: We study how salary variation coefficient growth rates are affected by two governance conditions (a decree law and a currency devaluation) and an extreme event (Covid‐19) in Argentina, using an event study approach. We find statistically significant novel evidence that, depending on the chosen model, (1) the Covid‐19 pandemic originated a negative daily average growth rate of the salary variation coefficient of approximately the same quantity as the positive effect of decree number 332/2022 in absolute value, when the salary variation coefficient was declared to be used to establish energy subsidies for clients with low and medium income; (2) we find that although a 50% currency devaluation has repercussions that increase nominal‐salary growth rates, decree number 332/2022 already accounts for at least half of the same dangerous effect—as if a 25% currency devaluation was applied—, or the same as a 50% currency devaluation, depending on the employed model. Our findings have relevant policy implications for regulators since they should know the consequences of changing governance conditions and extreme events.

title: Classifying and Differentiating Clinical Coding of Respiratory Syncytial Virus, Influenza, and COVID-19 in OpenSAFELY Between 2016 and 2024
abstract: Electronic health records (EHRs) are a rich source of data which can be used to analyse health outcomes using computable phenotypes. With the approval of NHS England we used the OpenSAFELY secure analytics platform to design and assess phenotypes to classify three key respiratory viruses - respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), influenza, and COVID-19 - in English coded health data between September 2016 and August 2024. We compared narrow and broad phenotypes to one another and to publicly available surveillance data. Cases from both phenotypes showed similar seasonal patterns to surveillance data. Broad phenotypes led to increased risk of misclassification than narrow phenotypes for mild cases. For severe cases the risk of misclassification was higher in infants than for older adults, irrespective of the phenotype used. The phenotypes presented here offer a solution to classifying respiratory viruses from coded health records in the absence of testing information.

title: Narrative Numbing and the Politics of Public Health Emergencies.
abstract: We examine how political polarization and prolonged crisis governance contribute to narrative numbing in public health emergencies and explore how these dynamics reshape executive emergency powers in the United States. Using Google Trends data, we assess changes in public attention to the opioid epidemic. We follow this with an explanatory case study of Pennsylvania's opioid state of emergency and a comparative review of national legislative reforms to state emergency powers. Prolonged emergency governance during COVID-19 coincided with narrative numbing, weakening the agenda-setting power of emergency declarations. In Pennsylvania, this shift was associated with legislative reforms that constrained executive authority with downstream effects on the opioid emergency. Nationally, state legislatures adopted time-limit, legislative termination, and scope constraints that reallocated authority from executives to legislatures. Narrative numbing is reflected in legislative reforms and has reshaped public health governance by limiting states' capacity to sustain emergency responses to prolonged or recurring public health crises. These changes carry implications for regional health equity and population health outcomes, demonstrating the need to maintain political legitimacy for sustained public health action. ( Am J Public Health . 2026;116(11):1719-1726. https://doi.org/10.2105/AJPH.2026.308730).

title: Bioinformatics-driven genomic surveillance and evolutionary tracking of emerging viral pathogens
abstract: Emerging viral pathogens pose a persistent threat to global health, making genomic surveillance and evolutionary tracking essential public health tools. This review evaluates bioinformatics tools, pipelines, and analytical approaches for genomic surveillance, pathogen tracking, and real-time evolutionary biology, assessing the strengths, limitations, and pathogen-specific applicability of each. Using a cross-pathogen, comparative framework, we examine five case studies: SARS-CoV-2, Ebola virus, monkeypox virus (MPXV), avian influenza virus, and honeybee viruses, each requiring a tailored combination of whole-genome sequencing, multiple-sequence alignment, phylogenetic tree building, and molecular clock reconstruction to reconstruct transmission chains and evolutionary dynamics. Key tools discussed include Nextstrain, GISAID, BEAST, IQ-TREE, MEGA, and Pangolin. These approaches have driven tangible public health outcomes, from mRNA vaccine development for SARS-CoV-2 to universal vaccine design efforts for avian influenza, but their impact remains constrained by uneven access to sequencing infrastructure, expertise, and computational resources. Across all five case studies, no single pipeline performs best universally: tool and platform choice must instead be matched to each pathogen’s biology and the surveillance infrastructure available in a given setting. Strengthening this capacity globally, particularly in under-resourced regions, is critical to ensuring emerging pathogens are detected and characterized in time for an effective public health response.

title: KmerSignificance score: A discriminative and biologically informed framework for viral k-mer prioritization.
abstract: Distinguishing closely related viral strains requires identifying genomic regions where subtle sequence differences carry biological significance. While k-mer-based approaches offer computational efficiency for genome analysis, existing methods lack standardized frameworks for evaluating which k-mers are most informative. Current selection strategies focus primarily on statistical discriminative power without integrating biological context. We introduce KmerSignificance Score (KSS), a k-mer prioritization framework combining three components: an information-theoretic method measuring strain-distinguishing capacity, an optimized amino acid substitution matrix (MIYATA_EVO) for mutation impact assessment, and a protein characterization score derived from annotations and database cross-references retrieved through UniProt. All three component scores and the integrated KSS are bounded in [0,1] by construction, providing a common numerical scale for ranking positions within a dataset. The discriminative component achieved a mean F1 of 0.881, not significantly different from chi-squared (0.876), the strongest of eight baselines. Top-ranked selections from the discriminative component nonetheless differed from those produced by chi-squared, especially for SARS-CoV-2 and HIV-1. The MIYATA_EVO matrix, optimized using a genetic algorithm, increased the composite agreement score across eight amino acid characteristics by 28.4% over the original MIYATA matrix. Across 17,471 viral proteins, the protein characterization score tracked UniProt's five-level annotation score closely (Kendall's τ=0.775), as expected for measures drawing on overlapping annotation content. Within each level, the continuous score provided finer numerical resolution among proteins. Literature cross-referencing on SARS-CoV-2 (278,738 sequences, 19 Pango-derived lineage labels), HIV-1 (12,223 sequences, 15 subtype labels), and human cytomegalovirus (HCMV; 399-646 sequences, 4-8 locus-specific genotypes) found that the top-ranked k-mers reported here map to established variant-defining mutations, subtype-specific polymorphisms, and genotype markers. KSS provides a standardized framework for viral k-mer prioritization with potential applications in variant surveillance, molecular epidemiology, and functional annotation. The tool is available at https://github.com/bioinfoUQAM/KmerSignificanceScore.

title: [Gender and age characteristics of cases of disability during the pandemic of coronavirus infection in Moscow].
abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic has been a global stress factor for population health in most countries, including Russia. The high prevalence and economic burden of diseases make it important to study the regional characteristics of population morbidity among different population groups. The aim of this study was to identify the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on temporary disability cases among residents of Moscow by gender and age, based on data from a primary healthcare organization. The assessment was based on data from 2019 to 2024. The dynamics of the total number of disability cases from 2019 to 2024, as well as their distribution by gender and age categories, were analyzed. The «disability coefficient» was calculated for the entire attached population and for specific gender and age groups. The average duration of days of disability due to respiratory diseases during the study period was also evaluated. It can be stated that the female part of the working population was more likely to apply for disability leaves, and the 35-49 age group had the highest number of temporary disability cases. There were no significant differences in the duration of temporary disability cases between men and women.

source_records.title: [Gender and age characteristics of cases of disability during the pandemic of coronavirus infection in Moscow].
source_records.abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic has been a global stress factor for population health in most countries, including Russia. The high prevalence and economic burden of diseases make it important to study the regional characteristics of population morbidity among different population groups. The aim of this study was to identify the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on temporary disability cases among residents of Moscow by gender and age, based on data from a primary healthcare organization. The assessment was based on data from 2019 to 2024. The dynamics of the total number of disability cases from 2019 to 2024, as well as their distribution by gender and age categories, were analyzed. The «disability coefficient» was calculated for the entire attached population and for specific gender and age groups. The average duration of days of disability due to respiratory diseases during the study period was also evaluated. It can be stated that the female part of the working population was more likely to apply for disability leaves, and the 35-49 age group had the highest number of temporary disability cases. There were no significant differences in the duration of temporary disability cases between men and women.

title: Risk of Preterm Birth, Congenital Structural Anomalies and Severe Postpartum Hemorrhage After Receipt of NVX-CoV2373 Vaccine During Pregnancy.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Information on maternal and neonatal outcomes following NVX-CoV2373 coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) vaccination in pregnant women is limited. METHODS: This retrospective cohort study utilized National Health Insurance Service data, linking maternal and neonatal records with COVID-19 vaccination registries in South Korea. Eligible pregnancies included those with recorded births among 20-49-year-old women between February 1 and December 31, 2022, excluding pregnancies with first-trimester severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 infections. Pregnant women who received NVX-CoV2373 during pregnancy were matched, 1:4, with COVID-19-unvaccinated women using propensity score methods to account for demographic and clinical variables. Adjusted risk ratios (aRR) and 95% confidence intervals (95% CIs) for preterm birth (PTB), congenital structural anomalies (CSAs) and severe postpartum hemorrhage (sPPH) were estimated using log-binomial regression models. To further characterize NVX-CoV2373 safety, a separate analysis estimated aRRs and 95% CIs comparing women who exclusively received either NVX-CoV2373 or BNT162b2 during pregnancy. RESULTS: Among 484 NVX-CoV2373 recipients during pregnancy and their matched sample of 1930 COVID-19-unvaccinated women, there was no observed difference in risk of PTB (aRR = 0.95, 95% CI: 0.75-1.21), CSAs (aRR = 0.57, 0.30-1.09) or sPPH (aRR = 0.65, 0.15-2.90) between groups. Between 476 NVX-CoV2373 and their matched sample of 1497 BNT162b2 recipients during pregnancy, there were no significant differences in risk of PTB (aRR = 1.01, 0.75-1.34), CSAs (aRR = 0.74, 0.42-1.29) or sPPH (aRR = 0.45, 0.10-1.97). CONCLUSIONS: The risk of PTB, CSAs and sPPH was not statistically different between NVX-CoV2373 and BNT162b2 recipients during pregnancy and COVID-19-unvaccinated women, reinforcing the antepartum safety of NVX-CoV2373 and COVID-19 vaccines in general.

title: Efficacy and safety of sivelestat in sepsis-induced acute respiratory distress syndrome: an updated meta-analysis based on disease severity and treatment strategy subgroups
abstract: Objective Sivelestat sodium hydrate is a selective neutrophil elastase inhibitor that attenuates neutrophil-mediated alveolar–capillary injury and is used in some East Asian countries for acute lung injury/ARDS. We evaluated the efficacy and safety of sivelestat in sepsis-induced acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) and explored whether disease severity, baseline mortality risk, and treatment background modify the mortality effect. Methods We searched PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Cochrane CENTRAL, Web of Science, CNKI, Wanfang, and ClinicalTrials.gov from database inception to August 27, 2026. Eligible studies were adult studies of sepsis-induced ARDS comparing a sivelestat-containing regimen with an otherwise comparable regimen without sivelestat. COVID-19-only cohorts, non-septic ARDS, mixed-etiology studies without a separable sepsis subgroup, and comparisons in which both groups received sivelestat were excluded. The primary outcome was all-cause mortality; secondary outcomes included P/F ratio, duration of mechanical ventilation, ICU length of stay, organ-function scores, inflammatory markers, and adverse events. Mortality was pooled as odds ratios (ORs) using a random-effects model with restricted maximum likelihood; Hartung–Knapp intervals were used for the primary and study-design analyses. This review was prospectively registered in PROSPERO. Results Fourteen studies were eligible for qualitative synthesis, and 10 studies (943 patients) provided extractable 2 × 2 mortality data. Deaths occurred in 73/431 patients receiving sivelestat and 125/512 controls. Sivelestat was associated with lower mortality (OR=0.55, 95% CI 0.36–0.84; I 2 = 0%). The signal persisted in randomized trials (OR=0.37, 95% CI 0.16–0.86; I 2 = 0%). Study-level point estimates appeared more favorable in cohorts with baseline P/F 30%; however, interaction tests were not statistically significant and severity analyses were ecological. Leave-one-out analyses were stable. Egger testing did not detect significant small-study asymmetry ( P = 0.197), although power was limited. Baseline-stratified treatment effects by IL-6, PCT, CRP, or neutrophil elastase were unavailable for quantitative effect-modification analyses. Conclusions In an updated and etiologically strict evidence synthesis, sivelestat was associated with lower mortality in sepsis-induced ARDS, including in randomized trials. Severe hypoxemia and high baseline risk remain plausible enrichment factors, but current aggregate evidence is insufficient to support a validated phenotype-guided prescribing rule. Co-intervention reporting was sparse, and residual confounding by prone positioning, sedation, neuromuscular blockade, and steroid background cannot be excluded. Systematic Review Registration PROSPERO CRD420261541158.

title: Seasonal changes of respiratory infections in Northern Finland 2019-2024: evaluation of different diagnostic tests in rapidly changing epidemiological environment.
abstract: ABSTRACT In primary health care, respiratory tract infections (RTIs) are one of the major causes of seeking medical attention. Diagnostic RTI laboratory tests provide information for both treating an individual patient as well as more generally epidemiological disease distribution of a given infection. In the case of SARS-CoV-2 pandemic, a diagnostic qPCR assay was rapidly developed in 2020, and the virus-specific test was subsequently incorporated into multiplex PCR tests that also detect other common seasonally occurring viruses, including influenza A and B, and RS-virus. We provide here the data on epidemiological distribution of 23 microbes between 2019 and 2024 in Northern Finland. While coronavirus was the most prominent detected microbe, adenovirus, RS-virus, influenzas, Mycoplasma pneumoniae , Chlamydia pneumoniae , and Bordetella pertussis/parapertussis were also commonly detected microbes. The incorporation of multiplex PCR into diagnostics of RTI, particularly in primary health care, will provide more epidemiological data; however, the cost-effectiveness of laboratory tests compared with data availability remains to be clarified. IMPORTANCE Respiratory tract infections (RTIs) are one of the major causes of health care visits. The role of laboratory diagnostics is important, as RTIs have numerous etiological pathogens, and the clinical symptoms may be similar. The distinction between viral and bacterial infections is important to avoid unnecessary antibiotic treatments. The data from RTI testing provide a wide perspective on the epidemiological situation before, during, and after the COVID-19 pandemic and provides insights into the differences in detection rates between age groups.

title: Reclaiming the Host: Why p53/NRF2-Directed Therapies Should Enter the Global Antiviral Policy Agenda
abstract: Respiratory viruses continue to challenge global preparedness because antiviral strategies remain largely pathogen specific. RSV, SARS-CoV-2, influenza, and emerging zoonotic viruses differ genetically, yet increasing evidence suggests that they converge on a common host vulnerability: suppression of the cellular stress-response regulators p53 and NRF2. RSV promotes p53 degradation and NRF2 loss, while SARS-CoV-2 similarly impairs these pathways and amplifies inflammatory signalling. Restoration of p53 and NRF2 reactivates antiviral microRNAs, suppresses viral-entry and inflammatory pathways, restores antioxidant defences, and induces p62/SQSTM1, a broad-spectrum antiviral restriction factor. These observations suggest that host-directed therapies could complement vaccines and direct-acting antivirals by establishing a mutation-resistant layer of protection. We argue that global preparedness frameworks should formally evaluate host-directed antiviral strategies as a third pillar of pandemic readiness.

title: Development and optimization of self-collected, field-stable, saliva-based immunoassays for scalable epidemiological surveillance of pathogen-specific immunity.
abstract: ABSTRACT Serological surveillance is fundamental to infectious disease research and informed public-health decision-making. Immunoassays used in the study of pathogen-specific immunity have historically relied on the collection of venous blood. While critical for many public-health applications, this sample collection method is invasive and resource-intensive. The costs and logistical barriers associated with venous blood collection are exacerbated in resource-limited regions, and the shift to less invasive sampling methods would increase sample availability for pathogen surveillance and study of pathogen-specific immunity. To this end, we have developed and optimized a self-collected, saliva-based immunoassay capable of quantifying pathogen-specific antibody binding in saliva samples. Using samples collected from geographically and epidemiologically diverse regions of the world, we compared antigen-specific IgG levels in paired plasma and saliva samples. We observed that levels of IgG against multiple pathogens of public health concern—including SARS-CoV-2 and dengue virus—were highly correlated in plasma and swab-collected saliva. In addition, the decay of maternally derived antibodies in saliva samples collected from infants was readily observed using this immunoassay, demonstrating the assay’s sensitivity and potential for use in measuring antibody kinetics. We posit that this assay represents a climate-stable, non-invasive tool that can aid in the surveillance and study of pathogen-specific immunity across a broad range of public-health indications. IMPORTANCE Traditional serological surveillance relies on venous blood collection, which is invasive, resource-intensive, and particularly burdensome in low-resource settings. To address these limitations, our team has developed and validated a self-collected, saliva-based immunoassay for quantifying pathogen-specific antibody levels. Testing paired plasma and saliva samples from geographically diverse populations, the authors found that IgG levels against SARS-CoV-2 and dengue virus were highly correlated between the two sample types. The assay was sensitive enough to detect the decay of maternally derived antibodies in infant saliva, demonstrating its utility for tracking antibody kinetics over time. The authors conclude that this non-invasive, climate-stable platform offers a practical alternative for broad pathogen surveillance and immune monitoring across a variety of public health contexts.

title: The Rising Burden of Atrial Fibrillation and Respiratory Failure Mortality in the United States: A 25-Year Nationwide Retrospective Analysis of Death Certificate Data.
abstract: ABSTRACT Background Atrial fibrillation (AF) and respiratory failure (RF) frequently co‐occur in critically ill patients, but long‐term national trends in deaths recording both remain unknown. Methods CDC WONDER multiple‐cause‐of‐death data identified U.S. adults aged ≥ 55 years with both AF (including atrial flutter) and RF listed on death certificates from 1999 to 2024. Age‐adjusted mortality rates (AAMRs) and annual percent changes (APCs) were estimated using joinpoint regression. Sensitivity analyses included adults aged ≥ 25 years, exclusion of COVID‐19‐related deaths, and stratification by co‐listed heart failure (HF). Results A total of 462 284 deaths listed both AF and RF. The AAMR increased roughly five‐fold (7.84 to 41.76 per 100 000), rising steadily through 2018 (APC 7.81), accelerating through 2021 (APC 18.78), and declining thereafter (APC −5.90). Excluding deaths listing COVID‐19, the 2018–2021 acceleration was not detected, and AAMRs rose through 2024 (2017–2024 APC 5.25). AAMRs for deaths without HF recorded rose over fourfold. Mean AAMRs were higher in males (26.19) than in females (19.04) and in non‐Hispanic (NH) White adults (24.06) than in other groups. The West and nonmetropolitan areas had the highest rates. The 2018–2021 surge was steepest among Hispanic (APC 25.62) and NH Black adults (APC 24.06). Conclusions Population mortality rates for deaths recording both AF and RF increased substantially over 25 years, beginning before the COVID‐19 pandemic, persisting after excluding deaths listing COVID‐19, and occurring with and without HF recorded. These data cannot separate changes in disease occurrence from changes in diagnosis or coding.

title: Maternal mRNA Vaccination: Immunological Principles and Evidence Gaps in Infant Protection
abstract: Maternal messenger RNA (mRNA) vaccination can generate maternal immunity and antibodies for passive infant protection. However, clinical evidence derives predominantly from the SARS-CoV-2 vaccines BNT162b2 and mRNA-1273, limiting generalization across the platform. This narrative review examines three questions: what determines maternal immune responses, what governs placental antibody transfer, and how immunological findings relate to infant clinical protection. Studies generally support preserved immune responsiveness during pregnancy, but associations with gestational timing are difficult to separate from dose number, previous infection, and time since antigen exposure. Transfer requires interpretation of maternal and cord-blood concentrations, because high transfer ratios do not necessarily indicate high infant antibody levels. Postnatal antibody decline and variant-dependent neutralization further limit inference from measurements at delivery. Observational studies associate maternal vaccination with reduced COVID-19-associated infant hospitalization, although residual confounding and heterogeneous exposure histories complicate comparisons between schedules. No validated infant antibody threshold predicts protection against SARS-CoV-2 infection or hospitalization. Evidence for other pathogens and self-amplifying RNA remains predominantly preclinical. Maternal immunogenicity, placental transfer, and antibody persistence therefore provide complementary evidence but cannot substitute for clinical outcomes. Future products require pregnancy-specific safety assessment and prospective studies linking maternal responses, functional antibody transfer, and postnatal persistence to clinically meaningful protection throughout infancy.

title: Air sampling for facility-based respiratory pathogen surveillance in rural Zambia: a prospective comparison with human surveillance
abstract: Respiratory infections are the leading cause of acute disease incidence globally and disproportionately burden low- and middle-income countries where surveillance capacity is limited. While facility-based surveillance remains the standard for respiratory pathogen monitoring in human populations, environmental air sampling offers potential advantages as a non-invasive supplementary method. We conducted a prospective environmental air sampling study nested within ongoing respiratory disease surveillance at Macha Hospital in Southern Province, Zambia, from July 2025 to June 2026. Air samplers were deployed continuously in the outpatient department and three inpatient wards, with filters collected and tested three times weekly. Surveillance in the patient population was conducted year-round with nasopharyngeal samples collected from patients with influenza-like illness. All samples were tested for influenza A/B virus, respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), and SARS-CoV-2 using the Cepheid GeneXpert platform. We analyzed concordance between air and nasopharyngeal samples using percent agreement, Cohen's Kappa, Spearman correlations, and logistic regression with generalized estimating equations. Over 12 months, 596 air samples and 701 human samples were analyzed. Influenza A virus was the most common pathogen, detected in 38 air samples and 87 nasopharyngeal samples, with most cases detected from July to September 2025. For Influenza A, there was strong same-week concordance between air and nasopharyngeal samples (80.4% overall agreement; 44.4% positive agreement; Cohen's Kappa = 0.5; Spearman's rho = 0.57). SARS-CoV-2 was also common, detected in 18 air samples and 16 nasopharyngeal samples, with cases detected sporadically throughout the year. For SARS-CoV-2, there was limited concordance between air and nasopharyngeal samples (68.6% agreement; 23.8% positive agreement; Cohen's Kappa = 0.2; Spearman's rho = 0.2). Influenza B virus (1 air and 13 nasopharyngeal samples positive) and RSV (0 air and 4 nasopharyngeal samples positive) circulated sporadically, and unsurprisingly, gave limited concordance between samples. Cycle threshold values for influenza A virus (median for target 1: 36.7 vs. 25.1; p<0.001; median for target 2: 39.5 vs. 28.6; p<0.001) and SARS-CoV-2 (median: 41.3 vs. 27.5; p<0.001) were significantly higher for positive air samples than for nasopharyngeal samples. Implementation challenges were documented, including intermittent power outages and compromised electrical outlets causing sampler shutdowns, as well as study awareness issues that required sensitization activities for both facility staff and patients. Air sampling was feasible and demonstrated promise as a supplementary method for facility-based respiratory pathogen surveillance in rural resource-limited settings. These findings support integrating environmental air sampling alongside surveillance in patient populations as part of a multimodal approach to respiratory pathogen monitoring.

title: Multi-Virus Surveillance Across Diverse Freshwater Systems in Tehran, Iran.
abstract: Environmental surveillance of viral contaminants in water systems is an essential tool for assessing exposure risk and supporting early-warning frameworks for emerging infectious diseases. In this study, a comprehensive one-year surveillance of SARS-CoV-2 and six enteric viruses was conducted across diverse freshwater systems in Tehran, Iran - including rivers, wells, and traditional qanat (underground aqueduct) infrastructures. Water quality parameters (turbidity, pH, Total Dissolved Solids, nitrate) and fecal bacterial indicators (total coliforms, fecal coliforms, and E. coli) were also measured to contextualize viral contamination within a broader environmental risk framework. Between September 2020 and August 2021, a total of 118 water samples were collected and analyzed using quantitative molecular detection methods. Overall, 61 of 118 samples (51.7%) tested positive for at least one virus. Surface water (rivers) showed substantially higher contamination rates (80.3%; 53/66 samples) compared to groundwater (15.4%; 8/52 samples). Among groundwater sources, qanat systems were markedly more vulnerable than conventional wells, with 25.0% (6/24) of qanat samples testing positive versus only 7.1% (2/28) of well samples. This elevated contamination in qanats was dominated by rotavirus (5/6 positive qanat samples, detection rate 20.8%) and was associated with higher fecal bacterial loads (total coliform geometric mean: 245 MPN/100 mL in qanats vs. 28 MPN/100 mL in wells), consistent with the susceptibility of shallow horizontal collection channels to fecal infiltration. SARS-CoV-2 RNA was detected in 34.8% of river samples and 3.9% of groundwater samples, with concentrations reaching 1.28 × 104 genome copies per liter (GC/L) in surface waters, demonstrating sustained fecal contamination across all seasons. The most prevalent viruses in river water were norovirus GII (45.5%), adenovirus (43.9%), rotavirus (42.4%), and norovirus GI (40.9%), with mean concentrations ranging from 1.26 × 102 to 3.76 × 103 GC/L. Hepatitis A and E viruses were not detected in any sample. Seasonal variation in viral detection was observed for enteric viruses, while SARS-CoV-2 and adenovirus showed year-round persistence. Strong correlations between fecal indicators and viral contamination (Spearman r = 0.61-0.63) support the use of bacterial monitoring as a cost-effective screening proxy. The results highlight the particular vulnerability of qanat systems and underscore the value of integrated environmental surveillance for water safety management in arid, water-stressed urban environments.

source_records.abstract: Environmental surveillance of viral contaminants in water systems is an essential tool for assessing exposure risk and supporting early-warning frameworks for emerging infectious diseases. In this study, a comprehensive one-year surveillance of SARS-CoV-2 and six enteric viruses was conducted across diverse freshwater systems in Tehran, Iran - including rivers, wells, and traditional qanat (underground aqueduct) infrastructures. title: Trends of delayed healthcare access in ocular injuries: a multicenter study in community hospitals, Central Thailand.
abstract: Aim To determine the annual trends and risk factors for delayed access to care in community hospitals across Central Thailand-an area with high occupational injury risk. Methods This retrospective cross-sectional study analyzed data from four community hospitals in Central Thailand over six years (October 1, 2018-September 17, 2024). Patients aged ≥20y with ocular injuries, identified via International Classification of Diseases-10 (ICD-10) codes, were included. Demographics, injury characteristics, and care-seeking behaviors were recorded. Delayed access was defined as presentation >24h post-injury. Linear and logistic regression models were used to identify associated risk factors. Annual fiscal trends were analyzed to assess year-to-year patterns in delayed healthcare access. Results Among 6571 ocular injury cases, 4034 (61.4%) were male, with median age 43y [interquartile range (IQR) 31-57y], and 3983 (79.3%) were manual laborers. Delayed healthcare access was observed in 2426 cases (36.9%). Significant risk factors included age ≥60y [aOR: 1.55; 95% confidence interval (CI): 1.32-1.82], visits to F2-level hospitals [adjusted odds ratio (aOR): 2.03; 95%CI: 1.73-2.38], and outpatient visits (aOR: 14.01; 95%CI: 12.18-16.12). In F2 hospitals, subgroup analysis revealed a U-shaped reduction in delayed healthcare access for ocular injuries during the COVID-19 pandemic (2019-2021), adjusted for age and gender. Conclusion This first in-depth study of ocular injuries in Central Thailand's community hospitals found persistently high delayed presentations, with older age, F2 hospital visits, and outpatient department (OPD) attendance as key contributing factors. The trend during the COVID-19 pandemic highlights the important role of lower-tier community hospitals in providing prompt and accessible care for patients. Strengthening healthcare infrastructure and public awareness is essential to ensure timely care and reduce preventable vision-related complications.

title: The north-south divide in English mortality, 1981-2024: a longitudinal population study.
abstract: Background The north-south mortality divide in England, UK, has persisted for several decades. Previous longitudinal analyses up to 2016 have highlighted a widening mortality gap among those aged 25-44 years since the mid-1990s. We aimed to update mortality trends in England and evaluate how trends differed by age and sex up to 2024. Methods We did a segmented longitudinal population study of the north-south mortality divide in England (1981-2024). Using registered deaths and mid-year population estimates by 5-year age group and sex, we calculated standardised mortality rates and estimated adjusted north-south rate ratios using within-year Poisson models. We used segmented Poisson regression to compare mortality trends between 2010-19 and 2020-24. Findings Despite overall declines in mortality, interrupted by the COVID-19 pandemic, the north-south mortality divide persisted during 1981-2024, widening among both female and male individuals aged 25-49 years. During 2010-19, northern excess mortality among those aged 25-49 years increased per year for female individuals (incidence rate ratio 1·018 [95% CI 1·013-1·022]) and male individuals (1·012 [1·009-1·016]). During 2020-24, these trends continued: Poisson models suggested a slowing among female individuals aged 25-49 years (0·987 [0·975-0·999]) and further widening among male individuals younger than 75 years (1·004 [1·000-1·007]), but neither change was robust to allowance for overdispersion, and the gap did not narrow in any age or sex group. By 2024, northern excess mortality reached 25·9% (95% CI 24·7-27·1) for those younger than 75 years, and 42·4% (38·5-46·3) for those aged 25-49 years. Interpretation Over the past four decades, England's regional mortality inequalities have widened among working‐age adults, with more rapid increases among female individuals than male individuals up to 2020 (before the COVID-19 pandemic). Pre-pandemic trends continued through 2020-24, with no narrowing of the north-south gap in any age or sex group by 2024. Reducing the north-south health divide will require sustained large-scale action across central government and regional authorities. Funding National Institute for Health and Care Research, British Heart Foundation, and The Pandemic Institute.

title: Clinical and laboratory features associated with dengue in central Taiwan during the 2023 outbreak.
abstract: Purpose: Dengue outbreaks in previously unaffected areas expose immunologically naive aging populations. Distinguishing dengue from influenza and COVID-19 in the emergency department (ED) is challenging. We identified factors associated with dengue in the 2023 outbreak in central Taiwan. This retrospective cohort study included adults with acute illness and suspected infection who underwent dengue testing at the ED of National Taiwan University Hospital Yunlin Branch from January 1 to December 31, 2023. Patients with confirmed dengue (positive NS1 antigen test) were compared with non-dengue patients. Variables with p < 0.01 in univariate analysis were selected for a multivariable logistic regression model after multiple imputation (m = 20). Subgroup models compared dengue with laboratory-confirmed influenza and COVID-19. Serial hemograms were summarized descriptively. Of 872 adults, 154 had confirmed dengue. Epidemic link (adjusted odds ratio [aOR], 9.59), age (aOR, 1.03 per year), myalgia or bone pain (aOR, 2.51), and hemoglobin (aOR, 1.35 per g/dL) were positively associated with dengue. Malignancy (aOR, 0.20), URI symptoms (aOR, 0.47), WBC count (aOR, 0.79 per 1 × 103/μL), and platelet count (aOR, 0.99 per 1 × 103/μL) were inversely associated. Epidemic link, the absence of URI symptoms, and lower platelet count remained associated with dengue in comparisons with influenza and COVID-19. WBC and platelet counts were lowest around Days 4-7. Among adults tested for dengue during an outbreak, epidemic link, the absence of URI symptoms, and lower platelet count were most consistently associated with dengue, including in comparisons with influenza and COVID-19. External validation is required before clinical application.

title: Advances and Translational Challenges in mRNA–Lipid Nanoparticle Vaccines Against Helicobacter pylori : From Rational Antigen Design to Mucosal Immunity
abstract: Helicobacter pylori chronically infects more than half of the global population and is the sole bacterium classified as a Group 1 carcinogen by the International Agency for Research on Cancer. Despite decades of effort, no prophylactic H. pylori vaccine has reached the market, largely because conventional subunit and whole-cell candidates failed to induce durable, mucosa-protective T-helper 1 (Th1)/Th17 immunity in humans. The clinical success of severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) mRNA–lipid nanoparticle (mRNA-LNP) vaccines has re-energized nucleic-acid vaccine research and provided a validated, scalable delivery platform. This review synthesizes the emerging mechanistic rationale and early preclinical evidence evaluating whether mRNA-LNP technology can address key bottlenecks in H. pylori vaccine development: cytoplasmic antigen expression naturally favors major histocompatibility complex (MHC) class I/II presentation and CD8+/Th1 responses (notably, recent human and murine evidence demonstrates that cytotoxin-associated gene A [CagA]-specific gastric CD8+ tissue-resident memory T [TRM] cells control early H. pylori infection), multi-antigen and conserved-epitope designs can be generated rapidly by reverse vaccinology, and the LNP carrier itself acts as an intrinsic innate immune adjuvant. We summarize the principal candidate antigens (urease subunit B [UreB], CagA, vacuolating cytotoxin A [VacA], neutrophil-activating protein [NAP], H. pylori adhesin A [HpaA], and γ-glutamyl transpeptidase [GGT]), dissect LNP composition and intracellular trafficking, and critically appraise the nascent body of preclinical H. pylori mRNA and nanocarrier studies published between 2021 and 2026—specifically distinguishing two recent in vivo mRNA-LNP preprints (encoding full-length UreB or UreB199–338 cytokine/immunoglobulin Z [IgZ] fusions) from peer-reviewed in silico multi-epitope mRNA and self-amplifying RNA (saRNA) designs, LNP-adjuvanted recombinant UreB/NapA protein vaccines, all-trans retinoic acid-loaded gut-tropic nanovaccines, and oral/lipid DNA vaccine benchmarks. We also reconcile classic evidence that bacterial clearance can proceed in B-cell-deficient mice via MHC class II-restricted CD4+ T cells with the ancillary role of functional adhesion- and urease-blocking antibodies, and we examine critical safety and immunopathological constraints—including post-immunization gastritis, oncogenic CagA EPIYA motif detoxification, and target-population stratification (uninfected children versus infected adults). We conclude that while mRNA-LNP represents a promising exploratory modality for an H. pylori vaccine, the current experimental evidence base remains narrow and preliminary; peer-reviewed validation of in vivo Th17 induction, antigen breadth, mucosal delivery route, and long-term durability in non-human primate and human challenge models will be required to establish clinical feasibility.

source_records.abstract: Helicobacter pylori chronically infects more than half of the global population and is the sole bacterium classified as a Group 1 carcinogen by the International Agency for Research on Cancer. The clinical success of severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) mRNA–lipid nanoparticle (mRNA-LNP) vaccines has re-energized nucleic-acid vaccine research and provided a validated, scalable delivery platform. title: Impact of Herb-Herb Interaction on Safety of Combinations of Botanical Hybrid Products Including Herba Andrographidis
abstract: Background: /Objectives: The same medicinal plant can interact differently with other plants in their combinations, with expectations of higher efficacy and improved safety. Kan Jang® is a fixed combination of standardized extracts of Herba Andrographidis and Radix Eleutherococci used to treat upper respiratory tract infections (URTIs), influenza, sinusitis, pharyngotonsillitis, and, more recently, mild COVID-19. However, recent pharmacovigilance signals indicate that Andrographis paniculata leaf extracts in combination with Radix Echinacea-containing preparations can unexpectedly cause serious allergic reactions, including anaphylaxis. The Australian Therapeutic Goods Administration (TGA) warning to exclude Andrographis from the list of low-risk products assumes its product-specific pharmacological profile remains the same when combined with other plant extracts. However, 9 clinical trials of Kang Jang involving 1544 patients with URTIs, along with post-marketing reports from 1989 to the present, show it to be harmless despite containing Andrographis. This review aims to explain why Kang Jang may be less harmful than other Andrographis-containing products. Methods: We conducted a mixed-methods narrative review using evidence from clinical trials, systematic reviews, transcriptomic investigations, network-pharmacology analyses, mechanistic studies, toxicology reports, and pharmacovigilance assessments, retrieving literature published between 1980 and 2026 from major scientific databases and regulatory sources. Results: Several factors explain Kan Jang's superior safety compared with other Andrographis-containing preparations. Kan Jang fundamentally differs by: (i) its chemical composition (presence of Eleutherococcus extract and lack of possible impurities forming as a result of other extractive solvents), (ii) pharmaceutical characteristics (different raw materials - leaves vs. aerial parts; solvents - 70% vs. methanol and water), (iii) clinical and postmarketing safety, and (iv) synergistic and antagonistic interactions of components of Kan Jang (Andrographis and Eleuthero-coccus) in the cells of the human body. Transcriptomic studies demonstrated that the combination produces a distinct gene-expression profile characterized by both synergistic and antagonistic interactions, including regulation of genes not affected by either constituent alone. Mechanistic analyses identified effects on interferon signaling, immune regulation, inflammatory pathways, KEAP1–Nrf2-mediated oxidative stress responses, cytoprotective mechanisms, and host-defense networks. Across clinical studies and post-marketing surveillance, Kan Jang exhibited a favorable safety profile with predominantly mild adverse events and no validated pharmacovigilance signal for serious hypersensitivity reactions. Conclusions: Kan Jang has a favorable observed clinical and post-marketing safety profile, in contrast to a validated pharmacovigilance signal for anaphylaxis associated with some other polyherbal products, including Andrographis and Radix Echinacea extracts. Preclinical transcriptomic and mechanistic findings provide a plausible biological basis for differences between the Kan Jang combination and Andrographis monotherapy. Clinical studies indicate that Kan Jang improves symptoms and recovery in URTIs, influenza, and mild COVID-19, with reported benefits including accelerated symptom resolution and improved physical functioning.

title: Health-Care Burden of Acute Exacerbation of Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease in Hong Kong in the Post-COVID Pandemic Era-Impact of Phenotype and Exacerbation History.
abstract: ABSTRACT Rationale Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) is known to be associated with substantial health‐care utilization and economic costs. Since the COVID‐19 pandemic, the epidemiology of various diseases has undergone significant changes, it is important to evaluate the health‐care impact and economic burden of acute exacerbations of COPD (AECOPD) in the post‐pandemic period, along with factors influencing this burden, to inform effective management strategies and health‐care planning. Objectives To assess the health‐care and economic burden of severe AECOPD from 2022 to 2024, and to identify factors associated with direct health‐care costs. Methods A territory‐wide retrospective cohort study was conducted. Adult patients with AECOPD admitted to acute public hospitals in Hong Kong were included. The primary outcomes were the total number of AECOPD admissions and the associated direct health‐care costs. Measurements and Main Results From 2022 to 2024, a total of 11,465 patients were admitted to acute public hospitals for severe AECOPD, resulting in 25,053 hospitalization episodes and 150,717 bed days. The estimated direct health‐care costs totaled 1.259 billion Hong Kong dollars (HKD). AECOPD admission numbers increased significantly over the 3 years. Patients with eosinophilic and non‐eosinophilic phenotypes had similar annual direct health‐care costs related to severe AECOPD. Patients with co‐existing bronchiectasis had a significantly higher annual number of severe AECOPD episodes and direct health‐care costs from severe AECOPD. Conclusions Severe AECOPD imposes a substantial burden on the health‐care system. The presence of bronchiectasis and a greater frequency of severe AECOPD episodes were identified as possible factors linked to increased direct health‐care costs.

title: Mechanistic insights into coronavirus inhibition by a distinct base-modified adenosine analog targeting the viral polymerase
abstract: Nucleoside analog (NA) inhibitors of viral polymerases are a chemically diverse and prominent class of antivirals, with most agents bearing sugar modifications to induce chain termination. Compounds with a modified base yet natural ribose are comparatively rare and typically incorporated to act as virus mutagens, raising significant safety concerns. How nucleobase modifications interfere with polymerization and the molecular basis of this effect remain poorly understood. We here define the mechanism of 6-ethyl-modified 7-deazaadenosine (EDA), a recently identified coronavirus (CoV) inhibitor that does not induce virus mutagenesis. Its strong activity spans across multiple CoVs and cell models and is dictated by the 6-ethyl substituent, with poor tolerance for smaller, larger or heteroatom-containing substituents. At the level of SARS-CoV-2 RNA-dependent RNA polymerase (RdRp), EDA-triphosphate incorporates as a mimic of ATP but not other NTPs, inducing immediate stalling but also excision by the viral 3′-to-5′ exonuclease. While EDA incorporation prevents extension with a second EDA residue, the stalling of natural NTP incorporation is transient and still allows the formation of longer products. A similar phenomenon is observed with template-embedded EDA. Cryo-EM analysis with SARS-CoV-2 RdRp revealed that 3′-terminal EDA is accommodated without distortion of the template:primer duplex, but its 6-ethyl group induces rearrangements in the NTP binding pocket that prevent stable binding of the incoming nucleotide. The mechanistic findings were validated through antiviral studies with SARS-CoV-2 mutants bearing core substitutions in the RdRp or exonuclease. Together, these findings position EDA as a mechanistically distinct base-modified NA prototype that has relevance beyond coronaviruses and underscores the ever-expanding versatility of NA-based polymerase inhibitors.

title: [THE STRUCTURAL AND DYNAMIC CHARACTERISTICS OF THE DISEASES OF BLOOD CIRCULATION ORGANS IN THE KYRGYZ REPUBLIC].
abstract: The diseases of circulatory system continue to occupy leading positions in structure of morbidity and mortality of population, remaining one of key public health problems. The purpose of the study is to investigate dynamics of primary morbidity and prevalence of diseases of circulatory system by main nosological forms among adult and adolescent population of the Kyrgyz Republic in 2018-2024. The study used official data from the Center for E-Health Care that was analyzed using retrospective, statistical and comparative analytical methods. It was found that indicators of primary morbidity and prevalence were characterized by pronounced variability with greatest increase in 2022, against the background of decrease in 2020-2021, that may be due to changes in availability of medical care in period of COVID-19 pandemic. The highest levels of morbidity and prevalence were found for hypertension, coronary heart disease and cerebrovascular diseases. Some nosologies, including myocardial infarction and other peripheral vascular diseases, demonstrated sharp increase in indicators, suggesting changes in disease detection and health care seeking behavior of population. The obtained results confirm necessity to improve system of monitoring, prevention and early detection of cardiovascular diseases, especially among high-risk groups.

title: Management of Drug–Drug Interactions, Safety Outcomes, and Potential Pharmacist Involvement in the Treatment of Tuberculosis and Respiratory Viral Coinfections: A Systematic Review of Case Reports and Case Series
abstract: Background/Objectives: Coinfection with tuberculosis (TB) and respiratory viral infections (RVIs) complicates clinical management due to polypharmacy, potential drug–drug interactions (DDIs), and adverse drug reactions (ADRs). We aimed to evaluate patient-level treatment data, focusing on potential DDIs, reported or suspected ADRs, clinical outcomes, and opportunities for pharmacist involvement in the management of TB/RVI coinfection. Methods: This systematic review was registered in PROSPERO CRD420251125786 and conducted following PRISMA guidelines. We searched MEDLINE, PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and Scopus for case reports and case series of TB/RVI coinfection. Study quality was assessed using the Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) tools. Potential DDIs between TB medicines and concomitant medicines were assessed using three drug interaction checkers and synthesized descriptively. Results: A total of 186 patients described in 108 studies were included. The studies reported 79 single-patient and 29 two- or more patient-level data on treatment. Severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) was the most frequently reported RVI (89.8%). An ADR was reported in 16 of 186 published cases (8.6%), mainly related to hepatotoxicity (11/21 ADR events; 52.4%), followed by anemia/cytopenia and gastrointestinal intolerance. Four contraindicated and 50 serious potential DDIs requiring close monitoring were identified, mostly involving rifampicin. Because the evidence consists of published case reports and case series, these proportions are descriptive rather than population risk estimates. Conclusions: TB/RVI coinfection is characterized by substantial polypharmacy, potential DDIs, and risk of ADRs. None of the included reports described pharmacist involvement. These findings suggest that pharmacist involvement in multidisciplinary TB services, together with co-treatment guidance, warrants evaluation to improve medication safety.

We aimed to evaluate patient-level treatment data, focusing on potential DDIs, reported or suspected ADRs, clinical outcomes, and opportunities for pharmacist involvement in the management of TB/RVI coinfection. Methods: This systematic review was registered in PROSPERO CRD420251125786 and conducted following PRISMA guidelines. We searched MEDLINE, PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and Scopus for case reports and case series of TB/RVI coinfection. Study quality was assessed using the Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) tools. Potential DDIs between TB medicines and concomitant medicines were assessed using three drug interaction checkers and synthesized descriptively. Results: A total of 186 patients described in 108 studies were included. The studies reported 79 single-patient and 29 two- or more patient-level data on treatment. Severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) was the most frequently reported RVI (89.8%). An ADR was reported in 16 of 186 published cases (8.6%), mainly related to hepatotoxicity (11/21 ADR events; 52.4%), followed by anemia/cytopenia and gastrointestinal intolerance. Four contraindicated and 50 serious potential DDIs requiring close monitoring were identified, mostly involving rifampicin. Because the evidence consists of published case reports and case series, these proportions are descriptive rather than population risk estimates. Conclusions: TB/RVI coinfection is characterized by substantial polypharmacy, potential DDIs, and risk of ADRs. None of the included reports described pharmacist involvement. These findings suggest that pharmacist involvement in multidisciplinary TB services, together with co-treatment guidance, warrants evaluation to improve medication safety.

title: The Impact of Socioeconomic and Geographic Factors in Respiratory Virus Testing in Australia.
abstract: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) causes significant disease burden in Australia, yet most confirmatory laboratory data come from acute healthcare settings. This study analyses RSV and other respiratory virus testing across different socio-demographic groups and healthcare settings using data from private and public laboratories Australia-wide. We analysed de-identified nucleic acid amplification test (NAATs) data for RSV (n=9.35 million), influenza A (n=9.42 million), influenza B (n=9.26 million), and SARS-CoV-2 (n=52.94 million) from 1 September 2017 to 31 August 2023, sourced from the three largest private and two public pathology providers in Australia. Data were stratified by socio-economic indexes for areas (SEIFA), remoteness, age, jurisdiction and care settings. Population-adjusted testing rates and positivity percentages were calculated. NAATs were highest in the most advantaged socio-economic quintile and major cities, declining with increased socio-economic disadvantage and geographic remoteness. Positivity rates were highest in the most advantaged quintile, but no consistent pattern was seen across other quintiles. Community settings accounted for most RSV testing, predominantly by private pathology providers. The COVID-19 pandemic from 2020 altered NAAT panels used and disrupted usual seasonal trends for RSV and influenza. Substantial variation exists in respiratory virus NAAT and positivity rates across socio-demographic groups, jurisdictions, and healthcare settings. Improving equitable access to testing among disadvantaged and remote populations is essential for accurate surveillance, timely intervention and effective prioritisation of public health interventions.

title: [THE TRENDS OF DEVELOPMENT OF SYSTEM OF PROTECTION OF REPRODUCTIVE HEALTH OF GIRLS-ADOLESCENTS OF ST. PETERSBURG].
abstract: The article presents results of comprehensive analysis of gynecological morbidity of girls-adolescents 15-17 years old in St. Petersburg in 2019-2024. It is established, on the basis of preventive examinations data, that average level of pathological affect made up to 105.04‰ and had pronounced trend to decreasing (β=-4.07; p=0.048). The comparative historical analysis demonstrated improvement of reproductive health indicators by 1.9 times as compared to basic data for 1996-1997. The characteristic of structure of gynecological morbidity of modern girls-adolescents in megalopolis is predominance of menstrual disorders (90.7% of newly diagnosed cases). At that, low medical activity of girls-adolescents continues that is proved by high percentage of newly diagnosed diseases detected only during preventive examinations (29.0%) and as well as significant prevalence of general morbidity over primary one. It is established that in St. Petersburg indicators of morbidity are 2.3-2.6 times higher than the National average indicators that is related to better accessibility of medical care and more efficient system of preventive examinations in the megalopolis. The analysis of the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on gynecological morbidity of girls-adolescents revealed significant decreasing of appealability in 2020 and subsequent incomplete reestablishment of indicators that testifies structural changes in pattern of medical activity of girls-adolescents. The study confirms efficiency of the system of protection of reproductive health of girls-adolescents in St. Petersburg but at the same time indicates at necessity to further enhance medical activity of girls-adolescents and to develop target preventive programs.

title: [THE MODERN DEMOGRAPHIC CHANGES IN THE KYRGYZ REPUBLIC].
abstract: The article presents results of analysis of medical demographic indicators of the Kyrgyz Republic in 2016-2024. The study was carried out concerning dynamics of population size, natality, mortality and migration processes based on statistical data from the National Statistical Committee and the Center of E-Health Care. The regional differences in demographic trends were revealed. The high natality is specific for Southern regions, while in Northern regions its steady decreasing was fixed. It is established that COVID-19 pandemic had short-term impact on mortality growth in 2020. Despite positive natural increase, its pace is decreasing that requires elaboration of state demographic policy and mechanisms stimulating natality, population health promotion and development of regional health care infrastructure. In 2022-2023 migration flows demonstrated positive balance that reflects changes in social economic priorities of population. The main motives for migration remain low wages, limited career opportunities and uncertainty about future. The obtained results confirm necessity of systematic approach to prognostication of demographic processes and development of measures stabilizing medical demographic situation in the Republic.
