title: Trust in Medicine in the Crisis of Epistemic Authority: Evidence from a Refused-Knowledge Community
abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic accelerated a broader crisis of epistemic authority in medicine, fostering the emergence of refused-knowledge communities as socially credible alternatives to official healthcare. This study examines the sociocognitive factors associated with extra-institutional care-seeking among members of a Facebook health community promoting therapeutic protocols misaligned with the clinical guidelines approved by the Italian Ministry of Health. A cross-sectional survey was administered between June and September 2022 to a purposive sample of members of the #TDC19 Facebook group (N = 574). Path-analytic mediation models were estimated to test the role of trust in official medicine, digital health literacy, and overconfidence as mediators of the relationship between refused-knowledge beliefs and extra-institutional care-seeking. Endorsement of refused-knowledge beliefs was positively associated with extra-institutional care-seeking. A significant indirect association via trust in official medicine emerged, while digital health literacy and overconfidence did not yield significant indirect effects. Perceived COVID-19 severity was indirectly associated with care-seeking via trust in official medicine. Lower trust in official medicine thus emerges as a relevant but not exhaustive correlate of extra-institutional care-seeking, which remained directly associated with refused-knowledge beliefs after adjustment for trust. The #TDC19 case illustrates how refused-knowledge communities driven by licensed physicians reconfigure rather than reject the expert/lay boundary, redirecting trust toward outsider professionals. Rebuilding trust in official medicine may require addressing the structural conditions of its erosion rather than focusing exclusively on individual health beliefs.

title: Predicting Depressive Symptoms From Cross-Sectional and Longitudinal Data Using XGBoost-SHAP and Cross-Lagged Model.
abstract: Objective University students face significant academic, social, and career-planning challenges. Under such stressors, deficient emotion regulation may increase vulnerability to depressive states, in which persistent symptoms could progress to clinical depression. This study investigates key risk and protective factors for depressive symptoms among university students, including negative life events, neuroticism, and social support. A longitudinal framework was further employed to assess changes in depressive symptoms before and after the COVID-19 pandemic, with the goal of informing early identification and intervention strategies. Methods The dataset included 18 024 valid responses from baseline assessments. Follow-up assessments conducted 1 year later included 6129 participants. The extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost) model with SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) was used to quantify the relative importance of specific factors (e.g., negative life events and social support) on depressive symptoms, while a cross-lagged panel model examined longitudinal directional associations between these factors and depressive symptoms. Results The prevalence of depressive symptoms was 15.2% among the student sample. Significant correlations were observed between symptom severity and adverse family relationships, childhood trauma, prior suicide attempts, and psychiatric history. Neuroticism and negative life events showed significant positive associations with depressive symptoms, while subjective support and support utilization demonstrated negative associations with symptom severity. Longitudinal analysis revealed an increase in both symptom severity and depression detection rates following the COVID-19 pandemic. The cross-lagged panel model identified neuroticism as a significant positive longitudinal predictor of depressive symptoms, whereas subjective support showed a significant negative longitudinal association with subsequent depressive symptoms. Conclusion This study identifies neuroticism as an important longitudinal risk indicator for depressive symptoms and subjective support as a protective indicator, while negative life events showed significant cross-sectional associations with symptom severity. The findings demonstrate how integrating longitudinal designs with interpretable machine learning elucidates complex mental health dynamics in student populations, providing an evidence-based framework for targeted interventions within campus mental health policies.

title: Bridging the gap: Evaluating communication effectiveness and satisfaction towards telepsychiatry services at a teaching hospital from the providers' and patients' perspectives.
abstract: BackgroundThe COVID-19 pandemic accelerated telepsychiatry adoption, proving its flexibility despite ongoing challenges.AimThis study investigated whether perceived communication effectiveness, satisfaction, and technology self-efficacy are associated with frequency of recent telepsychiatry use among mental health service providers (MHSPs) and patients at a Malaysian teaching hospital.MethodsA cross-sectional study was conducted between February and May 2024. Participants included MHSPs and patients with at least one telepsychiatry session. Independent variables-perceived communication effectiveness, satisfaction, and technology self-efficacy-were assessed using the Telehealth Usability Questionnaire (TUQ) and the Modified Technology Self-Efficacy Scale (MTSES). The dependent variable was frequency of recent telepsychiatry use within the past 2 months. Associated factors were identified via comparative analyses and ordinal logistic regression.ResultsAmong 92 MHSP respondents (median age 36; 65.7% female), perceived communication effectiveness significantly associated with frequency of recent use (adjusted OR: 2.05, p = 0.008); satisfaction and self-efficacy were not significant. For patients, only younger age significantly associated with recent telepsychiatry use (adjusted OR: 0.90, 95% CI: 0.82-0.98; p = 0.016).ConclusionPerceived communication effectiveness is associated with more frequent recent telepsychiatry use among providers, while satisfaction and technology self-efficacy are not. These findings suggest that enhancing the perceived utility is essential for broader adoption.

title: Determinants of personal protective measures use to prevent the spread of respiratory infectious diseases in early 2024, Canada: a cross-sectional study
abstract: This study explored how people in Canada make decisions regarding the use of personal protective measures (PPMs) to protect themselves and others from respiratory infectious diseases (RIDs). It examined patterns and perceptions of PPM use post-COVID-19 pandemic and potential determinants of ongoing PPM use. A cross-sectional survey with 6,611 respondents, selected from online panels to represent the Canadian population, was conducted in February 2024. Descriptive statistics and multivariate linear regression models were used to describe and understand the potential determinants of PPM use. While PPMs were generally perceived as effective, their adoption varied. Hand washing and covering coughs and sneezes were common hygiene habits post-pandemic. Cleaning high-touch areas and improving ventilation had more barriers to uptake. Staying home when sick, while perceived as effective by almost all respondents, was reported by only two thirds of those sick in the past 3 months. Mask-wearing in indoor public settings was viewed as the least effective and least adopted PPM. In each tested PPM’s multivariate linear regression model (adjusted R 2 ranged from 0.216–0.407 across 6 models) several factors were associated with PPM use, with perceived effectiveness of PPMs ( p < 0.001) and concern with getting sick ( p < 0.001) consistently associated with most PPMs. Commonly cited reasons for not using PPMs included them not being mandatory and having barriers to their implementation. Results from this study can help inform supports and public health communication strategies for PPM use during current and future seasonal RID outbreaks and during pandemics.

title: Modeling and simulation methods used in the maritime industry: evolution, applications and future perspectives
abstract: Modeling and simulation (M&S) techniques have evolved from optional engineering tools to indispensable pillars of modern maritime practice. This article presents a comprehensive systematic review of the most important modeling and simulation methodologies applied to maritime industry processes, including workflows for ship design, shipyard fabrication and construction, port and terminal operations, vessel traffic management, maintenance scheduling, supply chain logistics, and risk management procedures. The study demonstrates that M&S techniques enable safer, more efficient, and more environmentally sustainable operations, validated by scientific standards. The COVID-19 pandemic served as a critical catalyst, consolidating the strategic value of M&S as a central component of maritime resilience and innovation. This research traces the evolution of M&S adoption from 2010 to 2025, identifying four dominant research directions: maritime simulators, computational fluid dynamics (CFD)/finite element analysis (FEA), digital twins, and artificial intelligence-based methods. The analysis reveals that while traditional approaches dominated the 2010-2020 period, emerging technologies—particularly digital twins and AI-based methods—have accelerated exponentially since 2020, reflecting the maritime industry's accelerated digitalization. title: Vaccine Completion or Hospital Platforms First? A Country-Level Typology of Child Pneumonia Intervention Priorities in 204 Countries
abstract: Background: Global child pneumonia strategy increasingly asks whether marginal resources should go to completing vaccine programmes or to hospital platform investments. The answer cannot be uniform across countries. We operationalised this question as a country-level priority typology for 204 countries, treating the vaccine policy dimension, coverage with pneumococcal conjugate vaccine (PCV), Haemophilus influenzae type b (Hib) vaccine, and diphtheria-tetanus-pertussis vaccine (DTP), as a first-order input to classification rather than an after-the-fact check. Methods We combined Global Burden of Disease Study 2023 estimates of deaths from 29 pneumonia-relevant pathogens in ages 0–19 years for 204 countries in 2023, each pathogen assigned to a dominant intervention channel (vaccine-reachable, mixed, platform-sensitive) under previously published rules, with WHO/UNICEF Estimates of National Immunization Coverage (WUENIC) for PCV3, Hib3, DTP3 and BCG, and with WHO vaccine-introduction records. An EPI coverage index (mean of PCV3 and Hib3) summarised conjugate-vaccine programme strength. Countries were classified by declared thresholds into low-burden (<500 deaths), vaccine-priority (vaccine-channel share ≥40% and EPI index <80%), platform-priority (platform share ≥50%), or mixed-transitional. Vaccine residual space was computed as vaccine-channel deaths multiplied by the coverage gap. Robustness of the typology was verified by bootstrap resampling of the 204 countries (500 replicates; all four types perfectly stable, mean Jaccard 1.00, because classification is a deterministic per-country rule) and by ±5 percentage-point sensitivity on all three declared thresholds, which reclassified 4–11 countries (2.0–5.4%) per threshold (Supplementary Text S9, Tables S9–S10). Findings In 2023 the 29 pathogens accounted for 964,615 deaths: 45.7% vaccine-reachable, 13.1% mixed and 41.1% platform-sensitive. Thirty-two vaccine-priority countries carried 51.8% of all deaths; within them, 20 urgent-stratum countries (EPI index <60%) carried 209,807 deaths and 12 completion-stage countries (60-80%) carried 289,607. Ten vaccine-priority countries, including China, had not introduced PCV nationally, representing introduction space rather than within-programme coverage gaps. Forty-seven countries with DTP3 coverage below 80% carried 62.6% of global pertussis deaths. Eighteen platform-priority countries carried 7.8% of deaths; the same two pathogens (Klebsiella pneumoniae, Pseudomonas aeruginosa) led the platform channel across high-burden settings. Across the 2019-2023 pandemic window, the largest single-country share movements pushed platform shares down as COVID-19 entered the vaccine channel, but across the full set of 82 countries with at least 500 deaths the platform share rose in 61 countries and fell in 21 (median +1.8 percentage points), with the largest increases in South Africa (+8.1) and Lesotho (+8.0). Conclusions Whether vaccines or platforms come first is an empirical country attribute, not a global verdict. The 204-country typology and accompanying dataset offer a concrete starting point for allocating the next increment of child pneumonia resources.

title: PulmoDiagAI: An Intelligent Medical Diagnosis System for Automated Pulmonary Pathology Classification using Deep Learning
abstract: Abstract Lung cancer and Coronavirus Disease 2019 (COVID’19) remain among the leading causes of respiratory-related morbidity and mortality worldwide, highlighting the critical need for rapid, accurate, and automated diagnostic solutions. This study presents PulmoDiagAI, an intelligent computer-aided diagnosis (CAD) system that integrates state of the art deep learning techniques for the automated detection and classification of pulmonary diseases from chest X-ray and computed tomography (CT) images. Five pre-trained convolutional neural network (CNN) architectures, namely VGG19, ResNet50, MobileNetV3, EfficientNet-B3, and DenseNet121 were fine-tuned using a transfer learning strategy to identify the most effective model for each diagnostic task. A comprehensive preprocessing pipeline, including image standardization, median filtering, resizing, intensity normalization, and Contrast Limited Adaptive Histogram Equalization (CLAHE), was employed to enhance image quality and improve feature extraction. The proposed framework was evaluated on two publicly available benchmark datasets: IQ-OTH/NCCD for lung cancer detection and COVID-QU-Ex for COVID’19 diagnosis. Experimental results demonstrate that EfficientNet-B3 achieved superior performance for COVID’19 classifications, reaching an accuracy of 97.0% and an AUC-ROC of 99.43%. For lung cancer detection, MobileNetV3 and ResNet50 delivered outstanding results, achieving accuracies of 99.0% and 98.0%, respectively, with a perfect AUC-ROC of 100%. To facilitate clinical adoption, the proposed model was deployed as an intuitive graphical user interface (GUI) that provides real time diagnostic predictions along with confidence scores. By combining high diagnostic accuracy, computational efficiency, and practical usability, PulmoDiagAI offers a reliable decision-support system capable of assisting radiologists and clinicians in the early detection of pulmonary diseases, ultimately contributing to improved diagnostic workflows and patient outcomes.

title: Mapping policy architecture for vaccine research, development and manufacturing in Africa: a scoping review protocol
abstract: Introduction: Despite the unprecedented speed of COVID-19 vaccine development, manufacturing capacity remained geographically concentrated in a limited number of countries with established vaccine-production capacity and was insufficient to meet global demand promptly and equitably. This constrained production capacity, together with domestic political pressures and market power asymmetries, contributed to vaccine nationalism. Therefore, to secure Africa’s future access to vaccines, the African Union aims to produce at least 60 percent of the vaccines consumed locally in Africa by 2040, up from less than one percent, as part of the broader health security and future pandemic response agenda. Achieving this vision requires proactive policy coherence and coordination across the continent to prevent duplication of efforts, waste and unhealthy competition. Consequently, this review aims to map, assess and compare the content of national, regional, and continental-level policies for vaccine R&D and manufacturing in Africa, generating actionable insights to inform coordinated strategies and advance the AU’s 2040 vaccine manufacturing goal. Methods and analysis The review will be conducted following the Arksey and O’Malley framework and in accordance with the Joanna Briggs Institute’s methodological guidance for scoping reviews. Reporting will adhere to the PRISMA-ScR guidelines. Policy instruments relevant to human vaccine R&D and manufacturing in Africa will be included as the primary unit of analysis. The sources of evidence are policy databases – Overton, Policy Commons, and ProQuest Policy File Index – and the official websites of relevant governments, regional and continental institutions. The search will focus on Africa, using key terms relating to vaccine policies. Two independent reviewers will screen the retrieved documents in Covidence, and data extraction will be conducted using a pretested template in Microsoft Excel 2021. This review does not require ethical approval. Conclusion The results will contribute to the academic literature on vaccine security and the policy architecture for vaccine R&D and manufacturing in Africa.

title: High-Throughput FRET Affinity Screening Technique (HTFAST) for Cell-Free Expressed Binding Protein Characterization.
abstract: The rapid engineering of binding proteins is increasingly driven by cell-free, machine-learning-guided optimization. However, high-throughput, quantitative characterization of binding affinity remains a major bottleneck, particularly for proteins expressed in cell-free systems without purification. Here, we present High-Throughput FRET Affinity Screening Technique (HTFAST) for rapid affinity characterization of binders expressed directly in crude E. coli cell-free protein expression reactions. HTFAST leverages Förster resonance energy transfer (FRET) between cell-free expressed fluorescent-protein-fused binders and dye-labeled antigens to enable real-time, quantitative measurement of equilibrium dissociation constants. We systematically optimized fluorophore pairs and labeling parameters using the SpyTag003-SpyCatcher003 model system. HTFAST reliably quantified nanomolar binding affinities in crude lysates for the SpyTag003-SpyCatcher003 model system. It also resolved affinities spanning low-nanomolar to hundreds-of-nanomolar for nanobodies against multiple antigens, including CD4, HER2, and HSA. We further benchmarked HTFAST against a panel of five SARS-CoV-2 RBD nanobodies, demonstrating HTFAST's ability to rank binders targeting the same antigen with affinities correlating strongly with reported BLI/SPR measurements. Finally, we demonstrate that both binding partners can be expressed directly in CFE, further streamlining screening workflows. Overall, HTFAST provides a scalable, quantitative, and cell-free-compatible approach for high-throughput affinity screening, well-suited for DBTL protein engineering campaigns.

title: Disease-associated NK-cell state remodeling reveals transcriptional profiles predictive of clinical phenotypes
abstract: Natural killer (NK) cells adapt their cellular states to diverse tissue and inflammatory environments, yet how this plasticity manifests across pathological contexts and relates to patient-level disease phenotypes remains poorly defined. Here we established the Human NK-cell Atlas (HNKA) from over 1 million NK cells, including samples from 1,632 donors spanning 50 diseases. Within a shared NK-cell state architecture, analyses of state abundance and matched-reference exceedance distinguished disease-biased redistribution from transcriptional displacement. Fine-grained analyses localized disease-associated remodeling to specific NK-cell states, including CD56dim NK ISG15 in infection and autoimmunity and CD56bright NK ITM2C in tumors. These patterns were accompanied by recurrent interferon responses and state-specific regulatory activity. Cytokine perturbations recapitulated key transcriptional features of disease-associated NK-cell states. We developed NKceiver, a model based on state-specific NK-cell expression profiles for patient-level prediction. It distinguished 18 diseases and predicted COVID-19 severity and response to immune checkpoint inhibitors, with predictive performance retained in unseen patients and studies. Collectively, our results reveal that disease-associated remodeling within the diverse NK-cell state repertoire resolved by HNKA is biologically interpretable and clinically informative, supporting disease discrimination and prediction of clinical phenotypes.

title: Benchmarking Large Language Models for Transcriptomic Data Analysis and Visualization: Multi-Model Workflow Evaluation
abstract: This study presents a comprehensive benchmarking evaluation of large language models (LLMs) and agentic coding systems for automated analysis and visualization workflows for transcriptomic data, in particular human responses to COVID-19 infection. Multiple models, including ChatGPT 5.5, Claude Sonnet 4.6, Gemini 3.1, and Llama4-Scout, were assessed across a series of scientific prompts designed to test their ability to reproduce workflow components such as dimensionality reduction, clustering, outlier detection, reproducibility, and code generation. The benchmark protocol involved varying prompt specificity and examined both quantitative metrics such as clustering scores and outlier counts as well as qualitative aspects such as code quality and reproducibility. Results indicate that prompt specificity improves code structure and methodological correctness, but quantitative performance depends heavily on preprocessing choices and execution environment. While some models produced strong code and reproducible outputs, alignment with scientific targets like label-based clustering was inconsistent. The findings highlight the promise and limitations of current LLMs for automating scientific data analysis and visualization and suggest directions for future benchmarking and workflow standardization.

title: Multiple Sclerosis and Viruses: « Liaisons Dangereuses ».
abstract: Multiple sclerosis (MS) is a complex, multifactorial neurodegenerative disease with an aetiology that is still partially elusive. Several risk factors are associated with MS development including genetic predisposition and various environmental stressors; however, recently, viral infections have gained significant attention as a crucial environmental trigger. Despite the well-established link between Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) and MS susceptibility, a single-pathogen model fails to clearly characterise the molecular cascades driving the disease, suggesting that the transition from infection to autoimmune response involves more than one viral agent. In this review we examine the speculation that the interactions among different neurotropic viruses could serve a collective causative role in MS, which is under-researched in the literature at present. We summarise contradictory evidence on the role of different viral agents, including the Herpesviridae family (Human Cytomegalovirus, EBV, Herpes Simplex Viruses HSV-1 and HSV-2, and Varicella Zoster Virus), Paramyxoviridae family (Measles Virus and Rubella Virus), Influenza virus, SARS-CoV-2, and Human Endogenous Retroviruses (HERVs). Through interplay within shared molecular pathways, immune modulation, and activation of latent infections, these viruses may collectively influence the inflammatory and demyelinating processes that characterise MS. This review evaluates the etiological role of viral interplay in MS through the cumulative and interactive effects of these pathogens. The available epidemiological, immunological, and experimental data converge on the concept that viral co-exposures act synergistically to shape MS susceptibility in genetically predisposed individuals. Characterising these viral interactions presents a new research direction for the identification of novel biomarkers and the development of preventative strategies through the targeted control of viral networks.

We summarise contradictory evidence on the role of different viral agents, including the Herpesviridae family (Human Cytomegalovirus, EBV, Herpes Simplex Viruses HSV-1 and HSV-2, and Varicella Zoster Virus), Paramyxoviridae family (Measles Virus and Rubella Virus), Influenza virus, SARS-CoV-2, and Human Endogenous Retroviruses (HERVs). Through interplay within shared molecular pathways, immune modulation, and activation of latent infections, these viruses may collectively influence the inflammatory and demyelinating processes that characterise MS. This review evaluates the etiological role of viral interplay in MS through the cumulative and interactive effects of these pathogens. The available epidemiological, immunological, and experimental data converge on the concept that viral co-exposures act synergistically to shape MS susceptibility in genetically predisposed individuals. Characterising these viral interactions presents a new research direction for the identification of novel biomarkers and the development of preventative strategies through the targeted control of viral networks.

title: High-pressure macromolecular crystallography as a tool for studying protein flexibility.
abstract: Protein function depends on their conformational flexibility. Complementary to temperature-dependent studies, high-pressure (HP) macromolecular crystallography is well suited to exploring the conformational space of proteins at atomic resolution. We have developed a new HP cell concept for macromolecular X-ray crystallography that overcomes the limitations of current devices. It consists of a single-crystalline sapphire capillary, which is loaded with multiple crystals and pressurized with helium at freely adjustable gas pressures of up to 120 MPa. Studying five different proteins, we generally observed a compression of the protein structures and a decrease in thermal displacement parameters at high pressure. Structurally, observations included the compression of a central tunnel of a biotechnologically relevant enzyme and the stabilization of ligand binding in the membrane protein photosynthetic reaction center of Cereibacter sphaeroides. For two pharmaceutically relevant proteins, the human kinase DRAK2 and SARS-CoV-2 main protease, we identified concerted movements of subdomains. Such knowledge is essential for predictions of protein dynamics and defined conformational states, offering the potential for improved structure-based drug development.

title: Immunopathogenesis of MEWDS and the white dot syndromes: anatomical specificity and mechanistic heterogeneity
abstract: The white dot syndromes (WDS) are an umbrella term for a heterogeneous group of idiopathic inflammatory chorioretinopathies—including multiple evanescent white dot syndrome (MEWDS), acute posterior multifocal placoid pigment epitheliopathy (APMPPE), birdshot chorioretinopathy, multifocal choroiditis (MFC), and punctate inner choroidopathy (PIC). MEWDS is the subtype in which the debate over the primary anatomical site of disease initiation has been most intense: three competing hypotheses—choriocapillaritis, photoreceptoritis, and retinal pigment epithelium (RPE) dysfunction—remain unresolved. MEWDS has also accumulated substantial evidence for viral triggers, including SARS-CoV-2 infection and COVID-19 vaccination, whereas other WDS subtypes exhibit distinct mechanistic signatures (HLA-A29 in birdshot, choriocapillaris ischemia in APMPPE, Bruch's membrane disruption in MFC/PIC). This narrative review synthesizes the three MEWDS-specific hypotheses against multimodal imaging, genetic, and immunological evidence published through 2026, and contrasts them with disease-specific mechanisms across the WDS spectrum. Indocyanine green angiography (ICGA) findings support primary choriocapillaritis, whereas optical coherence tomography angiography (OCT-A) has yielded paradoxically preserved flow maps; RPE dysfunction remains plausible given fundus autofluorescence patterns and the RPE's immunoregulatory role. The Multimodal Imaging in Uveitis (MUV) Task Force Report 11 (2026) proposes an anatomical reclassification that assigns MEWDS to the photoreceptor/RPE group. Across WDS, the evidence supports mechanistically distinct diseases and motivates disease-specific, mechanism-driven nomenclature.

title: Development of a mortality prognostic model based on the Pneumonia Severity Index for older adults with pneumonia in integrated medical and older adult care institutions: a retrospective study
abstract: Background Population aging has increased the demand for integrated medical and long-term care services, particularly in China. Age-related respiratory impairment and immunosenescence render institutionalized older adults at a high risk for pneumonia-associated with poorer outcomes than community-acquired pneumonia. We aimed to investigate the prognostic value of the Pneumonia Severity Index (PSI) for mortality in older adults with pneumonia in integrated medical and elderly care facilities, and to develop a prognostic prediction model. Methods Medical records of older adult patients with pneumonia admitted to the integrated medical-elderly care ward of the Department of Geriatrics, Hefei First People's Hospital from June 2019 to June 2024 were retrospectively retrieved. A total of 312 patients were enrolled according to predefined inclusion and exclusion criteria. Patients were divided into a survival group ( n = 232) and a non-survival group ( n = 80) based on post-treatment clinical outcomes. Univariate analyses were performed to compare clinical characteristics between the two groups. All clinical variables were screened using Least Absolute Shrinkage and Selection Operator (LASSO) regression. Variables with non-zero coefficients were subsequently incorporated into Firth's bias-corrected logistic regression to construct the prediction model, followed by model validation. Results Univariate analysis revealed significant intergroup differences in age ≥80 years, coronary heart disease, white blood cell count (WBC),neutrophil count, multidrug-resistant organism (MDRO) infection, PSI score, hemoglobin, creatinine, coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19)infection, Clinical Frailty Scale (CFS) score >7, Prognostic Nutritional Index (PNI) 7, PNI 7, PNI <35, and CRP can effectively predict mortality risk in this population and has superior clinical utility compared with PSI alone.

title: Shifting viral aetiology, codetection and age-specific mortality in severe acute respiratory infection in Brazil, 2022–2025: a nationwide surveillance study
abstract: BACKGROUND: Respiratory viral aetiology and codetection among severe acute respiratory infection (SARI) notifications have evolved post-COVID-19. We examined temporal patterns, age heterogeneity, and severe outcome associations in Brazil. METHODS: We analysed nationwide SIVEP-Gripe SARI records (2022-2025; extracted July 2026) with RT-PCR viral detection. Seven mutually exclusive categories were evaluated using robust Poisson regression to estimate adjusted risk ratios (aRRs) for SARI-attributed mortality and a severe composite outcome (ICU admission, invasive ventilation, or death). RESULTS: Among 447,107 virus-positive records, 7.2% involved codetections and 25.4% included RSV. Isolated SARS-CoV-2 declined from 72.4% (2022) to 6.8% (2025), while codetections rose from 3.0% to 11.2%. Compared to isolated RSV, mortality was higher for codetection without RSV (aRR 1.80, 95% CI: 1.67-1.94), isolated SARS-CoV-2 (1.62, 1.54-1.70), and codetection with RSV (1.40, 1.27-1.55). Associations varied by age ($p < .001$). Among RSV-positive cases, codetection conferred increased mortality risk (aRR 1.46, 1.32-1.61). Excluding isolated SARS-CoV-2 attenuated the 2025-versus-2022 codetection prevalence ratio from 1.85 to 1.10. CONCLUSIONS: Viral detections shifted towards greater heterogeneity, strongly driven by changing surveillance composition. Varying testing indications and panels limit causal inference. Integrated, age-sensitive surveillance with standardized diagnostic reporting is essential; surveillance proportions do not reflect population incidence.

title: A Structured Decision-Support Framework for Technology Adoption to Advance Airport Sustainability and Resilience
abstract: Airports face challenges in integrating sustainability and resilience into their long-term operational plans due to climate change, regulatory mandates, financial constraints, and disruptions such as the COVID-19 pandemic. While technology adoption plays a key role in addressing these issues, many airports lack structured strategies for evaluating, selecting, and implementing sustainability and resilience-focused innovations. Technology is often adopted reactively, driven by crises or regulatory compliance, rather than through proactive, strategic planning. This study introduces an empirically supported decision-support framework that combines established technology adoption models, sustainability and resilience assessment logic, and airport-specific implementation needs into a structured process for sustainable and resilient technology adoption. The framework synthesizes engineering-based maturity assessment, strategic planning, cross-disciplinary implementation, and Envision-based sustainability and resilience criteria, providing a tool that merges engineering judgment with organizational, regulatory, and environmental considerations. It equips airport decision-makers with a practical methodology for aligning technological innovation with operational performance, sustainability objectives, and long-term adaptability. The framework was empirically supported through expert input and statistical analyses of survey responses representing 27 commercial airports across the United States. An illustrative case study demonstrates an application of the framework by translating strategic sustainability and resilience goals into actionable implementation steps. This study contributes to the body of knowledge by presenting an evidence-based decision-support methodology that bridges the gap among strategic commitments and implementation, supports decarbonization, operational resilience, and infrastructure sustainability, while providing practical guidance for planners, sustainability leaders, and policymakers.

title: Socioeconomic Disparities in Dental Diseases and Related Behaviors Among Adults in Japan, 2022: A Nationwide Cross-sectional Study
abstract: Objectives: Socioeconomic disparities in oral health have been widely reported worldwide, yet evidence among adults in Japan remains limited. This study aimed to examine the associations between socioeconomic status (SES) and both dental diseases and oral health-related behaviors in a nationally representative sample of Japanese adults. Methods: We analyzed data from 28,617 participants in the 2022 Japan “COVID-19 and Society” Internet Survey (JACSIS), a nationwide, cross-sectional, web-based questionnaire. The exposure variable was equivalent household income, categorized into quintiles. Outcomes included self-reported periodontal disease, dental caries, and four dental behaviors: Daily tooth brushing, daily snacking, annual preventive dental visits, and annual treatment dental visits. Logistic regression analyses were conducted using inverse probability weighting (IPW) to adjust for potential selection bias, adjusting for demographic, socioeconomic, health-related, and regional covariates. Results: Lower equivalent household income was significantly associated with higher odds of dental disease and lower engagement in preventive or treatment-related dental visits. Participants in the lowest income quintile were more likely to report periodontal disease (adjusted odds ratios [AOR], 1.32; 95% confidence interval (CI), 1.06–1.65) or dental caries (AOR, 1.63; 95% CI, 1.29–2.05) and less likely to undergo annual preventive dental visits (AOR, 0.59; 95% CI, 0.51–0.69) compared with those in the highest quintile. A dose–response relationship was observed for some outcomes. Conclusion: Clear socioeconomic disparities exist in both dental diseases and preventive behaviors among adults in Japan. Policies promoting preventive dental visits and reducing income-related inequalities are essential to achieving equitable oral health and mitigating broader health disparities.

title: Leveraging non-concurrent controls for time-to-event endpoints in platform trials for infectious diseases.
abstract: Platform trials offer an efficient framework for evaluating multiple therapies against a common control, with the flexibility to add or remove investigational arms. For newly added arms, leveraging non-concurrent controls can further enhance efficiency. However, naively pooling non-concurrent controls with concurrent controls can introduce bias due to time trends. In trials involving time-to-event outcomes, methods for addressing this problem are limited. This study addresses this gap by developing and evaluating frequentist and Bayesian approaches to incorporate non-concurrent controls data into the analysis of time-to-event endpoints, with a particular focus on drug development for infectious diseases. We propose extensions to both frequentist and Bayesian methods, employing a Cox proportional-hazards model and a Bayesian piecewise exponential model, respectively. We assess the practical performance of these methods through comprehensive simulations, including a resampling-based simulation of the COVID-19 platform trial, the ACTIV-1 IM study. Our simulations demonstrate that no single method is uniformly superior; the optimal approach is contingent on the specific characteristics of the underlying time trend. This finding highlights that the analytical method must be carefully selected based on the anticipated time trend and reinforces that naive pooling should be avoided. Therefore, we recommend pre-specifying sensitivity analyses using a range of methods to ensure the robustness of the trial conclusions.

title: Auswirkungen einer SRAS-CoV-2 Infektion während der Schwangerschaft auf Plazenta und Kind
abstract: Hintergrund Seit Dezember 2019 beschäftigen der Ausbruch, die anhaltenden Infektionen und weitreichenden Folgen des Coronavirus SARS-CoV-2 die Menschheit weltweit. Zahlreiche Studien wurden initiiert, um die Auswirkungen der Virusinfektion, unter anderem auf das ungeborene Leben, zu untersuchen. Schon früh ergaben sich erste Hinweise auf eine Infektion der Plazenta und erhöhte Raten an small for gestational age (SGA)-Neugeborenen. Die Rate an vertikalen Transmissionen wird im einstelligen Prozentbereich angegeben. Ziel dieser Promotion war es, mögliche Auswirkungen einer SARS-CoV-2 Infektion während der Schwangerschaft auf Plazenta und Fetus anhand fetaler MRTs zwischen der 24. Schwangeschaftswoche (SSW) zu untersuchen. Methoden 34 Patientinnen mit bestätigter SARS-CoV-2 Infektion während der Schwangerschaft wurden klinisch-prospektiv zwischen Dezember 2020 und Juni 2021 untersucht; bei sieben Patientinnen wurde 12 Wochen nach der ersten Untersuchung eine Folge-MRT durchgeführt. Im Rekrutierungszeitraum von Oktober 2020 bis Juni 2021 dominierte die Alpha-Variante des Virus als vorherrschende Form. Zu Beginn des genannten Zeitraums standen noch keine Impfstoffe zur Verfügung und waren nach Zulassung noch nicht für Schwangere empfohlen. Die fetalen MRTs wurden nach einem Standard-Protokoll mit einem 1,5 Tesla MRT-Gerät aufgenommen und von zwei zertifizierten Radiologinnen mit mindestens dreijähriger Erfahrung in fetaler MRT-Bildgebung ausgewertet. Darüber hinaus wurden klinische Parameter zu Anamnese, Schwangerschaft und Symptomen anhand eines standardisierten Fragebogens erhoben. Anschließend wurden plazentare und fetale Messungen und Volumetrien durchgeführt und statistisch (t-Test und general linear model - GLM) ausgewertet. Ergebnisse Das mittlere Gestationsalter (GA) zum Untersuchungszeitpunkt betrug 33,1 Wochen, mit einer Spanne von 24 bis 40 Wochen. Symptombeginn war im Schnitt bei einem GA von 19,1 Wochen, mit einer Spanne von 5 bis 34 Wochen. Das errechnete fetale Gewicht (eFG) zeigte keine Anzeichen von SGA. Die Volumetrie der fetalen Lungen zeigte im Vergleich zum Referenzwert signifikant verringerte Volumina in der gesamten Studiengruppe (p=0,009) mit einem verstärkten Effekt bei Infektion im dritten Trimenon. Ein Gruppenvergleich, normalisiert durch das eFG ausgedrückt als Prozent der 50. Perzentile des Referenzwertes, zwischen einer Infektion im 1. Trimenon (p=0,020) und einer Infektion im 3. einer gerätespezifischen prä-SARS-CoV-2 Kontrollgruppe (p=0,005) zeigte die Auswirkung des Infektionszeitpunktes auf das fetale Lungenvolumen (FLV). Das Assessment der Operkularisierung der Sylvischen Fissur, der kortikalen Faltung und des transversalen Kleinhirndurchmessers waren bei allen Feten altersentsprechend. Darüber hinaus wurden der anterior-posterior (ap)-Durchmesser und die cranio-caudale (cc)-Ausdehnung von Pons, Medulla oblongata, Mesencephalon und Kleinhirnwurm gemessen. Dabei ergaben sich keine pathologischen Befunde. Die Bildgebung der Plazenta zeigte ein signifikant höheres Maß an Heterogenität in der Studien- im Vergleich zur prä-SARS-CoV-2 Kontrollgruppe (p=0,0475). Schlussfolgerung Bei ungeimpften Patientinnen mit SARS-CoV-2 Infektion während der Schwangerschaft wurde eine signifikante Reduktion des fetalen Lungenvolumens nachweisen, sowohl im Vergleich zu etablierten Referenzwerten als auch zu einer lokalen prä-SARS-CoV-2 Kontrollgruppe. Der Effekt war besonders deutlich, wenn die Infektion im dritten Trimenon stattgefunden hatte. Es konnten keine weiteren fetalen Pathologien hinsichtlich des fetalen Gewichts, der strukturellen Hirnentwicklung oder struktureller Veränderungen des fetalen Körpers festgestellt werden. Die verfügbaren Geburtsberichte (U1) ergeben keinen Hinweis auf Atemnot oder akute Anpassungsstörungen an die extrauterine Umwelt.

title: ARE-Wochenbericht des RKI KW43
abstract: Die ARE-Aktivität liegt auf Bevölkerungsebene und im ambulanten Bereich auf einem moderaten Niveau, im stationären Bereich auf einem niedrigen Niveau. Weiterhin wird das ARE-Geschehen hauptsächlich durch Rhino-/Enteroviren und Parainfluenzaviren bestimmt. Die Aktivität von SARS-CoV-2, Influenzaviren und RSV ist derzeit in allen Systemen noch niedrig, jedoch zeigte sich bereits in den letzten Wochen in verschiedenen Systemen ein allmählicher Anstieg der SARS-CoV-2- und Influenza-Aktivität. Es gibt Hinweise, dass SARS-CoV-2 bereits flächendeckend bundesweit zirkuliert. Die Aktivität akuter respiratorischer Erkrankungen (ARE) in der Bevölkerung ist seit der 40. KW 2026 relativ stabil geblieben und befindet sich weiterhin auf einem moderaten Niveau. Im ambulanten Bereich ist die Zahl der Arzt¬besuche wegen ARE in der 43. KW im Vergleich zur Vorwoche ebenfalls stabil geblieben und lag ebenfalls auf einem moderaten Niveau. Im Nationalen Referenzzentrum (NRZ) für Influenzaviren wurden in der 43. KW 2026 in insgesamt 50 der 76 einge¬sandten Sentinel¬proben respiratorische Viren identifiziert, darunter hauptsächlich Rhino-/Enteroviren (43 %), gefolgt von Para¬influenzaviren (PIV; 14 %) und Adenoviren (7 %). Neben weiteren Viren des Erregerpanels wurden auch Influenzaviren (A und B) (3 %) und SARS-CoV-2 (3 %) nachgewiesen. Respiratorische Synzytial¬viren (RSV) wurden in der 43. KW nicht nachgewiesen. Im stationären Bereich ist die Inzidenz schwerer akuter respiratorischer Infektionen (SARI) unter Berücksichtigung von erwarteten weiteren SARI-Diagnosen (Nowcasting) in der 43. KW 2026 gesunken und lag auf einem niedrigen Niveau. Es erhielten jeweils 2 % der SARI-Patientinnen und -Patienten eine Influenza- bzw. COVID-19-Diagnose und weniger als 1 % eine RSV-Diagnose. In der virologischen SARI-Surveillance des NRZ für Influenzaviren wurden in der 43. KW 2026 hauptsächlich Rhino-/Enteroviren nachgewiesen. Die Zahl der an das RKI gemäß IfSG übermittelten Fälle mit Influenzavirusinfektion ist in der 43. Meldewoche (MW) 2026 im Vergleich zur 42. MW leicht zurückgegangen. Die COVID-19-Fallzahlen sind im Vergleich zur Vorwoche leicht angestiegen. Die Zahl der RSV-Infektionen blieb in der 43. MW weiterhin niedrig. Die rekombinante SARS-CoV-2-Variante XFG wurde in der 41. KW 2026 mit 13 Nachweisen weiterhin am häufigsten unter den zirkulierenden SARS-CoV-2-Linien detektiert. Die im Abwasser gemessene SARS-CoV-2-Last ist weiterhin niedrig, zeigte jedoch seit einigen Wochen einen ansteigenden Trend. Auch bei den Influenzaviren zeigte sich ein leichter Anstieg. Die RSV-Last im Abwasser ist weiter niedrig.

title: Professional development for primary science teachers: a systematic literature review of international and Chinese research
abstract: This study systematically reviews professional development for primary science teachers, emphasizing digital competencies and science, technology, engineering and mathematics or STEM-oriented instruction. There were 30 peer-reviewed studies published between 2020 and 2024 analyzed from Scopus and China National Knowledge Infrastructure (CNKI) databases, integrating international and Chinese perspectives. Quality assessment considered research design, instrument validity, data transparency, and alignment between findings and conclusions. The review identifies four professional development orientations: system-driven, innovation-driven, sustainability-oriented, and capacity-building. Chinese programs are largely centralized and policy-aligned, whereas international programs emphasize teacher autonomy, collaborative innovation, and long-term sustainability. The COVID-19 pandemic accelerated online and blended professional development adoption, revealing both opportunities for digital competency development and inequities in access. Findings contribute a cross-cultural synthesis of professional development structures, strategies, and outcomes for primary science teachers. Implications include designing scalable, equitable, and context-sensitive professional development programs, particularly in resource-limited settings such as rural China and developing countries. Future research should focus on longitudinal evaluation, cross-cultural comparisons, and rigorous assessment of digital competency integration to enhance teacher professional learning and inform policy and practice globally.

title: PatHoST: weakly supervised reconstruction of pathogen spatial distributions from host transcriptomes
abstract: Dual host-pathogen spatial transcriptomics enables spatially resolved investigation of infection, yet the completeness of pathogen detection remains poorly characterized. Here, we generated pathogen-only spatial transcriptomic sections from a chronic Mycobacterium abscessus lung infection model to experimentally benchmark pathogen detection, revealing substantially increased pathogen transcript recovery compared with conventional dual profiling. Building on these data, we developed PatHoST, a weakly supervised computational framework that uses pathogen-derived information to generate silver-standard labels and learns host transcriptional programs predictive of pathogen presence. PatHoST reconstructed pathogen spatial distributions across independent tissue sections and enabled the identification of localized host regulatory programs beyond conventional cluster-based analyses. Application to human SARS-CoV-2 lung spatial transcriptomics supported generalization across host species and pathogen classes. Together, PatHoST combines purpose-built experimental benchmarking with weakly supervised inference to recover latent pathogen information and extend the analytical capabilities of dual host-pathogen spatial transcriptomics.

title: Artificial Intelligence for Intelligent and Privacy-Preserving Healthcare: A Survey of Medical Image Analysis, Multimodal Diagnosis, Semi-Supervised Learning, and Personalized Healthcare Systems
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly embedded in healthcare, from image-based diagnosis to patient-facing management tools, yet the supporting literature is fragmented across communities that rarely read one another. Motivated by the need for a coherent view, this survey examines four recent peer-reviewed studies that together span multimodal COVID-19 diagnosis, privacy-preserving learning on encrypted medical images, graph-refined semi-supervised pathology classification, and an AI-enabled mobile application for personalized healthcare management and doctor recommendation. Using a structured narrative methodology, the reviewed studies are classified into a five-category taxonomy, compared along technical dimensions, healthcare capabilities, and reported limitations, and synthesized into a layered view that treats imaging, multimodal fusion, privacy preservation, label-efficient learning, and personalization as complementary layers of intelligent healthcare rather than independent technologies. The synthesis indicates that each study advances one layer under its own experimental setting, and that none addresses privacy, label efficiency, multimodality, explainability, and clinical validation together. Recurring gaps include limited clinical validation, dataset constraints, unquantified generalization across institutions, privacy–performance trade-offs, and inconsistent evaluation protocols that prevent direct numerical comparison. Future directions include privacy-preserving multimodal learning, reduced reliance on annotations, explainable and robust models, integration of imaging with clinical records, and multi-site clinical validation. This review is not exhaustive, and no new experiments are presented.

source_records.title: Artificial Intelligence for Intelligent and Privacy-Preserving Healthcare: A Survey of Medical Image Analysis, Multimodal Diagnosis, Semi-Supervised Learning, and Personalized Healthcare Systems
source_records.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly embedded in healthcare, from image-based diagnosis to patient-facing management tools, yet the supporting literature is fragmented across communities that rarely read one another. Motivated by the need for a coherent view, this survey examines four recent peer-reviewed studies that together span multimodal COVID-19 diagnosis, privacy-preserving learning on encrypted medical images, graph-refined semi-supervised pathology classification, and an AI-enabled mobile application for personalized healthcare management and doctor recommendation. Using a structured narrative methodology, the reviewed studies are classified into a five-category taxonomy, compared along technical dimensions, healthcare capabilities, and reported limitations, and synthesized into a layered view that treats imaging, multimodal fusion, privacy preservation, label-efficient learning, and personalization as complementary layers of intelligent healthcare rather than independent technologies. The synthesis indicates that each study advances one layer under its own experimental setting, and that none addresses privacy, label efficiency, multimodality, explainability, and clinical validation together. Recurring gaps include limited clinical validation, dataset constraints, unquantified generalization across institutions, privacy–performance trade-offs, and inconsistent evaluation protocols that prevent direct numerical comparison. Future directions include privacy-preserving multimodal learning, reduced reliance on annotations, explainable and robust models, integration of imaging with clinical records, and multi-site clinical validation. This review is not exhaustive, and no new experiments are presented.

title: Standardized Annotation of Quantitative Proteomics Datasets Using SDRF-Proteomics.
abstract: Proteomics datasets require detailed and standardized metadata annotation to ensure reproducibility, reusability, and alignment with FAIR (Findable, Accessible, Interoperable, Reusable) principles. This chapter presents a practical, hands-on workflow for annotating a label-free proteomics dataset using the Sample and Data Relationship Format for Proteomics (SDRF-Proteomics), a HUPO-PSI and EuBIC-MS standard that has been adopted by major proteomics data repositories. We demonstrate the process on a COVID-19 nasal-swab dataset (PXD020394), showing how to derive sample and assay metadata from the study files, encode them in SDRF with the lesSDRF web application, and validate the result. Although the worked example is label-free, the approach can be generalized to other quantification strategies.

title: Engineering probiotics for mucosal vaccination: from the Escherichia coli Nissle 1917 paradigm to a translational vaccine platform
abstract: Mucosal vaccination is attracting renewed interest because many clinically relevant pathogens first encounter the host at gastrointestinal or respiratory surfaces, whereas most established vaccines are administered parenterally and are optimized primarily to induce systemic immunity. Engineered probiotics are emerging as living antigen-delivery vectors that may combine mucosal delivery, transient biological persistence, microbial immune signals, and programmable antigen presentation within a single platform. This strategy is particularly relevant to gastrointestinal vaccination, where access to gut-associated lymphoid tissue (GALT) may support local secretory IgA together with systemic responses. SARS-CoV-2 provides an informative experimental bridge because, despite its dominant respiratory manifestations, it can involve intestinal epithelial cells and gastrointestinal mucosal immunity. Using the pAIDA–Escherichia coli Nissle 1917 (EcN) system as a bounded proof of concept, this Perspective defines an integrated translational framework linking GALT-directed immune priming, effective mucosal antigen dose, genetic stability, chassis de-risking, biocontainment, manufacturing, potency, and post-administration clearance. We explicitly distinguish antigen delivery and immunogenicity from functional immunity, protection, and clinical efficacy, and identify the experiments required to advance probiotic-vectored mucosal vaccines toward clinically testable products.

title: Staying at Home or Getting Together? Hurricane Evacuation Compliance and Policy Tools Under Public Health Risk
abstract: The COVID‐19 pandemic introduced a distinctive challenge for crisis management during hurricane evacuations. In this dual‐risk context, emergency officials confronted competing imperatives: mandatory evacuation orders called for population movement, while public health guidance emphasized minimizing social contact and maintaining physical distance. These overlapping risks complicated residents' decision environments, particularly given longstanding evidence that evacuation behavior is often marked by bounded rationality under uncertainty and time pressure. Drawing on unique survey data collected in Florida during the 2020 Atlantic hurricane season, this study examines how perceptions of policy tools moderate the influence of property‐related concern on intentions to comply with mandatory evacuation orders. The analysis focuses on two tools relevant to shelter decision‐making: contracted shelter options and crowd‐sourced shelter recommendations. The findings suggest that the influence of the concerns about protecting their property can be lower among residents who prefers crowd‐sourced shelter recommendations. By locating the influence of policy tools on evacuation decision‐making within a compound emergency, this study extends crisis management scholarship on compliance under overlapping hazards. It also contributes to research on crisis governance by showing that information‐oriented policy tools are closely tied to how target populations interpret and respond to competing risk signals during disasters.
journal: Journal of Contingencies and Crisis Management

title: From Systemic Infection to Central Nervous System Pathology: Virus-Induced Neuroinflammatory Cascades and Blood–Brain Barrier Disruption
abstract: Background: Viral infections are recognized triggers of neurological disease through immune-mediated mechanisms that induce acute and chronic neuroinflammation. Although the central nervous system (CNS) is protected by the blood–brain barrier (BBB), several pathogens can access the CNS through mechanisms including leukocyte-mediated “Trojan Horse” entry, endothelial transcytosis, and neuronal transport. Neuropathology frequently seems to be primarily caused by dysregulated host immune responses that activate glial cells and compromise the integrity of the blood–brain barrier. Main Body: This mini-review summarizes current evidence linking BBB dysfunction to sustained neuroinflammatory cascades, emphasizing microglia–astrocyte interactions and downstream neuronal injury, including synaptic dysfunction and neurodegenerative changes. Using Epstein–Barr virus (EBV), human immunodeficiency virus (HIV), and severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) as representative examples, we discuss mechanisms of CNS entry, BBB disruption, microglial activation, astrocyte dysfunction, and excitotoxic neuronal injury. We further examine factors governing the transition from protective immune responses to persistent neuroinflammation, including viral latency, chronic immune activation, and microglial priming. Finally, we highlight recent advances in systems biology and systems bioinformatics that enable integration of multi-omics and network-level data to identify conserved pathways underlying virus-associated neurological disease and post-viral syndromes. Conclusions: BBB disruption represents a critical interface linking viral infection to CNS pathology. Convergent inflammatory mechanisms involving glial activation and impaired neurological and immune regulation contribute to persistent neurological dysfunction across diverse viral infections. Integrative systems-level approaches can assist in investigating these mechanisms, while they may also facilitate the identification of biomarkers and therapeutic targets capable of distinguishing resolving from persistent neuroinflammatory states.

title: Microbead-Based Heterodimer Assay for Amplification-Free Detection of Single-Stranded DNA
abstract: Direct detection of rare nucleic-acid targets without molecular amplification requires specific recognition events to be made observable while remaining distinguishable from nonspecific interactions. Here, we introduce a microbead-based heterodimer assay (MBHA) that converts two-site recognition of single-stranded DNA into spatially resolved, two-color bead-pairing events for direct nucleic acid detection. Two spectrally distinct microbead populations are functionalized with partially double-stranded DNA probes exposing target-binding domains complementary to separate regions of the target. Target-mediated bridging produces heterotypic bead pairs that are classified by fluorescence identity and an interparticle-distance criterion, while residual background is evaluated relative to blank measurements. Under the tested conditions, 166 fM was the lowest target concentration exceeding the blank-derived detection threshold. A sequence-scrambled synthetic non-target DNA remained below threshold across the tested concentration range, and detection at 166 fM was retained in the presence of 1 uM non-target DNA, corresponding to an approximately six-million-fold molar excess. Probe redesign further extended the assay to a second 60-nucleotide synthetic DNA target derived from the SARS-CoV-2 ORF1ab sequence. This proof-of-concept study establishes heterodimer counting as an amplification-free measurement strategy in which rare molecular-recognition events are made directly observable and individually classifiable without increasing target copy number.

title: A New Outlook on Infection-Associated Chronic Conditions and Illnesses
abstract: Infection-associated chronic conditions and illnesses (IACCI) encompass several debilitating syndromes with overlapping symptoms that have been identified and documented for decades, primarily following infectious disease outbreaks. Conditions following infection that are diagnosed with objective clinical tests have been relatively well characterized and accepted by the medical establishment, although the relationship to infection can be challenging to establish. In contrast, syndromes that lack objective tests, even when following a recognized infection, such as myalgic encephalomyelitis/chronic fatigue syndrome (ME/CFS), post-treatment Lyme disease syndrome, and dysautonomia, are underrecognized and often stigmatized. The COVID-19 pandemic and subsequent recognition of Long COVID as the newest example of IACCI offers new opportunities to address all aspects of IACCI. Lessons learned from the government’s multi-agency public health response to Long COVID could be beneficial to ensure readiness for the long-term consequences of sporadic infections, outbreaks, and future pandemics.

title: Multi-Line Recognition and Quantitative Assessment of Strip-Type Biosensors Using an Automated Image Processing Algorithm
abstract: Abstract Lateral flow assays (LFAs) are widely used point-of-care (POC) diagnostics, valued for their portability, simplicity, and rapid results. However, their conventional visual readout limits quantitative analysis and can lead to subjective interpretation and false results. In this work, we present, a novel, Python-based, automated image processing algorithm for the qualitative and quantitative analysis of multi-line LFAs capable of simultaneously detecting multiple analytes. Two multiplex formats were developed: a 4plex LFA for pathogens ( Escherichia coli (EC), Streptococcus pneumoniae (SP), Haemophilus influenzae (HI), and severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2)) and a 3plex LFA for microRNAs (miR-21, miR-let-7a, and miR-155). The developed algorithm processes captured images in five stages—strip case detection, region-of-interest extraction, line segmentation, boundary detection, and density quantification—yielding both qualitative classification and quantitative analyte concentration. Performance evaluation demonstrated high specificity, no cross-reactivity, and very good quantitative accuracy compared to ImageJ-based analysis. The classification metrics of the algorithm for both multi-line LFAs provided excellent sensitivity, specificity, and overall accuracy. This integrated approach overcomes the limitations of conventional LFA interpretation, offering low-cost, portable, and scalable multi-analyte diagnostics suitable for POC applications in healthcare, food and environmental monitoring, and resource-limited settings. The platform also enables future integration with artificial intelligence (AI)-driven analytics and cloud-based remote health monitoring, supporting rapid, decentralized diagnostic capabilities.

title: A novel predictive tool for pulmonary aspergillosis in critically ill patients with viral pneumonia: a multi-center, ambispective cohort study
abstract: Background Viral pneumonia-associated pulmonary aspergillosis (VAPA) is a lethal complication in critically ill patients. We aimed to develop a generalizable and methodologically robust prediction tool for early VAPA risk, overcoming key limitations of existing models. Methods In a multi-center, ambispective cohort of 4,966 patients with influenza or COVID-19 admitted to ICU (Jan 2023–Jun 2025), we developed and validated two prediction models for VAPA using LASSO-selected variables: a standard Cox proportional hazards model and a Fine-Gray subdistribution hazards model accounting for non-VAPA death as a competing risk. For both models, restricted cubic splines were used to address nonlinear associations between continuous predictors and VAPA. Performance was assessed at 7 and 14 days post-ICU admission. Subgroup analysis was employed to examine the virus-specific models’ performance. Results The incidence of VAPA was 8.8%. The Fine-Gray model demonstrated excellent discrimination and calibration in both derivation and validation cohorts. In contrast, the standard Cox model substantially overestimated VAPA risk, particularly among high-risk patients (by 20-30%). Key predictors included haematological malignancy, halo sign, use of priority antibiotic combinations, SOFA score, neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR), and pre-ICU corticosteroid dose; the latter three exhibited J-shaped associations with VAPA risk. A significant interaction was observed between viral subtype and pre-ICU corticosteroid dose ( P = 0.006), with a stronger association in COVID-19 patients (sHR=1.17, 95% CI: 1.09-1.26). Overall model performance remained consistent across viral subtypes. An interactive web-based tool was then deployed, which generates both individualized VAPA risk estimates and corresponding clinical management recommendations. Conclusions In critically ill patients with viral pneumonia, a competing-risk model accounting for non-VAPA death provides more accurate estimates of VAPA risk than traditional approaches. The model demonstrates robust generalizability across influenza and COVID-19 pneumonia and offers a practical tool for early, personalized VAPA prediction.
journal: Frontiers in Cellular and Infection Microbiology

title: Hybrid architectures of CNN-ViT and SE-CNN with grad-CAM for monkeypox disease detection
abstract: In the aftermath of the coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) pandemic, the monkeypox virus (MPV) emerged as a significant global health concern, leading the World Health Organization (WHO) to declare it a public health emergency. Accurate detection of monkeypox (Mpox) is challenging due to its similarity to other pox viruses such as measles and chickenpox. Conventional diagnostic methods often struggle to distinguish between these diseases, necessitating the development of more advanced diagnostic tools. These models are employed for the classification of medical images into two categories: Monkeypox and Others. The proposed models are applied to a dataset of 1140 images, and utilize fine-tuning for the models’ hyperparameters. Data augmentation techniques are implemented for training images to maximize the models’ performance. Additionally, a gradient-weighted class activation mapping (Grad-CAM) visualization technique is applied to explain the decision of the models and aid doctors in clinical decision-making. Experimentally, the accuracy, error matrix, area under the receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve, Recall, F1-score, and Precision are used to measure the performance of the proposed models. The proposed models provide a rapid and accurate method to differentiate Mpox from other cases, offering a valuable tool for healthcare professionals in the screening and diagnosis of Mpox.

title: Detection of airborne virus particles using hyperspectral dark field microscopy and machine learning
abstract: Abstract The development of technologies that rapidly screen airborne respiratory viruses providing near real-time data is essential for swift assessment and response to potential outbreaks, ultimately protecting public health. However, many current technologies require laboratory settings, specialised equipment, and trained personnel, which limits their applicability for widespread and real-time monitoring. Implementing these systems can be cost-prohibitive and logistically complex, especially in low-resource settings, highlighting the need for easily deployable technologies. This paper presents a novel proof-of-concept technology for near-real-time screening of specific viral targets, employing a machine-learning-enhanced optical system to analyse hyperspectral scattering data from airborne virus particles. This approach enables non-destructive and label-free identification of specific morphological particle classes by using enhanced dark-field microscopy to capture unique spectral signatures of the captured targets, which are then classified by a machine-learning algorithm. We demonstrate the laboratory-validated potential of this technology for rapid screening of airborne viral proxies, including inactivated SARS-CoV-2 as a target, offering a promising preliminary screening approach for indoor anomaly detection and potential early warning indicators.

title: Identifying adverse event clusters and treatment effects in randomised trials using latent class analysis: an application in the COV-BOOST trial
abstract: Randomised controlled trials (RCTs) are essential for evaluating treatment efficacy and safety, particularly in vaccine trials, where adverse events are systematically collected and assessed. The high volume of reported adverse events often presents challenges in discerning meaningful associations between treatments and adverse events. Traditional analytical approaches rely on multiple pairwise treatment comparisons of individual adverse events, which can be difficult to interpret. This study explores the use of latent class analysis (LCA) to identify adverse event profiles and estimates the average treatment effects (ATE) for these in an RCT setting. Data from the COV-BOOST trial (ISRCTN registration 73765130), which assessed the safety and efficacy of seven COVID-19 booster vaccines, was used. This trial monitored a predefined set of 17 adverse events, graded by severity, over a 7-day period following immunisation. LCA was applied to classify participants into adverse event subgroups based on shared event profiles. After identifying these classes, the ATE was estimated for each identified adverse event profile to quantify the causal impact of different vaccine boosters. This was achieved by regressing treatment on the latent adverse event class membership outcome. Fatigue, pain, and headache were commonly reported adverse events across all vaccine arms. LCA identified three distinct adverse event profiles among participants: (class 1) minimal AEs, (class 2) mild AEs, and (class 3) severe AEs reports. Four vaccines, ChAd after BNT/BNT primer, Ad26, CVn, and MOD after both primer vaccines, were associated with higher reactogenicity, with most recipients falling into class 2 or 3. This study demonstrates the utility of LCA in identifying adverse event profiles within an RCT and uniquely integrates the latent adverse event class membership of participants as an outcome for ATE estimation. By examining the varying effects of booster vaccines in the COV-BOOST trial, this method advances the understanding of these vaccines’ safety. The successful application of this innovative approach in this study could pave the way for its adoption by researchers in future clinical trials across various medical domains. More broadly, integrating LCA with ATE estimation provides a novel framework for enhancing vaccine pharmacovigilance and improving safety assessments for medical interventions.

title: Changes over time and determinants of medical imaging devices utilization in Türkiye: A panel data analysis, 2013-2022
abstract: Objective: This study aims to examine the regional and temporal variations in the demand for medical imaging services in Türkiye during the 2013-2022 period and to empirically determine the macro-health, socio-demographic, infrastructural, and digital dynamics driving these changes using panel data analysis and analysis of variance methods.Methods: Utilizing data from the Turkish Statistical Institute and the Ministry of Health, a balanced panel dataset was constructed covering the Nomenclature of Territorial Units for Statistics (NUTS) Level-1 regions of Türkiye for the 2013-2022 period. Statistical analyses were conducted using STATA 14.2 software. One-Way Analysis of Variance (ANOVA) and Bonferroni post-hoc tests were applied to investigate the geographical asymmetries in imaging intensities. The most efficient estimator between fixed and random effects models was determined using the Hausman test. Results: Econometric analyses revealed that geriatric population dynamics dominantly drive Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) and Computed Tomography (CT) demand. Ultrasonografi (USG) functions as a routine physical examination extension, whereas Doppler requisitions confirm supplier-induced demand. Coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) induced sharp negative structural breaks in MRI, Echocardiography (ECHO), and mammography screenings due to suspended elective/prophylactic services, while chest CT utilization experienced an anomalous pandemic peak. NUTS-1 ANOVA proved that CT imaging is geographically homogeneous. Conversely, MRI, Doppler USG, ECHO, and mammography asymmetrically cluster in developed western metropolises, whereas USG concentrates in eastern and central regions due to prenatal/pediatric requirements.Conclusion: High-tech imaging demand in Türkiye has decoupled from physical supply, driven instead by defensive medicine reflexes; conversely, vital preventive services face structural and socio-cultural barriers. Rather than investing in redundant equipment, policymakers should establish legal safeguards against malpractice anxieties, promote digital health literacy, and deploy targeted mobile public health strategies to eliminate diagnostic access gaps in underserved regions.

title: Respiratory pathogens detected by multiplex PCR in Malaysian public hospitals: prevalence and epidemiologic patterns from January 2023 until July 2024.
abstract: Respiratory tract infections remain an important cause of hospitalisation and diagnostic uncertainty, and multiplex polymerase chain reaction testing offers rapid detection of multiple pathogens in routine clinical practice. We aimed to describe the prevalence, demographic associations, and temporal trends of respiratory pathogens detected by the QIAstat-Dx Respiratory SARS-CoV-2 Panel in Malaysian public hospitals. This multicentre retrospective cross-sectional study included nasopharyngeal swab samples from cases with suspected acute respiratory infections tested between 1 January 2023 and 31 July 2024. Data were collected from participating sites using standardised record forms and analysed. We assessed overall positivity, pathogen frequencies, age-group and regional distributions, and monthly and quarterly trends. A total of 8,361 samples were included, of which 5,252 (62.8%) had at least one pathogen detected. Single detections were identified in 4,279 samples (51.2%), while co-detections were observed in 973 samples (11.6%). Viral pathogens predominated. Rhinovirus/enterovirus was the most frequently detected pathogen (23.8%), followed by respiratory syncytial virus A/B (13.7%) and influenza A H1N1/2009 (4.8%). Positivity was highest among children aged 1 to 4 years and infants aged 1 to 11 months, and age-related variation was more pronounced than regional variation. The leading pathogens also demonstrated distinct temporal profiles, with different peak months across the study period. In conclusion, respiratory pathogen detection in this hospital-based population was characterised by a high positivity rate, predominance of viral pathogens, marked age-related differences, and distinct temporal patterns. These findings support the value of multiplex PCR for respiratory pathogen surveillance in Malaysian public hospitals.

title: CRISPR/Cas12-powered electrochemical biosensor for chikungunya virus DNA detection using gold-modified screen-printed carbon electrodes
abstract: Background and purpose: Chikungunya virus (CHIKV) remains a health concern because its symptoms overlap with dengue and Zika, often leading to misdiagnosis. Conventional diagnostic methods, including viral isolation, enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA) and reverse transcription-polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR), are time-consuming, costly, and dependent on specialized laboratories. This study aimed to develop a rapid, selective, and sensitive electrochemical biosensor integrated with CRISPR/Cas12 for CHIKV DNA detection. Experimental approach: A CHIKV-specific guide RNA targeting a conserved region of the E1 gene was designed in silico and selected by specificity score (99.15) and E-value (1.7). The platform used a gold particle-modified screen-printed carbon electrode (SPCE/Au) functionalized with a ferrocene-labelled DNA reporter. The electrode was characterized electrochemically, and the biosensor was tested for its response to CHIKV DNA, its selectivity against dengue virus (DENV) and SARS-CoV-2, and its detection performance across target concentrations. Key results: Au deposition enhanced the electrochemical properties of the electrode. Recognition of CHIKV DNA activated the CRISPR/Cas12 complex, whose collateral cleavage of the reporter reduced the ferrocene oxidation signal. The biosensor exhibited a concentration-dependent response over 0.01 to 10 ppb, with a limit of detection of 0.92 ppb and a limit of quantification of 2.77 ppb. The biosensor showed excellent selectivity against CHIKV competitors. Conclusion: This work shows that combining CRISPR/Cas12 collateral cleavage with a ferrocene-labelled reporter on SPCE/Au enables rapid, selective, and sensitive CHIKV detection. Validation with clinical samples is still needed. The platform supports early diagnosis and disease surveillance, in line with Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) 3 (Good Health and Well-being).

title: An ecological study of trends in medical and surgical hospital admissions in Tuscany over 25 years
abstract: Since 1995, hospital admissions in Italy have been classified using diagnosis-related groups (DRGs). Hospital discharge records provide a valuable basis for reconstructing long-term trends in hospital activity and examining these patterns in the context of organizational reforms and the COVID-19 pandemic. We conducted a retrospective ecological study using Tuscany regional healthcare administrative data to examine trends in hospital admissions from 1999 to 2024 and compare them with national Italian trends. Admissions were classified as medical or surgical, and analyzed by care setting, length of stay, age, and case-mix index (CMI). Ordinary and day-case hospitalization rates in Tuscany decreased by 35.8% and 23.1%, respectively. Medical hospitalization rates fell by 47.5%, while outpatient chemotherapy surged by 233.6% (2014–2024). Medical CMI rose from 0.5 to 0.8, and mean patient age reached 66.9 years. Surgical hospitalization rates fluctuated but returned to near-baseline levels, while outpatient surgery increased markedly. Ordinary surgical LOS decreased by 1.3 days, while surgical CMI increased from 0.9 to 1.5. An observed divergence from national trends occurred in 2009, coinciding with regional reforms. Over 25 years, hospital care in Tuscany shifted toward lower medical inpatient and day-case volumes, greater use of outpatient services, and shorter surgical stays. These trends occurred in the context of organizational reform, demographic aging, and administrative reclassifications. Findings reflect a progressive concentration of hospital resources on older patients with higher case-mix complexity. Causal interpretations should remain cautious because the analysis centers on aggregated routinely collected data.
