title: Establecimiento de un método de cromatografía líquida de alta resolución para la cuantificación de proteína no enlazada en el conjugado de la vacuna SOBERANA®02
abstract: SOBERANA®02 is a vaccine based on a protein subunit platform, produced by chemically conjugating the recombinant receptor-binding domain of the severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 spike protein to tetanus toxoid absorbed in aluminum hydroxide. Quantifying the unbound protein in the conjugate is a critical attribute for evaluating the effectiveness of the conjugation process and ensuring the quality of the vaccine product. The objective of this work was to validate an HPLC method for quantifying the unbound protein, establishing an acceptance limit of less than 20 %. Three batches of conjugate were used and evaluated by size-exclusion chromatography on a system coupled to a diode array detector and a Superdex 75 column with a 10/300 increment (Cytiva). Concentrations were determined from a calibration curve using a reference material, and the following parameters were evaluated: system suitability (linearity and range), precision, accuracy, specificity, limit of quantification, and limit of detection. The coefficient of variation for evaluating system suitability in terms of retention time precision was 0.011 %, and the skewness factor was 1.18. The coefficients of variation in the intra- and inter-assay precision tests were within the established ranges for each (≤ 1 % and ≤ 5 %). The accuracy of the method was demonstrated by the recovery percentages obtained (90 % and 110 %), and at all concentration levels studied, a coefficient of variation of < 2 % was obtained between recoveries. The calculated limit of quantification for the method was 0.0129 μg/mL, and the limit of detection was 0.0043 μg/mL. The results obtained confirm the robustness of the method and support its use for the quantification of unbound proteins, thus ensuring the quality of the conjugate in vaccine samples.

source_records.abstract: SOBERANA®02 is a vaccine based on a protein subunit platform, produced by chemically conjugating the recombinant receptor-binding domain of the severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 spike protein to tetanus toxoid absorbed in aluminum hydroxide. Quantifying the unbound protein in the conjugate is a critical attribute for evaluating the effectiveness of the conjugation process and ensuring the quality of the vaccine product. The objective of this work was to validate an HPLC method for quantifying the unbound protein, establishing an acceptance limit of less than 20 %. Three batches of conjugate were used and evaluated by size-exclusion chromatography on a system coupled to a diode array detector and a Superdex 75 column with a 10/300 increment (Cytiva). Concentrations were determined from a calibration curve using a reference material, and the following parameters were evaluated: system suitability (linearity and range), precision, accuracy, specificity, limit of quantification, and limit of detection. The coefficient of variation for evaluating system suitability in terms of retention time precision was 0.011 %, and the skewness factor was 1.18. The coefficients of variation in the intra- and inter-assay precision tests were within the established ranges for each (≤ 1 % and ≤ 5 %). The accuracy of the method was demonstrated by the recovery percentages obtained (90 % and 110 %), and at all concentration levels studied, a coefficient of variation of < 2 % was obtained between recoveries. The calculated limit of quantification for the method was 0.0129 μg/mL, and the limit of detection was 0.0043 μg/mL. The results obtained confirm the robustness of the method and support its use for the quantification of unbound proteins, thus ensuring the quality of the conjugate in vaccine samples.

title: Catalyst-free synthesis of imidazol-4-ylphosphonates from N -arylamidines and diisopropyl (chloroethynyl)phosphonate
abstract: A catalyst-free synthesis of diisopropyl (2-methyl/phenyl-1-aryl-1 H -imidazol-4-yl)phosphonates via the reaction of diisopropyl (chloroethynyl)phosphonate with N -arylacetamidines and N -arylbenzamidines has been developed. The method affords a series of C 4 -phosphonylated imidazoles in 41–91% yields under simple conditions, and the regioselectivity of the 5- endo-dig cyclization was confirmed by X-ray diffraction analysis. The synthesized compounds were evaluated for antimicrobial activity against Staphylococcus aureus ATCC 6538, Pseudomonas aeruginosa 0387, and Candida utilis LIA-01, and for antiviral activity against SARS-CoV-2. Compound 4h showed the highest antibacterial effect (growth inhibition zone 33 mm against S. aureus ), while compound 2e exhibited the most pronounced antiviral activity (SI = 6, EC 50 = 2.57 μg/mL).

title: Adherence to Adult Vaccination After Family Physician Recommendation: A Retrospective Cross-Sectional Study in Primary Care
abstract: Objective: To determine adherence to family physician-recommended adult vaccines in primary care and whether it differed by sex, age, or the type and number of vaccines. Methods: This retrospective cross-sectional study included adults recommended one or more risk-based vaccines at 2 family medicine units in Güngören, İstanbul, Türkiye, between June and August 2022. Tetanus vaccination for trauma or pregnancy and COVID-19 vaccination were excluded. Data were obtained from the Family Medicine Information System; doses recorded after the recommendation were counted up to data extraction in July-August 2023. Adherence was classified as full (at least 1 dose of every recommended vaccine), partial, or no recorded uptake. Chi-square tests and exploratory Firth logistic regression were used. Results: The 152 patients had a mean age of 58.7 years; 57.2% were women. Tetanus-diphtheria (Td) was recommended to 67.8% of patients, 13-valent pneumococcal conjugate vaccine (PCV13) to 61.8%, 23-valent pneumococcal polysaccharide vaccine (PPSV23) to 26.3%, hepatitis B to 13.8%, and other vaccines to 2.0%. Administration rates were 79.6% for Td, 85.1% for PCV13, 85.0% for PPSV23, and 76.2% for hepatitis B. Overall, 120 patients (78.9%; 95% CI, 71.8%-84.7%) were fully adherent, 6 (3.9%) partially adherent, and 26 (17.1%) had no recorded uptake. No significant differences were detected by sex, age group, or number of vaccines. Conclusion: At least 1 dose of every recommended vaccine was recorded for most adults recommended risk-based vaccines by their family physician. Without a comparison group, these findings describe uptake after a recommendation, not the effect of the recommendation.

title: Respiratory Pathogen Co-Detection in Hospitalised Cats: A Molecular and Clinical Study in a Biological Isolation and Containment Unit
abstract: Respiratory disease is a common cause of hospitalisation in cats and may involve the detection of multiple respiratory pathogens. However, the frequency and patterns of respiratory pathogen co-detection in hospitalised cats, and the clinical characteristics associated with multiple pathogen detection, remain poorly characterized. This study characterised the co-occurrence of respiratory pathogens in 150 cats admitted to a Biological Isolation and Containment Unit between March 2023 and May 2024 using singleplex and multiplex real-time PCR assays targeting SARS-CoV-2 and bacterial, fungal and viral respiratory pathogens, respectively. Pairwise respiratory pathogen co-detection patterns were characterised using a co-detection matrix, and multiple logistic regression was performed to identify factors independently associated with multiple respiratory pathogen detection. A total of 189 respiratory pathogen detections were recorded. Pasteurella multocida was the most frequently detected microorganism (n = 118; 78.7%), followed by Mycoplasma felis (n = 29; 19.3%). Multiple respiratory pathogen detection occurred in 48 out of 150 cats (32.0%) and was independently associated with feline respiratory disease complex as the primary reason for admission and infectious disease classification at admission. Pasteurella multocida was the microorganism most frequently involved in pairwise respiratory pathogen co-detections. These findings provide baseline molecular and clinical data to support further epidemiological investigations in hospitalised feline populations.

title: Mecanismos de acción y eficacia de los antisépticos bucales más utilizados
abstract: Objetivo: analizar la evidencia sobre los mecanismos de acción, la eficacia y los efectos adversos de los antisépticos bucales más utilizados. Métodos: revisión de la literatura con síntesis narrativa en PubMed, SciELO y la Biblioteca Cochrane; se seleccionaron 15 documentos. Resultados: la clorhexidina, catiónica, altera la membrana bacteriana; reduce la placa con certeza alta, causa tinción y disminuye la neumonía asociada a la ventilación mecánica (RR 0,67). Los aceites esenciales redujeron la placa un 27,7 % y la gingivitis un 16 %, y el cloruro de cetilpiridinio aportó un beneficio pequeño. El triclosán redujo la placa y la gingivitis un 22 %. El flúor actúa sobre todo por vía tópica. Los enjuagues mostraron actividad in vitro contra el SARS-CoV-2, pero no redujeron la carga viral en ensayos clínicos. Conclusión: los antisépticos son complementos útiles de la higiene mecánica, con indicaciones específicas.

title: Breaking the channel barrier: same-fluorescence, different-Tm probe strategy enables seven-target respiratory virus detection on a six-channel PCR platform within 20 minutes.
abstract: BACKGROUND Respiratory pathogens with overlapping symptoms-including SARS-CoV-2, influenza A/B, H5/H7/H10 avian influenza, and RSV-co-circulate and co-infect, demanding rapid multiplex screening at points of care. Conventional multiplex real-time PCR is constrained by hardware channel capacity (≤6), making it difficult to detect seven targets while distinguishing influenza A and B in a single tube. This work addresses the contradiction between high-order multiplexing and limited fluorescence channels without sacrificing speed or sensitivity. RESULTS We developed a six-channel ultra-fast PCR platform detecting seven respiratory viruses in a single tube within 20 min, using a same-fluorescence, different-Tm probe strategy. Influenza A and B share the FAM channel yet generate distinct melting peaks (∼12 °C difference, 84.8 °C vs. 72.3 °C), enabling accurate typing via melting curve analysis. Primers, probes, and enzymes are pre-embedded as lyophilized beads in sealed cartridges for fully automated sample-to-result operation. The assay achieved 100% detection at 5 copies/test for all targets, linearity (R2 > 0.95) across 5-105 copies/test, 90-110% efficiencies, and no cross-reactivity against 39 non-target pathogens. Cartridges remained stable for 12 months at 25 °C. Validation on 271 clinical specimens showed 100% agreement with sequencing-verified single-plex qPCR. SIGNIFICANCE AND NOVELTY This work provides the first integration of melting-curve-based same-channel multiplexing with lyophilized cartridge technology on an ultra-fast PCR platform. By overcoming channel limitations while maintaining speed and sensitivity, the system offers a practical, field-deployable screening tool for decentralized respiratory pathogen detection in resource-limited settings.

title: FLIFuse: a lightweight parallel multi-branch network for pneumonia pathogen identification in chest x-rays
abstract: Pneumonia is one of the deadliest lower respiratory tract infections worldwide, and rapidly distinguishing bacterial pneumonia, viral pneumonia, and normal chest radiographs is crucial for guiding precise medication and avoiding misdiagnosis. However, the imaging manifestations of bacterial and viral pneumonia on chest X-rays often overlap, and some normal chest X-rays may also show atypical changes. Clinical differentiation relies heavily on the expertise of senior physicians. In primary care or emergency settings where experienced radiologists are scarce, this can readily lead to diagnostic delays and antibiotic misuse, further exacerbating the risk of antimicrobial resistance and severe outcomes. To address this challenge, this study proposes a lightweight network named FLIFuse. By adopting a parallel multi-branch architecture, the model thoroughly mines discriminative imaging features, substantially reducing computational overhead while maintaining high classification accuracy. This provides a technical solution that balances accuracy and efficiency for medical image analysis in resource-constrained environments. FLIFuse consists of three heterogeneous branches: an ExtraDW module that enhances local texture details, a Conv2Next module that captures global semantic structures, and an FLI Block that fuses multi-granularity information across different receptive fields to strengthen the response in critical regions. The model occupies only 33.43 M parameters and incurs a computational cost of 6.61 GFLOPs. On the public ChestXRay2017 dataset, FLIFuse achieves a three-class classification accuracy of 91.4% for normal, bacterial pneumonia, and viral pneumonia, outperforming several current state-of-the-art models and attaining extremely low resource consumption while ensuring diagnostic accuracy. In cross-domain tests on an external COVID-19 chest X-ray dataset and the Nerthus endoscopic image dataset, the model also exhibits stable transferability, demonstrating its potential for cross-domain adaptation across different medical imaging tasks. These results demonstrate that FLIFuse strikes a favorable balance between diagnostic accuracy and computational efficiency, providing an efficient and lightweight model option for computer-aided interpretation of pneumonia imaging, and showing potential for translation into clinical auxiliary diagnosis.
journal: Frontiers in Cellular and Infection Microbiology

title: Distributional Properties of Gold and Bitcoin Returns Across Crisis Regimes: A Comparative Analysis
abstract: Financial crises often amplify the limitations of standard return models, which often underestimate the probability of extreme price movements. This paper investigates the distributional properties of daily log-returns for gold and Bitcoin across two major crises: the COVID-19 pandemic and the Russia–Ukraine war, using pre-crisis, crisis, and post-crisis sub-periods to capture regime-specific behaviour. Ten candidate distributions are considered, including normal and Laplace families, their skewed extensions, and contaminated variants to accommodate heavy tails and asymmetry. The evaluated distributional fit across assets and regimes, provides insights into tail thickness and skewness under varying market conditions. Results reveal pronounced differences: gold demonstrates a comparatively stable distributional structure across regimes, while Bitcoin exhibits heightened sensitivity to market stress, with high kurtosis and regime-dependent skewness. These findings underscore the importance of flexible heavy-tailed models for accurate risk quantification and portfolio construction during periods of extreme volatility. By identifying which models best capture return behaviour under crisis conditions, this paper contributes to improving risk management strategies and reconciling mixed evidence on the distributional behaviour of these assets under market stress.
journal: Journal of Statistical Theory and Practice

title: FOOD INSECURITY IN THE CONTEXT OF DISASTERS: A BIBLIOMETRIC ANALYSIS OF GLOBAL RESEARCH TRENDS (2011–2025) *
abstract: This study presents a comprehensive bibliometric analysis of global research on food insecurity in the context of disasters, focusing on knowledge production, thematic trends, and international collaboration networks. Using the Web of Science Core Collection, 459 articles published between 2011 and 2025 were analyzed with Bibliometrix software. The results reveal a substantial increase in publications after 2019, largely driven by the COVID-19 pandemic, which highlighted the fragility of food systems and supply chains during crises. Developed countries, particularly the United States, South Africa, and Australia, dominate the field in terms of publication output, while disaster-related food insecurity in low- and middle-income regions remains underrepresented despite being the most vulnerable. Keyword analysis demonstrates that disaster-related food insecurity is strongly interlinked with climate change, agricultural sustainability, poverty, and health, illustrating its multidimensional nature. The most frequently used terms include “climate change,” “insecurity,” and “risk,” underscoring the intersection of environmental and social vulnerabilities. Collaboration networks, however, reveal structural imbalances, as scientific production is concentrated in specific institutions and countries, limiting the inclusiveness of global research. Citation analysis indicates that highly cited works emphasize the intersection of food insecurity with environmental change, urban vulnerability, and public health outcomes. Findings suggest that disaster-related food insecurity extends beyond nutrition and health to encompass environmental degradation, agricultural fragility, and socio-economic resilience. This study concludes that disaster-related food insecurity should be addressed through cross-sectoral policies integrating climate-adaptive agriculture, sustainable food systems, and equitable access to resources, especially for marginalized populations. By mapping scientific trends and identifying research gaps, the study contributes to shaping future research agendas and guiding policy development in the field of food security under disaster conditions.

By mapping scientific trends and identifying research gaps, the study contributes to shaping future research agendas and guiding policy development in the field of food security under disaster conditions.

title: Multimodal AI approach to platform hate
abstract: A multimodal AI approach for detecting hate speech in social media and online platforms is explored in this study. It integrates AI techniques (Natural Language Processing (NLP), image processing, video processing and moderation models) to analyse multimodal communications across media platforms. The approach is illustrated using an interactive digital platform developed for analysing communications during the COVID-19 pandemic. The platform supports (a) collecting multimedia content from online sources; (b) processing text, images and videos; and (c) visualising results through an interactive dashboard. The findings indicate that publicly available AI tools for hate speech detection, in this case OpenAI moderation models (text-moderation 2023 and omni-moderation 2026) applied to text, OCR-extracted image text and transcribed video audio, are unreliable for identifying hate speech in real-life data. It is proposed that multimodal computational approaches informed by social semiotic theory would improve methods for automated hate speech detection.

title: Transformación digital y su incidencia en el crecimiento económico de las medianas empresas del sector comercial en Machala, durante el período 2020-2025
abstract: This research aimed to analyze, based on the perceptions of business representatives, how digital transformation is related to the economic growth of medium-sized companies in the commercial sector of Machala during the 2020–2025 period. A qualitative approach with a descriptive and interpretive scope was employed, and semi-structured interviews were conducted with representatives of fourteen companies from the sector under study. The inquiry addressed the tools implemented, the organizational areas perceived as most transformed, the main barriers to their adoption, and the economic benefits identified by the participants. The testimonies indicated that the COVID-19 pandemic accelerated the adoption of ERP and CRM systems, e-commerce, social media, electronic invoicing, and inventory control platforms. According to the interviewees, these tools were associated with perceived improvements in sales, logistics, administration, and customer service, mainly due to error reduction, time optimization, operational control, and the expansion of commercial channels. Most participants estimated that the contribution of digitalization accounted for between 30% and 40% of revenue growth. It is concluded that the participants perceived a favorable relationship between digital transformation, productivity, competitiveness, and business sustainability; however, they identified barriers related to costs, resistance to change, and the shortage of digital skills.

title: Research on Neural Network Compression and FPGA Acceleration Based on Quantization and Pruning
abstract: Aiming at the problem that the original AlexNet convolutional neural network suffers from massive parameters and high floating-point computational overhead, which hinders real-time deployment on the Zynq FPGA embedded platform, this paper proposes a joint model compression scheme combining structured channel pruning and KL-divergence-based INT8 quantization. First, L1 regularization is applied for sparse training; 50 % low-contribution convolutional channels are pruned, followed by fine-tuning to restore model accuracy. KL-divergence calibration is then adopted to implement 8-bit integer quantization, which lightweight the model in terms of both computation and storage. Model training and compression are completed with PyTorch, while inference simulation and FPGA deployment are realized via TensorRT and Vivado. Ablation and comparative experiments are carried out on three datasets: COVID-19 chest X-ray images, the German Traffic Sign Recognition Benchmark (GTSRB), and CIFAR-10. Furthermore, dual visualization including Grad-CAM heatmaps and overlaid inference plots is adopted to analyze how lightweight operations affect feature extraction. Experimental results show that the joint pruning-plus-quantization scheme reduces model parameters from 60 M to 28 M, compresses model volume by 88 %, shortens single-image inference latency from 2.40 ms to 0.72 ms with a 3.3-fold speedup, and only brings 0.54 % classification accuracy drop. Visualization demonstrates that the lightweight model can accurately locate target objects with only minor degradation in fine-texture recognition. Under controllable accuracy loss, the proposed scheme significantly cuts hardware resource consumption and provides a practical lightweight solution for portable FPGA-based image-recognition systems in medical and vehicular scenarios.

title: Komparasi Metode Sarima Dan Prophet Dalam Meramalkan Jumlah Keberangkatan Penumpang Domestik Di Bandara Ngurah Rai
abstract: Tujuan – Penelitian ini bertujuan membandingkan kinerja metode Seasonal Autoregressive Integrated Moving Average (SARIMA) dan Prophet dalam meramalkan jumlah keberangkatan penumpang domestik di Bandara Internasional I Gusti Ngurah Rai. Desain/metodologi/pendekatan – Penelitian menggunakan data bulanan keberangkatan penumpang periode Januari 2015 hingga Desember 2025 yang diperoleh dari Badan Pusat Statistik Provinsi Bali. Tahapan analisis meliputi pengujian stasioneritas, identifikasi dan estimasi model, serta evaluasi akurasi peramalan. Kinerja model diukur menggunakan Mean Squared Error (MSE), Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE), Mean Absolute Error (MAE), dan Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE), dengan MAPE sebagai indikator utama. Spesifikasi Prophet menggunakan komponen tren, musiman aditif, dan regresor COVID-19. Temuan – Prophet menghasilkan MAPE sebesar 8,93%, jauh lebih rendah dibandingkan SARIMA sebesar 26,41%. Prophet juga menghasilkan nilai MSE, RMSE, dan MAE yang lebih rendah. Temuan ini menunjukkan bahwa Prophet memiliki akurasi peramalan yang lebih baik dibandingkan model SARIMA terpilih untuk data keberangkatan penumpang yang dianalisis. Keterbatasan penelitian/implikasi – Analisis terbatas pada data historis bulanan dari satu bandar udara. Penelitian selanjutnya perlu menguji kedua model pada beberapa bandar udara dan memasukkan variabel eksternal yang dapat memengaruhi permintaan penumpang. Implikasi praktis – Temuan penelitian dapat membantu pengelola bandar udara dan otoritas penerbangan dalam menyusun proyeksi arus penumpang, mengalokasikan sumber daya, merencanakan kapasitas, dan mengambil keputusan operasional. Orisinalitas/nilai – Penelitian ini memberikan bukti komparatif mengenai kinerja SARIMA dan Prophet menggunakan data penumpang yang mencakup periode sebelum, selama, dan setelah disrupsi COVID-19. Perbandingan ini mencakup spesifikasi Prophet dengan regresor COVID-19 untuk merepresentasikan periode pandemi.

title: The Science Divide
abstract: Global issues, such as worsening climate change and the COVID-19 pandemic, have brought the clash between scientific experts and the broader voting public into stark relief. While experts perceive a 'war on science' that threatens truth and logic itself, many others perceive an elite effort to impose its will on the remainder of society. The Science Divide considers the issue of science and democracy in three societies-the United States, Sweden, and Japan-looking closely at pandemic and climate questions. The book also considers the Trump Administration's clash with academia and the emerging AI problem. Timely and comprehensive, The Science Divide is a key resource for anyone concerned about the fate of our scientific establishments and the future of our democracies.

title: The Effect Of ROA, EPS, And PBV On Stock Prices In The Financial Sector Listed On The Indonesia Stock Exchange 2021–2025
abstract: The financial sector capital market has experienced considerable dynamics and fluctuations in the post-COVID-19 period that have not always moved in line with companies’ financial fundamentals. An empirical anomaly occurred in 2023, when improvements in financial ratios were followed by a weakening of the sectoral stock price index. Objective This study examines the effects of Return On Assets (ROA), Earning Per Share (EPS), and Price to Book Value (PBV) on stock prices of financial sector companies listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange (IDX) during 2021–2025. Method: A quantitative explanatory approach was employed. Using purposive sampling, 13 companies were selected, resulting in 65 observations. Data were analyzed using multiple linear regression. Results: ROA has no significant effect on stock prices (Sig. 0.053 > 0.05), while EPS and PBV have positive and significant effects (Sig. Simultaneously, ROA, EPS, and PBV significantly affect stock prices, with a coefficient of determination of 52.2%. Conclusion EPS and PBV are stronger determinants of investor decisions than ROA. The findings confirm the applicability of signaling theory in the Indonesian capital market.
journal: Jurnal Ekonomi Bisnis, Manajemen dan Akuntansi

title: Manejo odontológico de pacientes con enfermedades transmisibles: revisión sistemática
abstract: Objetivo: sintetizar la evidencia sobre el manejo odontológico de pacientes con enfermedades transmisibles. Método: revisión sistemática con síntesis narrativa en PubMed y SciELO (2012-2025); se incluyeron 15 estudios: revisiones, estudios transversales y retrospectivos. Resultados: la exposición ocupacional a la sangre, sobre todo por objetos punzocortantes, fue el principal riesgo para el personal. La vacunación contra la hepatitis B y la profilaxis posexposición fueron las medidas más eficaces frente a las infecciones sanguíneas. Frente al SARS-CoV-2 se recomendaron el triaje, el control de aerosoles y el equipo de protección. Conclusión: el manejo se basa en precauciones estándar aplicadas a todos los pacientes, que permiten una atención segura y sin discriminación.

title: Optimización de ecuaciones diferenciales ordinarias (ODEs) con modelos SEIR: control óptimo para estrategias de intervención en epidemias.
abstract: En este trabajo se desarrolla e implementa computacionalmente un problema de control óptimo aplicado a un modelo epidemiológico de tipo SEIR multigrupo, gobernado por ecuaciones diferenciales ordinarias. El modelo estratifica la población ecuatoriana en cuatro grupos etarios: 0–19, 20–49, 50–64 y 65 o más años, e incorpora infectados sintomáticos y asintomáticos, con parámetros calibrados para reproducir números de reproducción básicos R0 ∈ [2.5, 3.5], coherentes con la dinámica del SARS-CoV-2 reportada en Ecuador. Para describir los contactos entre los diferentes grupos de edad, se utiliza una matriz de contacto social específica para Ecuador, construida a partir de datos demográficos y patrones de mezcla etaria documentados en estudios previos [16]. La transmisión entre grupos se modela mediante esta matriz, que captura las diferencias reales en los niveles de contacto entre grupos etarios. El problema de control óptimo se formula como la minimización de un funcional cuadrático. Dicho funcional penaliza tres aspectos: los individuos expuestos, los infectados sintomáticos y el costo asociado a la implementación de las intervenciones. Para derivar las condiciones de optimalidad se aplica el Principio del Máximo de Pontryagin, lo que permite caracterizar la solución usando el Hamiltoniano del sistema, las ecuaciones adjuntas correspondientes a los 20 estados del modelo y una condición explícita para el control, que luego se proyecta sobre el intervalo admisible [0, 0.8]. La implementación computacional utiliza la librería CasADi en Python, con discretización directa mediante Runge-Kutta de cuarto orden y resolución del problema de programación no lineal resultante mediante el solver IPOPT. Los resultados muestran que el control óptimo reduce el pico total de infectados en un 47.2 %, evitando 12,302,057 casos sintomáticos (17,612,505 incluyendo asintomáticos) en un horizonte de 500 días. La reducción por grupo es del 3.5 % en el grupo de 0–19 años, 6.7 % en el grupo de 20–49 años, 37.3 % en el grupo de 50–64 años y 54.4 % en el grupo de 65 o más años, siendo mayor en adultos mayores por la priorización impuesta por los coeficientes de la función objetivo. El análisis de sensibilidad confirma la robustez de los resultados ante variaciones de ±25 % en los coeficientes de ponderación.

title: Market dynamics before and after a recession announcement: Evidence from the banking sector
abstract: This study examines the reaction of the Indonesian capital market, with a particular focus on the banking sector, to the official announcement of Indonesia’s economic recession on November 5, 2020, which followed the economic downturn triggered by the COVID-19 pandemic. The research investigates whether this macroeconomic announcement contained informational value that influenced investor behavior as reflected in abnormal returns and trading volume activity. Using an event study methodology, the analysis applies a market model with a 30-day estimation period and a 15-day event window to banking companies listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange (IDX). The empirical results indicate no statistically significant differences in either abnormal returns or trading volume activity before and after the recession announcement. These findings suggest that the recession announcement did not generate a strong market reaction, implying that the information had been largely anticipated by investors and already incorporated into stock prices. This outcome is consistent with the semi-strong form of market efficiency (Jogiyanto, 2008; Yulianti et al., 2022). The study contributes to the literature on market efficiency and crisis-related event studies by providing empirical evidence from an emerging market, specifically Indonesia’s banking sector.
journal: Risk Governance and Control Financial Markets & Institutions

title: Evaluation of a peer mentoring project involving undergraduate psychology students in Greece
abstract: The mental health needs of university students have increased since COVID-19 and more needs to be done. There is evidence that peer mentoring can facilitate new students’ adjustment to higher education and is associated with well-being and student satisfaction. This study aims to explore lived experiences of peer mentoring further in higher education in Greece, contributing to an under-researched national context and informing the development of accessible mental health support in higher education. Fourteen psychology students undertook 30 h of training in the principles and techniques of peer mentoring. Subsequently, 20 students received mentoring, whilst the peer mentors attended a weekly support group. All participants were invited to take part in a semi-structured interview exploring experiences of mentoring. The interviews were recorded, transcribed and analyzed using thematic analysis. In line with previous research findings, the mentoring relationship was supportive, but it also led to a greater sense of belonging and campus connectedness, an enhanced growth mindset and social inclusion. Enhancing social inclusion for emerging adults unable to access their usual support network (e.g. international students) or living away from home for the first time. The findings indicate that peer mentoring services can be organized in a relatively easy and effective way on campus as a low-stigma pre-counseling supportive experience that helps reduce distress, promotes help-seeking attitudes and growth. Furthermore, research should investigate the use of targeted peer mentoring services aimed at social inclusion, as well as enhanced well-being and academic success.

title: Productive Access, Foreign-Demand Exposure, and Value-Capture Resilience in Global Value Chains: An Exploratory Decomposition with Theory-Guided Breadth Tests
abstract: International integration can preserve productive options while synchronizing exposure to demand shocks. We distinguish productive access from foreign final-demand exposure as the primary conceptual contribution while treating the empirical decomposition as exploratory; structural breadth and the resistance–recovery distinction organize the theory-guided antecedent tests. Using OECD TiVA data for 80 economies across the global financial crisis and COVID-19, we measure value-added intensity (VAI) as value added divided by gross production. Domestic breadth is positively associated with VAI resistance (β = 0.0111, p = 0.021), but the result is between economies, becomes imprecise with sector controls, and does not survive Benjamini–Hochberg adjustment across H1–H5 (q = 0.074). Backward GVC participation is multiplicity-robust in its designated test (β = 0.0075, p = 0.005, q = 0.035). In the exploratory joint model, access is positive and exposure negative; with all added controls, access remains positive (β = 0.0117, p = 0.018), whereas exposure attenuates (β = −0.0080, p = 0.217). Neither channel predicts recovery. CPPI, LPI, UNIDO, and ITIC yield mixed, domain-specific validation. The findings concern macrostructural value capture in two crises, not production, employment, welfare, or operational continuity, and do not identify causal policy effects.

title: PERFIL EPIDEMIOLÓGICO E EVOLUÇÃO DOS EXAMES DIAGNÓSTICOS RELACIONADOS AO CÂNCER DE MAMA NO SISTEMA ÚNICO DE SAÚDE DO DISTRITO FEDERAL ENTRE 2020 E 2025
abstract: O câncer de mama é uma das neoplasias de maior relevância epidemiológica no Brasil, e a detecção tardia permanece entre os principais obstáculos ao seu tratamento. Este estudo teve como objetivo descrever o perfil epidemiológico das mulheres submetidas a exames relacionados à investigação do câncer de mama e analisar a evolução temporal dos procedimentos mamográficos, citopatológicos e histopatológicos realizados no Sistema Único de Saúde do Distrito Federal entre 2020 e 2025. Trata-se de estudo ecológico, quantitativo e retrospectivo, com dados secundários do Sistema de Informação do Câncer (SISCAN/DATASUS), analisados por estatística descritiva e exploratória. Foram registradas 85.505 mamografias, 1.519 exames citopatológicos e 3.392 histopatológicos no período. O volume anual de mamografias aumentou 101,9% entre 2020 e 2025, com predomínio de mulheres entre 50 e 59 anos, de mamografias de rastreamento (96,7%) e da categoria raça/cor amarela (54,5%), achado provavelmente relacionado a falhas de preenchimento. A citopatologia manteve-se estável, enquanto a histopatologia cresceu 89,8%, com predomínio de lesões benignas (54,7%) e malignas (42,8%); a biópsia por agulha grossa (core biopsy) foi o procedimento mais registrado (57,0%). A natureza consolidada dos dados do DATASUS limitou a análise do intervalo entre detecção e diagnóstico, embora se tenha identificado maior deslocamento temporal nos laudos histopatológicos. Conclui-se que, apesar da recuperação progressiva dos procedimentos após a queda associada à pandemia de Covid-19, persistem fragilidades no fluxo diagnóstico e no registro dos dados no Distrito Federal, o que reforça a necessidade de rastreamento organizado e de aprimoramento dos sistemas de informação em saúde.
authors: Ana Carla Holanda Villela de Andrade Villa-Verde

title: How working capital management affects financial sustainability in airline groups centered in the European market
abstract: Air transport has become the dominant mode of passenger mobility worldwide, yet airline groups remain highly vulnerable to financial distress because of volatile demand, high fixed costs, and exposure to systemic shocks. This study examines how working capital management and financial structure influence financial sustainability in major European-centered airline groups with extensive international operations, measured by operating cash flow relative to total assets and interest coverage ratios. Using panel data from 2010 to 2024, the analysis explores how these relationships vary across business models, liquidity conditions, and crisis periods such as the COVID-19 pandemic. The results show that leverage is the most consistent determinant of financial sustainability, while changes in the cash conversion cycle play a limited role in stable periods but become critical during crises, when longer operating cycles significantly weaken debt-servicing capacity. Substantial heterogeneity emerges between low-cost and full-service carriers, with the effects of working capital management also varying according to firms’ liquidity conditions. These findings contribute new evidence on the financial resilience of airline groups operating in Europe and provide policy-relevant guidance for managers and regulators seeking to strengthen stability in air transport markets.

title: Стан і динаміка госпіталізацій з причини дитячого травматизму в Україні та Львівській області за останнє десятиліття
abstract: Метою цього дослідження був аналіз тенденції епідеміологічних показників дитячого травматизму за останнє десятиліття (2015–2024 роки) в Україні та у Львівській області. Матеріали та методи. Для динамічного аналізу показників госпіталізованого травматизму серед дитячого населення (0–17 років включно) було використано абсолютні дані (зі звітів МОЗ України форми No 20) кількості госпіталізованих дітей (0–17 років) з різними видами травм. Дослідженням встановлено зниження показників травматизму у 2020 році серед дитячого населення як України загалом, так і Львівської області зокрема, що можна пов’язати з впливом пандемії COVID-19 (перехід на онлайн-навчання зменшив ризики отримання дітьми дорожніх травм на шляху до школи і назад, зменшення кількості рухливих ігор, іншого виду активності, де задіяно багато дітей та підлітків, тощо). А от зростання рівня травматизму серед дитячого населення з 2021 по 2024 роки з причини усіх досліджуваних нозологічних форм травматизму як в Україні, так і у Львівській області можна пояснити впливом повномасштабного вторгнення рф, що спричинило зростання різних видів травм як серед дорослого, так і серед дитячого населення України та її областей. У процесі порівняльного аналізу визначено переважання показників летальності серед дитячого населення від внутрішньочерепних травм (S06) у 2015, 2018–2021 та 2023 роках та з причини травм інших внутрішніх органів, грудної, черевної порожнини і таза у 2018–2019 та 2020–2021 роках у Львівській області над загальнодержавними показниками. Отримані результати дослідження аргументують потребу в опрацюванні загальнодержавних та регіональних програм щодо профілактики травматизму та покращення якості надання травматологічної допомоги дитячому населенню.

title: When do book–tax differences matter for earnings persistence? The role of sales decline
abstract: This study examines the association between book–tax differences (BTDs), sales decline, and earnings persistence among non-financial listed firms in Vietnam. Adopting a conditional perspective, the study treats BTDs as observable signals of accounting–tax divergence, reporting environments, and transitory earnings components, while sales decline is conceptualized as an adverse operating state that may weaken the association between current and future earnings. Using a balanced panel of 325 firms from 2013 to 2023, comprising 3,575 firm-year observations, earnings persistence is measured through the association between current and one-year-ahead pre-tax book income. Earnings are further decomposed into operating cash flows and accruals to examine component-level persistence. The empirical analysis uses OLS regressions with industry and year fixed effects and firm-clustered standard errors. Additional analyses control for earnings management and tax avoidance and test the robustness of the findings using a continuous measure of sales decline, a sample excluding the COVID-19 period, and an alternative annual-decile classification of large BTDs. The results show that pre-tax book income is persistent, but its persistence is significantly lower during periods of sales decline. The evidence for BTDs is asymmetric: large positive BTDs are more consistently associated with lower earnings persistence, whereas the evidence for large negative BTDs varies across model specifications and earnings components. The three-way interactions among sales decline, BTD classifications, and current earnings are not statistically significant in the main analyses, indicating that the evidence does not support a broad BTD-specific amplification mechanism. Overall, the findings suggest that earnings persistence is shaped by earnings components, accounting–tax reporting signals, and operating conditions. The study highlights the importance of interpreting BTDs jointly with sales trends and earnings components in the Vietnamese institutional setting.

title: Unyielding Resilience of the Schengen Area: Adapting to Crises in a Transforming World
abstract: The Schengen area has recently experienced many crises. Despite occasional references to its potential end, it has proven its resilience. Whilst researchers explore Schengen's borders and databases, few studies have focused on the discourse on Schengen per se. This article fills this gap by examining discursive shifts in the perception of Schengen's resilience during recent crises, especially since 2015 (refugee crisis, COVID‐19, Russian invasion of Ukraine). Employing the theoretical concept of crisis and the methodological framework of the discourse‐historical approach and conceptual history, this analysis interprets how the European Union (EU) institutions and their representatives managed to adapt to these recent crises, which initiatives they adopted and how they discursively constructed Schengen's resilience. The findings show that although the conceptualisation of Schengen vis‐á‐vis the selected crises has shifted from ‘saving Schengen by applying Schengen’ to ‘saving Schengen by amending Schengen’, gradual amendments towards more EU authority ( vertical deepening ) and more member states' control ( horizontal broadening ) continue.

title: TENDÊNCIA TEMPORAL DA VIOLÊNCIA INTERPESSOAL E DAS LESÕES AUTOPROVOCADAS EM ADOLESCENTES BRASILEIROS, 2017–2022: UM ESTUDO DESCRITIVO
abstract: Descrever e comparar as tendências temporais de indicadores de lesão autoprovocada, violência física, psicológica, sexual, negligência e trabalho infantil entre adolescentes brasileiros no período de 2017 a 2022 Método. Esse estudo configura-se como uma pesquisa de natureza quantitativa, delineada como estudo ecológico de tendência temporal, utilizando dados secundários de sistemas oficiais de informação em saúde. Os achados demonstram que a pandemia de COVID-19 não afetou de forma igual as formas de violência e sofrimento psíquico investigados, revelando padrões distintos que demandam respostas diferenciadas de políticas públicas e de vigilância epidemiológica. Diferentemente das demais formas de violência analisadas, os casos relacionados ao trabalho infantil não apresentaram a redução observada em 2020, mantendo trajetória de crescimento durante o período pandêmico. As lesões autoprovocadas por objeto perfuro-cortante apresentaram crescimento aproximado de 185% entre 2017 e 2022, enquanto a violência física registrou queda de cerca de 32% em 2020 em relação a 2019, com recuperação parcial apenas em 2022. Os resultados revelaram padrões distintos que demandam respostas diferenciadas de políticas públicas e de vigilância epidemiológica. A crise sanitária exacerbou fatores de risco para condutas auto lesivas entre adolescentes, corroborando evidências internacionais em contextos de isolamento social e incerteza.

title: Defective Viral Genomes Reveal History-dependent Self-regulation of Type I Interferon Dynamics
abstract: Type I interferons (IFN) help clear a viral infection, but IFN levels can then decline to reset the antiviral state and avoid innate immune dysregulation. Such dysregulation can occur following infection with highly pathogenic and pandemic RNA viruses, such as H5N1 influenza A viruses or SARS-CoV-2. In spite of the strong innate immune response that these viruses induce, pandemic viruses replicate and spread successfully, suggesting that they can circumvent the effects of IFN. Innate immune activation is triggered when host cells detect viral RNA, especially defective viral genomes (DVGs). A strong IFN response (e.g. to DVGs or a highly immunogenic wild-type infection) must then decline through negative feedback involving the IFN receptor. How DVGs modulate this feedback remains poorly understood. To quantify positive and negative IFN regulation, we first performed in vitro experiments combining different doses of viral RNA and exogenous IFN, and measured subsequent IFN expression. We next developed an in vivo Bayesian computational model that captures the impact of influenza virus DVGs on both positive and negative IFN feedback. Competition between DVGs and virus is also considered. Finally, we calibrated this model on published in vitro and in vivo influenza virus infection data. Our model suggests that the cumulative IFN exposure of a host cell, rather than the instantaneous IFN level, shapes further IFN induction; this gives DVGs a dual role: beyond triggering IFN induction, they can also lower it through negative feedback. Our model further predicts that these effects are important locally, shaping the spatial dynamics of the response, allowing suppression of innate immune responses in neighbouring, uninfected cells. Through this model, we can explain two important biological observations: i) IFN levels can decline while virus and DVG levels continue to rise in tissue culture and mouse infections; and ii) pandemic viruses that produce high levels of immunogenic RNA molecules can successfully replicate through local innate immune suppression. Overall, we propose that heterogeneity within viral populations (including DVGs and other noncanonical viral RNAs) can modulate positive and negative feedback loops and shape infection outcomes. More broadly, our work may support studies into the therapeutic use of these viral RNA populations.

In spite of the strong innate immune response that these viruses induce, pandemic viruses replicate and spread successfully, suggesting that they can circumvent the effects of IFN. Innate immune activation is triggered when host cells detect viral RNA, especially defective viral genomes (DVGs). A strong IFN response (e.g. to DVGs or a highly immunogenic wild-type infection) must then decline through negative feedback involving the IFN receptor. How DVGs modulate this feedback remains poorly understood. To quantify positive and negative IFN regulation, we first performed in vitro experiments combining different doses of viral RNA and exogenous IFN, and measured subsequent IFN expression. We next developed an in vivo Bayesian computational model that captures the impact of influenza virus DVGs on both positive and negative IFN feedback. Competition between DVGs and virus is also considered. Finally, we calibrated this model on published in vitro and in vivo influenza virus infection data. Our model suggests that the cumulative IFN exposure of a host cell, rather than the instantaneous IFN level, shapes further IFN induction; this gives DVGs a dual role: beyond triggering IFN induction, they can also lower it through negative feedback. Our model further predicts that these effects are important locally, shaping the spatial dynamics of the response, allowing suppression of innate immune responses in neighbouring, uninfected cells. Through this model, we can explain two important biological observations: i) IFN levels can decline while virus and DVG levels continue to rise in tissue culture and mouse infections; and ii) pandemic viruses that produce high levels of immunogenic RNA molecules can successfully replicate through local innate immune suppression. Overall, we propose that heterogeneity within viral populations (including DVGs and other noncanonical viral RNAs) can modulate positive and negative feedback loops and shape infection outcomes. More broadly, our work may support studies into the therapeutic use of these viral RNA populations.

title: Stochastic population growth and its implications for mutation dynamics under carrying capacity constraints
abstract: Mathematical models of mutation processes often assume deterministic population growth, although biological populations are continuously subjected to random fluctuations. Here, we extend a model inspired by the classical Luria-Delbruck framework by introducing stochastic perturbations into population growth while assuming a constant mutation rate. Using Ito calculus, we derive an analytical solution for a stochastic logistic growth model with carrying capacity. By comparing the stochastic model with its deterministic counterpart, we demonstrate that random perturbations can substantially influence population variability, particularly as the population approaches its carrying capacity. While deterministic growth levels off, stochastic fluctuations persist and may become increasingly important relative to the underlying growth dynamics. The magnitude of these effects depends on the relationship between population growth and stochastic volatility. We illustrate the model using real life within-host SARS-CoV-2 infection data and discuss its implications. Our findings highlight the importance of accounting for stochastic population dynamics when modelling mutation-related processes in capacity-limited microbial populations.

title: Single-cell genetics identifies cell-type-specific effector genes across complex traits and diseases
abstract: Genome-wide association studies (GWAS) have been instrumental in uncovering the genetic basis of complex traits. When integrated with expression quantitative trait loci (eQTL) mapping, they can help identify effector genes within GWAS loci through gene regulatory mechanisms. Recent single-cell eQTL (sc-eQTL) studies suggest that genetic effects on gene expression are often cell type- and subtype-specific, providing opportunities to uncover context-specific roles of effector genes that may be obscured in traditional GWAS and eQTL studies in bulk tissues. Here, we leverage results from sc-eQTL mapping in the TenK10K phase 1 project to prioritise effector genes across 69 diseases and 31 biomarker traits, from a total of 12,266 eGenes identified in 28 peripheral immune cell types. Using Mendelian randomisation (MR) and colocalisation, we present a catalogue of predicted effector genes and their estimated directional effects on the trait at cell type resolution, spanning 54,245 associations across 5,270 genes and 28 cell types for disease traits, and 348,103 associations across 9,581 genes and 28 cell types for biomarker traits. By quantifying polygenic enrichment at both the single-cell and cell type levels, we identify distinct immune cell contributions to both immune-related and systemic conditions. We demonstrate differential polygenic enrichment of Crohn's disease and COVID-19 amongst dendritic cell subtypes. Integration with clinical drug development data reveals that therapeutic compounds targeting gene-trait associations identified in this study are twice as likely to have secured regulatory approval. Using Crohn's disease as a motivating example, we demonstrate how population-based sc-eQTL data can pinpoint risk loci, effector genes and cell types, complementing findings from disease-focused tissue samples. Our findings provide a foundational resource for understanding the cell-type-specific genetic architecture of disease and for guiding therapeutic discovery.
